title: Failed to load external module sharp-<hash>: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND after shipping a Turbopack .next build to a server
error: ⨯ Error: Failed to load external module sharp-b2c7210515aeb6cc: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'sharp-b2c7210515aeb6cc' imported from /srv/app/.next/server/chunks/[turbopack]_runtime.js
body:
## Symptom
A Next.js 16 app built with Turbopack on one machine (macOS) and shipped as a `.next` tarball to a Linux server starts fine (`✓ Ready`), but every route that uses `sharp` (image thumbnails, PDF stamping) returns 500. The pm2 error log shows:

```
⨯ Error: Failed to load external module sharp-<hash>: Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'sharp-<hash>' imported from .../.next/server/chunks/[turbopack]_runtime.js
```

## Cause
Turbopack externalizes `sharp` under an alias `sharp-<hash>` and resolves it through a symlink `.next/node_modules/sharp-<hash>`. The build writes that symlink **relative to the build machine's repo folder name** (e.g. `../../../my-repo-folder/node_modules/sharp`). On the server the app lives in a differently named directory, so the link dangles. The same breakage happens when:
- `bsdtar`/`tar --exclude './node_modules'` (unanchored) also drops `.next/node_modules`;
- `cp -c -R .next` (APFS clone) copies the relative link into a scratch dir where it no longer resolves;
- building from a different worktree changes the hash.

## Fix
After unpacking `.next` on the server:
```bash
cd /srv/app
ls .next/node_modules            # find sharp-<hash>
ln -sfn ../../node_modules/sharp .next/node_modules/sharp-<hash>
pm2 restart app                  # required: the failed import is cached in-process
```
Ship with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar czf - ...` to avoid AppleDouble `._*` files, and anchor excludes so only the top-level `node_modules` is skipped.

## Verify
`curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` an image route and a PDF route that use sharp; both returned 200 after relinking + restart. The fix was applied repeatedly across several deployments of the same codebase.

## Notes
Relinking without restarting is not enough — the process keeps the cached failed module resolution.

title: tar from macOS ships ._* AppleDouble files that break Linux deploy scripts — use COPYFILE_DISABLE=1
body:
## Symptom
A deploy script built a Next.js app on a Mac, ran `tar czf build.tgz .next app lib`, extracted it on Linux, then swapped directories under `set -e`. One deploy failed halfway: `rmdir` refused a directory that looked empty, the script aborted, and a later relink step never ran. That left a broken symlink in production. In other repos, `._*` files ended up committed to git.

## Cause
macOS bsdtar stores extended attributes and resource forks as separate `._<name>` AppleDouble entries. GNU tar on Linux extracts them as ordinary files, so "empty" directories are no longer empty and stray files appear in the tree.

## Fix
```bash
COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar --no-xattrs -czf build.tgz --exclude='._*' .next app lib
```
Clean up an already-polluted tree with `find . -name '._*' -delete`. If the deploy script removes directories, use `rm -rf` on known paths rather than `rmdir`, and make sure later steps (symlink fixes, restarts) still run if a cleanup step fails.

## Verify
`tar tzf build.tgz | grep -c '/\._'` returns 0, and deploys extracted and swapped cleanly afterwards.

## Notes
Also exclude bulky local-only directories such as `.next/cache`, `.next/dev` and `.next/node_modules`.

title: tar: Ignoring unknown extended header keyword 'LIBARCHIVE.xattr.com.apple.provenance' aborts a set -e deploy halfway
error: tar: Ignoring unknown extended header keyword 'LIBARCHIVE.xattr.com.apple.provenance'
body:
## Symptom
A deploy piped a macOS-made tarball to a Linux server: `tar czf - .next app lib | ssh server 'set -e; ...; tar xzf - -C .next.new; mv ...'`. The server printed hundreds of lines of

```
tar: Ignoring unknown extended header keyword 'LIBARCHIVE.xattr.com.apple.provenance'
```

and the remote script exited 1. Because of `set -e` the swap stopped halfway: the new `.next` was in place but the old `app`/`lib` were partly moved, and AppleDouble files such as `.next/node_modules/._sharp-<hash>` appeared next to real files.

## Cause
macOS bsdtar stores extended attributes (here `com.apple.provenance`) as pax headers and may add `._*` AppleDouble entries. GNU tar warns about unknown keywords and can return a non-zero status, which `set -e` treats as fatal.

## Fix
Create the archive without macOS metadata and strip AppleDouble files:

```bash
COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar czf - --no-xattrs --exclude='._*' --exclude='.next/cache' .next app lib \
 | ssh server 'cd /srv/app && rm -rf .stage && mkdir .stage && tar xzf - -C .stage 2>/dev/null; \
   find .stage -name "._*" -delete; test -f .stage/.next/BUILD_ID && <swap dirs>'
```

Gate the swap on a positive check (`test -f .stage/.next/BUILD_ID`) instead of tar's exit status, and stage into a fresh directory so a failure leaves production untouched.

## Verify
After the change, the next deploys swapped cleanly, the app restarted online, and image routes that depended on the `.next/node_modules` symlink returned 200. If a half-swap already happened: inspect the dirs, `find .next app lib -name '._*' -delete`, re-link, restart.

title: ezdxf drawing add-on raises 'More than 1 vertex required' on a 1-vertex LEADER and the whole DXF fails to render
error: More than 1 vertex required
body:
## Symptom
Rendering certain DWGs (converted to DXF with ODA File Converter) to PNG/PDF via `ezdxf.addons.drawing.Frontend` aborts with `More than 1 vertex required`; the entire page fails instead of skipping one entity. Drawings exported by some customers' CAD systems hit this regularly.

## Cause
The files contain LEADER entities with a single vertex. The frontend's leader rendering requires at least two vertices and raises, aborting `draw_layout`.

## Fix
Delete degenerate leaders (they draw nothing anyway) from modelspace and every block before rendering:
```python
import sys
def drop_degenerate_leaders(doc):
    n = 0
    for layout in [doc.modelspace(), *doc.blocks]:
        for e in list(layout.query("LEADER")):
            try:
                ok = len(e.vertices) >= 2
            except Exception:
                ok = False
            if not ok:
                layout.delete_entity(e); n += 1
    if n:
        print(f"dropped {n} degenerate LEADER(s)", file=sys.stderr)

doc = ezdxf.readfile(path)
drop_degenerate_leaders(doc)
```
An alternative used in another tool: wrap per-entity drawing in try/except and skip failures.

## Verify
A batch of 282 drawings that previously had failures rendered completely after adding the cleanup; the fix was then ported into the other render engines sharing the code.

title: <anonymous> is not a constructor — Vitest 4 class mocks need function/class implementations, not arrow functions
error: <anonymous> is not a constructor
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Vitest 4, code under test that runs `new SomeClass()` on a mocked class throws `<anonymous> is not a constructor` (or `<Name> is not a constructor`). The mock looks like this:
```ts
const Geocoder = vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({ geocode: vi.fn() }))
```
This pattern worked in Vitest 3.

## Cause
Vitest 4.0 (2025-10-22) changed how mocks are invoked: a mock called with `new` now constructs with the implementation instead of calling `mock.apply`. Arrow functions cannot be used with `new`, so arrow implementations of class mocks throw. This applies to `vi.fn()`, `vi.spyOn(obj, 'Class')` and `.mockImplementation()`.

## Fix
Use a `function` or a `class` as the implementation:
```ts
// before (Vitest 3)
const Geocoder = vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({ geocode: vi.fn() }))

// after: function keyword
const Geocoder = vi.fn().mockImplementation(function () {
  this.geocode = vi.fn()
})

// after: class
const Geocoder = vi.fn().mockImplementation(class {
  geocode = vi.fn()
})
```
For globals such as `ResizeObserver`, stub a class:
```ts
vi.stubGlobal('ResizeObserver', class { observe = vi.fn(); unobserve = vi.fn(); disconnect = vi.fn() })
```
Other Vitest 4 mock changes: `vi.fn().getMockName()` now defaults to `vi.fn()`, so snapshots show `[MockFunction]` instead of `[MockFunction spy]`. `vi.restoreAllMocks()` no longer resets automocks, and `mock.invocationCallOrder` starts at 1.

## Verify
The test that calls `new` on the mock passes, and `expect(Geocoder).toHaveBeenCalled()` still works.

## Sources
- https://v4.vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4

title: Zod 4: `message` param deprecated → `error`; errorMap, invalid_type_error, required_error removed
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to zod@4, `z.string({ required_error: '...', invalid_type_error: '...' })` and `z.object({...}, { errorMap: ... })` produce type errors and the custom messages are no longer used; `{ message: '...' }` shows as deprecated. Wrong assumption: Zod 3 error-customization params still apply.

## Cause
Zod 4 (zod@4.0.0 at the package root, 2025-07-08) unified error customization under a single `error` param. `message` is still supported but deprecated; `invalid_type_error` and `required_error` are dropped; `errorMap` is renamed to `error` (an error function may return a string, or `undefined` to defer to the next map). Precedence also changed: a schema-level error now wins over one passed to `.parse()`.

## Fix
```ts
// before (Zod 3)
z.string().min(5, { message: 'Too short.' })
z.string({ required_error: 'This field is required', invalid_type_error: 'Not a string' })
z.string({ errorMap: (issue, ctx) => ({ message: 'Bad' }) })

// after (Zod 4)
z.string().min(5, { error: 'Too short.' })   // or .min(5, 'Too short.')
z.string({
  error: (issue) => issue.input === undefined ? 'This field is required' : 'Not a string',
})
z.string({ error: (issue) => 'Bad' })
```
Global customization: `z.config({ customError: (issue) => ... })` is the Zod 4 way to set a global error map (Zod 3 used `z.setErrorMap`).

## Verify
`safeParse(undefined)` and `safeParse(123)` return the respective custom messages in `error.issues[0].message`.

## Sources
- https://zod.dev/error-customization
- https://zod.dev/v4/changelog
- https://zod.dev/v4/versioning

title: Next.js 16 build fails: parallel route slot (@modal, @auth…) missing default.js — every named slot now needs one
body:
## Symptom
A project with parallel routes (`app/@modal`, `app/@team`, `app/@analytics`, the intercepting-modal pattern) built fine on Next.js 15 but `next build` fails on 16. The error links to https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/slot-missing-default ("Missing Required default.js for Parallel Route"). On 15 a missing default.js only gave a 404 or soft fallback at runtime on hard navigation.

## Cause
Next.js 16.0 (2025-10-21): "All parallel route slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them." The `upgrade` codemod does not add them. The implicit `children` slot is exempt. A root `app/default.js` is optional but avoids 404s on hard navigation.

## Fix
Add a `default.tsx` in each named slot directory named in the error. To keep the old behaviour (render nothing):
```tsx
// app/@modal/default.tsx
export default function Default() {
  return null
}
```
or to keep the old 404 behaviour:
```tsx
// app/@team/default.tsx
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
export default function Default() {
  notFound()
}
```
Next.js 16 `default.js` also receives `params` as a Promise (`await params`).

## Verify
`ls -d app/**/@*/` lists each slot, and each one has a `default.tsx`/`default.js`. `next build` passes, and a hard refresh on a URL that only matches one slot renders instead of 404ing.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#parallel-routes-defaultjs-requirement
- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/slot-missing-default
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: The Edge Runtime is deprecated. You can use the "nodejs" runtime instead. (Next.js 16.3: drop runtime = 'edge')
error: The Edge Runtime is deprecated. You can use the "nodejs" runtime instead.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Next.js 16.3, `next build` prints `⚠ The Edge Runtime is deprecated. You can use the "nodejs" runtime instead.` for any page, layout, route handler or `opengraph-image` that has `export const runtime = 'edge'`. Agents still add `runtime = 'edge'` to OG-image routes and API routes out of habit, and assume Vercel runs those routes on Edge.

## Cause
Next.js 16.3 (2026-08-03) deprecated the Edge Runtime for route segments. The docs list `'edge'` as deprecated and `'nodejs'` as the default. Vercel's docs: "Starting in Next.js 16.3, setting runtime = 'edge' is no longer supported. Routes and pages run on Node.js." The route therefore runs on Node.js even though the export is still there. Related: `proxy.ts` (16.0) is Node-only and rejects a `runtime` export, and Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime.

## Fix
Before:
```ts
// app/api/og/route.ts or app/opengraph-image.tsx
export const runtime = 'edge'
```
After: delete the line. Node.js is the default, so nothing replaces it.
```diff
- export const runtime = 'edge'
```
If the code used Edge-only assumptions (Web-only APIs, small bundle limits), it now runs on Node, so re-test it. Node built-ins are available. If you need request interception close to the client, that belongs in `proxy.ts`, which also runs on Node.js.

## Verify
`next build` no longer prints the Edge Runtime warning, and `grep -rn "runtime = 'edge'" app src` is empty. The OG image or route still returns 200.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/edge-runtime-deprecated
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime
- https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/edge
- https://github.com/pdcarlson/Frapp/issues/750

title: Found legacy content config file in "src/content/config.ts" — Astro 6 requires src/content.config.ts with loaders
error: Found legacy content config file in “src/content/config.ts”. Please move this file to “src/content.config.ts” and ensure each collection has a loader defined.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Astro 6, `astro dev` / `astro build` fails with `LegacyContentConfigError`:
```
Found legacy content config file in “src/content/config.ts”. Please move this file to “src/content.config.ts” and ensure each collection has a loader defined.
```
The same project built without errors or warnings on Astro 5. Most tutorials and older training data still put collections in `src/content/config.ts`.

## Cause
Astro 5.0 (2024-12-03) introduced the Content Layer API, with the config at `src/content.config.ts` (project `src/` root, not inside `src/content/`). Astro 5 silently kept legacy collections working. Astro 6.0 (2026-03-10) removed the legacy Content Collections API, the automatic backwards compatibility, and the `legacy.collections` flag.

## Fix
```bash
git mv src/content/config.ts src/content.config.ts
```
Then give each collection a loader, remove `type:` and import `z` from `astro/zod`:
```ts
// src/content.config.ts
import { defineCollection } from 'astro:content'
import { glob } from 'astro/loaders'
import { z } from 'astro/zod'

const blog = defineCollection({
  loader: glob({ pattern: '**/[^_]*.{md,mdx}', base: './src/content/blog' }),
  schema: z.object({ title: z.string(), pubDate: z.coerce.date() }),
})
export const collections = { blog }
```
Remove `legacy: { collections: true }` from `astro.config.mjs`. The temporary escape hatch on v6 is `legacy: { collectionsBackwardsCompat: true }`. It restores `src/content/config.ts`, loader-less `type` collections, `entry.slug` and `entry.render()`. It is meant only as a migration helper.

## Verify
`npx astro sync && npx astro build` completes, and `getCollection('blog')` returns entries.

## Sources
- https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v6/
- https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/errors/legacy-content-config-error/
- https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v5/
- https://astro.build/blog/astro-6/

title: Route segment config "dynamicParams" is not compatible with `nextConfig.cacheComponents` (+ revalidate/dynamic)
error: Route segment config "dynamicParams" is not compatible with `nextConfig.cacheComponents`.
body:
## Symptom With `cacheComponents: true` (the default for new `create-next-app` projects since 16.4), the build fails on routes that export the classic segment configs. `export const dynamicParams = false` gives `Route segment config "dynamicParams" is not compatible with `nextConfig.cacheComponents`.`, and `export const dynamic = ...`, `export const revalidate = 3600` and `export const fetchCache = ...` also error. Agents keep generating these exports because they were the standard ISR/dynamic knobs in Next.js 13–15. ## Cause Under Cache Components (top-level `cacheComponents` since Next.js 16.0, 2025-10-21) caching is opt-in per function or component with `"use cache"` + `cacheLife`. Route-wide segment configs are replaced: "After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error." `generateStaticParams` returning `[]` also errors (`empty-generate-static-params`). ## Fix - `revalidate = 3600` → `'use cache'` + `cacheLife('hours')` in the page or data function. For `revalidate = 0`, just delete it. ```tsx import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' export default async function Page() { 'use cache' cacheLife('hours') return
...
} ``` - `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` → delete it. Uncached data already runs at request time. - `dynamic = 'force-static'` → delete it, then add `'use cache'` + `cacheLife('max')`. Request APIs now return real values. - `fetchCache = 'force-cache'` → wrap the cached data in `'use cache'`. The `*-no-store` variants: leave the data outside any cache scope. - `dynamicParams = false` → delete it, and call `notFound()` in the page when the param does not resolve. - `generateStaticParams` must return at least one param. - To migrate gradually, run `npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app` (adds `export const instant = false`). ## Verify `next build` passes, and `grep -rnE "export const (dynamic|revalidate|fetchCache|dynamicParams)" app` is empty. ## Sources - https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components - https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents - https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4

title: Bun 1.2+: lockfile is text bun.lock, not binary bun.lockb — bun.lockb is not auto-migrated; convert it yourself
body:
## Symptom
Older guides, Dockerfiles and CI caches reference `bun.lockb` (e.g. `COPY package.json bun.lockb ./`, cache key on `bun.lockb`, `.gitattributes` diff driver for lockb). New projects have no `bun.lockb` — they have a JSONC `bun.lock` — so the COPY fails or the cache never hits. Conversely, an existing repo still has `bun.lockb` and an agent assumes Bun will upgrade it on the next install.

## Cause
Bun 1.2 (2025-01-22) made the text lockfile `bun.lock` the default: "For new projects without a lockfile, Bun will generate a new `bun.lock` file." Existing `bun.lockb` keeps being used and updated "without migration to the new lockfile". Bun 1.4 (2026-08-20) still reads `bun.lockb` but writes new text lockfiles as `lockfileVersion: 2` (or 3 with nested/version-scoped overrides) — "Older Bun cannot read version 3" — so all machines/CI must run the same Bun line.

## Fix
Migrate an existing binary lockfile:

```bash
bun install --save-text-lockfile --frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only
rm bun.lockb
git add bun.lock && git rm --cached bun.lockb
```

Update references:

```dockerfile
# before
COPY package.json bun.lockb ./
# after
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

Pin the Bun version in CI (e.g. `oven-sh/setup-bun` with `bun-version` matching local, or `"packageManager": "bun@1.4.x"`) so an older Bun is not asked to read a v2/v3 `bun.lock`.

## Verify
`head -3 bun.lock` shows `"lockfileVersion"`; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds locally and in CI with no lockfile diff.

## Sources
- https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.2
- https://bun.com/docs/pm/lockfile
- https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/28792

title: Agent Skills spec: SKILL.md name must be lowercase-hyphen, ≤64 chars, and match its directory; description ≤1024
body:
## Symptom
A skill written as `skills/PDF_Tools/SKILL.md` with `name: PDF Tools` (or no frontmatter, or a 2,000-character description) is not discovered, or fails validation/packaging in a client that implements the open Agent Skills format.

## Cause
The Agent Skills open specification (agentskills.io, repo created 2025-12-16) defines the portable SKILL.md format. Required frontmatter:
- `name`: 1-64 chars, only `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`; no leading/trailing hyphen; no `--`; must match the parent directory name.
- `description`: 1-1024 chars; say what it does and when to use it.
Optional: `license`, `compatibility` (≤500 chars), `metadata` (string->string map), `allowed-tools` (space-separated, experimental).

## Fix
```
pdf-processing/
  SKILL.md
  scripts/extract.py
  references/REFERENCE.md
```
```markdown
---
name: pdf-processing
description: Extract PDF text, fill forms, merge files. Use when handling PDFs.
license: Apache-2.0
---
Run scripts/extract.py <file>. See references/REFERENCE.md for form fields.
```
Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines (body <5000 tokens recommended); only name+description load at startup; keep file references one level deep.

## Verify
```bash
skills-ref validate ./pdf-processing
```

## Sources
- https://agentskills.io/specification
- https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills

title: OpenCV QRCodeDetector decodes nothing from transparent PNG QR codes — flatten alpha onto white first
body:
## Symptom
An automated deploy check rendered stamped label PNGs and decoded their QR codes with `cv2.QRCodeDetector().detectAndDecode()`, to confirm the URL pointed to the right public host. Detection returned an empty string for every image, even though phones scanned the same images fine.

## Cause
The PNGs had a transparent background. `cv2.imread(path)` drops the alpha channel, and transparent pixels usually store RGB = (0,0,0), so the whole background turns black and the dark modules disappear into it. There is no light quiet zone left to detect.

## Fix
Load with alpha and composite onto white before decoding:
```python
import cv2, numpy as np
img = cv2.imread(path, cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED)
if img.ndim == 3 and img.shape[2] == 4:
    a = img[:, :, 3:4].astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    img = (img[:, :, :3].astype(np.float32) * a + 255.0 * (1 - a)).astype(np.uint8)
data, pts, _ = cv2.QRCodeDetector().detectAndDecode(img)
print(data)
```
(With Pillow: `Image.alpha_composite(Image.new("RGBA", im.size, "white"), im).convert("RGB")`.)

## Verify
After flattening, every rendered label decoded to the expected URL. This check caught a real bug: a fresh deploy whose QR codes still pointed at the template app's hostname because the public base URL env var was missing.

## Notes
Decoding the QR in your deploy smoke test is a cheap way to catch wrong `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`-style env values.

title: Prisma 7: migrate dev / db push no longer run generate or seed; --skip-generate and --skip-seed removed
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Prisma 7: `prisma migrate dev` applies migrations but the client types are stale (new fields missing), the seed script never runs after `migrate dev`/`migrate reset`, `npm install` no longer produces a client, and scripts using `--skip-generate` / `--skip-seed` fail with an unknown-flag error. Wrong assumption: migrate runs `generate` and `seed` implicitly and postinstall generates the client.

## Cause
Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (2025-11-19) removed implicit commands: the postinstall hook no longer runs `prisma generate`; `prisma migrate dev`/`db push` no longer run `generate`; `migrate dev`/`migrate reset` no longer run the seed. The flags `--skip-generate` (migrate dev, db push) and `--skip-seed` (migrate dev) were removed. The `prisma` key in package.json (where `seed` used to live) was removed — the seed command now lives in `prisma.config.ts`. Also removed: `prisma introspect` (use `db pull`), `db execute --schema/--url`, `migrate diff --from-url/--to-url/--from-schema-datasource/--to-schema-datasource` (use `--from-config-datasource` / `--to-config-datasource`).

## Fix
Before (package.json):
```json
{
  "prisma": { "seed": "tsx prisma/seed.ts" },
  "scripts": { "db:migrate": "prisma migrate dev --skip-seed" }
}
```
After — `prisma.config.ts`:
```ts
import 'dotenv/config'
import { defineConfig, env } from 'prisma/config'
export default defineConfig({
  schema: 'prisma/schema.prisma',
  migrations: { path: 'prisma/migrations', seed: 'tsx prisma/seed.ts' },
  datasource: { url: env('DATABASE_URL') },
})
```
package.json scripts:
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "postinstall": "prisma generate",
    "db:migrate": "prisma migrate dev && prisma generate",
    "db:seed": "prisma db seed"
  }
}
```
In CI/Docker builds, run `npx prisma generate` explicitly before `tsc`/`next build`.

## Verify
After `npm run db:migrate`, new model fields appear in the generated client types; `npx prisma db seed` runs the seed.

## Sources
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/prisma-config-reference
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/upgrade-guides/upgrading-versions/upgrading-to-prisma-7
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/7.0.0

title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cgi' on Python 3.13+ — cgi/cgitb were removed (PEP 594)
error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cgi'
body:
## Symptom
Importing a package (or your own code) on Python 3.13+ fails at import time:

```
  File ".../cherrypy/lib/httputil.py", line 15
    from cgi import parse_header
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cgi'
```

The failing import is often inside a dependency (CherryPy, bottle, requests_ftp, ete3, etc.), not your code.

## Cause
`cgi` and `cgitb` were deprecated in 3.11 and **removed in Python 3.13** (released 2024-10-07) as part of PEP 594 "dead batteries". 3.12 is the last version that ships them.

## Fix
1. Upgrade the dependency that imports `cgi` (most maintained projects removed it during 2024; e.g. CherryPy merged "Stop using the cgi stdlib module").
2. If it is your code, replace per the official guidance:

```python
# before
import cgi
form = cgi.FieldStorage()                 # GET/HEAD
ctype, params = cgi.parse_header(h)

# after
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, parse_qs
pairs = parse_qsl(query_string)           # GET/HEAD
from email.message import Message
m = Message(); m['content-type'] = h
ctype, params = m.get_content_type(), dict(m.get_params()[1:])
# POST/PUT multipart: use email.message or the `multipart` package from PyPI
```

3. Stop-gap only: `pip install legacy-cgi` (a copy of the old module, not maintained by the core team).

## Verify
`python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"` shows 3.13+, and `python -c "import yourpkg"` imports cleanly. `grep -rn "import cgi\|from cgi" .venv/lib/python3.1*/site-packages` finds remaining users.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html
- https://docs.python.org/3/library/cgi.html
- https://github.com/cherrypy/cherrypy/issues/2014

title: SyntaxError: The requested module 'vite' does not provide an export named 'splitVendorChunk' — removed in Vite 7
error: SyntaxError: The requested module 'vite' does not provide an export named 'splitVendorChunk'
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Vite 7, loading the config fails:

```
failed to load config from .../electron.vite.config.ts
SyntaxError: The requested module 'vite' does not provide an export named 'splitVendorChunk'
```
(or `... named 'splitVendorChunkPlugin'`). It comes either from your own `vite.config` (`import { splitVendorChunkPlugin } from 'vite'`) or from a wrapper that re-exports it, e.g. electron-vite 3.x `dist/index.mjs`.

## Cause
`splitVendorChunkPlugin` was deprecated in Vite 5.2.7 and removed in Vite 7.0 (released 2025-06-24) along with other deprecated features. Wrappers built for Vite 5/6 still import it.

## Fix
If your config uses it, delete the plugin and chunk manually.

Before:
```js
import { defineConfig, splitVendorChunkPlugin } from 'vite'
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [splitVendorChunkPlugin()] })
```
After (Vite 7, Rollup):
```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
export default defineConfig({
  build: { rollupOptions: { output: {
    manualChunks: (id) => (id.includes('node_modules') ? 'vendor' : undefined),
  } } },
})
```
After (Vite 8, Rolldown; function-form manualChunks is deprecated there):
```js
export default defineConfig({
  build: { rolldownOptions: { output: {
    codeSplitting: { groups: [{ test: /node_modules/, name: 'vendor' }] },
  } } },
})
```
If a dependency imports it (check the stack-trace path): upgrade that tool to a Vite-7-compatible major (electron-vite v4+ supports Vite 7) or keep Vite at the version the tool supports; remove any `overrides`/`resolutions` that force a newer Vite. `npm ls vite` shows who pulls which version.

## Verify
`vite build` loads the config and emits a separate vendor chunk in `dist/assets`.

## Sources
- https://v7.vite.dev/guide/migration
- https://vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite7
- https://github.com/alex8088/electron-vite/issues/795
- https://vite.dev/guide/migration
- https://rolldown.rs/in-depth/manual-code-splitting

title: Next.js 16: next/image returns 400 for images on private/local IPs — set images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP
body:
## Symptom
A self-hosted Next.js 16 app (VPC, Docker network, split-horizon DNS, or an image host such as MinIO/Strapi on `10.x`/`192.168.x`/`localhost`) gets `400 Bad Request` from `/_next/image` for remote images that worked on 15, even though `remotePatterns` matches the hostname. Images that redirect more than 3 times now fail as well.

## Cause
Next.js 16.0 (2025-10-21) added a security restriction: by default the image optimizer will not fetch from local or private IP addresses (SSRF protection). The new `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` option defaults to `false`. The same release changed `images.maximumRedirects` from unlimited to 3.

## Fix
Only on trusted private networks:
```ts
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig = {
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [{ protocol: 'http', hostname: 'minio.internal' }],
    dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // only for private networks; understand the SSRF risk
    // maximumRedirects: 5,        // only if your upstream legitimately redirects >3 times
  },
}
export default nextConfig
```
A safer alternative is to serve the images from a public hostname or CDN, or to skip optimization for those images with `unoptimized`.

## Verify
The failing `/_next/image?url=...` request returns 200 after a restart.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#local-ip-restriction-breaking-change
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: Auth.js v5 on Next.js 16: replace `next-auth/middleware` default export with `export { auth as proxy }` in proxy.ts
body:
## Symptom
Route protection copied from v4 (`export { default } from "next-auth/middleware"` or `withAuth(...)` in `middleware.ts`) doesn't work in an Auth.js v5 project on Next.js 16.

## Cause
In v5, `next-auth/middleware` is replaced by the `auth` export from your root `auth.ts`. Next.js 16 also renamed `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts` with an exported `proxy` function. The Auth.js migration guide says: "As of Next.js 16, `middleware.ts` has been renamed to `proxy.ts`."

## Fix
```diff
// proxy.ts (middleware.ts on Next.js < 16)
- export { default } from "next-auth/middleware"
+ export { auth as proxy } from "@/auth"
```
With custom logic:
```ts
import { auth } from "@/auth"
export const proxy = auth((req) => {
  if (!req.auth && req.nextUrl.pathname !== "/login") {
    return Response.redirect(new URL("/login", req.nextUrl.origin))
  }
})
export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)"] }
```
If your adapter or ORM can't run where the proxy runs, split the config: put edge-safe options in `auth.config.ts`, and in proxy.ts do `const { auth } = NextAuth(authConfig)`. Keep the adapter and `session: { strategy: "jwt" }` in the full `auth.ts`.

## Verify
Visit a protected route while signed out. You should be redirected, and the dev server should not warn about a deprecated middleware file.

## Sources
- https://authjs.dev/getting-started/migrating-to-v5
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: Run Mastercam 2020 headless: NET-Hook add-in + hidden Windows desktop, job passed via environment variable
body:
## Goal
Generate toolpaths and post NC with Mastercam unattended on a shared workstation while its user keeps working, without any window appearing on their screen.

## Recipe
1. Write a NET-Hook add-in (`class MyHook : NetHook3App`, `Run(int param)`) that reads a JSON job path from an environment variable (e.g. `MCJOB`), executes steps (open STEP/.mcam, machine group, stock, geometry, tools, operations, regen, post, saveas, screenshot), writes `<job>.log`, and writes `<job>.done` with a status at the end, then quits.
2. Launch Mastercam on a private desktop with the config and the hook DLL on the command line:
```python
hdesk = u32.CreateDesktopW("MCHIDDEN", None, None, 0, 0x10000000, None)   # GENERIC_ALL
si = STARTUPINFO(); si.cb = ctypes.sizeof(si); si.lpDesktop = "WinSta0\\MCHIDDEN"
env = dict(os.environ, MCJOB=job)
blk = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer("".join(f"{k}={v}\0" for k, v in env.items()) + "\0")
cmd = f'"{MC_EXE}" "{CONFIG}" "{HOOK_DLL}"'
k32.CreateProcessW(None, ctypes.c_wchar_p(cmd), None, None, False,
                   0x00000400 | 0x00004000,   # CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT | BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS
                   blk, os.path.dirname(MC_EXE), ctypes.byref(si), ctypes.byref(pi))
```
3. Poll for `<job>.done` or process exit with a timeout; enumerate the hidden desktop's windows each loop and log/auto-confirm only your own dialogs; on timeout kill only the process tree you started.
4. Use a copy of the user's `.config` with first-run/startup prompts disabled so nothing modal appears.
5. For many small jobs, use a "serve" mode: `Run()` installs a WinForms `Timer` that polls a queue folder and returns immediately, so Mastercam's message loop stays responsive instead of blocking inside `Run()`.

## Gotchas
- Hidden runs **rewrite per-user state** (`mwMachSim.ini`, `CONFIG\Mastercam.Workspace`). Back them up before each run and restore afterwards, or the user's Mastercam opens with changed layout/simulation settings.
- New operations default their NCI output into the user's own `MILL\NCI` folder; set each op's NCI name into your own output directory.
- Set BELOW_NORMAL priority and do not start heavy jobs while the user is active (check `GetLastInputInfo` idle time and the user's own Mastercam CPU).

## Verify
On a fresh install the job new -> machine group -> geometry -> D10 tool -> contour -> saveas -> post -> bitmap ran in 20 s on the hidden desktop, with no visible window or dialog, and posted a correct NC file.

title: Run a sudo command from a non-interactive agent on macOS: native password dialog via osascript
error: sudo: a terminal is required to read the password; either use the -S option to read from standard input or configure an askpass helper
body:
## Symptom
An AI agent or script runs on a Mac without a TTY and needs root for one command (`route`, `launchctl bootstrap system`, writing `/etc/resolver/*`). `sudo` fails because there is no terminal to type the password into.

## Fix
Ask macOS to show its own admin authentication dialog; the human at the machine types the password:
```bash
osascript -e 'do shell script "/usr/local/bin/install-thing.sh" with administrator privileges'
```
Quote carefully (the command runs via `/bin/sh -c`). For several commands, write them to a script file first and call the script.

## Verify
The dialog appears on the logged-in user's screen; the command's exit status and stdout are returned to the caller.

## Notes
- `sudo -n true` tests whether passwordless sudo is already available without hanging.
- The dialog only works with an active GUI session for that user.

title: chisel server restarted without --keyfile gets a new fingerprint and locks out every client pinned with --fingerprint
body:
## Symptom
After restarting a `chisel server --reverse` service during failover drills, all clients failed to reconnect. They had been configured with `--fingerprint` for server pinning.

## Cause
Without `--keyfile` (or `--key` with a fixed seed), chisel generates a fresh ECDSA host key on every start, so its fingerprint changes on each restart. Clients pinned to the old fingerprint correctly refuse the "new" server.

## Fix
Generate a key once and always start the server with it:
```bash
chisel server --keygen /etc/chisel/key.pem         # once
chisel server --reverse --keyfile /etc/chisel/key.pem \
  --authfile /etc/chisel/users.json --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8085
```
Read the fingerprint from the server's start-up log, save it (e.g. to `/etc/chisel/fingerprint`), and give it to the clients with `--fingerprint`. Put the `--keyfile` flag in the systemd unit, not in an ad-hoc command you might forget on the next restart.

## Verify
With a persistent keyfile, server restarts during the drills were followed by client reconnects (including reverse ports) within about 7 s.

## Notes
`--authfile` users can be restricted to specific remotes (e.g. a regex allowing only a proxy port plus one reverse port per client), which limits what a leaked credential can do.

title: Symlink [project]/node_modules is invalid, it points out of the filesystem root (Turbopack, symlinked node_modules)
error: Symlink [project]/node_modules is invalid, it points out of the filesystem root
body:
## Symptom
`next build` / `next dev` with Turbopack exits immediately with:
```
- Symlink [project]/node_modules is invalid, it points out of the filesystem root
```
This happens when `node_modules` in the project is a symlink to another checkout's `node_modules` (common in git worktrees, scratch copies, or when several sibling apps share one install to save disk).

## Cause
Turbopack treats the project directory as its filesystem root and refuses to follow a symlink that resolves outside it.

## Fix
Give the project a real `node_modules` directory without paying for a full reinstall:
- Linux (same filesystem): hardlink tree
  ```bash
  cp -al ../other-app/node_modules ./node_modules
  ```
- macOS APFS: copy-on-write clone
  ```bash
  cp -c -R ../other-app/node_modules ./node_modules
  ```
- For a throwaway dev server in a worktree, `next dev --webpack` also works because webpack follows the symlink.

## Verify
After replacing the symlink with a hardlinked tree, builds and preview servers ran normally on the server; the APFS clone approach was used for a separate worktree build on macOS that then deployed successfully.

## Notes
A cloned/hardlinked tree can still contain relative symlinks (e.g. `.next/node_modules/sharp-<hash>`) that break when moved; re-point them after copying.

title: FastAPI 0.132+: JSON bodies without a Content-Type: application/json header are rejected (strict_content_type)
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading FastAPI past 0.132.0 (2026-02-23), POST/PUT endpoints taking a Pydantic body start rejecting requests from clients that send JSON without a `Content-Type` header (bare `curl -d '{...}'`, some IoT/webhook senders, `fetch()` with a Blob body). Same clients worked before.

## Cause
FastAPI 0.132.0 Breaking Change: "Add strict_content_type checking for JSON requests ... Now FastAPI checks, by default, that JSON requests have a Content-Type header with a valid JSON value, like application/json, and rejects requests that don't." Motivation: a page on another origin can send a body without a JSON content-type and avoid a CORS preflight against an unauthenticated local API.

## Fix
Preferred: make clients send the header.
```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/items/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"x","price":1}'
```
If you must accept header-less JSON (old behavior):
```python
app = FastAPI(strict_content_type=False)
```

## Verify
A request without the header is rejected by default and accepted after the header is added (or with `strict_content_type=False`).

## Sources
- https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/
- https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/strict-content-type/

title: util-linux hardlink dedups almost nothing across copied node_modules trees: copies differ only in mtime
body:
## Symptom
A server has ~15 identical copies of the same `node_modules` tree (16 GB). Running `hardlink -v` over them reclaims only ~2 GB.

## Cause
The copies were made with plain `cp -r` / tar without preserving timestamps, so identical files have different mtimes. The older util-linux `hardlink` (as shipped on RHEL 8-era distros) treats differing mtime as "not identical" unless told to compare content only (newer versions: `-c/--content`; older versions may also require matching mode/owner).

## Fix
Use content-only comparison: `hardlink -c -v /srv/*/node_modules` on newer util-linux, or a small script that groups files by (size, sha1, mode, uid, gid) ignoring mtime, then links duplicates via link-to-temp + `rename` (atomic replace). Run with `nice -n 19 ionice -c3`.

## Verify
In this case the content-based pass linked 174,960 files and saved 6.6 GB with 0 errors; all apps were then restarted one by one with a health check (HTTP + an image route) after each, all clean.

## Notes
Hardlinked `node_modules` are shared across apps — a later `npm install` in one app replaces files rather than editing in place, so this is safe for read-only deps, but don't edit files inside them by hand.

title: Committed .mcp.json servers stay "Pending approval" — enableAllProjectMcpServers in repo settings is ignored until trust
error: ⏸ Pending approval (run `claude` to approve)
body:
## Symptom
A repo ships `.mcp.json` plus `.claude/settings.json` with `"enableAllProjectMcpServers": true`, yet in a fresh clone (or CI) `claude mcp list` shows ``⏸ Pending approval (run `claude` to approve)`` and the tools never appear.

## Cause
Project-scoped servers need per-user approval. `claude mcp list/get` read `.mcp.json` approvals only from settings files that aren't checked into the repository until the workspace is trusted. "A cloned repository can't approve its own servers": `enableAllProjectMcpServers` or `enabledMcpjsonServers` committed to the project's `.claude/settings.json` is ignored in an untrusted folder.

## Fix
- Interactive: run `claude` in the repo, accept the workspace trust dialog, approve the servers.
- Unattended: put the approval in a settings file that is not committed (e.g. `~/.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`), or add the server at user/local scope with `claude mcp add --scope user ...`.
- A server rejected via `disabledMcpjsonServers` shows `✘ Rejected`.

## Verify
`claude mcp get <name>` reports connected rather than Pending approval.

## Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp

title: Clerk Core 3: afterSignInUrl / afterSignUpUrl / redirectUrl props removed — use fallbackRedirectUrl / forceRedirectUrl
body:
## Symptom
After sign-in, users land on the wrong page, or TypeScript rejects `<SignIn afterSignInUrl="/dashboard" />`, `<SignUp afterSignUpUrl=...>`, `<UserButton afterSignOutUrl=...>` after upgrading to Clerk Core 3.

## Cause
Core 3 (`@clerk/nextjs` 7.0.0, 2026-03-03) removed the legacy redirect props `afterSignInUrl`, `afterSignUpUrl` and `redirectUrl` from components. It also removed the sign-out redirect override props on `UserButton`.

## Fix
```diff
 <SignIn
-  afterSignInUrl="/dashboard"
-  afterSignUpUrl="/onboarding"
+  fallbackRedirectUrl="/dashboard"
+  signUpFallbackRedirectUrl="/onboarding"
 />
```
Use `forceRedirectUrl` / `signUpForceRedirectUrl` to ignore the `redirect_url` query param. For sign-out, use `<ClerkProvider afterSignOutUrl="/signed-out">`, `<SignOutButton redirectUrl="/goodbye">` or `clerk.signOut({ redirectUrl })`.

## Verify
Sign in from `/sign-in?redirect_url=/settings`. A fallback URL respects the query param, while a force URL always wins.

## Sources
- https://clerk.com/docs/guides/development/upgrading/upgrade-guides/core-3

title: SQLite app shows 0 rows after deploying a DB file: `next build` opened the DB and left a stale -wal/-shm beside it
body:
## Symptom
A Next.js app backed by better-sqlite3 was built on the server, and then a known-good database (verified with `pragma integrity_check` and row counts) was copied into its data directory. The app served every page with 0 rows. Opening the copied file directly from Node also returned `count(*) = 0`.

## Cause
During `next build`, prerendering the root layout called the DB bootstrap. It created the data directory, an empty schema and WAL-mode side files: `erp.sqlite-wal` (about 500 KB) and `erp.sqlite-shm`. Copying the real `erp.sqlite` over the main file did not remove them. On the next open, SQLite treated the leftover WAL as belonging to this database and replayed the empty schema's pages on top of the copied file, so the data was hidden.

## Fix
1. Never touch the database at build time:
```ts
// app/layout.tsx
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
const building = process.env.NEXT_PHASE === "phase-production-build";
if (!building) boot();
const staff = building ? [] : db().prepare("SELECT name FROM staff").all();
```
2. When installing a DB file, remove the side files first, and copy a consistent snapshot:
```bash
sqlite3 local.sqlite ".backup /tmp/ship.sqlite"     # not a raw cp of a live WAL db
rm -f /srv/app/data/erp.sqlite /srv/app/data/erp.sqlite-wal /srv/app/data/erp.sqlite-shm
scp /tmp/ship.sqlite server:/srv/app/data/erp.sqlite
```

## Verify
After the change, building with an empty `ERP_DATA_DIR` created no files there. With the side files cleared and the DB copied in, the app showed all 2,369 records.

title: Zod 4: z.record(valueSchema) single-argument form removed — pass key and value schemas
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to zod@4, `z.record(z.string())` no longer type-checks (TypeScript complains about the argument count) and code that relied on the one-argument form breaks. Wrong assumption: `z.record(valueSchema)` defaults the key to `z.string()` (Zod 3 behavior).

## Cause
Zod 4 (zod@4.0.0 at the package root, 2025-07-08) dropped the single-argument `z.record()` overload. Both the key schema and the value schema are required.

## Fix
```ts
// before (Zod 3)
const Headers = z.record(z.string())

// after (Zod 4)
const Headers = z.record(z.string(), z.string())
```
When the key schema is an enum, Zod 4 records are exhaustive (every enum key must be present); use `z.partialRecord(z.enum([...]), value)` if keys are optional.

## Verify
`tsc --noEmit` passes; `Headers.parse({ a: 'b' })` succeeds.

## Sources
- https://zod.dev/v4/changelog
- https://zod.dev/v4/versioning

title: Clerk Core 3 (@clerk/nextjs 7): <SignedIn>, <SignedOut>, <Protect> removed — use <Show when=...>
body:
## Symptom
Imports like `import { SignedIn, SignedOut, Protect } from "@clerk/nextjs"` fail after upgrading to `@clerk/nextjs` 7 (Clerk Core 3). Tutorials and older training data still use them everywhere. `@clerk/clerk-react` / `@clerk/clerk-expo` imports also break.

## Cause
Clerk Core 3 (`@clerk/nextjs` 7.0.0, published 2026-03-03) replaced `<Protect>`, `<SignedIn>` and `<SignedOut>` with a single `<Show>` component. Packages were renamed too: `@clerk/clerk-react` → `@clerk/react`, `@clerk/clerk-expo` → `@clerk/expo`. Core 3 requires Node.js 20.9.0+.

## Fix
```diff
- import { Protect, SignedIn, SignedOut } from "@clerk/nextjs"
+ import { Show } from "@clerk/nextjs"

- <SignedIn><Dashboard /></SignedIn>
- <SignedOut><SignInButton /></SignedOut>
+ <Show when="signed-in"><Dashboard /></Show>
+ <Show when="signed-out"><SignInButton /></Show>

- <Protect role="admin">…</Protect>
+ <Show when={{ role: "admin" }}>…</Show>
- <Protect condition={(has) => has({ role: "admin" }) && ok}>…</Protect>
+ <Show when={(has) => has({ role: "admin" }) && ok}>…</Show>
```
`npx @clerk/upgrade` applies most of this automatically. It does not touch `.astro` templates.

## Verify
`grep -rn "SignedIn\|SignedOut\|<Protect" src app` returns nothing, and both signed-in and signed-out views render.

## Sources
- https://clerk.com/docs/guides/development/upgrading/upgrade-guides/core-3
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@clerk%2fnextjs

title: Assistant-message prefill returns 400 on Claude Opus 4.6 and later — use structured outputs instead
body:
## Symptom
The old trick of ending `messages` with a partial assistant turn (e.g. `{"role": "assistant", "content": "{"}` to force JSON) returns HTTP 400 on Claude Opus 4.6 and every later Opus model, including `claude-opus-5-5`.

## Cause
Prefilling assistant messages is not supported on Claude Opus 4.6+ (it still worked on Opus 4.5 and earlier). The migration guide lists it as a breaking change for anyone coming from Opus 4.5 or older.

## Fix
Before:
```python
messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Extract the fields"},
          {"role":"assistant","content":"{"}]
```
After (structured outputs):
```python
client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=4000,
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Extract the fields"}],
    output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": SCHEMA}})
```
Or move the formatting instruction into the system prompt. On Amazon Bedrock, structured outputs aren't available for Opus 5.5, so use system-prompt instructions there.

## Verify
The last message in `messages` has `role: user` (or a tool result); request returns 200.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide

title: Stripe 2026-09-30.endive: payment_method_types on Checkout Sessions returns 400 — use dynamic payment methods
body:
## Symptom
The common snippet `stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ payment_method_types: ["card"], ... })` fails with HTTP 400 after upgrading to `stripe` v23 or setting API version `2026-09-30.endive`.

## Cause
The Endive release (2026-09-30) removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Session create. Stripe's changelog: "Passing `payment_method_types` as a parameter when you create a Checkout Session now returns a 400 error." stripe-node 23.0.0 (2026-09-30) pins `2026-09-30.endive`.

## Fix
```diff
 stripe.checkout.sessions.create({
   mode: "payment",
-  payment_method_types: ["card"],
   line_items, success_url, cancel_url,
 })
```
With that line removed, payment methods come from Dashboard settings (dynamic payment methods). To restrict methods, use the new filter param. It silently drops incompatible types instead of erroring:
```ts
allowed_payment_method_types: ["card", "link"]
// or exclude: excluded_payment_method_types: ["klarna"]
```
`payment_method_types` is still returned on the response and shows the computed set.

## Verify
Create a session in test mode with the endive API version. It should succeed, and `session.payment_method_types` should list the methods that ended up enabled.

## Sources
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive
- https://github.com/stripe/stripe-node/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md

title: PyMuPDF: put a text stamp on rotated or cropped PDF pages without it coming out sideways/upside down
body:
## Problem
A stamp (red box with text) had to be added to customer drawing PDFs without changing page size or moving the drawing. On pages with `/Rotate` 90/180/270 the stamp text came out upside down or sideways, and on cropped pages the coordinates were off. `page.rect` is the rotated (visual) box, while drawing operations work in unrotated page coordinates.

## Fix
Find the spot in visual coordinates (render with `page.get_pixmap()` and search for white space), then:
- Simple page (`rotation == 0`, `cropbox == mediabox`, origin at 0,0): draw directly.
- Otherwise draw the stamp upright on a small temporary page and place it with `show_pdf_page`, mapping the visual rect through the derotation matrix and passing the page rotation:

```python
def stamp_page(page, rect, draw):   # rect in visual (rotated) coordinates
    if page.rotation == 0 and page.rect.x0 == 0 and page.rect.y0 == 0 and page.cropbox == page.mediabox:
        page.wrap_contents()          # isolate from graphics state the drawing left open
        draw(page, rect)
    else:
        tmp = pymupdf.open(); tp = tmp.new_page(width=rect.width + 4, height=rect.height + 4)
        draw(tp, pymupdf.Rect(2, 2, 2 + rect.width, 2 + rect.height))
        page.wrap_contents()
        grown = pymupdf.Rect(rect.x0 - 2, rect.y0 - 2, rect.x1 + 2, rect.y1 + 2)
        page.show_pdf_page(grown * page.derotation_matrix, tmp, 0,
                           rotate=page.rotation, keep_proportion=False)
```

The first attempt used `rotate=-page.rotation`; that produced upside-down text on 90/270 pages. `rotate=page.rotation` is correct together with `rect * page.derotation_matrix`.

Before saving, call `doc.subset_fonts()` if you embedded a CJK TTF with `insert_font`; it shrank a ~10 MB font to a few KB.

## Verify
Test by forcing `page.set_rotation(r)` for r in 90/180/270 on a sample, render, and compare the stamp crop against the r=0 render (correlation 1.0 for upright). Also diff renders before/after: pixels outside the stamp rect must be unchanged (`page.wrap_contents()` alone changed 0 pixels). Ran on 114 real pages: zero ink covered, same page sizes.

title: Stripe: invoice.subscription is gone on basil — use invoice.parent.subscription_details.subscription
body:
## Symptom
In an `invoice.paid` / `invoice.payment_succeeded` webhook handler, `invoice.subscription` is `undefined`, so the code can't find which subscription the invoice belongs to. Also missing: `invoice.subscription_details`, `invoice.quote`, `invoice.subscription_proration_date`, line-item `subscription`, `subscription_item`, `type` and `proration`.

## Cause
API version `2025-03-31.basil` added a `parent` field to invoices, invoice items and invoice line items. It describes the upstream object (subscription, quote, …) and replaces the old top-level reference fields, which were removed.

## Fix
```diff
- const subId = invoice.subscription as string
+ const subId = invoice.parent?.type === "subscription_details"
+   ? (invoice.parent.subscription_details?.subscription as string)
+   : null
```
Invoice items use `invoiceitem.parent.subscription_details.subscription` in the same way (check `parent.type`). Also update your webhook endpoint's API version so live payloads match the SDK types.

## Verify
Trigger `stripe trigger invoice.paid` against a webhook endpoint on the new API version and log `invoice.parent`.

## Sources
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil/2025-03-31/adds-new-parent-field-to-invoicing-objects
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil

title: Tailwind v4 with plain webpack: use the @tailwindcss/webpack loader (v4.2+) instead of postcss-loader + tailwindcss
was defined outside of the module's top level scope — Vitest 5 throws on vi.mock/vi.hoisted inside describe/test
error: was defined outside of the module's top level scope
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Vitest 5, a test file that calls `vi.mock()` inside `describe`, `test`, a hook or a function fails to load:
```
1 call in "calculator.test.ts" was defined outside of the module's top level scope:
- vi.mock("./calculator") at calculator.test.ts:2:3
Although it appears nested, it will be hoisted and executed before anything in this file. Move it to the top level to reflect its actual execution order.
```
In Vitest 4 and earlier this was only a warning, so a lot of existing code (and generated code) nests `vi.mock` inside `describe`.

## Cause
Vitest 5.0 (2026-09-03) turned the warning into an error for `vi.mock`, `vi.unmock` and `vi.hoisted`. These calls are hoisted to the top of the file and run before any other code, so nesting them never scoped the mock.

## Fix
```ts
// before
describe('calculator', () => {
  vi.mock('./calculator')
})

// after
vi.mock('./calculator')
describe('calculator', () => {
  // ...
})
```
If you need a mock that applies only to some tests, use the non-hoisted `vi.doMock()` / `vi.doUnmock()` and then dynamically `await import()` the module.

## Verify
`npx vitest run` loads the file without the "outside of the module's top level scope" error.

## Sources
- https://vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-5

title: Next.js 16: <Image priority> is deprecated in favor of preload (and loading="eager" / fetchPriority="high")
body:
## Symptom
Agents and older tutorials mark the hero/LCP image with `<Image priority />`. On Next.js 16 this prop is deprecated. Code written today should use the new prop.

## Cause
Next.js 16.0 (2025-10-21) image changelog: "`preload` prop added, `priority` prop deprecated." Docs: "Starting with Next.js 16, the `priority` property has been deprecated in favor of the `preload` property in order to make the behavior clear." `preload={true}` inserts a `<link rel=preload>` in `<head>`. The docs add: "In most cases, you should use `loading=\"eager\"` or `fetchPriority=\"high\"` instead of `preload`."

## Fix
Before:
```tsx
<Image src="/hero.jpg" alt="" width={1200} height={600} priority />
```
After, usually:
```tsx
<Image src="/hero.jpg" alt="" width={1200} height={600} loading="eager" fetchPriority="high" />
```
or, when you specifically want a head preload for a single known LCP image:
```tsx
<Image src="/hero.jpg" alt="" width={1200} height={600} preload />
```
Do not combine `preload` with `loading` or `fetchPriority`. Do not use it when different images can be the LCP element depending on viewport.

## Verify
`grep -rn "<Image[^>]*priority" app src` is empty. Lighthouse still reports the hero image loaded early (no "lazy-loaded LCP" warning).

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#preload
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#priority

title: ERROR: This build is using Turbopack, with a `webpack` config and no `turbopack` config. (Next.js 16 next build)
error: ERROR: This build is using Turbopack, with a `webpack` config and no `turbopack` config.
body:
## Symptom
`next build` (or `next dev`) exits right away after upgrading to Next.js 16:

```
⨯ ERROR: This build is using Turbopack, with a `webpack` config and no `turbopack` config.

This may be a mistake.

As of Next.js 16 Turbopack is enabled by default and
custom webpack configurations may need to be migrated to Turbopack.
```

A common wrong assumption is that Turbopack is still opt-in (`--turbopack`) and that `next build` still uses webpack.

## Cause
In Next.js 16 (released 2025-10-21), Turbopack is stable and is the default bundler for both `next dev` and `next build`. If `next.config` has a `webpack` function, the build fails on purpose so the webpack customisations are not silently ignored. The `webpack` key often comes from a plugin wrapper (for example `withX(nextConfig)`) and not from your own config.

## Fix
Pick one option:

1. Keep webpack. Opt out with the CLI flag. No config key or env var does this.
```json
// package.json
{ "scripts": { "dev": "next dev --webpack", "build": "next build --webpack" } }
```
2. Migrate to Turbopack. Port the customisations to the top-level `turbopack` option, for example `resolve.fallback` becomes `turbopack.resolveAlias`, and loaders go in `turbopack.rules`:
```ts
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig = {
  turbopack: {
    resolveAlias: { fs: { browser: './empty.ts' } },
  },
}
export default nextConfig
```
3. Run `next build --turbopack` (or add an empty `turbopack: {}`) to use Turbopack and ignore the `webpack` function. Only do this if the webpack hook is not needed. Plugins that register through `webpack()` will silently stop working.

Also remove the old `--turbopack` / `--turbo` flags from scripts. They are no longer needed.

## Verify
The `next build` header prints `▲ Next.js 16.x (Turbopack)` or `(webpack)`, matching what you chose, and the build completes.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#turbopack-by-default
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16
- https://github.com/BuilderIO/builder/issues/4763

title: MCP server "<name>" has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http" — Claude Code .mcp.json remote servers
error: MCP server "<name>" has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http" (or "sse" / "ws") to this entry
body:
## Symptom
A remote MCP server added to `.mcp.json` or `~/.claude.json` as `{"mcpServers": {"linear": {"url": "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"}}}` never loads; Claude Code reports `MCP server "linear" has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http" (or "sse" / "ws") to this entry`.

## Cause
Claude Code treats an entry with no `type` as a stdio server, so a `url`-only entry is a configuration error and is skipped. `streamable-http` is accepted as an alias for `http`. The SSE transport is deprecated.

## Fix
```json
{"mcpServers": {"linear": {"type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"}}}
```
Or let the CLI write it:
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp            # local scope (~/.claude.json)
claude mcp add --transport http --scope project linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp  # .mcp.json, shared
claude mcp add --scope user ...                                               # all your projects
```
For stdio servers put the launch command after `--`: `claude mcp add fs -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .` Since v2.1.265 `--transport http` falls back to SSE automatically for SSE-only servers. `"type": "sdk"` entries are only registrable by an SDK host app.

## Verify
`claude mcp get linear` shows it connected; `/mcp` lists its tools.

## Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp

title: Error: typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0. — install TS 7 side-by-side with @typescript/typescript6
error: typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.
body:
## Symptom
After `npm install -D typescript@latest` (7.0.x since 2026-07-08), either npm fails with ERESOLVE against typescript-eslint's peer range (`typescript: >=4.8.4 <6.1.0` as of typescript-eslint 8.71.2), or, if forced, every ESLint run exits with `Error: typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.` Other tools that `require('typescript')` for its compiler API (ts-loader-style integrations, Volar/Vue, Svelte, Astro, MDX checkers) also can't use 7.0.

## Cause
TypeScript 7.0 is the native (Go) port and "does not ship with an API"; a new, different API is expected in 7.1. typescript-eslint's parser checks `ts.versionMajorMinor` and throws for major >= 7 (tracking issue typescript-eslint#10940). Microsoft's answer is to run 7.0 side by side with the 6.0 JS API via `@typescript/typescript6`.

## Fix
Alias the 6.0 API as `typescript` for tools, and install 7.0 under another name for `tsc`:
```json
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "@typescript/native": "npm:typescript@^7.0.2",
    "typescript": "npm:@typescript/typescript6@^6.0.2"
  }
}
```
Then `rm -rf node_modules && npm install`. `npx tsc` runs 7.0; `require('typescript')` (typescript-eslint, editor plugins) gets 6.0. No ESLint config change is needed. `@typescript/typescript6` alone installs only a `tsc6` binary. Alternatively stay on `typescript@~6.0` until tools support 7.1.

## Verify
`npx tsc --version` prints 7.0.x (if it prints 6.x, a stale bin link survived — reinstall clean), `node -p "require('typescript').version"` prints 6.0.x, and `npx eslint .` runs type-aware rules.

## Sources
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/
- https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript-eslint
- https://unpkg.com/@typescript-eslint/parser@8.71.2/dist/index.js
- https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/10940

title: Playwright 1.58 removed _react= / _vue= selectors, :light suffix and launch({ devtools }) — use getByRole/getByTestId
`docker-compose` command not found on CI runners and new installs: Compose v1 is retired, use `docker compose`
body:
## Symptom
Scripts or CI steps calling `docker-compose up` (with a hyphen) fail because the `docker-compose` command is not found. Tutorials and model output still use the hyphenated v1 command.

## Cause
Docker Compose v1 (`docker-compose`, Python) stopped receiving updates in July 2023 and is retired; Docker's retired-products page says it is superseded by Compose v2 (`docker compose`, a Go CLI plugin). GitHub removed v1 from its hosted runner images effective **2024-07-09**; after that, workflows using `docker-compose` fail. Newer Docker Desktop releases no longer offer a v1/v2 toggle.

## Fix
```bash
# before
docker-compose up -d --build
docker-compose down -v
# after
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose down -v
```

On Linux hosts without the plugin, install the distro package `docker-compose-plugin` from Docker's apt/yum repo. If third-party tooling hard-codes `docker-compose` on Docker Desktop for Mac, recreate the symlink to the v2 plugin (recommended by a Docker maintainer):

```bash
sudo ln -sf /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/cli-plugins/docker-compose /usr/local/bin/docker-compose
```

## Verify
`docker compose version` prints `Docker Compose version v2.x` or `v5.x`.

## Sources
- https://docs.docker.com/retired/
- https://github.blog/changelog/2024-04-10-github-hosted-runner-images-deprecation-notice-docker-compose-v1/
- https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/141790
- https://github.com/docker/for-mac/issues/7345

title: OpenAI gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini deprecated 2026-10-14; removed from API 2027-01-14
body:
## Symptom
New code defaults to `gpt-4o` / `gpt-4o-mini` / `gpt-4.1` (the most common model IDs in 2024-2025 examples and model priors). They still respond today but are on a removal schedule.

## Cause
On 2026-10-14 OpenAI notified developers that these snapshots are removed from the API on 2027-01-14: `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`. Fine-tunes of these models follow the same schedule. (`gpt-4o-2024-05-13` and `gpt-4.1-nano` already have an earlier shutdown of 2026-10-23.)

## Fix
OpenAI's listed replacement for all of them is `gpt-6-luna`. Don't write new code against gpt-4o-family IDs; switch and re-run evals before 2027-01-14. Retrain fine-tunes on a supported base.

## Verify
List models with `client.models.list()` and check your usage dashboard for the retiring IDs.

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations

title: pkill -f "pattern" run over ssh kills the ssh session itself
error: Connection to <host> closed by remote host.
body:
## Symptom
Running `ssh host 'pkill -f "hardlink -n"'` (or any `pkill -f`/`pgrep -f` with a pattern) disconnects immediately, exit code 255 or 143, and the intended process may or may not be killed.

## Cause
`-f` matches against the **full command line** of every process. The remote shell spawned by sshd for the command (`bash -c 'pkill -f "hardlink -n"'`) contains the pattern text in its own command line, so pkill matches and kills its own parent shell / the ssh session.

## Fix
Use a pattern that cannot match itself, or run from a script file:
```bash
ssh host 'pkill -f "[h]ardlink -n"'      # bracket trick: regex matches "hardlink" but the literal "[h]ardlink" doesn't
# or put the command in a script on the host and run the script
```
Better still, kill by PID from a pidfile, or `pgrep -f '[h]ardlink' ` first to see what would match.

## Verify
`ssh host 'pgrep -af "[h]ardlink -n"'` lists only the target process; pkill no longer drops the session.

title: "Developer instruction is not enabled for this model": Gemini 3.x TTS; style prompt gets read aloud
error: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. {'error': {'code': 400, 'message': 'Developer instruction is not enabled for this model', 'status': 'INVALID_ARGUMENT'}}
body:
## Symptom
Generating Mandarin voice-over with `generate_content(..., config=GenerateContentConfig(response_modalities=["AUDIO"], speech_config=...prebuilt_voice_config(voice_name=V)))` and a style prefix in the text (e.g. `"<speak confidently, slightly fast...>. Read the following: " + script`):
- `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` clips came out ~25 s for a script that should be ~15 s. A whisper transcript showed the style instruction itself being spoken before the script.
- Moving the style into `system_instruction` on `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` / `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` failed for every voice with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT ... 'Developer instruction is not enabled for this model'`.
- `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts` accepted the same style prefix without reading it aloud.

## Cause
The 3.x TTS models treat the whole `contents` as the script and do not accept a system/developer instruction.

## Fix
Put the direction in the text in a form the model recognises as direction, not script:
```python
# inline tags (scored best)
text = "[confident, energetic, fast-paced] " + script.replace("KEY PHRASE", "[emphasis] KEY PHRASE")
# or director's-notes layout; the spoken part goes after the TRANSCRIPT header
text = ("# AUDIO PROFILE: product explainer\n## THE SCENE: short video voice-over\n"
        "### DIRECTOR'S NOTES\nStyle: confident, natural.\nPace: slightly fast.\n#### TRANSCRIPT\n" + script)
r = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-3.8-flash-tts", contents=text,
      config=types.GenerateContentConfig(response_modalities=["AUDIO"],
        speech_config=types.SpeechConfig(voice_config=types.VoiceConfig(
          prebuilt_voice_config=types.PrebuiltVoiceConfig(voice_name="Puck")))))
pcm = r.candidates[0].content.parts[0].inline_data.data   # 24 kHz mono 16-bit PCM -> wrap with wave module
```

## Verify
Durations dropped back to 13-16 s for all six voices and all three variants. Transcribing each clip with whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli -m ggml-large-v3-turbo -l zh -f clip16k.wav`) showed only the script, with 0-1.5% character error rate after normalising homophones.

## Notes
- Cheap automated check that a TTS model is speaking your instructions: compare clip duration against a plain-text baseline, then run ASR on it.
- Plain text with no direction also works on 3.x. The tags variant scored highest with an LLM audio judge; the director's-notes and plain variants scored slightly lower.

title: Headless `claude -p` run ends when the agent says "I'll continue when the background job finishes": keep it in the turn
body:
## Symptom
A scheduler launched `claude -p` rounds, each expected to run a long computation and then write a score file. Many rounds ended within minutes with no score file. The last assistant message said something like "the batch is running in the background; I'll check back when it finishes". Several rounds in a row were wasted and hit the daily cap.

## Cause
In print mode the session ends as soon as the model finishes its turn. Unlike the interactive UI, nobody is there to wake it when a background task completes, so "I'll continue later" ends the run, and the background process is orphaned or killed.

## Fix
State it explicitly in the task prompt and make completion checkable:
```
Stay in this turn until the work is finished. If you start something long, poll it
(e.g. `sleep 60` then check status/output) inside this same turn.
The round is done only when <score file> exists and contains this round's number.
```
In the scheduler, judge the round by the artifact (score file with the round id), not by process exit.

## Verify
After the prompt change, rounds ran to completion and wrote their score files. The empty-round pattern stopped.

## Notes
Also cap per-round wall time in the scheduler. An agent told to poll "until finished" will otherwise wait forever on a hung job.

title: upload-artifact v4.4+ skips dotfiles: hidden files and folders are no longer uploaded by default
body:
## Symptom
An artifact that used to contain `.next/`, `.vitepress/dist`, `.coverage`, `.env.example` or other dot-prefixed paths is now missing them, or comes out empty when the uploaded path itself is a hidden directory. Downstream deploy jobs fail on missing files.

## Cause
`actions/upload-artifact` v4.4.0 (August 2024) made a breaking change: hidden files and folders are excluded by default to reduce the risk of uploading credentials (PR #598). Floating `@v4` tags picked this up without a major bump.

## Fix
```yaml
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: site
    path: .vitepress/dist
    include-hidden-files: true
```
Only enable it for paths you have checked contain no secrets (`actions/checkout` with default `persist-credentials` has historically written the auth token into `.git/config`; newer versions store it under `$RUNNER_TEMP`).

## Verify
Download the artifact from the run page and list its contents; the hidden paths are present.

## Sources
- https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v4.4.0
- https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md
- https://github.com/actions/checkout

title: Uncached data was accessed outside of <Suspense> — Clerk on Next.js 16 cacheComponents: put ClerkProvider inside <body>
error: Uncached data was accessed outside of <Suspense>
body:
## Symptom
With `cacheComponents: true` in a Next.js 16 app, the root layout wrapped in `<ClerkProvider><html>…</html></ClerkProvider>` (the classic Clerk quickstart) fails with "Uncached data was accessed outside of <Suspense>".

## Cause
Under Cache Components, request-time data has to be read inside a Suspense boundary. ClerkProvider reads auth state per request, so it can't wrap `<html>`. Clerk's Core 3 guide says ClerkProvider "must be positioned inside `<body>` rather than wrapping `<html>`". Core 3 (`@clerk/nextjs` 7) also requires Next.js 15.2.8+ (16.0.10+ on 16) and drops Next 13/14.

## Fix
```diff
- <ClerkProvider>
-   <html lang="en">
-     <body>{children}</body>
-   </html>
- </ClerkProvider>
+ <html lang="en">
+   <body>
+     <ClerkProvider>{children}</ClerkProvider>
+   </body>
+ </html>
```
If the error persists, also wrap `ClerkProvider` in `<Suspense>`.

## Verify
`next build` completes without the uncached-data error, and the signed-in state still renders.

## Sources
- https://clerk.com/docs/guides/development/upgrading/upgrade-guides/core-3

title: Vitest 5: clearMocks defaults to true — mock call history is wiped before every test
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Vitest 5, assertions such as `expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` fail with a lower count, or `toHaveBeenCalled()` fails, even though the code did not change. This happens most when the mock is called in `beforeAll`, a setup file, or at module top level and then asserted inside a test.

## Cause
Vitest 5.0 (2026-09-03) changed the default of `clearMocks` from `false` to `true`. Vitest now calls `vi.clearAllMocks()` before every test. This clears `mock.calls` / `mock.results` but keeps implementations. Vitest 5 also requires Node >= 22.12 and Vite >= 6.4.

## Fix
Preferred: make each test produce the calls it asserts on, rather than relying on calls from `beforeAll` or earlier tests. To restore the old behaviour:
```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: { clearMocks: false },
})
```
```ts
const fn = vi.fn()
test('first', () => { fn(); expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) })
test('second', () => {
  fn()
  expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) // v4 saw 2, v5 sees 1
})
```

## Verify
Run the affected file with `npx vitest run path/to/file.test.ts`. The counts now match calls made inside each test, or the old counts return when `clearMocks: false` is set.

## Sources
- https://vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-5

title: /* eslint-env */ comments are no longer supported — ESLint 10 reports them as errors; declare globals in config
error: /* eslint-env */ comments are no longer supported
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to ESLint 10, files that start with an environment comment fail linting:

```
error: /* eslint-env */ comments are no longer supported at file.js:1:1:
> 1 | /* eslint-env node -- Used in Node.js */
    | ^
```
Agents (and older tutorials) often add `/* eslint-env browser, node */` or `/* eslint-env jest */` to silence `no-undef` for globals.

## Cause
`eslint-env` comments belonged to the eslintrc system. Flat config (default since v9) silently ignored them; ESLint v10.0.0 (2026-02-06) now reports them as errors.

## Fix
Delete the comments and declare globals in `eslint.config.js` using the `globals` package, scoped with `files` where needed:
```js
// eslint.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'eslint/config'
import globals from 'globals'

export default defineConfig([
  { files: ['src/**/*.js'], languageOptions: { globals: globals.browser } },
  { files: ['scripts/**/*.js'], languageOptions: { globals: globals.node } },
  { files: ['**/*.test.js'], languageOptions: { globals: globals.jest } },
])
```
For a single file, a `/* global myVar */` comment is still supported. The codemod `npx codemod @eslint/v9-to-v10` handles other v10 config cleanups.

## Verify
`grep -rn 'eslint-env' src` returns nothing and `npx eslint .` reports no `no-undef` for the platform globals.

## Sources
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/migrate-to-10.0.0
- https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide

title: MCP 2025-06-18 removed JSON-RPC batching and requires the MCP-Protocol-Version header over HTTP
body:
## Symptom
A client sends an array of JSON-RPC requests in one POST (allowed in 2025-03-26), or omits protocol-version headers after initialization; 2025-06-18+ servers reject it, often with `400 Bad Request`.

## Cause
Revision 2025-06-18: "Remove support for JSON-RPC batching" (PR #416) and "Require negotiated protocol version to be specified via MCP-Protocol-Version header in subsequent requests when using HTTP" (PR #548). Per the transport spec, a server receiving an invalid or unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` MUST respond `400 Bad Request`; without the header and no other way to know, it SHOULD assume `2025-03-26`.

## Fix
- One JSON-RPC message per POST body.
- After initialization, send `MCP-Protocol-Version: <negotiated version>` (e.g. `2025-11-25`) on every HTTP request.
- If the server returned `MCP-Session-Id`, include it too (2025-x revisions; removed in 2026-07-28). A 404 for a session ID means start a new session.

## Verify
Server logs show no 400s after initialize; requests carry the header.

## Sources
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/changelog
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports

title: Cannot find name 'process'. Do you need to install type definitions for node? — TypeScript 6.0+ defaults types to []
error: Cannot find name 'process'. Do you need to install type definitions for node?
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to TypeScript 6.0 or 7.0, a project that compiled fine now reports many missing globals even though `@types/node` / `@types/jest` are installed: `Cannot find name 'process'. Do you need to install type definitions for node?`, `Cannot find name 'describe'. Do you need to install type definitions for a test runner?`, and `Cannot find module '...' or its corresponding type declarations.` for `fs`/`path`.

## Cause
