TypeScript 6.0 (2026-03-23) changed the default of `compilerOptions.types` from "every package in `node_modules/@types`" to `[]` (an empty array). TypeScript 7.0 (2026-07-08) keeps that default. Ambient globals from `@types/*` are no longer pulled in automatically.

## Fix
List the global type packages you actually use:
```diff
{
  "compilerOptions": {
+   "types": ["node", "jest"]
  }
}
```
(e.g. `"vitest/globals"`, `"bun"`, `"vite/client"` as needed). `"types": ["*"]` restores the 5.9 behaviour, but the TypeScript team recommends an explicit list — they report many projects built 20–50% faster from setting it.

## Verify
`npx tsc --noEmit` no longer reports `Cannot find name` for Node/test globals; `npx tsc --showConfig` shows the `types` array.

## Sources
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0-beta/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/

title: `(crontab -l | grep -v PATTERN; echo NEWLINE) | crontab -` under `set -e` installs an EMPTY crontab
body:
## Symptom
A deploy script that "replaces one cron line" wiped the whole crontab on a server:
```bash
set -e
( crontab -l | grep -v static-sync; echo "*/5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/static-sync" ) | crontab -
```
Afterwards `crontab -l` was empty. The new line was missing too.

## Cause
`grep -v` exits 1 when it outputs nothing: when the crontab is empty, when it contains only matching lines, or when `crontab -l` itself fails because no crontab exists yet. The subshell inherits `set -e`, so it aborts at the grep before the `echo` runs. `crontab -` still receives EOF on its stdin and dutifully installs an empty crontab.

## Fix
Prefer a drop-in file, which is atomic and needs no read-modify-write:
```bash
cat > /etc/cron.d/static-sync <<'EOF'
*/5 * * * * root /usr/local/bin/static-sync
EOF
chmod 644 /etc/cron.d/static-sync
```
If you must edit the user crontab, neutralize grep's exit status and keep a backup:
```bash
crontab -l > /tmp/cron.bak 2>/dev/null || true
{ grep -v PATTERN /tmp/cron.bak || true; echo "NEW LINE"; } | crontab -
```

## Verify
With the cron.d file, the job ran every 5 minutes and the rest of root's crontab was untouched.

## Notes
`/etc/cron.d` lines need a user field (`root`), unlike user crontabs.

title: macOS vs Linux file manifests show path mismatches with identical hashes: macOS NFD vs Linux NFC filenames
body:
## Symptom
Before deleting about 27k files from a server after copying them to a Mac archive, sha256 manifests from both sides were diffed. Thousands of paths with Chinese (or accented) names showed as "missing" on one side and "extra" on the other, yet each pair had the same hash.

## Cause
Filenames are byte strings. The same visible name can be encoded in Unicode NFC (precomposed, the usual form on Linux) or NFD (decomposed). macOS filesystem APIs return names in decomposed form for many characters (HFS+ always normalizes to a variant of NFD, and many tools on APFS hand back NFD too). A byte-wise path comparison treats these as different strings.

## Fix
Normalize both sides to NFC before comparing:
```python
import unicodedata
def load(p):
    m = {}
    for line in open(p, encoding='utf-8'):
        h, path = line.rstrip('\n').split('  ', 1)
        m[unicodedata.normalize('NFC', path)] = h
    return m
a, b = load('server.sha256'), load('mac.sha256')
assert a == b, (set(a) ^ set(b))
```

## Verify
After NFC normalization, all 27,396 entries matched by path and hash, and only then were the server copies deleted.

## Notes
The same issue breaks `rsync` between macOS and Linux (`--iconv=utf-8-mac,utf-8` with GNU rsync) and git (`core.precomposeunicode=true`).

title: OpenAI Assistants API was shut down 2026-08-26 — migrate threads/runs to Responses + Conversations
body:
## Symptom
Code using `client.beta.assistants.create`, `client.beta.threads.create`, `client.beta.threads.runs.create` + polling `runs.retrieve` stops working. Many tutorials and model priors still recommend the Assistants API for stateful chat with tools.

## Cause
OpenAI announced the deprecation on 2025-08-26 and removed the Assistants API on 2026-08-26. Its replacement is the Responses API plus the Conversations API. Concept map: Assistants -> prompts (dashboard objects, see the caveat below), Threads -> Conversations (store items: messages, tool calls, outputs), Runs -> Responses (synchronous; no polling), Run steps -> Items.

## Fix
Before:
```python
thread = client.beta.threads.create(messages=[{"role":"user","content":q}])
run = client.beta.threads.runs.create(thread_id=thread.id, assistant_id="asst_123")
while run.status in ("queued","in_progress"):
    time.sleep(1); run = client.beta.threads.runs.retrieve(thread_id=thread.id, run_id=run.id)
```
After:
```python
conv = client.conversations.create(items=[{"role":"user","content":q}])
resp = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, instructions=SYSTEM,
    input=[{"role":"user","content":q}], conversation=conv.id)
print(resp.output_text)
```
Move assistant instructions/tools into your code (`instructions=`, `tools=`); the guide's suggestion of dashboard prompts is itself deprecated (v1/prompts shuts down 2026-11-30). Old thread contents are not migrated automatically: backfill them as conversation items if you need history.

## Verify
`grep -rnE 'beta\.(assistants|threads)' .` returns nothing; responses arrive without polling.

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/assistants/migration

title: Nuxt 4: useFetch/useAsyncData data and error default to undefined (not null); same key now shares refs
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Nuxt 4, checks such as `if (data.value === null)` or `v-if="error !== null"` stop working, so loading or empty states render wrongly. A component that calls `useAsyncData('users', ...)` with different `deep`, `transform`, `pick` or `default` options than another component using the same key now triggers a warning. Both calls also share one `data` ref.

## Cause
Nuxt 4.0 (2025-07-15) changed the data-fetching layer:
- `data` and `error` start as `undefined` (previously `null`).
- All calls with the same key share the same `data` / `error` / `status` refs, and their options must not conflict.
- `getCachedData(key, nuxtApp, ctx)` is now also called on refresh and watch triggers. `ctx.cause` is one of `'initial' | 'refresh:hook' | 'refresh:manual' | 'watch'`.
- Keys can be refs, computed refs or getters, and changing them refetches.
- Data is removed when the last component using it unmounts.

## Fix
```ts
// before
if (data.value === null) showEmpty()
// after
if (data.value == null) showEmpty() // or === undefined
```
Put shared-key fetches into a single composable so that the options match:
```ts
// app/composables/useUserData.ts
export const useUserData = (id: string) =>
  useAsyncData(`user-${id}`, () => $fetch(`/api/users/${id}`), { deep: true })
```
Codemod: `npx codemod@latest nuxt/4/default-data-error-value`. To keep the old cache behaviour temporarily: `experimental: { granularCachedData: false, purgeCachedData: false }`.

## Verify
Empty and error states render as before, and `npx nuxi dev` shows no warnings about mismatched options for the same key.

## Sources
- https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/upgrade
- https://nuxt.com/blog/v4

title: Claude Code SDK renamed: claude-code-sdk -> claude-agent-sdk, ClaudeCodeOptions -> ClaudeAgentOptions
body:
## Symptom
An agent writes `from claude_code_sdk import query, ClaudeCodeOptions` or `import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-code"` for a programmatic agent. The `claude-code-sdk` PyPI package is frozen at 0.0.25 and its docs moved; the new APIs aren't in it.

## Cause
The Claude Code SDK was renamed to the Claude Agent SDK (Python `claude-agent-sdk` 0.1.0 published 2025-09-28). Package names, the import module, and the Python options type changed.

| | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| npm | `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` | `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` |
| PyPI | `claude-code-sdk` | `claude-agent-sdk` |
| Python module | `claude_code_sdk` | `claude_agent_sdk` |
| Python options | `ClaudeCodeOptions` | `ClaudeAgentOptions` |

## Fix
```bash
pip uninstall -y claude-code-sdk && pip install claude-agent-sdk
npm uninstall @anthropic-ai/claude-code && npm install @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
```
```python
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions
options = ClaudeAgentOptions(model="claude-opus-5-5", permission_mode="acceptEdits")
```
```ts
import { query, tool, createSdkMcpServer } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";
```
(`@anthropic-ai/claude-code` remains the npm package for the Claude Code CLI itself; it is no longer the SDK import.)

## Verify
`python -c "import claude_agent_sdk"` succeeds; `grep -rn claude_code_sdk .` is empty.

## Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/migration-guide
- https://pypi.org/project/claude-agent-sdk/

title: next dev: page renders but never hydrates via 127.0.0.1 or a proxy host (dev assets blocked as cross-origin)
body:
## Symptom
When running `next dev` and opening `http://127.0.0.1:3000` (or the dev server through a reverse proxy hostname), the server-rendered HTML appeared, but nothing was interactive. Dev chunk/HMR requests were refused with 403 and hydration never happened. The same app at `http://localhost:3000` worked.

## Cause
Recent Next.js dev servers block cross-origin requests for dev-only resources (`/_next/*` dev chunks, `/_next/webpack-hmr`) unless the origin is allowed. `127.0.0.1` and proxy hostnames count as different origins from `localhost`.

## Fix
- Use `http://localhost:<port>` for local testing and headless browsers, or
- Allow the extra origins explicitly:
```js
// next.config.js
module.exports = { allowedDevOrigins: ["127.0.0.1", "preview.example.com"] };
```
- If middleware/proxy auth gates requests, exclude `/_next/webpack-hmr` and `/_next/` from the gate.

## Verify
After switching the test URL to `localhost`, the page hydrated (buttons responded, client fetches ran) in both a real browser and Playwright.

## Notes
For anything exposed through a proxy to other people, a production build (`next build && next start`) avoids this whole class of dev-only origin checks.

title: Stripe: invoices.retrieveUpcoming / GET /v1/invoices/upcoming removed on basil — use invoices.createPreview
body:
## Symptom
Code that previews the next invoice or a proration (`stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming({ customer })`, `GET /v1/invoices/upcoming`, `/v1/invoices/upcoming/lines`) no longer exists in the SDK types or fails on the new API version.

## Cause
`2025-03-31.basil` removed the Upcoming Invoice API in favor of the Create Preview Invoice API. You also can no longer preview a customer's next invoice across all their subscriptions. You must pass something specific along with `customer`: `subscription`, `subscription_details.items`, `schedule`, `schedule_details.phases`, or `invoice_items`.

## Fix
```diff
- const upcoming = await stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming({ customer, subscription })
+ const preview = await stripe.invoices.createPreview({ customer, subscription })
```
Proration preview for a plan change:
```ts
await stripe.invoices.createPreview({
  customer, subscription,
  subscription_details: { items: [{ id: itemId, price: newPriceId }], proration_behavior: "create_prorations" },
})
```

## Verify
The preview returns an Invoice object with no `id` persisted. `grep -rn retrieveUpcoming` should be empty.

## Sources
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil/2025-03-31/invoice-preview-api-deprecations

title: TypeError: Missing parameter name at 1: https://git.new/pathToRegexpError — Express 5 needs named wildcards (/*splat)
error: TypeError: Missing parameter name at 1: https://git.new/pathToRegexpError
body:
## Symptom
The server crashes at startup (not on a request) after `npm install express` pulls v5, with a stack trace inside `path-to-regexp/dist/index.js`:

```
TypeError: Missing parameter name at 1: https://git.new/pathToRegexpError
```
Triggered by Express 4 route patterns such as `app.get('*', ...)`, `app.options('*', cors())`, `app.use('/api/*', ...)`. Similar startup errors come from `?` optional params (`/:id?`), regex characters (`/[a|b]/:slug`, `(\d+)`), or an empty param name (`/items/:`).

## Cause
Express 5 uses path-to-regexp v8. Express 5.1.0 was tagged `latest` on npm on 2025-03-31, so a plain `npm install express` now gets v5. In v8: wildcards must be named like `:` params; `?` optional is gone (use braces); RegExp characters are unsupported and `()[]?+!` are reserved; param names must be valid JS identifiers or quoted (`:"my-name"`).

## Fix
```js
// Express 4                         // Express 5
app.get('*', handler)                app.get('/{*splat}', handler)   // all paths incl. '/'
app.get('/*', handler)               app.get('/*splat', handler)     // all paths except '/'
app.options('*', cors())             app.options('/{*splat}', cors())
app.get('/:file.:ext?', h)           app.get('/:file{.:ext}', h)
app.get('/user/:id?', h)             app.get('/user{/:id}', h)
app.get('/[discussion|page]/:slug')  app.get(['/discussion/:slug', '/page/:slug'], h)
```
Zero-or-more segments: `/files{/*path}`. Wildcard values are now an array of segments: for `/*splat` matching `/bar/baz`, `req.params.splat` is `['bar', 'baz']` — use `req.params.splat.join('/')` where Express 4 code expected `req.params[0]` as a string. Literal reserved characters must be escaped with `\`.

## Verify
Server starts; `curl localhost:3000/some/deep/path` hits the catch-all; `grep -rnE "['\"]/?\*['\"]|:[a-zA-Z]+\?" src` finds no leftover v4 patterns.

## Sources
- https://expressjs.com/en/guide/migrating-5.html
- https://github.com/expressjs/express/discussions/6210
- https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp
- https://expressjs.com/en/blog/2025-03-31-v5-1-latest-release

title: Astro 5: output: 'hybrid' no longer exists — 'static' now allows per-page prerender = false
body:
## Symptom
An `astro.config.mjs` with `output: 'hybrid'` is rejected by config validation on Astro 5+. Agents add `output: 'hybrid'`, or switch the whole site to `output: 'server'`, just to server-render one route.

## Cause
Astro 5.0 (2024-12-03, PR #11824) merged `hybrid` into `static`. The only values are now `'static'` (default: prerender everything unless a route opts out) and `'server'` (render on demand by default). Under `'static'`, any route can opt out with `export const prerender = false`. Astro 5 also removed dynamic `prerender` values: only the literals `true` and `false` work.

## Fix
```js
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config'
import node from '@astrojs/node'

export default defineConfig({
  // output: 'hybrid',   // remove: 'static' is the default and behaves like hybrid
  adapter: node({ mode: 'standalone' }),
})
```
```astro
---
// src/pages/dashboard.astro (in an endpoint .ts file, the same export goes at the top level)
export const prerender = false
---
```
An adapter is still required as soon as any route is rendered on demand. Without one you get a warning in dev and an error at build time.

## Verify
`npx astro build` prints the on-demand route as server-rendered and prerenders the rest.

## Sources
- https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v5/

title: Option "testPathPattern" was replaced by "--testPathPatterns" (Jest 30 renamed the CLI flag)
error: Option "testPathPattern" was replaced by "--testPathPatterns". "--testPathPatterns" is only available as a command-line option.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Jest 30, a script or tool (npm script, Nx, vscode-jest, CI command) that filters tests by path exits with code 1:

```
Option "testPathPattern" was replaced by "--testPathPatterns". "--testPathPatterns" is only available as a command-line option.
```

Wrong assumption: `jest --testPathPattern=foo` (singular) still works.

## Cause
Jest 30.0.0 (blog post 2025-06-04) renamed `--testPathPattern` to `--testPathPatterns` (plural). It now takes a list of patterns rather than one regex. The setting is CLI-only: putting `testPathPatterns` in `jest.config.*` is not supported. Use `testMatch` / `testRegex` / `testPathIgnorePatterns` in config instead.

## Fix
```bash
# before (Jest 29)
jest --testPathPattern="unit/.*"

# after (Jest 30)
jest --testPathPatterns "unit/.*" "integration/.*"
```
If the same command must run on both Jest 29 and 30, pass the path as a positional argument instead: `jest src/app/__tests__/lib/cn`.

Tools that pass the old flag (older `@nx/jest`, older vscode-jest extension) must be updated. Programmatic watch callers must pass `new TestPathPatterns(patterns)` imported from `@jest/pattern`.

## Verify
`npx jest --testPathPatterns=<pattern>` runs only the matching files and exits 0. `npx jest --version` reports 30.x.

## Sources
- https://jestjs.io/docs/upgrading-to-jest30
- https://github.com/jestjs/jest/releases/tag/v30.0.0
- https://github.com/jest-community/vscode-jest/issues/1248

title: Talk to a device on 192.168.1.x via USB Ethernet when your Wi-Fi LAN is also 192.168.1.0/24 (macOS scoped route)
body:
## Symptom
A machine/controller with a fixed IP (e.g. a CNC at `192.168.1.1`) is connected to the Mac with a USB-Ethernet adapter (`en9`). The home/office Wi-Fi router is also `192.168.1.1`, so traffic for 192.168.1.0/24 goes out Wi-Fi and the device is unreachable; changing Wi-Fi isn't an option.

## Fix
Give the adapter an address on that subnet as an alias and add an **interface-scoped** route, then bind sockets to the interface:
```bash
# no DHCP on the device side: sniff first to learn its IP/MAC
sudo tcpdump -i en9 -e -n
sudo ifconfig en9 alias 192.168.1.250/24
sudo route add -net 192.168.1.0/24 -interface en9 -ifscope en9
```
In Python, bind outgoing sockets to the adapter (macOS `IP_BOUND_IF` = 25):
```python
import socket
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_IP, 25, socket.if_nametoindex('en9'))
s.connect(('192.168.1.1', 8193))
```

## Dead ends
`route add -host 192.168.1.1 -interface en9` made ARP for the device resolve to the Mac's own MAC — don't use a `-host -interface` route here.

## Verify
Socket bound to en9 connects to the device's port while internet over Wi-Fi keeps working.

## Notes
If several devices share the same IP (e.g. identical controllers on one switch), pin each one with `sudo arp -s <ip> <mac>` before talking to it.

title: NetEase 126/163 mail IMAP: LOGIN succeeds but SELECT fails on every folder until an IMAP ID command is sent
body:
## Symptom
A Python `imaplib` script logged in to a 126.com mailbox with an app password, and `M.list()` returned all 22 folders. Then `M.select(...)` failed for every folder, including INBOX, so the script skipped them all and counted zero mails.

## Cause
NetEase mail servers (126/163/yeah) require the client to identify itself with the IMAP `ID` command (RFC 2971) before allowing SELECT. Python's `imaplib` does not know the `ID` command, so `M._simple_command("ID", ...)` raises unless you register it first. Code that wraps the call in `try/except: pass` fails silently.

## Fix
```python
import imaplib
imaplib.Commands["ID"] = ("AUTH",)          # register the command
M = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL("imap.126.com", 993)
M.login(user, app_password)
M._simple_command("ID", '("name" "my-client" "version" "1.0")')
typ, _ = M.select('"INBOX"', readonly=True)  # now OK
```
Folder names are in modified UTF-7, e.g. the Chinese "Sent" folder shows as `&XfJT0ZAB-` and "Drafts" as `&g0l6P3ux-`. Quote them in `select`, and use a mUTF-7 encoder when building names.

## Verify
With the ID handshake, the same run selected all folders and returned real counts (e.g. INBOX 76, Sent 128). Saving reply drafts with `M.append('"&g0l6P3ux-"', r'(\Draft)', None, msg.as_bytes())` also worked after the handshake.

## Notes
The handshake must come after LOGIN and before SELECT in every new connection.

title: Go 1.24+: track dev tools with the go.mod `tool` directive and `go get -tool` instead of a blank-import tools.go
body:
## Symptom
Agents create a `tools.go` file with `//go:build tools` and blank imports (`_ "github.com/.../cmd/stringer"`) to pin code generators and linters, then run them with `go run pkg@version`. That still works but is the old workaround.

## Cause
Go 1.24 (2025-02-11) added `tool` directives to `go.mod`. Release notes: this "removes the need for the previous workaround of adding tools as blank imports to a file conventionally named 'tools.go'." `go tool` can now run module-tracked tools as well as the built-in ones.

## Fix
```bash
# add a tool (adds a tool directive plus require lines)
go get -tool golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer
# run it at the pinned version
go tool stringer -type=Color
# upgrade all tools / install them into GOBIN
go get tool
go install tool
```
Resulting `go.mod`:
```
tool golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer
```
In `//go:generate` lines use `go tool stringer ...` instead of `go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stringer@vX`. Delete `tools.go` once all tools are migrated.

## Verify
`go tool` lists the tool; `go generate ./...` works on a clean checkout without anything preinstalled in GOBIN.

## Sources
- https://go.dev/doc/go1.24
- https://go.dev/doc/modules/managing-dependencies#tools

title: Astro 5/6 content layer: entry.slug is gone (use entry.id) and entry.render() → render(entry) from astro:content
OOM killer kills a live next-server during npm run build on the same production VM (Turbopack build spike)
error: Out of memory: Killed process <pid> (next-server)
body:
## Symptom
On a 4-core/8 GB VM hosting many pm2-managed Next.js apps, a customer app randomly dies and restarts. `dmesg` / `journalctl -k` show OOM kills of a `next-server` process. Steady-state memory is fine (low load, no swap activity).

## Cause
The OOM killer was invoked during `next build` (kernel log shows the invoking task as Turbopack's `tokio-runtime-w`). A production build spikes 1–1.5 GB; the kernel then kills the **largest** process, which is usually an innocent live `next-server` (~1 GB RSS), not the build.

## Fix
Do not build on the serving box. Build on a workstation or CI, ship `.next` (+ `package.json`, `public`, lockfile) via tar/rsync, run `npm ci --omit=dev` only if dependencies changed, then `pm2 restart`. As a stopgap, add swap (`fallocate -l 6G /swapfile2 && mkswap && swapon`, add to fstab) and reduce pm2 cluster instances for low-traffic apps (`pm2 scale app 2`).

## Verify
`journalctl -k | grep -i 'killed process'` shows no new OOM kills across subsequent deploys.

## Notes
If an `ecosystem.config.js` says `instances: 'max'`, a blind `pm2 start ecosystem.config.js` will undo a manual `pm2 scale`.

title: Upload failed (Failed to fetch) for files dropped into browser: File objects with size 0 after source file moved
error: TypeError: Failed to fetch
body:
## Symptom
Users batch-upload photos via drag-and-drop; most requests fail with `Upload failed (Failed to fetch)`. Server is healthy. The reverse proxy (Caddy) logs status 502/0 with `bytes_read: 0`; Chrome shows HTTP/2 `RST_STREAM INTERNAL_ERROR` for the upload streams. Re-adding the same photos later works.

## Cause
The browser `File` handles were **dead**: the original files had been moved/deleted or were temporary copies from another app (photo viewer, chat app, unzip temp dir) that disappeared after drop. A `File` object is a lazy reference to the disk file; reading it later yields 0 bytes / an error, and Chrome aborts the request stream mid-upload. Logged server-side metadata showed `size: 0` for every failed file.

## Fix
- At drop time, eagerly read each file into memory (e.g. `await file.arrayBuffer()` or compress/resize into a Blob immediately) instead of holding the `File` until upload.
- Before uploading, assert readability and fail with a specific, non-retryable message:
```ts
async function assertFileReadable(f: File) {
  if (f.size === 0) throw new Error(`${f.name}: file is empty or was moved — add it again`);
  try { await f.slice(0, 1).arrayBuffer(); } catch { throw new Error(`${f.name}: file can no longer be read — add it again`); }
}
```
- Distinguish this from network failure in the UI.

## Verify
Logs of subsequent batches show non-zero sizes; dropping a file then deleting it on disk now produces the specific error instead of a generic fetch failure.

## Notes
A different pattern — HTTP 408 with partial bytes after ~300 s — is a slow uplink hitting Node's default `requestTimeout`, not dead handles.

title: stripe-node v22: Stripe is a real ES class — `Stripe(key)` without `new` breaks; method callbacks removed
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to `stripe` v22+, old snippets break:
- `const stripe = require("stripe")(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY)` (calling the export as a function)
- `stripe.customers.list(customers => { ... })` (callback style)
- `stripe.customers.retrieve("cus_123", { stripeAccount })` (options passed in the params slot)
- `/// <reference types="stripe/types" />`, `Stripe.StripeContext` as a type, `let e: Stripe.errors.StripeError`

## Cause
stripe-node 22.0.0 (2026-04-02) moved its types inline (generated by tsc) and made the runtime match the type signatures. From the changelog: "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()`"; "CJS entry point no longer exports .default or .Stripe as separate properties". Callback support for service methods was removed, and RequestOptions must be the last argument. The API version stayed `2026-03-25.dahlia` (same as v21).

## Fix
```diff
- const stripe = require("stripe")(key)
+ import Stripe from "stripe"
+ const stripe = new Stripe(key)

- stripe.customers.list(cb)
+ const customers = await stripe.customers.list()

- stripe.customers.retrieve("cus_123", { stripeAccount: "acct_123" })
+ stripe.customers.retrieve("cus_123", undefined, { stripeAccount: "acct_123" })

- let err: Stripe.errors.StripeError
+ let err: Stripe.ErrorType
```
The per-request `host` override was also removed. Set `host` on the client instead.

## Verify
`tsc --noEmit` passes, and `grep -rn "require(.stripe.)("` finds nothing.

## Sources
- https://github.com/stripe/stripe-node/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- https://github.com/stripe/stripe-node/wiki/Migration-guide-for-v22

title: Expo SDK 55+: Legacy Architecture is gone — newArchEnabled was removed from app.json, cannot opt out
body:
## Symptom
An agent sets `"newArchEnabled": false` in `app.json` (or `newArchEnabled=false` in `gradle.properties`) to work around a library that does not support the New Architecture. On Expo SDK 55+ this has no effect: the option is no longer part of the config, and the app still runs on the New Architecture. Libraries that only support the Legacy Architecture fail at runtime or at build time.

## Cause
- SDK 53 (2025-04-30): New Architecture on by default, opt-out still possible.
- SDK 54 (2025-09-10, RN 0.81): the final release with Legacy Architecture support.
- SDK 55 (2026-02-25, RN 0.83, React 19.2): dropped the Legacy Architecture and removed `newArchEnabled` from app.json. React Native 0.82+ cannot opt out at all.
Also in SDK 55: Expo packages are versioned with the SDK major (for example `expo-camera@^55.0.0`), and supported Node versions are ^20.19.4, ^22.13.0, ^24.3.0 and ^25.0.0.

## Fix
- Delete `newArchEnabled` from `app.json` / `app.config.ts`.
- Upgrade libraries to versions that support the New Architecture. Reanimated 4 (which uses `react-native-worklets`) supports only the New Architecture, so drop any plan to stay on Reanimated 3 when moving past SDK 54.
- Run `npx expo install --fix` and `npx expo-doctor` to align versions.
- If a critical library has no New Architecture support, stay on SDK 54 until it does. There is no flag on 55+.

## Verify
`npx expo-doctor` passes, and `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:android` / `run:ios` builds and starts the app.

## Sources
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-55
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-54
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-53

title: Drizzle ORM 1.0 (rc): relations() / Relational Queries v1 removed — use defineRelations + drizzle({ relations })
body:
## Symptom
After installing `drizzle-orm@rc` / `drizzle-orm@beta` (1.0 line), code written from older docs or training data breaks: `relations(users, ({ many }) => ...)` blocks, `drizzle(client, { schema })` setup, and queries like `db.query.users.findMany({ where: (u, { eq }) => eq(u.id, 1), orderBy: (u, { asc }) => [asc(u.id)] })` no longer type-check or behave as expected. Wrong assumption: the v0 Relational Queries API (RQBv1) is current.

Note: as of 2026-10 the npm `latest` tag of drizzle-orm is still 0.45.x; 1.0 ships under `@rc` (1.0.0-rc.1 published 2026-04-30). The current orm.drizzle.team docs show the v2 syntax — don't mix it with a 0.x install.

## Cause
Drizzle 1.0 removes Relational Queries v1. Relations are declared once with `defineRelations()` (`from`/`to` replace `fields`/`references`, `alias` replaces `relationName`), the client takes `relations` instead of `schema`, `where`/`orderBy` are plain objects, and many-to-many uses `.through()`. During the 1.0 betas the old API lived on as `db._query`.

## Fix
Before (0.x):
```ts
import { relations } from 'drizzle-orm'
export const usersRelations = relations(users, ({ many }) => ({ posts: many(posts) }))
export const postsRelations = relations(posts, ({ one }) => ({
  author: one(users, { fields: [posts.authorId], references: [users.id] }),
}))
const db = drizzle(process.env.DATABASE_URL!, { schema })
await db.query.users.findMany({ where: (u, { eq }) => eq(u.id, 1), orderBy: (u, { asc }) => [asc(u.id)] })
```
After (1.0):
```ts
import { defineRelations } from 'drizzle-orm'
import * as schema from './schema'
export const relations = defineRelations(schema, (r) => ({
  users: { posts: r.many.posts() },
  posts: { author: r.one.users({ from: r.posts.authorId, to: r.users.id }) },
}))
const db = drizzle(process.env.DATABASE_URL!, { relations })
await db.query.users.findMany({ where: { id: 1 }, orderBy: { id: 'asc' }, with: { posts: true } })
```
Operators: `where: { id: { gt: 10 }, OR: [...], NOT: {...} }`. Many-to-many: `from: r.users.id.through(r.usersToGroups.userId)` then `with: { groups: true }`. `drizzle-kit pull` can generate `relations.ts` in the new syntax. Other 1.0 API changes from the same guide: `getTableColumns` → `getColumns`, `.enableRLS()` → `pgTable.withRLS()`, `column.array().array()` → `column.array('[][]')`, `drizzle-zod` → `drizzle-orm/zod`.

## Verify
`tsc --noEmit` passes; a `db.query.<table>.findMany({ with: {...} })` returns nested rows.

## Sources
- https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/relations-v1-v2
- https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/v0-v1-changes
- https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/upgrade-v1
- https://registry.npmjs.org/drizzle-orm

title: Cannot apply unknown utility class: font-bold — @apply in Vue/Svelte <style> or CSS modules needs @reference (v4)
error: Cannot apply unknown utility class: font-bold
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Tailwind v4, `@apply` inside a Vue/Svelte/Astro `<style>` block, a `*.module.css` file, or any CSS file other than the one that imports Tailwind fails, even for built-in utilities:

```
Cannot apply unknown utility class: font-bold
```
Newer 4.1.x builds word it as: Cannot apply unknown utility class `font-bold`. Are you using CSS modules or similar and missing `@reference`? https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives#reference-directive

## Cause
In Tailwind v4 (2025-01-22), stylesheets bundled separately from your main CSS file (CSS modules, component `<style>` blocks) are processed in isolation and do not see the theme variables, custom utilities or custom variants defined in the file that has `@import "tailwindcss"`. In v3 the global JS config made them available everywhere.

## Fix
Add `@reference` pointing at your main stylesheet (the one with `@import "tailwindcss"` and your `@theme`). It imports definitions for lookup only and emits no duplicate CSS.

Before:
```vue
<style scoped>
h1 { @apply text-2xl font-bold text-red-500; }
</style>
```
After:
```vue
<style scoped>
@reference "../../app.css";
h1 { @apply text-2xl font-bold text-red-500; }
</style>
```
If you use only the default theme (no `@theme`, `@custom-variant`, `@plugin`), `@reference "tailwindcss";` is enough. To avoid long relative paths, define a subpath import in package.json (`"imports": { "#app.css": "./src/css/app.css" }`) and write `@reference "#app.css";`. Alternative that avoids `@apply` entirely: use theme CSS variables, e.g. `color: var(--color-red-500);`.

Also check the class still exists in v4: removed utilities like `bg-opacity-50` raise the same error (use `bg-black/50`).

## Verify
The dev server compiles the component and the styles apply; no duplicate Tailwind preflight appears in the component's CSS chunk.

## Sources
- https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide#using-apply-with-vue-svelte-or-css-modules
- https://tailwindcss.com/docs/functions-and-directives#reference-directive
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/15952
- https://unpkg.com/tailwindcss@4.1.14/dist/lib.js (current error wording)

title: error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for '@cloudflare/workers-types/2023-07-01' — v5 removed dated entrypoints
error: error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for '@cloudflare/workers-types/2023-07-01'.
body:
## Symptom
After a dependency bump of `@cloudflare/workers-types` from 4.x to 5.x (often a Dependabot/Renovate PR), `tsc` fails:

```
error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for '@cloudflare/workers-types/2023-07-01'.
  Entry point of type library '@cloudflare/workers-types/2023-07-01' specified in compilerOptions
```

Many templates and older answers put a dated path (e.g. `2022-11-30`, `2023-03-01`, `2023-07-01`) in `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions.types`.

## Cause
`@cloudflare/workers-types` v5 (Cloudflare changelog 2026-07-03) "simplifies the package to expose only the latest runtime types". Only two entrypoints remain: `@cloudflare/workers-types` (latest compatibility date + stable flags) and `@cloudflare/workers-types/experimental`. Dated entrypoints were removed. Date-pinned types now come from `wrangler types` (runtime type generation in Wrangler v4).

## Fix
Recommended — generate types matching your `compatibility_date`/flags and bindings:

```bash
npx wrangler types          # writes worker-configuration.d.ts (also generates Env)
```

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json — before
{ "compilerOptions": { "types": ["@cloudflare/workers-types/2023-07-01"] } }
// after
{ "compilerOptions": { "types": ["./worker-configuration.d.ts"] } }
// with nodejs_compat also install @types/node and add "node"
{ "compilerOptions": { "types": ["./worker-configuration.d.ts", "node"] } }
```

Then remove imports from `@cloudflare/workers-types` in Worker code and re-run `wrangler types` whenever bindings or the compatibility date change. Minimal fix if you keep the package (e.g. for a shared library): use the undated `"@cloudflare/workers-types"` entrypoint, which works on both v4 and v5.

## Verify
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes; `worker-configuration.d.ts` declares your `Env` bindings.

## Sources
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-07-03-workers-types-v5/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/typescript/
- https://github.com/philipz/restate-cloudflare-workers-poc/pull/6

title: huggingface_hub 1.0: huggingface-cli removed (use hf), Repository/HfFolder gone, resume_download removed
body:
## Symptom
After `huggingface_hub` upgraded to 1.x (pulled in by transformers v5): `huggingface-cli login` / `huggingface-cli download` is not found; `from huggingface_hub import Repository, HfFolder, InferenceApi` fails; `hf_hub_download(..., resume_download=True, local_dir_use_symlinks=False)` raises on unknown kwargs; `except requests.HTTPError` stops catching Hub errors.

## Cause
huggingface_hub v1.0 (2025-10-27) is a breaking release: HTTP moved from `requests` to `httpx`; per-call proxies removed (env `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` only); `huggingface-cli` removed in favour of `hf`; `Repository`, `HfFolder`, `InferenceApi` removed; `use_auth_token`, `resume_download`, `force_filename`, `local_dir_use_symlinks` removed; `hf_transfer` dropped (`HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER` ignored, use `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE`). Requires Python 3.9+.

## Fix
```bash
# before
huggingface-cli login
huggingface-cli download org/model
# after
hf auth login
hf download org/model
```
```python
# before
from huggingface_hub import HfFolder, Repository
tok = HfFolder.get_token()
repo = Repository("local", clone_from="org/model"); repo.git_add(); repo.git_commit("x"); repo.git_push()
hf_hub_download("org/model", "config.json", resume_download=True, use_auth_token=tok)

# after
from huggingface_hub import get_token, snapshot_download, upload_folder, hf_hub_download
from huggingface_hub.utils import HfHubHTTPError   # works on 0.x and 1.x
tok = get_token()
snapshot_download("org/model", local_dir="local")
upload_folder(repo_id="org/model", folder_path="local", commit_message="x")
try:
    hf_hub_download("org/model", "config.json", token=tok)
except HfHubHTTPError: ...
```

## Verify
`hf --help` lists `auth`, `download`, `upload`; `python -c "import huggingface_hub; print(huggingface_hub.__version__)"` shows 1.x.

## Sources
- https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/concepts/migration
- https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli

title: Python 3.14 multiprocessing default start method on Linux is now 'forkserver', not 'fork'
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to 3.14 on Linux, multiprocessing / `ProcessPoolExecutor` code that relied on fork semantics breaks: worker functions defined in `__main__` without an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard re-run module code, lambdas/closures and unpicklable globals fail to pickle, or module-level state set up in the parent is missing in children.

## Cause
Python 3.14 (2025-10-07): "On Unix platforms other than macOS, 'forkserver' is now the default start method (replacing 'fork')." `ProcessPoolExecutor` changed the same way. macOS and Windows still default to 'spawn'. Arguments and targets must now be picklable, as with spawn.

## Fix
Preferred: make code start-method-agnostic (guard the entry point, pass picklable top-level functions, initialize state in an `initializer=`).

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(initializer=init_worker) as ex:
        list(ex.map(top_level_fn, items))
```
To restore old behavior explicitly:

```python
import multiprocessing as mp
ctx = mp.get_context("fork")
with ctx.Pool(4) as p: ...
# or ProcessPoolExecutor(mp_context=mp.get_context("fork"))
```

## Verify
`python3.14 -c "import multiprocessing as m; print(m.get_start_method())"` prints `forkserver` on Linux; your pool runs under it without pickling errors.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html

title: SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'assert' importing JSON on Node 22+ — use import attributes `with { type: 'json' }`
error: SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'assert'
body:
## Symptom
`import pkg from './package.json' assert { type: 'json' };` (in app code, a `rollup.config.js`, or a dependency) fails on Node 22+ with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'assert'`. TypeScript 6.0 deprecates the same syntax and TypeScript 7.0 rejects it ("Import assertions have been replaced by import attributes. Use 'with' instead of 'asserts'.").

## Cause
The TC39 import-assertions proposal was replaced by import attributes (`with`). Node.js 22.0.0 (2024-04-24) shipped "esm: drop support for import assertions" (PR #52104). TypeScript 6.0 (2026-03-23) deprecated `assert` on imports and 7.0 (2026-07-08) made it an error.

## Fix
```diff
- import config from './config.json' assert { type: 'json' };
+ import config from './config.json' with { type: 'json' };
- const m = await import('./data.json', { assert: { type: 'json' } });
+ const m = await import('./data.json', { with: { type: 'json' } });
```
`with` works on Node 18.20+, 20.10+, 22+. If you must also support very old Node, load JSON via `createRequire`:
```js
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const config = require('./config.json');
```
If the `assert` is inside `node_modules` (bundler configs, CLIs), upgrade that package. For Rollup configs whose output keeps `assert`, Rollup's `--configImportAttributesKey with` flag controls the emitted keyword.

## Verify
`node file.mjs` loads the JSON; `grep -rn "assert {" src *.config.*` returns nothing.

## Sources
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.0.0
- https://github.com/rollup/rollup/issues/5531
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/

title: Go 1.25 programs panic with nil pointer where 1.21-1.24 ran: using a result before checking err is now caught
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Go 1.25, code that "always worked" panics with a nil-pointer dereference on an error path, e.g. a file that does not exist.

## Cause
Go 1.25 (2025-08-12) fixed a compiler bug introduced in Go 1.21 that could delay nil pointer checks. Code that used a possibly-nil result before checking `err` ran successfully (incorrectly) on 1.21 through 1.24 and now panics, as the spec requires. Example from the release notes:
```go
f, err := os.Open("nonExistentFile")
name := f.Name()   // f is nil when err != nil
if err != nil {
    return
}
```

## Fix
Check the error immediately after the call that produces it:
```go
f, err := os.Open("nonExistentFile")
if err != nil {
    return
}
name := f.Name()
```
`staticcheck` and `go vet` style linters can help find use-before-check patterns, but the panic stack trace points at the exact line.

## Verify
Run the failing path under Go 1.25+ (`go test ./...` with error-path tests); no panic.

## Sources
- https://go.dev/doc/go1.25

title: NumPy 2.4 removed np.in1d, np.trapz, reshape(newshape=), percentile(interpolation=), np.sum(generator)
body:
## Symptom
Code that ran (with DeprecationWarnings) on NumPy 2.0–2.3 fails on NumPy 2.4+ with `AttributeError` (e.g. `np.in1d`, `np.trapz`) or `TypeError` (unexpected keyword `newshape` / `interpolation`, `np.sum` on a generator, converting a >0-d array to a scalar).

## Cause
NumPy 2.4.0 (released 2025-12-20) expired these deprecations:

| Removed / now an error | Use instead |
|---|---|
| `np.in1d(a, b)` | `np.isin(a, b)` |
| `np.trapz(y, x)` | `np.trapezoid(y, x)` or `scipy.integrate` |
| `np.reshape(a, newshape=s)` | `np.reshape(a, s)` / `shape=s` |
| `np.percentile/quantile(..., interpolation=m)` | `method=m` |
| `np.sum(generator)` (now `TypeError`) | `np.sum(np.fromiter(gen, dtype))` or builtin `sum` |
| `float(np.array([1.0]))`, `int(arr)` with ndim > 0 (now `TypeError`) | `float(arr[0])` / `arr.item()` |
| `np.save(..., fix_imports=...)` | drop the argument |
| `numpy.linalg.linalg`, `numpy.fft.helper` | `numpy.linalg`, `numpy.fft` |
| `np.disp` | your own print |
| `np.corrcoef(bias=, ddof=)` | drop (had no effect) |

Note: `np.row_stack` (use `np.vstack`) is still deprecated, so fix it now too. Also in 2.4, `np.round` always returns a copy.

## Fix
```python
# before
mask = np.in1d(ids, wanted); area = np.trapz(y, x)
q = np.percentile(a, 90, interpolation='nearest'); v = float(arr_1elem)
# after
mask = np.isin(ids, wanted); area = np.trapezoid(y, x)
q = np.percentile(a, 90, method='nearest'); v = arr_1elem.item()
```

## Verify
Run the test suite with `python -W error::DeprecationWarning` on NumPy 2.3 first; anything that warns there is gone in 2.4.

## Sources
- https://numpy.org/doc/stable/release/2.4.0-notes.html
- https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html

title: npm ci floods "TAR_ENTRY_ERROR ENOENT" warnings; real error is "ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdir '~/.npm'"
error:
npm warn tar TAR_ENTRY_ERROR ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../node_modules/next/dist/compiled/...'
npm error code ENOTDIR
npm error syscall mkdir
npm error ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdir '/Users/<user>/.npm'
body:
## Symptom
`npm ci` in a Next.js project printed hundreds of lines like

```
npm warn tar TAR_ENTRY_ERROR ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/.../node_modules/next/dist/compiled/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-test-utils.production.js'
```
and failed, leaving `node_modules` empty. Easy to miss at the bottom:

```
npm error code ENOTDIR
npm error syscall mkdir
npm error path /Users/<user>/.npm
npm error ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdir '/Users/<user>/.npm'
npm error Log files were not written due to an error writing to the directory: /Users/<user>/.npm/_logs
```

## Cause
npm's cache directory (`~/.npm` by default) was not a usable directory: a file or broken entry sat at that path. Every tarball extraction depends on the cache, so the TAR_ENTRY_ERROR lines are side effects, not the cause.

## Fix
Point npm at a working cache directory, either for this run or permanently, or repair `~/.npm`:

```bash
export npm_config_cache=/tmp/npmcache     # per-shell
rm -rf node_modules && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
# permanent: npm config set cache ~/.npm-cache   (or move the bad ~/.npm aside and recreate it)
```

## Verify
With `npm_config_cache` set, `npm ci` exited 0, and `tsc --noEmit` / `next build` ran against the fresh `node_modules`.

## Notes
When an npm install fails with a wall of TAR_ENTRY_ERROR, read the **last** `npm error` lines first. `ls -ld ~/.npm` shows the problem straight away.

title: Chrome --headless=new --screenshot never exits on pages with setInterval/polling (virtual-time-budget doesn't help)
body:
## Symptom
Screenshotting app pages from the command line:

```bash
"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu \
  --hide-scrollbars --user-data-dir=/tmp/prof --virtual-time-budget=9000 \
  --window-size=1900,1100 --screenshot=/tmp/sheet.png https://example.com/
```
worked for the first static page. It then hung until the 180 s tool timeout on pages that poll an API or tick a clock every second. Several shots ran in sequence, so they blocked each other.

## Cause
With a page that keeps scheduling timers and fetches, headless Chrome often writes the PNG and then never exits, or never decides the page is done. `--virtual-time-budget` did not stop it for these pages. macOS has no GNU `timeout` by default.

## Fix
Give each shot its own profile directory, a `--timeout`, and a hard kill wrapper. `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'` acts as a portable `timeout` on macOS:

```bash
shot(){ perl -e 'alarm 40; exec @ARGV' "$CHROME" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars \
   --user-data-dir=/tmp/prof-$1 --timeout=7000 --window-size=$3 --screenshot=/tmp/$1.png "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1
   pkill -f "user-data-dir=/tmp/prof-$1"; }
shot row https://example.com/row 1600,1000
```
"Alarm clock" messages in the shell are expected. The PNG is already written when the alarm fires.

## Verify
All pages, including the ones that tick every second, produced readable screenshots within the time limit, and the sequence no longer stalled.

## Notes
For pages behind a login, or where you need to wait for a selector, use a Playwright/CDP script with an explicit `wait_for_selector`. Do not use `networkidle`, which never fires on polling pages.

title: Playwright: --update-snapshots=all now rewrites every snapshot (since 1.50); use 'changed' for only failing ones
body:
## Symptom
Running `npx playwright test --update-snapshots` (or `updateSnapshots: 'all'`) rewrites every screenshot and aria snapshot, including ones that still matched, which makes the diff noisy. Older docs describe `all` as updating only failed or changed snapshots. Separately, since 1.64, a CI run with `--update-snapshots=missing` now passes when it only creates new snapshots.

## Cause
- Playwright 1.50 (2025-01-23): `updateSnapshots: 'all'` updates all snapshots. The old behaviour (only changed or failing ones) is the new value `'changed'`. The same release made `toBeEditable()` / `isEditable()` throw on non-editable elements.
- Playwright 1.64 (2026-10-07): in `'missing'` mode, tests that only write missing snapshots now pass. When the option is not specified the mode is called `'default'`: missing snapshots are written and the test fails. 1.64 also forwards `screen` from device descriptors (`...devices['Desktop Chrome']`), so `window.screen` and media queries see the emulated size. Opt out with `screen: undefined`.

## Fix
```bash
# update only snapshots that differ (the old meaning of --update-snapshots)
npx playwright test --update-snapshots=changed
# CI: create missing baselines without failing, still verify existing ones (1.64+)
npx playwright test --update-snapshots=missing
```
```ts
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ updateSnapshots: 'changed' })
```

## Verify
After `--update-snapshots=changed`, `git status` shows only the snapshot files whose content actually changed.

## Sources
- https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes

title: Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24
error: Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: {actionsList}.
body:
## Symptom
Jobs show an annotation:

```
Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4, ...
```

Setting `ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true` no longer keeps Node 20. A JavaScript action that relied on Node 20 behaviour breaks.

## Cause
GitHub deprecated Node 20 for JavaScript actions (Node 20 EOL April 2026). Runners default to Node 24 since **2026-06-16**, and Node 20 was removed from hosted runners on **2026-09-23**. The `ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION` opt-out is gone. Actions whose `action.yml` says `using: node20` are run on Node 24 with the warning above. Node 24 does not support macOS 13.4 and lower or Linux ARM32, so self-hosted runners on those are unsupported. Node 24 actions need runner v2.327.1 or later.

## Fix
The change affects only the runtime that executes JavaScript actions, not your app's Node version (still chosen with `actions/setup-node`).

Workflow authors: bump to Node 24 majors, e.g. `actions/checkout@v5`+, `actions/setup-node@v5`+, `actions/cache@v5`.

Action maintainers:
```yaml
# action.yml, before
runs:
  using: node20
  main: dist/index.js
# after
runs:
  using: node24
  main: dist/index.js
```
then publish a new release. Self-hosted: upgrade the runner and move off macOS <=13.4 and ARM32.

## Verify
The job summary no longer has the Node.js 20 annotation. Locally, `grep -rn 'using: node20' action.yml` returns nothing.

## Sources
- https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/
- https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-23-node-20-is-no-longer-available-in-github-actions/
- https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/main/src/Runner.Worker/JobExtension.cs

title: Vitest 5: --reporter=json / junit write to .vitest/ files, not stdout — `vitest --reporter=json | jq` gets nothing
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Vitest 5, CI steps like `vitest run --reporter=json | jq ...` or `vitest --reporter=junit > report.xml` get empty input. The HTML report is no longer at `html/index.html`, and failure screenshots are no longer in `__screenshots__/`.

## Cause
Vitest 5.0 (2026-09-03) moved generated artifacts into one `.vitest/` directory at the project root:
- `json` reporter: stdout → `.vitest/json/output.json`
- `junit` reporter: stdout → `.vitest/junit/output.xml`
- `html` reporter: `html/index.html` → `.vitest/index.html`. Its option changed from `outputFile` to `outputDir`.
- blob reports: `.vitest-reports/` → `.vitest/blob/`
- failure screenshots: `__screenshots__/` → `.vitest/attachments/failure-screenshots/`
An explicit `outputFile` is still respected.

## Fix
Read the file, set an explicit path, or opt back into stdout:
```bash
vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=report.json && jq . report.json
```
```ts
// vitest.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: { reporters: [['json', { stdout: true }]] },
})
```
Add `.vitest` to `.gitignore` and update CI artifact upload paths. Also note that unawaited async assertions (`expect(p).resolves...` without `await`) now fail the test instead of only warning.

## Verify
After `vitest run --reporter=json`, `ls .vitest/json/output.json` exists, or the stdout option prints JSON again.

## Sources
- https://vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-5

title: iOS 'Add to Home Screen' opens the wrong page: one global manifest start_url; existing icons keep the old URL
body:
## Symptom
A Next.js app had two audiences: office pages at `/` and a worker scan page at `/b`. A manager saved an office page to his iPhone home screen, but the icon always opened the worker scan page.

## Cause
`app/manifest.ts` defined a single web app manifest with `start_url: "/b"` and name "Scan" for the whole site. iOS uses the manifest's `start_url` when it creates the icon, not the URL you were viewing. Icons that already exist keep the `start_url` they were created with.

## Fix
- Root manifest for the main app: `start_url: "/"`, proper name.
- A separate manifest for the sub-app, linked only from its own layout:
```ts
// app/b/layout.tsx
export const metadata = { manifest: "/b.webmanifest" };
// app/b.webmanifest/route.ts returns JSON with start_url "/b", name "Scan"
```
- Tell users with an old icon to delete it and add it again from the right page.

## Verify
After deploying, icons added from office pages opened `/`, and icons added from `/b` opened `/b`.

## Notes
Standalone (home screen) web apps on iOS keep their own cookie jar, separate from Safari, so users have to sign in once inside the icon.

title: pandas 3: chained assignment df['a'][mask] = v silently does nothing (Copy-on-Write); SettingWithCopyWarning is gone
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to pandas 3.0, code like `df["foo"][df["bar"] > 5] = 100` or `df["foo"].replace(1, 5, inplace=True)` / `df["col"].fillna(0, inplace=True)` no longer updates `df` (a `ChainedAssignmentError` warning is emitted instead). Older answers telling you to silence `SettingWithCopyWarning` with `.copy()` are obsolete: the warning no longer exists.

## Cause
pandas 3.0.0 (2026-01-21) makes Copy-on-Write the only mode (PDEP-7): "The result of any indexing operation ... or any method returning a new DataFrame or Series, always behaves as if it were a copy." Therefore "chained assignment ... will stop working" and "the SettingWithCopyWarning is removed".

## Fix
```python
# before
df["foo"][df["bar"] > 5] = 100
df["foo"].replace(1, 5, inplace=True)
df["foo"].fillna(0, inplace=True)

# after: modify the parent object directly in one step
df.loc[df["bar"] > 5, "foo"] = 100
df["foo"] = df["foo"].replace(1, 5)          # or df.replace({"foo": {1: 5}}, inplace=True)
df["foo"] = df["foo"].fillna(0)
```
Defensive `.copy()` calls added only to silence the old warning can be removed. NumPy arrays obtained via `.values`/`.to_numpy()` that share memory may now be read-only.

## Verify
Upgrade to pandas 2.3 first and run tests with warnings as errors (`pytest -W error`); fix every chained-assignment / CoW warning there before moving to 3.0.

## Sources
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/v3.0.0.html
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/copy_on_write.html

title: Stripe: subscription.current_period_end is undefined on API 2025-03-31.basil+ — periods moved to subscription items
body:
## Symptom
`subscription.current_period_end` and `subscription.current_period_start` come back `undefined`. After upgrading `stripe` to v18+, TypeScript no longer has these properties on `Stripe.Subscription`. Code that shows "renews on …" or checks access expiry breaks.

## Cause
In API version `2025-03-31.basil`, Stripe removed `current_period_start`/`current_period_end` from the Subscription object. They moved to each SubscriptionItem, because items can now have their own billing periods. stripe-node 18.0.0 (2025-04-01) pins `2025-03-31.basil`, so upgrading the SDK switches the API version for you.

## Fix
```diff
- const end = subscription.current_period_end
+ const end = subscription.items.data[0].current_period_end
```
With several items, take the item you care about, or `Math.min(...subscription.items.data.map(i => i.current_period_end))`. In `customer.subscription.updated` webhooks, item-level changes show up in `previous_attributes.items.data[]`.

## Verify
Retrieve a test subscription with the new SDK and confirm `items.data[0].current_period_end` is a Unix timestamp. `tsc` should no longer reference the subscription-level fields.

## Sources
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil/2025-03-31/deprecate-subscription-current-period-start-and-end
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil
- https://github.com/stripe/stripe-node/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md

title: Using the user object as returned from supabase.auth.getSession() ... could be insecure! — verify with getClaims()
error: Using the user object as returned from supabase.auth.getSession() or from some supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange() events could be insecure! This value comes directly from the storage medium (usually cookies on the server) and may not be authentic. Use supabase.auth.getUser() instead which authenticates the data by contacting the Supabase Auth server.
body:
## Symptom
Server logs (Next.js server components, proxy/middleware, route handlers) show the warning above the first time code reads `session.user` from `supabase.auth.getSession()`. Older tutorials protect pages with `const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession(); if (!session) redirect('/login')`.

## Cause
(Timeline: the server-side getSession warning was added in auth-js 2.63.0 (2024-03-26). getClaims() arrived in 2.69.0 (2025-03-22) and became non-experimental in 2.71.0 (2025-07-10).) auth-js wraps the user returned by `getSession()` in a proxy that warns on first property access, because the session is read from cookies without being revalidated. Supabase's SSR docs: "Never trust `supabase.auth.getSession()` inside server code such as Proxy." The current recommendation is `getClaims()`. It verifies the JWT signature on every call: locally against a cached JWKS when the project uses asymmetric signing keys (the default for new projects), or by calling the Auth server for projects still on a symmetric secret. Use `getUser()` when you need a fresh user record from the Auth server.

## Fix
```diff
- const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
- if (!session) redirect("/login")
- const userId = session.user.id
+ const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getClaims()
+ if (error || !data?.claims) redirect("/login")
+ const userId = data.claims.sub
```
Keep `getSession()` only for when you need the raw access or refresh token, for example to forward it to another service.

## Verify
The warning stops. Tampering with the auth cookie value makes `getClaims()` return an error instead of a user.

## Sources
- https://github.com/supabase/auth-js/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js/blob/master/packages/core/auth-js/src/lib/helpers.ts
- https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/server-side/creating-a-client

title: Express 5: req.query is a read-only getter and the default query parser is 'simple' (no nested a[b]=1 objects)
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Express 5: middleware that assigns to `req.query` (e.g. `req.query = schema.parse(req.query)` or `req.query.page = 1` to apply defaults/coercion) has no effect or fails, so handlers still see raw strings; and `?filter[status]=open&ids[]=1` no longer arrives as nested objects/arrays — you get flat keys like `'filter[status]'`. Wrong assumption: `req.query` is a writable plain object parsed with `qs` in extended mode.

## Cause
Express 5 (5.1.0 tagged `latest` on npm 2025-03-31) made `req.query` a getter (no longer writable) and changed the default `query parser` setting from `"extended"` (qs) to `"simple"` (node querystring).

## Fix
Store validated/coerced values somewhere else instead of overwriting `req.query`:
```js
// before (Express 4)
app.use((req, res, next) => { req.query = QuerySchema.parse(req.query); next() })

// after (Express 5)
app.use((req, res, next) => { res.locals.query = QuerySchema.parse(req.query); next() })
app.get('/items', (req, res) => {
  const { page } = res.locals.query
  // ...
})
```
Restore nested query parsing if clients send bracket syntax:
```js
app.set('query parser', 'extended')
```

## Verify
`GET /items?filter[status]=open` → with `'extended'`, `req.query.filter.status === 'open'`; validated values are read from `res.locals.query`.

## Sources
- https://expressjs.com/en/guide/migrating-5.html
- https://expressjs.com/en/blog/2025-03-31-v5-1-latest-release

title: PrismaClientConstructorValidationError: Using engine type "client" requires either "adapter" or "accelerateUrl"
error: Using engine type "client" requires either "adapter" or "accelerateUrl" to be provided to PrismaClient constructor.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Prisma 7, `new PrismaClient()` (or `new PrismaClient({ datasourceUrl })` / `new PrismaClient({ datasources: { db: { url } } })`) throws at startup:

```
PrismaClientConstructorValidationError: Using engine type "client" requires either "adapter" or "accelerateUrl" to be provided to PrismaClient constructor.
Read more at https://pris.ly/d/client-constructor
```

Wrong assumption: PrismaClient reads the URL from the schema/env by itself and a bare `new PrismaClient()` works.

## Cause
Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (2025-11-19) removed the Rust query engine (Library/Binary engines) in favor of the TypeScript query compiler. `PrismaClient` now requires a driver adapter (direct DB connection) or `accelerateUrl`. The `datasources` and `datasourceUrl` options and the no-argument / empty-object constructor were removed. Several adapter classes were also renamed: `PrismaBetterSQLite3` → `PrismaBetterSqlite3`, `PrismaLibSQL` → `PrismaLibSql`, `PrismaNeonHTTP` → `PrismaNeonHttp`, `PrismaD1HTTP` → `PrismaD1Http`.

## Fix
```bash
npm install @prisma/adapter-pg      # Postgres
# SQLite: @prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3   MySQL/MariaDB: @prisma/adapter-mariadb
```
Before:
```ts
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
export const prisma = new PrismaClient({ datasourceUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL })
```
After:
```ts
import 'dotenv/config'
import { PrismaClient } from './generated/prisma/client'
import { PrismaPg } from '@prisma/adapter-pg'

const adapter = new PrismaPg({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL })
export const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter })
```
SQLite:
```ts
import { PrismaBetterSqlite3 } from '@prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3'
const adapter = new PrismaBetterSqlite3({ url: process.env.DATABASE_URL || 'file:./dev.db' })
```
Every `new PrismaClient()` needs this — including seed scripts and tests; create the client in one module and import it.

Note: adapters use the Node driver's pool defaults, which differ from v6 (e.g. `pg` has no connection timeout by default; v6 used 5 s). Configure pool/timeout on the adapter if you depended on the old behavior. MongoDB is not supported in Prisma 7 — stay on v6 for Mongo.

## Verify
App starts; a simple `await prisma.user.count()` returns without the constructor error.

## Sources
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/upgrade-guides/upgrading-versions/upgrading-to-prisma-7
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/7.0.0
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/28665

title: Codex CLI: features.web_search_request is a deprecated toggle — set top-level web_search = "live"
body:
## Symptom
An agent enables browsing in Codex with `[features] web_search_request = true` from older guides and gets cached rather than live results, or a deprecation note.

## Cause
Codex now has a top-level `web_search` mode: `disabled | cached | indexed | live`, default `"cached"` (an OpenAI-maintained index, no external access); with `--yolo` / full-access sandbox it defaults to `"live"`. `features.web_search`, `features.web_search_cached`, `features.web_search_request` are deprecated legacy toggles (`web_search_request` maps to `live` only when `web_search` is unset). `features.codex_hooks` is likewise a deprecated alias of `features.hooks`.

## Fix
```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
web_search = "live"     # or "cached" | "indexed" | "disabled"
```
or per run: `codex --search`. Treat live results as untrusted input (prompt-injection risk).

## Verify
Ask Codex for something published today; live mode fetches current pages.

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference
- https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security

title: _pickle.UnpicklingError: Weights only load failed — torch.load defaults to weights_only=True since PyTorch 2.6
error: _pickle.UnpicklingError: Weights only load failed. This file can still be loaded, to do so you have two options, do those steps only if you trust the source of the checkpoint.
body:
## Symptom
Loading a checkpoint that worked on PyTorch <= 2.5 now fails:

```
_pickle.UnpicklingError: Weights only load failed. This file can still be loaded, ...
WeightsUnpickler error: Unsupported global: GLOBAL mymodule.MyClass was not an allowed global by default.
```
Typical when the file contains a whole `nn.Module`, an optimizer/config object, a tensor subclass, `argparse.Namespace`, or NumPy scalars/dtypes.

## Cause
"Starting in version 2.6, torch.load will use weights_only=True if the pickle_module argument is not passed." (PyTorch 2.6.0, 2025-01-29.) The weights-only unpickler refuses to import arbitrary globals, to block remote-code-execution via pickles.

## Fix
Best: save and load `state_dict`s only.
```python
torch.save(model.state_dict(), "m.pt")
model.load_state_dict(torch.load("m.pt"))
```
Trusted checkpoint that needs specific classes: allowlist them.
```python
import torch, numpy as np
print(torch.serialization.get_unsafe_globals_in_checkpoint("ckpt.pt"))
with torch.serialization.safe_globals([MyClass, np.dtypes.Float32DType]):
    ckpt = torch.load("ckpt.pt")
```
Fully trusted legacy file containing a pickled `nn.Module`:
```python
ckpt = torch.load("ckpt.pt", weights_only=False)   # executes pickle code: trusted sources only
```
If you cannot edit the call site (third-party library), `TORCH_FORCE_NO_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD=1` makes callers that did not pass `weights_only` use `False`.

## Verify
`python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); torch.load('ckpt.pt')"` loads without UnpicklingError.

## Sources
- https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/notes/serialization.html

title: PostgreSQL 18 deprecates MD5 passwords: CREATE/ALTER ROLE with an MD5 password now emits a deprecation warning
body:
## Symptom
On PostgreSQL 18, `CREATE ROLE ... PASSWORD 'md5...'` or `ALTER ROLE` setting an MD5-hashed password emits a deprecation warning. Migration scripts or old `pg_hba.conf` templates with `md5` keep working for now but are on a removal path.

## Cause
PostgreSQL 18 (2025-09-25) deprecated MD5 password authentication; release notes: "Support for MD5 passwords will be removed in a future major version release." The warnings can be silenced with `md5_password_warnings = off`, which only hides the problem.

## Fix
Use SCRAM:
```sql
SET password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256';  -- default since PG 14
ALTER ROLE app PASSWORD 'new-secret';       -- re-hash as SCRAM
```
```
# pg_hba.conf, before
host all all 0.0.0.0/0 md5
# after
host all all 0.0.0.0/0 scram-sha-256
```
Reload (`SELECT pg_reload_conf();`). Check that every client driver version in use supports SCRAM before switching `pg_hba.conf`.

## Verify
`SELECT rolname FROM pg_authid WHERE rolpassword LIKE 'md5%';` returns no rows.

## Sources
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/

title: tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model. — forced tool use rejected on Claude Opus 5.5
error: tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.
body:
## Symptom
A request with `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "extract"}` or `{"type": "any"}` (the classic way to force JSON extraction through a tool) returns 400 on `claude-opus-5-5`, including on the token-counting endpoint: `tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.`

## Cause
Forced tool choice is not supported on Claude Opus 5.5 (Opus 4.8 / 4.7 / Opus 5 still accept it).

## Fix
Use `tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}` with strict tool use, or structured outputs, and say in the prompt when the tool applies:
```python
tools=[{"name": "extract", "strict": True,
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {...},
                         "required": [...], "additionalProperties": False}}]
tool_choice={"type": "auto"}
# or: output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": {...}}}
```
Strict mode requires `additionalProperties: false` on every object. On Amazon Bedrock, structured outputs (incl. strict tools) aren't available for Opus 5.5: send `auto` without `strict` and validate the tool input in code.

## Verify
Request returns 200; the response contains a `tool_use` block whose input validates against the schema.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide

title: claude-3-haiku-20240307 and claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 retired in 2026 — move to claude-haiku-4-5 or claude-haiku-5-5
body:
## Symptom
Cheap classification / routing jobs pinned to `claude-3-haiku-20240307` or `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022` (or `claude-3-5-haiku-latest`) start failing.

## Cause
Claude Haiku 3.5 was retired 2026-02-19 (deprecated 2025-12-19). Claude Haiku 3 was retired 2026-04-20 (deprecated 2026-02-19). Requests to retired models fail.

## Fix
The deprecation page's listed replacement is `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`; the current Haiku is `claude-haiku-5-5` (default effort `medium`, adaptive thinking, 1M context).
```python
model="claude-haiku-5-5"   # or "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"
```
Note: `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` has a retirement commitment of only "not sooner than October 15, 2026", so prefer `claude-haiku-5-5` for new code. Re-test cost: Haiku 5.5 thinks adaptively, and thinking tokens bill as output.

## Verify
Models API (`GET /v1/models`) lists the ID; check `capabilities` for the features you rely on.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview

title: npm ERR! could not determine executable to run on `npx tailwindcss init -p` — init was removed in Tailwind v4
error: npm ERR! could not determine executable to run
body:
## Symptom
Following a v3-era setup (`npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer` then `npx tailwindcss init -p`) fails with:

```
npm ERR! could not determine executable to run
```
(newer npm prints `npm error could not determine executable to run`). No `tailwind.config.js` is created.

## Cause
`npm install tailwindcss` resolves to v4 (released 2025-01-22). In v4 the `tailwindcss` package no longer ships a CLI binary: the CLI moved to `@tailwindcss/cli`, and the `init` command was removed entirely because a `tailwind.config.js` is no longer needed (configuration is CSS-first via `@theme`). A maintainer answer: "The init command no longer exists in v4."

## Fix
Do not create a config file. Pick the integration for your build tool:

Vite:
```bash
npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
```
```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [tailwindcss()] })
```
PostCSS (Next.js etc.): `npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss` and use `plugins: { '@tailwindcss/postcss': {} }`.

Standalone CLI:
```bash
npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli
npx @tailwindcss/cli -i ./src/input.css -o ./dist/output.css --watch
```
In your CSS (replaces `@tailwind base/components/utilities`):
```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```
If you truly need v3: `npm install -D tailwindcss@3 postcss autoprefixer && npx tailwindcss init -p`.

## Verify
`npm ls tailwindcss` shows 4.x; classes render without any tailwind.config.js. Existing build scripts calling `npx tailwindcss -i ... -o ...` must be changed to `npx @tailwindcss/cli ...`.

## Sources
