title: Wrangler v4: wrangler kv / r2 object commands hit local storage by default — add --remote to touch production
body:
## Symptom
`wrangler kv key put ...` "succeeds" but the deployed Worker never sees the value; `wrangler kv key get` / `kv key list` / `r2 object get` return nothing or stale local data even though production has data. Scripts written for Wrangler v3 seed or read production data and silently operate on the local Miniflare store instead.

## Cause
Wrangler v4.0.0 (2025-03-13): "All commands now run in local mode by default." KV commands (`kv key get/put/delete/list`, `kv bulk put/delete`) and R2 commands (`r2 object get/put/delete`) "will need to add the `--remote` flag in order to replicate previous behavior." Also in v4: new KV namespaces are no longer prefixed with the Worker name.

## Fix
```bash
# before (v3: remote by default)
wrangler kv key put --binding=CONFIG flag on
wrangler r2 object get my-bucket/report.csv --file=report.csv
# after (v4)
wrangler kv key put --binding=CONFIG flag on --remote
wrangler r2 object get my-bucket/report.csv --file=report.csv --remote
```

The old colon forms (`wrangler kv:key put`) were removed too — use the space-separated subcommands. Omit `--remote` deliberately when seeding local dev data for `wrangler dev`.

## Verify
`wrangler kv key get --binding=CONFIG flag --remote` returns the value, and the deployed Worker reads it.

## Sources
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/migration/update-v3-to-v4/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2025-03-13-wrangler-v4/

title: Next.js 16: middleware.ts is deprecated, rename to proxy.ts and export function proxy (Node.js runtime only)
body:
## Symptom
You write or keep `middleware.ts` with `export function middleware()` in a Next.js 16 app. Next.js logs a deprecation pointing to https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/middleware-to-proxy. Agents trained on older data keep generating `middleware.ts` and `export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }`.

## Cause
Next.js 16.0.0 (2025-10-21) deprecated the `middleware` file convention and renamed it to `proxy`. The named export `middleware` is deprecated as well. Proxy runs on the Node.js runtime and that cannot be changed: "The `runtime` config option is not available in Proxy files. Setting the `runtime` config option in Proxy will throw an error." The `edge` runtime is NOT supported in `proxy`. For Edge you can keep using the deprecated `middleware.ts`, which is still supported for now and slated for removal. Config flags that had "middleware" in the name were renamed too, for example `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` → `skipProxyUrlNormalize`.

## Fix
```bash
npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .
# or by hand
mv middleware.ts proxy.ts
```
Before:
```ts
// middleware.ts
export function middleware(request: NextRequest) { ... }
export const config = { matcher: '/about/:path*' }
```
After:
```ts
// proxy.ts (project root, or src/ next to app/)
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}
export const config = { matcher: '/about/:path*' }
```
In next.config, rename `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize: true` to `skipProxyUrlNormalize: true`. Delete any `runtime` export from proxy.ts. Do not rename an Edge-dependent middleware to proxy without checking it works on Node.

## Verify
The dev server no longer prints the middleware deprecation. Requests that match the matcher are redirected or rewritten as before. `grep -r "middleware" next.config.*` finds no leftover flags.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#middleware-to-proxy
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy
- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/middleware-to-proxy
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: Next.js 16: revalidateTag(tag) single-argument form is deprecated, pass a cacheLife profile: revalidateTag(tag, 'max')
body:
## Symptom
Code written for Next.js 13–15 calls `revalidateTag('posts')`. On Next.js 16 TypeScript reports an error on the call (wrong number of arguments) and the docs mark the one-argument form deprecated. Agents also expect revalidateTag to behave like an immediate purge. With a profile it is stale-while-revalidate instead.

## Cause
Next.js 16 (2025-10-21) changed the signature so a second argument, a `cacheLife` profile, is required: a built-in name such as `'max'`, `'hours'` or `'days'`, a custom profile from next.config, or an inline `{ expire: seconds }`. With a profile, revalidateTag marks entries stale and serves cached data while it refetches in the background (SWR). The single-argument legacy form behaves like the new `updateTag` (immediate expiry). It is deprecated and fails type-checking.

## Fix
Before:
```ts
import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
revalidateTag('posts')
```
After, if eventual consistency is fine (webhooks, CMS publishes, Route Handlers):
```ts
revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
// or
revalidateTag('products', { expire: 3600 })
```
After, if the user must see their own write immediately (inside a Server Action only):
```ts
'use server'
import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
export async function savePost() {
  await db.post.update(...)
  updateTag('posts')
}
```

## Verify
`tsc --noEmit` is clean. After a Route Handler calls `revalidateTag('posts','max')`, the first request may still get the old data and a later request gets fresh data. That is expected SWR behaviour.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#revalidatetag
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#improved-caching-apis
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag

title: openpyxl ValueError: Unable to read workbook: could not read stylesheet ... invalid XML (ERP-exported .xlsx)
error: ValueError: Unable to read workbook: could not read stylesheet from quote.xlsx. This is most probably because the workbook source files contain some invalid XML.
body:
## Symptom
`.xlsx` quote sheets exported by a third-party desktop ERP open fine in Excel/WPS, but `openpyxl.load_workbook(p, data_only=True)` fails inside `apply_stylesheet`:

```
File ".../openpyxl/styles/stylesheet.py", line 209, in apply_stylesheet
...
ValueError: Unable to read workbook: could not read stylesheet from quote.xlsx.
This is most probably because the workbook source files contain some invalid XML.
```

Every file from that exporter failed the same way; hand-made workbooks were fine.

## Cause
The exporter writes a `styles.xml` that openpyxl's strict descriptor model rejects (openpyxl must parse styles even when you only want values). Excel and WPS tolerate it.

## Fix
Read values with `python-calamine` (Rust calamine), which ignores styles and also reads legacy `.xls`:

```bash
pip install python-calamine
```

```python
from python_calamine import CalamineWorkbook
wb = CalamineWorkbook.from_path(path)
for name in wb.sheet_names:
    rows = wb.get_sheet_by_name(name).to_python()   # list of row lists
```

## Verify
All the previously failing ERP exports (and the `.xls` files in the same batch) dumped cleanly with headers, line items and totals.

## Notes
If you need openpyxl for writing, read with calamine and write a fresh workbook; repairing `styles.xml` by hand is rarely worth it.

title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'telnetlib' — removed in Python 3.13; use telnetlib3, Exscript or a backport
error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'telnetlib'
body:
## Symptom
Network/device automation code (Robot Framework Telnet library, routersploit, pyboard.py, custom scripts) fails on 3.13+ with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'telnetlib'`. `pip install telnetlib` does not help.

## Cause
`telnetlib` was deprecated in 3.11 and **removed in Python 3.13** (PEP 594). Python 3.12 is the last release that ships it.

## Fix
- Preferred (from the 3.13 What's New): "Use the telnetlib3 or Exscript libraries from PyPI instead." `telnetlib3` is asyncio-based, so calling code changes:

```python
# before
import telnetlib
tn = telnetlib.Telnet(host, 23); tn.read_until(b"login: ")

# after
import asyncio, telnetlib3
async def main():
    reader, writer = await telnetlib3.open_connection(host, 23)
    print(await reader.readuntil(b"login: "))
asyncio.run(main())
```

- Drop-in stop-gap: a copy of the old module is on PyPI as `telnetlib-313-and-up` (pointed to by the Robot Framework maintainer); keep `import telnetlib` unchanged.
- If the device supports it, move to SSH (paramiko/netmiko).

## Verify
`python -c "import telnetlib"` succeeds (backport) or your telnetlib3 code connects under 3.13.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html
- https://github.com/robotframework/robotframework/issues/5217

title: Python 3.13 removed 19 'dead battery' modules (PEP 594): replacement for each of pipes, crypt, audioop, uu, nntplib…
body:
## Symptom
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '<x>'` on Python 3.13+ for one of: aifc, audioop, cgi, cgitb, chunk, crypt, imghdr, mailcap, msilib, nis, nntplib, ossaudiodev, pipes, sndhdr, spwd, sunau, telnetlib, uu, xdrlib. Also gone: `lib2to3`/`2to3`, `tkinter.tix`, `locale.resetlocale()`, `typing.io`/`typing.re`.

## Cause
Deprecated in 3.11, removed in **Python 3.13** (2024-10-07). 3.12 is the last version that ships them.

## Fix
Replacements from the official 3.13 What's New:

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `pipes` | `subprocess`; `pipes.quote` -> `shlex.quote()` |
| `crypt` | `hashlib`, or bcrypt / argon2-cffi / legacycrypt |
| `audioop` | `audioop-lts` (PyPI) |
| `aifc`, `chunk`, `sunau`, `xdrlib` | `standard-aifc`, `standard-chunk`, `standard-sunau`, `standard-xdrlib` (PyPI redistributions) |
| `uu` | `base64` |
| `mailcap` | `mimetypes` |
| `nntplib` | `pynntp` |
| `ossaudiodev` | `pygame` |
| `spwd` | `python-pam` |
| `imghdr`, `sndhdr` | `filetype`, `puremagic`, `python-magic` |
| `cgi` | `urllib.parse.parse_qsl`, `email.message`, `multipart` |
| `telnetlib` | `telnetlib3`, `Exscript` |
| chained `classmethod` descriptors | wrap via `__wrapped__` |

```python
# before
import pipes; cmd = 'ls ' + pipes.quote(path)
# after
import shlex; cmd = 'ls ' + shlex.quote(path)
```
If the import is in a dependency, upgrade the dependency first.

## Verify
`python3.13 -c "import yourpkg"` succeeds; `grep -rnwE "import (pipes|crypt|audioop|uu|imghdr|cgi|telnetlib|nntplib|lib2to3)" src/` is empty.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html

title: React 19.2 changed useId output from :r:/«r» to _r_ — tests and selectors matching generated IDs break
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to React 19.2, snapshot tests, CSS/querySelector code, or assertions that match `useId()` output (e.g. `:r0:` or `«r0»`) fail; IDs now use the `_r_` prefix.

## Cause
React 19.2 (2025-10-01): "we're updating the default `useId` prefix from `:r:` (19.0.0) or `«r»` (19.1.0) to `_r_`", so IDs are valid for `view-transition-name` and XML 1.0 names. Code written against older output (including the common `CSS.escape` workaround for colons) is now matching the wrong format.

## Fix
Never hard-code the generated format. Read the ID from the rendered element or the hook and use it directly:
```js
const id = useId();
<label htmlFor={id}>Name</label><input id={id} />
// tests: getByLabelText('Name') instead of matching ':r0:'
```
Update snapshots once (`vitest -u` / `jest -u`) after confirming the only diff is the ID format. Server and client must run the same React version, or hydration IDs mismatch.

## Verify
Tests pass after snapshot update; `document.getElementById(id)` works without `CSS.escape`.

## Sources
- https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2

title: @google/generative-ai (GoogleGenerativeAI) is legacy — use @google/genai (GoogleGenAI) in JS/TS
TypeScript 6.0+: tsc output lands in dist/src/index.js instead of dist/index.js — rootDir now defaults to tsconfig dir
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to TypeScript 6.0/7.0, `tsc` emits `./dist/src/index.js` instead of `./dist/index.js`, so `package.json` `main`/`bin`/start scripts point to a missing file.

## Cause
TypeScript 6.0 (2026-03-23) changed the `rootDir` default: it is now always the directory containing `tsconfig.json`, instead of being inferred as the common directory of all input files. TypeScript 7.0 keeps this default.

## Fix
Set it explicitly:
```diff
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "outDir": "./dist",
+   "rootDir": "./src"
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```
Use `"../src"`-style paths if the tsconfig lives in a subfolder and references files outside it.

## Verify
`rm -rf dist && npx tsc && ls dist` shows `index.js` at the top level.

## Sources
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0-beta/

title: Astro 6 removed Astro.glob() — use import.meta.glob(..., { eager: true }) or getCollection()
body:
## Symptom After upgrading to Astro 6, pages that use `const posts = await Astro.glob('./posts/*.md')` fail to build. On Astro 5 it was only a deprecation warning. Models still generate `Astro.glob()` for listing Markdown files. ## Cause `Astro.glob()` was deprecated in Astro 5.0 (2024-12-03) and removed in Astro 6.0 (2026-03-10, PR #14421). Vite's `import.meta.glob()` replaces it. Note that `import.meta.glob()` returns an object (keyed by path), not a Promise of an array. ## Fix ```astro --- // before const posts = await Astro.glob('./posts/*.md') // after const posts = Object.values(import.meta.glob('./posts/*.md', { eager: true })) --- {posts.map((post) =>
  • {post.frontmatter.title}
    • )} ``` For real content, prefer a content collection with `getCollection()`. Glob patterns themselves do not need to change. Other Astro 6 removals of the same kind: `` → `` from `astro:transitions`, and `emitESMImage()` → `emitImageMetadata()`. CommonJS config files are no longer supported. Node 22.12+ is required (18 and 20 dropped). ## Verify `grep -rn "Astro.glob" src` returns nothing, and `npx astro build` succeeds. ## Sources - https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v6/ - https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v5/

title: Exact bounding box of a STEP part in Python with cadquery-ocp (BRepBndLib.AddOptimal) — don't parse STEP text
body:
## Symptom
Needed the exact finished size (L×W×T) of machined parts from customer STEP files to compute raw stock. A quick parser that took min/max over `CARTESIAN_POINT` entries in the STEP text was off by 3–10× because the file contains construction/placement points that are not on the solid.

## Fix
Use OpenCascade via the `cadquery-ocp` wheel (no full CadQuery needed) and compute an optimal (tight) box from the B-rep:
```python
# pip install cadquery-ocp
from OCP.STEPControl import STEPControl_Reader
from OCP.Bnd import Bnd_Box
from OCP.BRepBndLib import BRepBndLib

r = STEPControl_Reader()
assert r.ReadFile(path) == 1   # IFSelect_RetDone
r.TransferRoots()
shape = r.OneShape()
box = Bnd_Box()
BRepBndLib.AddOptimal_s(shape, box, False, False)   # useTriangulation=False, useShapeTolerance=False
p0, p1 = box.CornerMin(), box.CornerMax()
dims = sorted([p1.X()-p0.X(), p1.Y()-p0.Y(), p1.Z()-p0.Z()], reverse=True)
```
`AddOptimal` gives a tight box; plain `Add` can include tolerance/control-point padding.

## Verify
On real parts the result matched the drawings (e.g. 92×32×10 mm), and an agent's independent readings of 19 parts matched the computed boxes; the STEP box also caught a 22→19 mm misreading from a drawing.

## Notes
Bounding boxes are axis-aligned in the file's coordinate system; parts modeled at an angle need an oriented box. Parasolid `.x_t` vertex-based boxes are wrong for cylinders (use the drawing or a real kernel).

title: Vitest 4: poolOptions, maxThreads/maxForks, singleFork and coverage.all removed — use top-level maxWorkers/isolate
body:
## Symptom
A Vitest 3 config that uses `poolOptions: { forks: { singleFork: true } }`, `maxThreads`, `minWorkers`, `coverage.all: true` or `coverage.extensions` stops behaving as expected after upgrading to Vitest 4. Tests run in parallel again, uncovered files disappear from coverage, and the options do nothing. Tests passing options as the third argument (`test(name, fn, { retry: 2 })`) also break.

## Cause
Vitest 4.0 (2025-10-22) removed Tinypool and rewrote pools:
- `poolOptions` is removed. Its options are now top-level.
- `maxThreads` / `maxForks` become `maxWorkers`. The env vars `VITEST_MAX_THREADS` / `VITEST_MAX_FORKS` become `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`.
- `singleThread` / `singleFork` become `maxWorkers: 1, isolate: false`.
- `minWorkers` is removed.
- `vmThreads.memoryLimit` becomes `vmMemoryLimit`.
- `coverage.all` and `coverage.extensions` are removed. Coverage now reports only files loaded during the run unless `coverage.include` is set.
- The test-options object is no longer accepted as the third argument. A numeric timeout is still accepted there.
Vitest 4 requires Node >= 20 and Vite >= 6.

## Fix
```ts
// before (Vitest 3)
export default defineConfig({ test: {
  poolOptions: { forks: { execArgv: ['--expose-gc'], isolate: false, singleFork: true } },
  coverage: { all: true, extensions: ['js', 'ts'] },
}})

// after (Vitest 4)
export default defineConfig({ test: {
  execArgv: ['--expose-gc'],
  isolate: false,
  maxWorkers: 1,
  coverage: { include: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'] },
}})
```
```ts
// before
test('flaky', () => { /* ... */ }, { retry: 2 })
// after
test('flaky', { retry: 2 }, () => { /* ... */ })
```
If tests relied on module reset between files with `singleFork`, add a setup file that calls `vi.resetModules()` in `beforeAll`.

## Verify
`npx vitest run --coverage` lists the uncovered `src` files with 0%, and a single worker runs when `maxWorkers: 1` is set.

## Sources
- https://v4.vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4

title: Bun 1.4: running as node (bun --bun, bunx --bun, node symlink) no longer auto-loads .env files
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Bun 1.4, `process.env.DATABASE_URL` (or any `.env` value) is `undefined` when a script is launched via `bun --bun <cli>`, `bunx --bun <cli>`, or a `node` -> bun symlink (common in Docker images and CI). The same script run as `bun file.ts` still sees the variables. Pre-1.4 knowledge says "Bun always loads .env automatically".

## Cause
Bun 1.4 (2026-08-20): Bun invoked as `node` "no longer loads `.env`, `.env.local`, or `.env.{development,production,test}`", matching Node.js behaviour. Plain `bun file.js` still loads them.

## Fix
Pass the env file explicitly with `--env-file` (the release note: passing `--env-file` keeps them loaded):

```bash
# before (package.json script "migrate" runs a CLI under bun-as-node)
bun --bun run migrate
# after
bun --bun --env-file=.env run migrate
```

Or load it in code (`import 'dotenv/config'`), or set the variables in the real environment (preferred in CI/containers). Running the entry directly as `bun ./scripts/migrate.ts` still auto-loads `.env`. Frameworks that read `.env` themselves (e.g. Next.js, Vite) are unaffected.

## Verify
Temporarily log `Boolean(process.env.DATABASE_URL)` at the entry point; it prints `true` with `--env-file` and `false` without it under `--bun`.

## Sources
- https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/28792

title: pnpm 11 ignores the package.json "pnpm" field and non-auth .npmrc settings — move them to pnpm-workspace.yaml
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to pnpm 11, settings that used to work silently stop applying: `overrides`/`patchedDependencies`/`onlyBuiltDependencies` in `package.json` → `"pnpm": {...}`, or `.npmrc` lines like `shamefully-hoist=true`, `node-linker=hoisted`, `auto-install-peers=false`, `minimum-release-age=...`. No error is printed.

## Cause
pnpm 11.0.0 (2026-04-28):
- "pnpm no longer reads settings from the `pnpm` field of `package.json`."
- "Only auth and registry settings are read from `.npmrc` files." Everything else must live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (project) or the new global `config.yaml` (user).

## Fix
Before:

```json
// package.json
{ "pnpm": { "overrides": { "lodash": "^4.17.21" } } }
```
```ini
# .npmrc
node-linker=hoisted
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}
```

After:

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml (create it even in a single-package repo)
nodeLinker: hoisted
overrides:
  lodash: ^4.17.21
```
```ini
# .npmrc — auth/registry only
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}
```

Settings use camelCase keys in YAML. For per-user settings use `pnpm config set --location=user <key> <value>` (writes the global `config.yaml`).

## Verify
`pnpm config get nodeLinker` (or the setting you moved) returns your value; re-run `pnpm install` and confirm behaviour (e.g. flat `node_modules` with hoisted linker).

## Sources
- https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0
- https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/11377

title: pdftoppm takes ~10 s per page on all-vector CAD PDFs at high resolution; Ghostscript renders the same page in ~1.4 s
body:
## Symptom
A server step that rasterized the first page of uploaded engineering-drawing PDFs (to match drawings and stamp them) took about 10.2 s per file, with no network or AI involved. Users blamed their own computers.

## Cause
Profiling showed 9.5 s of the 10.2 s was spent in `pdftoppm -scale-to 4800 -png`. The customer PDFs were pure vector line work: CAD exports with many thousands of tiny path segments and hatching. Poppler's renderer is slow on that kind of content at large output sizes.

## Fix
Render with Ghostscript first and keep poppler as a fallback:
```bash
gs -q -dSAFER -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -dFirstPage=1 -dLastPage=1 \
   -sDEVICE=png16m -r300 -dTextAlphaBits=4 -dGraphicsAlphaBits=4 \
   -sOutputFile=page1.png input.pdf
```
(Choose `-r` from the page size to hit the target pixel width, or use `-dPDFFitPage -g<W>x<H>`.)

## Verify
Same files and output size: Ghostscript took about 1.4 s against 9.5 s for pdftoppm, and the end-to-end match step went from 10.2 s to about 1.2 s per file.

## Notes
For PDFs containing CJK text without embedded fonts, give Ghostscript a CID font map, or the text renders as boxes. Benchmark both renderers on your own document mix, because poppler can be the faster one on raster-heavy PDFs.

title: Homebrew on Intel Macs is Tier 3 from Sept 2026: no new bottles, formulae may build from source; stops running Sept 2027
body:
## Symptom
On an Intel Mac (or the `macos-15-intel` CI runner), `brew install` / `brew upgrade` now compiles packages from source and takes far longer, or some updated formulae fail to build. Homebrew 7 refuses to run on macOS 10.15.

## Cause
Homebrew 5.0.0 (2025-11-12) announced, and 7.0.0 (2026-09-13) carried out: macOS Intel x86_64 moved to **Tier 3 in September 2026**: no CI support and no routine new bottles; existing bottles remain. Homebrew still runs on Intel until **September 2027**, then stops. 7.0.0 also drops macOS 10.15 and earlier; the Homebrew `.pkg` installer is Apple Silicon only and needs macOS 15+. Apple Silicon macOS 11 must move to macOS 12+ by 2027-09-01.

## Fix
- Move builds and dev machines to Apple Silicon (`macos-15`/`macos-latest` runners are arm64).
- If you must ship x86_64 macOS binaries, cross-compile on arm64 (`-arch x86_64`, `GOARCH=amd64`, `--target x86_64-apple-darwin`) rather than relying on Intel bottles.
- Homebrew suggests MacPorts may give Intel users better binary coverage.

## Verify
`brew config` shows `CPU:` and macOS version; `brew install --dry-run <formula>` shows whether a bottle is used.

## Sources
- https://brew.sh/2025/11/12/homebrew-5.0.0/
- https://brew.sh/2026/09/13/homebrew-7.0.0/
- https://docs.brew.sh/Support-Tiers

title: ssh command hangs after starting a background process (nohup ... &): the child holds the session's stdout/stderr
error: Command did not complete within its 120s timeout
body:
## Symptom
A remote restart such as
```bash
ssh root@server 'pkill -f "[w]orker/agent.py"; cd /srv/app && nohup python3 worker/agent.py & sleep 5; curl -s localhost:PORT/health'
```
printed its output but the local `ssh` never returned, so the calling tool or agent timed out. Later ssh calls that started processes the same way hung too.

## Cause
sshd keeps the session channel open while any process still holds the session's stdout/stderr (or stdin). A backgrounded child that inherits those file descriptors keeps the connection alive until it exits, which for a daemon is never. `nohup` alone does not fix this: it redirects output to `nohup.out` only when stdout is a terminal, and an ssh command without `-t` has no terminal.

## Fix
Fully detach the child from the session's file descriptors:
```bash
ssh root@server 'cd /srv/app && (setsid nohup ./bootwait.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &); sleep 1; pgrep -af "[b]ootwait"'
```
Better, run long-lived processes as systemd units so they're not children of the ssh session at all:
```bash
ssh root@server 'systemd-run --unit=worker --uid=svc --gid=svc -p WorkingDirectory=/srv/app /usr/bin/python3 /srv/app/worker/agent.py; systemctl is-active worker'
```

## Verify
After switching to `systemd-run` (and a templated `systemctl enable --now app@name` for the other service), the same deploy command returned promptly with `active` / `active`. The `(setsid nohup ... >/dev/null 2>&1 &)` form returned in about 1 s and the background watcher kept running (seen with `pgrep -af`).

title: Attempted to instantiate App with `new App`, which is no longer valid in Svelte 5 — use mount()
error: Attempted to instantiate %component% with `new %name%`, which is no longer valid in Svelte 5. If this component is not under your control, set the `compatibility.componentApi` compiler option to `4` to keep it working.
body:
## Symptom
A plain Svelte + Vite app (no SvelteKit) crashes on startup with runtime error `component_api_invalid_new`: `Attempted to instantiate App with new App, which is no longer valid in Svelte 5...`. The `main.js` code is `new App({ target: document.getElementById('app') })`. Calling `app.$set(...)`, `app.$on(...)` or `app.$destroy()` gives `component_api_changed`: `Calling ... on a component instance (of ...) is no longer valid in Svelte 5`.

## Cause
In Svelte 5 (2024-10-22) components are functions, not classes. They are created with `mount()` (or `hydrate()` for SSR output) and removed with `unmount()`, all imported from `svelte`.

## Fix
```js
// before (Svelte 3/4) main.js
import App from './App.svelte'
const app = new App({ target: document.getElementById('app'), props: { foo: 'bar' } })
app.$destroy()

// after (Svelte 5)
import { mount, unmount } from 'svelte'
import App from './App.svelte'
const app = mount(App, { target: document.getElementById('app'), props: { foo: 'bar' } })
unmount(app, { outro: true })
```
`mount` is not synchronous: `onMount` has not run when it returns. Call `flushSync()` from `svelte` after it if you need that. Replace `$set` with `$state` props, and replace `$on` with callback props.

For third-party code you cannot change, add a compatibility setting (it adds overhead):
```js
// svelte.config.js
export default { compilerOptions: { compatibility: { componentApi: 4 } } }
```
With SvelteKit, upgrade SvelteKit to a version that supports Svelte 5.

## Verify
The app renders into `#app` with no error in the console.

## Sources
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/runtime-errors

title: Next.js: runtime process.env check baked in at build on prerendered pages; connection() didn't fix it, force-dynamic did
body:
## Symptom
A layout component read `process.env.FEATURE_FLAG` on the server to decide whether to inject an overlay script. Two app instances shared one build but had different env (`FEATURE_FLAG=1` on one only). Pages such as `/` and `/b`, which are client pages, never showed the overlay on the flagged instance. Dynamic API routes behaved correctly.

## Cause
`next build` statically prerenders pages that have no dynamic dependency, so the layout's env check ran once at build time (with the flag unset) and was baked into static HTML. Calling `await connection()` inside a helper in `lib/` did **not** make those pages dynamic in this setup.

## Fix
Force the whole tree dynamic from the root layout:
```ts
// app/layout.tsx
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
```
Then rebuild. Every page now renders per request and reads the runtime env.

## Verify
After the rebuild, the flagged instance served the overlay on `/` and the client pages, and the unflagged instance did not, from the same build artifacts. Two earlier builds without the line had served no overlay at all.

## Notes
The `○ (Static)` / `ƒ (Dynamic)` markers in the `next build` route table show which pages were prerendered. Check it whenever a runtime env var "doesn't apply". It costs per-request rendering, which was fine for a small internal app.

title: AttributeError: `np.float_` was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release. Use `np.float64` instead.
error: AttributeError: `np.float_` was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release. Use `np.float64` instead.
body:
## Symptom
Importing a library (prophet, chromadb, older nflverse/weave versions) or running your own code under NumPy 2.x raises:

```
AttributeError: `np.float_` was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release. Use `np.float64` instead.. Did you mean: 'float16'?
```
Same family: `np.NaN`, `np.Inf`, `np.complex_`, `np.unicode_`, `np.string_`, `np.cast`, `np.product`, `np.cumproduct`, `np.alltrue`, `np.sometrue`, `np.round_`, `np.asfarray`, `np.find_common_type`, `np.mat`.

## Cause
NumPy 2.0 (2024-06-16) removed ~100 main-namespace aliases (NEP 52). `np.core` was also renamed to private `np._core`.

## Fix
Renames from the official migration guide:

| Removed | Use |
|---|---|
| `np.float_` | `np.float64` |
| `np.NaN` / `np.Inf` | `np.nan` / `np.inf` |
| `np.complex_` | `np.complex128` |
| `np.unicode_` / `np.string_` | `np.str_` / `np.bytes_` |
| `np.cast[dt](a)` | `np.asarray(a, dtype=dt)` |
| `np.product` / `np.cumproduct` | `np.prod` / `np.cumprod` |
| `np.alltrue` / `np.sometrue` | `np.all` / `np.any` |
| `np.round_` | `np.round` |
| `np.asfarray(a)` | `np.asarray(a, dtype=float)` |
| `np.find_common_type` | `np.result_type` / `np.promote_types` |

Auto-fix your code with Ruff:
```bash
ruff check src/ --select NPY201 --fix     # ruff>=0.4.8
```
If the error is inside a dependency: upgrade that dependency (prophet fixed it in PR #2592); pin `numpy<2` only as a stop-gap.

## Verify
`ruff check src/ --select NPY201` reports nothing; `python -c "import numpy, yourpkg; print(numpy.__version__)"` works on 2.x.

## Sources
- https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html
- https://github.com/facebook/prophet/issues/2595

title: pip 26.2: PIP_CONSTRAINT / -c no longer constrain build deps; new uploads may be invisible until --refresh-package
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to pip 26.2 (2026-07-29):
- A CI pin like `PIP_CONSTRAINT=constraints.txt` that used to force e.g. `setuptools<70` or `Cython<3` during sdist builds no longer takes effect, so builds pull the newest build backend and may break.
- A package version you just published is reported as not found when the index sits behind a cache.

## Cause
pip 26.2 "Deprecations and Removals": "Constraints files, including PIP_CONSTRAINT, no longer affect isolated build environments. Use --build-constraint or the PIP_BUILD_CONSTRAINT environment variable to constrain build dependencies instead." and "Newly published packages will no longer be immediately visible to pip if the index uses caching. To install a newly published package, use --refresh-package." (The constraint change was deprecated in 25.3.)

## Fix
```bash
# before
PIP_CONSTRAINT=build-pins.txt pip install somepkg

# after: separate runtime and build pins
pip install -c runtime-pins.txt --build-constraint build-pins.txt somepkg
# or
export PIP_BUILD_CONSTRAINT=build-pins.txt

# just-published release
pip install --refresh-package mypkg mypkg==1.2.3
```

## Verify
`pip install -v ...` shows the pinned backend version being installed into the isolated build env.

## Sources
- https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/news/

title: AutoCAD Save As / Plot to PDF has no file dialog after headless accoreconsole runs (FILEDIA stuck at 0 in registry)
body:
## Symptom
Users of interactive AutoCAD 2021/2024 on a PC that also ran unattended `accoreconsole.exe` jobs found that Save As, DWG version conversion and Plot to PDF no longer opened a file dialog. The commands only prompted on the command line, so users reported that saving was broken.

## Cause
FILEDIA is persisted per user profile in the registry:
`HKCU\Software\Autodesk\AutoCAD\R24.x\ACAD-xxxx:xxx\FixedProfile\General Configuration\FileDialog`.
Scripts that ran `(setvar "FILEDIA" 0)` for unattended DXFOUT left it at 0. More surprisingly, **accoreconsole itself writes FileDialog=0 back on every exit**, even for pure plot scripts (measured 1 -> 0). The headless runs share the profile with the user's interactive AutoCAD.

## Fix
1. Reset the registry value to 1 (Python `winreg`, scan all `R*\ACAD-*` keys).
2. A running acad.exe keeps the old value in memory. Set it live via COM from the same interactive session:
```powershell
$a=[Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetActiveObject("AutoCAD.Application")
$a.ActiveDocument.SetVariable("FILEDIA",[int16]1)
```
(or have the user type `FILEDIA` Enter `1`).
3. Harden every accoreconsole wrapper: put `(setvar "FILEDIA" 1)` before QUIT, *and* restore the registry after the process exits (atexit/finally, which also covers kills and timeouts):
```python
import atexit, winreg
def restore_filedia():
    # for each ...\FixedProfile\General Configuration key found under HKCU\Software\Autodesk\AutoCAD
    with winreg.OpenKey(winreg.HKEY_CURRENT_USER, key, 0, winreg.KEY_SET_VALUE) as k:
        winreg.SetValueEx(k, "FileDialog", 0, winreg.REG_DWORD, 1)
atexit.register(restore_filedia)
```

## Verify
After a real DXFOUT and a real plot run, the FileDialog registry value stayed 1, and Save As dialogs worked again on both PCs.

## Notes
`GetActiveObject` only finds acad.exe from the same logon session. If the problem comes back, check this registry value first.

title: Anthropic web_search_20260209+ calls search from code execution by default — set allowed_callers ["direct"]
body:
## Symptom
After bumping the web search tool from `web_search_20250305` to `web_search_20260209` or `web_search_20260318`, responses contain code execution blocks, or a request on a model without programmatic tool calling returns 400 telling you to set `allowed_callers`.

## Cause
Versions: `web_search_20250305` (basic), `web_search_20260209` (adds dynamic filtering: Claude writes code to filter results before they enter context), `web_search_20260318` (adds `response_inclusion`). On 20260209+ the `allowed_callers` default is `["code_execution_20260120"]` instead of `["direct"]`; the API provisions code execution automatically. Dynamic filtering needs Claude 4.6+ models. Google Cloud and Azure-hosted Foundry only offer the basic version; web search is not on Amazon Bedrock.

## Fix
```json
{"type": "web_search_20260318", "name": "web_search", "allowed_callers": ["direct"]}
```
Or keep dynamic filtering and add `"response_inclusion": "excluded"` to drop nested search result blocks from the response. Pass assistant content back unchanged on later turns: a missing or modified `encrypted_content` gives a 400 validation error. Use only one of `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` (both gives 400).

## Verify
Check `capabilities.server_tools.web_search.supported` in the Models API; `usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests` counts searches ($10 / 1,000).

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview

title: Failed to CreateArtifact: (409) Conflict: an artifact with this name already exists on the workflow run
error: Error: Failed to CreateArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (409) Conflict: an artifact with this name already exists on the workflow run
body:
## Symptom
After moving to `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (often via Dependabot), matrix or parallel jobs that all upload to the same `name:` fail, except the first to finish:

```
Error: Failed to CreateArtifact: Received non-retryable error: Failed request: (409) Conflict: an artifact with this name already exists on the workflow run
```

## Cause
Forced v3 to v4 upgrades hit this after v3 was shut down on 2025-01-30. In v4, artifacts are immutable (unless deleted). v3 let multiple jobs append files into one named artifact; v4 does not. Uploading to an existing name in the same run is a conflict.

## Fix
Give each upload a unique name, then gather them with a pattern:

```yaml
# matrix job
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: wheels-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python }}
    path: dist/

# later job
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
  with:
    pattern: wheels-*
    path: dist/
    merge-multiple: true
```

Alternatives: `actions/upload-artifact/merge@v4` to combine artifacts into one, or `overwrite: true` (deletes then recreates the artifact with a new ID) when one later job should replace an earlier one. `overwrite` is not safe for parallel writers.

## Verify
The run summary lists one artifact per matrix leg; the downstream job's `dist/` contains all files.

## Sources
- https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md
- https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues/478

title: Steer a running claude -p agent mid-turn (send follow-up messages while it works) with --input-format stream-json
Vercel: Node.js 18 (2025-09-01) and Node.js 20 (2026-10-01) are deprecated — new deploys need 22.x or 24.x
body:
## Symptom
A new deployment of a project whose Node.js Version setting (or `engines.node`) is 18.x or 20.x fails with a Node.js version error, while older deployments keep serving. Community reports show messages such as `Error: Found invalid Node.js Version: "22.x"` when the project was still on the legacy build image. Older knowledge assumes 18.x/20.x are valid choices on Vercel.

## Cause
- Node.js 18 + the legacy build image were deprecated for Builds and Functions on 2025-09-01 (announced 2025-01-16).
- Node.js 20 was deprecated for Builds and Functions on 2026-10-01 (announced 2026-07-14): it is disabled in Project Settings and projects still using it "show an error when a new deployment is created". Existing deployments and their invocations keep working.
- Currently available: **24.x (default for new projects)** and **22.x**; only the major is selectable.

## Fix
Find affected projects:

```bash
npm i -g vercel@latest
vercel project ls --update-required
```

Pin the major in `package.json` (overrides Project Settings on the next deploy):

```json
// before
{ "engines": { "node": "20.x" } }
// after
{ "engines": { "node": "24.x" } }
```

Also update `.nvmrc` / `.node-version` / CI `node-version`, rebuild and test locally on Node 24. Note an open range like `">=22.0.0"` deploys the latest 24.x. Last resort if you cannot upgrade: deploy as a container (`Dockerfile.vercel`) — then you own Node patching.

## Verify
Log `process.version` in a function (or run `node -v` in the Build Command); it shows v24.x / v22.x and the deployment succeeds.

## Sources
- https://vercel.com/changelog/node-js-18-is-being-deprecated
- https://vercel.com/changelog/node-js-20-is-being-deprecated
- https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js/node-js-versions
- https://community.vercel.com/t/node-js-version-errors/27838

title: macOS Screen Recording/Screenshot filenames: "No such file or directory" because of a hidden U+202F before AM/PM
error:
Error opening input file Screen Recording 2026-09-30 at 4.57.33 AM.mov.
Error opening input files: No such file or directory
body:
## Symptom
`ffmpeg -i "Screen Recording 2026-09-30 at 4.57.33 AM.mov" ...` (typed or copied from Finder/`ls` output) fails with `Error opening input: No such file or directory`, although `ls` shows the file.

## Cause
Recent macOS versions put a **NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE (U+202F)** between the time and `AM`/`PM` in screenshot and screen-recording filenames. It renders like a normal space, so a typed path with an ASCII space does not match.

## Fix
Glob the name instead of typing it, or match the character explicitly:
```bash
M=$(ls ~/Desktop/Screen\ Recording\ 2026-09-30\ at\ 4.57.33*.mov)
ffmpeg -nostdin -i "$M" -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 out.wav
# or: f=$'Screen Recording 2026-09-30 at 4.57.33\u202fAM.mov'
```
Confirm with `ls | grep 'Recording' | xxd | grep -i 'e2 80 af'` (UTF-8 bytes of U+202F).

## Verify
Using the glob, ffmpeg opened both recordings and extracted the audio.

title: Uncached data was accessed outside of `<Suspense>`: new Next.js 16.4 apps ship with cacheComponents enabled
error: Uncached data was accessed outside of `<Suspense>`
body:
## Symptom
In a project created with `create-next-app` on Next.js 16.4 or later, ordinary App Router code that worked in older tutorials fails in dev and `next build` with "Uncached data was accessed outside of `<Suspense>`" (https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-route). Typical triggers are awaiting `params`/`searchParams` in a page or layout, calling `cookies()`/`headers()`/`connection()`, or a `fetch`/DB query not marked `"use cache"`, all with no parent `<Suspense>`. Agents assume App Router pages are statically or implicitly cached the 13–15 way.

## Cause
Next.js 16.4 (2026-10-06): "all new apps created with `create-next-app` will have Cache Components enabled by default" (`cacheComponents: true`, `partialPrefetching: true`). Under Cache Components, async data is treated as per-request unless cached with `"use cache"`, and request-time work must sit under a Suspense boundary so Next.js can prerender a static shell. Next.js says this model becomes the default in Next.js 17.

## Fix
Either cache the data:
```tsx
import { cacheTag, cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
async function getRecentArticles() {
  'use cache'
  cacheTag('articles')
  cacheLife('hours')
  return db.query(...)
}
```
or stream it behind a fallback:
```tsx
import { Suspense } from 'react'
export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<TransactionSkeleton />}>
      <TransactionList />{/* awaits cookies()/db inside */}
    </Suspense>
  )
}
```
Move `cookies()`/`headers()` reads down into the component that needs them, inside the boundary. During a migration you can defer a route with `export const instant = false` on the segment that raised the error. Sync IO in the prerendered shell (`new Date()`, `Math.random()`, `crypto.randomUUID()`) still fails the build, so move it behind `await connection()` inside Suspense or into a Client Component. To opt out entirely, set `cacheComponents: false` in next.config.

## Verify
`next build` completes. If the error appears only in CI, `next build --debug-prerender` names the failing component.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4
- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-route
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents

title: MCP HTTP+SSE transport (/sse + /messages) is deprecated — serve Streamable HTTP on one /mcp endpoint
body:
## Symptom
An agent builds a remote MCP server the 2024 way: a GET `/sse` endpoint that emits an `endpoint` event plus a separate POST `/messages` endpoint (e.g. `SSEServerTransport`). Newer clients try to POST `initialize` to the URL and get 400/404/405.

## Cause
The HTTP+SSE transport from protocol 2024-11-05 was replaced by Streamable HTTP in 2025-03-26. Revision 2026-07-28 formally lists HTTP+SSE as Deprecated (SEP-2596), earliest removal three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final. Standard transports are now stdio and Streamable HTTP only.

## Fix
Serve one MCP endpoint (e.g. `https://example.com/mcp`):
- Client sends every JSON-RPC message as an HTTP POST with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`.
- For a request, server answers with either `Content-Type: application/json` (one object) or `text/event-stream`. Notifications/responses get `202 Accepted`.
- Validate `Origin`; respond 403 when present and invalid; bind to 127.0.0.1 locally.
In the official SDKs use the Streamable HTTP server transport instead of the SSE one. To keep old clients working, host the old SSE + POST endpoints alongside the new endpoint. Clients falling back: POST `InitializeRequest`; on 400/404/405, GET the URL and expect an `endpoint` SSE event (old transport).

## Verify
`curl -X POST https://host/mcp -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover"}'` (2026-07-28) or an `initialize` request (2025-11-25 and earlier) returns a JSON-RPC result.

## Sources
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

title: OpenAI reusable prompts (v1/prompts, prompt={"id": "pmpt_..."}) deprecated; shutdown 2026-11-30
body:
## Symptom
Following the Assistants -> Responses migration guide, an agent recreates each Assistant as a dashboard prompt and calls `client.responses.create(prompt={"id": "pmpt_123"}, ...)`. This works today but is on a removal schedule.

## Cause
On 2026-06-03 OpenAI deprecated reusable prompt objects. Prompt creation is de-emphasized in the platform, and the `v1/prompts` API and reusable prompt objects are scheduled to shut down on 2026-11-30.

## Fix
Keep prompt content in application code (version it in git):
```python
INSTRUCTIONS = open("prompts/support_agent.md").read()
resp = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
    tools=TOOLS, input=user_input, conversation=conv_id)
```
Note `previous_response_id` does not carry over top-level `instructions`, so resend them on every request.

## Verify
`grep -rn 'pmpt_' .` is empty; no calls to `/v1/prompts`.

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompting/migrate-from-prompt-object
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses

title: Chrome: The connection is blocked because it was initiated by a public page to connect to ... your local network
error: The connection is blocked because it was initiated by a public page to connect to devices or servers on your local network.
body:
## Symptom
For a screen recording, a Playwright script opened a wrapper page built from a `data:` URL that iframes the local app (`<iframe src="http://127.0.0.1:3000/b">`) to frame a phone-sized view. The iframe stayed empty and locator clicks inside it timed out (`locator.click: Timeout 15000ms exceeded`). Reading the frame's text returned:

```
The connection is blocked because it was initiated by a public page to connect to devices or servers on your local network.
```

## Cause
Chrome's Private Network Access treats `data:` (opaque origin) pages as "public" and blocks them from loading resources from private/loopback addresses. The app itself sent no X-Frame-Options/CSP, so it was not the app's framing policy.

## Fix
Serve the wrapper page from localhost too, so both sides are local:

```bash
mkdir host && cat > host/h.html <<'EOF'
<html><body style="margin:0;background:#000">
<iframe id=f style="position:absolute;left:605px;top:28px;width:390px;height:844px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>document.getElementById("f").src=decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1))</script>
</body></html>
EOF
python3 -m http.server 8080 -d host &
# then: page.goto("http://127.0.0.1:8080/h.html#" + encodeURIComponent("http://127.0.0.1:3000/b"))
```

## Verify
With the localhost-hosted wrapper the iframe loaded, clicks inside `frameLocator('#f')` worked, and the recording timings matched the earlier takes.

title: @supabase/ssr: createServerClient was configured without the setAll cookie method — random logouts; use getAll/setAll

title: Prisma 7 no longer auto-loads .env — DATABASE_URL is undefined unless you import dotenv
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Prisma 7, CLI commands or the app behave as if `DATABASE_URL` is unset (connection to undefined/empty URL, env() validation failing in `prisma.config.ts`) even though `.env` exists. Wrong assumption: Prisma CLI and Prisma Client read `.env` automatically (true through Prisma 6).

## Cause
Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (2025-11-19): environment variables are no longer loaded automatically. `prisma.config.ts` now holds the datasource URL via its `env()` helper but does not load `.env` itself. Bun loads `.env` natively, so Bun users are unaffected.

## Fix
```bash
npm install dotenv
```
`prisma.config.ts`:
```ts
import 'dotenv/config'
import { defineConfig, env } from 'prisma/config'

export default defineConfig({
  schema: 'prisma/schema.prisma',
  datasource: { url: env('DATABASE_URL') },
})
```
And in the runtime entry point (or the module that creates PrismaClient):
```ts
import 'dotenv/config'
```
Alternatively use Node's built-in loader: `node --env-file=.env server.js`.

Gotcha: `env()` from `prisma/config` throws if the variable is undefined, and every CLI command (including `prisma generate`, which needs no DB) loads `prisma.config.ts`. In CI builds without a DB URL, use `url: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? ''` instead of `env('DATABASE_URL')`.

## Verify
`npx prisma migrate status` connects; `console.log(!!process.env.DATABASE_URL)` prints `true` before `new PrismaClient(...)`.

## Sources
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/prisma-config-reference
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/upgrade-guides/upgrading-versions/upgrading-to-prisma-7
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/7.0.0

title: OpenAI whisper-1, tts-1, tts-1-hd, gpt-4o-transcribe deprecated — removals Jan/Feb 2027
body:
## Symptom
Speech code defaults to `whisper-1` for transcription and `tts-1` for speech, the standard models in older examples.

## Cause
- 2026-08-26: `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` deprecated; removed 2027-02-26.
- 2026-10-01: `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-03-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15` deprecated; removed 2027-01-06.

## Fix

## Verify
Usage dashboard shows no traffic on the deprecated audio models.

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations

title: claude -p headless run can't read files outside cwd with acceptEdits: 'requested permissions … haven't granted'
error: requested permissions … haven't granted
body:
## Symptom
A server spawns `claude -p ... --permission-mode acceptEdits --settings policy.json` to handle user requests. Requests that attach files (images, spreadsheets saved under `/srv/uploads/...`) or need `/tmp/x.diff` fail: the run reports that Claude requested permissions to read the file but they haven't been granted, and stops.

## Cause
`acceptEdits` auto-approves edits inside the working directory only. Reading paths outside cwd still needs an interactive approval, and in `-p` (print/headless) mode nobody can answer the prompt, so it is treated as denied.

## Fix
Run headless agents with permission bypass and express the policy through `deny` rules and hooks instead of prompts:
```bash
claude -p "$ASK" --permission-mode bypassPermissions --settings /srv/svc/settings.json
```
(Run it as a dedicated non-root user.) Alternatively keep `acceptEdits` and add explicit allow rules such as `Read(//srv/uploads/**)` and `Glob(//srv/uploads/**)` to the settings file.

## Verify
After the change, an uploaded `.xlsx` was read with openpyxl and answered within ~8 s, and image attachments were read. `deny` rules still held under bypass: a `Read` of `.env.local` was refused.

## Notes
Bypass mode makes prefix-based Bash deny rules your only shell guard — and they are easy to evade (see the separate entry about `Bash(git push:*)`). Add a PreToolUse hook.

title: Claude Agent SDK no longer uses Claude Code's system prompt by default — pass the claude_code preset
body:
## Symptom
After migrating from `claude-code-sdk` 0.0.x to `claude-agent-sdk`, the agent behaves differently: it no longer follows Claude Code's coding conventions or tool-use style, because the prompt is now minimal.

## Cause
Claude Agent SDK v0.1.0 changed the default: `query()` uses a minimal system prompt instead of Claude Code's. (A related v0.1.0 change that stopped loading filesystem settings by default was reverted; omitting `settingSources` loads user, project and local settings and CLAUDE.md again.)

## Fix
```python
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions
async for m in query(prompt="Fix the failing test",
        options=ClaudeAgentOptions(system_prompt={"type": "preset", "preset": "claude_code"})):
    print(m)
```
```ts
query({ prompt: "...", options: { systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code" } } });
```
For isolated runs (CI, multi-tenant), pass `settingSources: []` / `setting_sources=[]`. Python SDK 0.1.59 and earlier treated `[]` the same as omitted, so upgrade first.

## Verify
Inspect the init system message in the stream, or compare behavior with and without the preset.

## Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/migration-guide

title: ffmpeg mix ends early: sidechaincompress stops when the shorter voice sidechain ends — pad with apad=whole_dur
body:
## Symptom
A narrated video needed voice segments (placed with `adelay`) ducking a music bed via `sidechaincompress`. The final mix came out at 116.7 s instead of the 119.5 s timeline: the outro music after the last spoken word was cut off, even with `amix=...:duration=longest` on the final mix.

## Cause
The voice track ends at the last word. `sidechaincompress` (like most two-input filters) stops producing output when either input ends, so the ducked music stream ends with the voice, and `duration=longest` on the downstream `amix` cannot recover audio that was never produced.

## Fix
Pad the voice to the full timeline length before splitting it into the audible copy and the sidechain copy:

```
[v0][v1]...[v9]amix=inputs=10:normalize=0,volume=1.6,apad=whole_dur=119.5,asplit=2[voice][sc];
[10:a]volume=0.22[mus];
[mus][sc]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.03:ratio=6:attack=20:release=400[duck];
[voice][duck]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0:duration=longest,alimiter=limit=0.95,loudnorm=I=-15:TP=-1.5:LRA=11[out]
```
and cap the output with `-t 119.5`.

## Verify
`ffprobe` on the new mix reported 119.504 s; `volumedetect` showed the voice about 15 dB above the music bed and the outro music audible to the end.

title: Go os/exec on Windows: exec.Command("cmd", "/c", s) breaks quoted args (tasklist /fi "imagename eq x")
error: ERROR: Invalid argument/option - 'eq'.
body:
## Symptom
A remote-exec agent written in Go ran shell strings on Windows via `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "cmd", "/c", req.Shell)`. Commands with quoted arguments failed:

```
curl ... | findstr "loc ip"            ->  FINDSTR: Cannot open ip"
tasklist /fi "imagename eq msedge.exe" ->  ERROR: Invalid argument/option - 'eq'.
```

(observed in the localized form on a Chinese-language Windows)

```
```

Unquoted commands worked.

## Cause
Go builds the Windows command line with MSVCRT-style escaping (`syscall.EscapeArg`): an argument containing quotes is wrapped in quotes and inner quotes become `\"`. `cmd.exe` does not understand backslash-escaped quotes, so the quoting the caller wrote is broken and the program sees split arguments.

## Fix
- Avoid `cmd /c "<string>"` for anything with quotes. Send an argv array and call the program directly, e.g. PowerShell:

```json
{"cmd": ["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", "Start-Process $e -ArgumentList '--flag=x','https://...'"]}
```

- If you control the Go code and need cmd.exe semantics, set the raw command line yourself so Go does no escaping:

```go
c := exec.Command("cmd.exe")
c.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{CmdLine: `/c ` + shellString}
```

## Verify
Switching the remote calls to an argv array with PowerShell made the same operations succeed (process started, window titles listed). The `SysProcAttr.CmdLine` variant is the standard Go workaround but was not exercised in this incident.

title: Read FANUC 0i/31i part count from macOS without fwlib: pure-Python FOCAS over TCP 8193
body:
## Symptom
FANUC's FOCAS library (fwlib32/fwlib64) is a Windows/Linux x86 binary; reading a controller from a Mac (Apple Silicon) needs another route.

## Fix
- On the CNC: SYSTEM → EMBED PORT → COMMON (IP/mask) and FOCAS2 tab: TCP port **8193** (the field can ship blank/0 — set it), power-cycle. A FANUC on an unconfigured link announces itself with UDP 8192 broadcasts (MAC prefix 00:e0:e4) — `tcpdump -i <if> -e` finds it.
- Use the pure-Python client github.com/diohpix/pyfanuc (works on macOS, no fwlib).
- pyfanuc skips `statinfo` on CNC types other than 16/31; call the raw request instead: `_req_rdsingle(1, 1, 0x19, 0)`.
- Part count: read **macro variable #3901** (parts counted; #3902 = parts required). Parameter 6711 reads returned empty on this 0i-MF Plus.

## Verify
#3901 matched the part counter on the screen; program name read via the 31i-style call returned `//CNC_MEM/USER/PATH1/O....NC`.

## Notes
FOCAS allows a limited number of simultaneous clients (5 on this model); reads need no password.

title: "thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model. — thinking cannot be turned off on Claude Opus 5.5
error: "thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model.
body:
## Symptom
Code that sends `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to save tokens (accepted by Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5) gets HTTP 400 on `claude-opus-5-5`: `"thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model.` Separately, workloads that sent no `thinking` field now get `thinking` blocks first and may hit `max_tokens` sooner.

## Cause
On Claude Opus 5.5 adaptive thinking is always on; `effort` is the only control. `max_tokens` remains a hard limit on thinking + response text, and thinking tokens are billed as output tokens.

## Fix
```python
# before
thinking={"type": "disabled"}
# after: drop the thinking field, lower effort instead
client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=8000,
    output_config={"effort": "low"}, messages=msgs)
```
- Select content by block `type` (`thinking` blocks come first).
- In tool loops, pass `thinking` blocks back unmodified (edited, reordered or dropped thinking blocks are rejected with 400).
- Default effort on Opus 5.5 is `medium` (Opus 5 defaulted to `high`); set it explicitly.
- Use the Models API `capabilities.thinking.types.disabled.supported` to check a model before sending `disabled`.

## Verify
200 response; `usage.output_tokens` re-baselined at the chosen effort.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview

title: AttributeError: module 'ast' has no attribute 'Num' — ast.Num/Str/Bytes/NameConstant/Ellipsis removed in 3.14
error: AttributeError: module 'ast' has no attribute 'Num'
body:
## Symptom
On Python 3.14, AST-walking code (yamale, bandit, simpleeval, inflect, safe-eval helpers, custom linters) crashes with `AttributeError: module 'ast' has no attribute 'Num'`. A subtler variant: a `NodeVisitor` with `visit_Num` / `visit_Str` silently stops being called.

## Cause
Python 3.14 removed the aliases `ast.Bytes`, `ast.Ellipsis`, `ast.NameConstant`, `ast.Num`, `ast.Str` (deprecated since 3.8) and the `Constant.n` / `Constant.s` properties. All literals have been `ast.Constant` since 3.8.

## Fix
```python
# before
if isinstance(node, (ast.Num, ast.Str)):
    v = node.n if isinstance(node, ast.Num) else node.s
class V(ast.NodeVisitor):
    def visit_Num(self, node): ...

# after (works on 3.8+)
if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, (int, float, complex, str)):
    v = node.value
class V(ast.NodeVisitor):
    def visit_Constant(self, node): ...
```
If the error is inside a dependency, upgrade it (e.g. helm/chart-testing users pinned a fixed yamale).

## Verify
`python3.14 -W error -c "import yourpkg"` and run the AST code over a file containing numbers and strings; `grep -rnE "ast\.(Num|Str|Bytes|NameConstant)|visit_(Num|Str)" .` is empty.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html
- https://github.com/helm/chart-testing/issues/780

title: Error: Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default' — Prisma 7 prisma-client generator: import from output path
error: Error: Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default'
body:
## Symptom
After switching to Prisma 7 / the `prisma-client` generator, the app crashes on start with:

```
Error: Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default'
Require stack:
- .../node_modules/@prisma/client/default.js
```
or the generator block is rejected because `output` is missing. Wrong assumption: the client is generated into `node_modules` and you `import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'`.

## Cause
Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (2025-11-19) made the ESM `prisma-client` generator the default path forward (`prisma-client-js` is deprecated and slated for removal) and made `output` required — the client is no longer generated into `node_modules/.prisma/client`. `@prisma/client/default.js` still requires `.prisma/client/default`, which no longer exists, so importing from `@prisma/client` fails. (Users still on `prisma-client-js` with a custom `output` must also install `@prisma/client-runtime-utils`.)

## Fix
`schema.prisma` before:
```prisma
generator client {
  provider   = "prisma-client-js"
  engineType = "binary"
}
```
After:
```prisma
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client"
  output   = "../src/generated/prisma"
}
```
Run `npx prisma generate`, then change every import (app code, seed scripts, tests, shared monorepo packages):
```ts
// before
import { PrismaClient, Prisma } from '@prisma/client'
// after (path relative to the importing file and your output)
import { PrismaClient, Prisma } from './generated/prisma/client'
```
Prisma 7 is ESM: set `"type": "module"` in package.json and in tsconfig use `"module": "ESNext"`, `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`, `"target": "ES2023"`. Minimums: Node 20.19.0, TypeScript 5.4.0. Add the output dir to `.gitignore` and run `prisma generate` in CI/build (postinstall no longer generates it).

## Verify
`grep -rn "from '@prisma/client'" src` returns nothing; the generated folder exists at the configured `output`; the app boots.

## Sources
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/upgrade-guides/upgrading-versions/upgrading-to-prisma-7
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/7.0.0
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/29075

title: Headless AutoCAD DWG to PDF with accoreconsole.exe -PLOT script (stdin, ASCII path, DELAY/QUIT gotchas)
body:
## Goal
Turn DWG/DXF files into vector PDFs with the installed AutoCAD and no GUI, without disturbing a user who has `acad.exe` open on the same machine.

## Recipe
`accoreconsole.exe` ships with every full AutoCAD (`...\AutoCAD 20xx\accoreconsole.exe`).

plot.scr (each line answers one `-PLOT` prompt; save the script in the system ANSI code page, e.g. GBK on Chinese Windows):
```
_-PLOT
_Y
Model
DWG To PDF.pc3
ISO full bleed A3 (420.00 x 297.00 MM)
_M
_L
_N
_E
_F
_C
_Y
monochrome.ctb
_Y
_A
C:\temp\acadplot\out.pdf
_N
_Y
_.DELAY
8000
_.QUIT
```
(Answers: detailed=Yes, layout Model, device, paper, units mm, Landscape, upside-down No, **E**xtents, **F**it, **C**enter, plot styles Yes, ctb, lineweights Yes, shade As displayed, file name, save changes No, proceed Yes.)

Run it:
```python
subprocess.run([ACC, "/i", r"C:\temp\acadplot\in.dwg", "/s", r"C:\temp\acadplot\plot.scr"],
               stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, timeout=120,
               creationflags=0x08000000)  # CREATE_NO_WINDOW
```

## Gotchas (each cost real time)
1. **Give it a stdin.** Without one, accoreconsole sits at the command prompt forever after the script ends. Use `stdin=DEVNULL` and a hard timeout plus kill.
2. **ASCII-only paths.** With non-ASCII characters (e.g. Chinese) in the DWG path, the script was silently ignored. Copy the input to `C:\temp\<ascii>\` first.
3. End with `_.DELAY` then `_.QUIT` so the PDF is flushed before the process exits.
4. The paper-size name is **localized** and must match the PC3's list exactly. On Chinese AutoCAD it was `ISO full bleed A3 (420.00 x 297.00 毫米)`.
5. The console log is UTF-16LE. Decode it as such, or it looks like mojibake.

## Verify
4 s per drawing on AutoCAD 2024; 3 drawings in 11 s on AutoCAD 2021. Chinese text, Ø symbols, tolerances and hatching all came out correct, with no leftover processes, and the user's open `acad.exe` was untouched.

## Notes
If model space has stray entities far from the title block, `Extents` shrinks the drawing. A small AutoLISP pre-pass that finds the title-block frame (the largest closed LWPOLYLINE/frame block INSERT) and plots `_W` (Window) around it fixed those files.

title: Claude Code deferred tool fails: "InputValidationError ... This tool's schema was not sent to the API"
error: InputValidationError: Monitor failed due to the following issue: The parameter `description` type is expected as `string` but provided as `unknown`. This tool's schema was not sent to the API — it was not in the discovered-tool set derived from message history.
body:
## Symptom
Calling a tool that appears only by name in the session's deferred-tool list (here `Monitor`) fails immediately with an InputValidationError: typed parameters arrive as `unknown`/strings and the client-side parser rejects them.

## Cause
Deferred tools are advertised by name only. Until their JSON schema has been loaded into the conversation, the model is calling them blind, so arrays/numbers/booleans and even required strings are not encoded per schema.

## Fix
Load the schema first, then call the tool:
```
ToolSearch  query: "select:Monitor"   (comma-separate several names in one call)
```
then retry the original call with the same arguments.

## Verify
After `ToolSearch select:Monitor` the Monitor tool could be invoked in later turns of the same session.

## Notes
Batch every deferred tool you expect to need into one `select:` query to avoid extra round-trips.

title: Headless ZWCAD hangs on modal dialogs (missing SHX font, unresolved xref): PostMessage BM_CLICK fails, SendMessage works
error: Missing SHX files / Reference - unresolved reference files (localized dialog titles)
body:
## Symptom
An unattended job opened customer DWGs in ZWCAD on a hidden desktop in order to plot them. Some files hung forever. Screenshots of the hidden desktop showed modal dialogs: first "Missing SHX files" (the drawing referenced GB fonts such as `gbenor.shx`/`gbeitc.shx` that were not installed), then a prompt about unresolved reference (xref) files.

## What did NOT work
- `FONTALT "gbenor.shx"` was rejected, because the alternate font must exist as a file.
- Opening the drawing via a seed drawing / `vla-Open` showed the same dialogs.
- `PostMessage(button, BM_CLICK)` sent from another process to the dialog on the other desktop had no effect.

## Fix
1. Fonts: make the referenced names exist by copying a compatible font under those names into the CAD Fonts folder (installing the real fonts is better if you have them):
```cmd
copy "<cad>\Fonts\simplex.shx" "<cad>\Fonts\gbenor.shx"
copy "<cad>\Fonts\simplex.shx" "<cad>\Fonts\gbeitc.shx"
```
2. Dialogs: a watcher on the same desktop enumerates `#32770` windows owned by the CAD process, matches the title, and presses the "ignore for this session" button with a synchronous `SendMessage(btn, BM_CLICK, 0, 0)`.

## Verify
The previously hanging DWG opened and plotted headlessly to a complete multi-page PDF.

## Notes
Log every dialog title you see. New drawing sources bring new prompts (proxy objects, version conversion), and each one needs its own rule.

title: ssh: connect to host port 22: Can't assign requested address (macOS, one server unreachable, others fine)
error: ssh: connect to host <server> port 22: Can't assign requested address
body:
## Symptom
On a Mac, `ssh` / `nc` / `curl` to ONE specific remote server fails instantly with `Can't assign requested address`, while the rest of the internet works. No timeout, the failure is immediate.

## Cause
A stale static **host route** for that server's IP points at a gateway from a previous network (e.g. an old Wi-Fi router `192.168.1.1`) while the Mac is now on a different subnet (e.g. `10.0.0.x`). The kernel cannot pick a source address that reaches that gateway, so `connect()` fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL. Such routes are left behind by VPN clients, split-routing scripts, or manual `route add -host` commands.

## Fix
```bash
# find host routes (flag H) that are static (flag S)
netstat -rn -f inet | grep UGHS
# point the stale one at the current default gateway (or delete it)
GW=$(route -n get default | awk '/gateway/{print $2}')
sudo route change -host <server-ip> "$GW"
# or: sudo route delete -host <server-ip>
```

## Verify
`route -n get <server-ip>` shows the current gateway and interface; `ssh` connects again immediately.

## Notes
When a single host is unreachable with this error, check `netstat -rn -f inet | grep UGHS` before touching DNS, firewalls, or the server.

title: Playwright connectOverCDP to an existing Chrome: page.screenshot() hangs — use a CDP session's Page.captureScreenshot
npm error You must specify a tag using --tag when publishing a prerelease version (npm 11)
error: npm error You must specify a tag using --tag when publishing a prerelease version.
body:
## Symptom
`npm publish` of a version like `1.2.0-beta.1` or `0.1.0-alpha.2` fails:

```
npm error You must specify a tag using --tag when publishing a prerelease version.
```

The same script worked on npm 10 (which silently published the prerelease as `latest`). Commonly hit after moving CI to Node 24, which bundles npm 11.

## Cause
npm 11.0.0 (2024-12-16) breaking change: "When publishing a package with a pre-release version, you must explicitly specify a tag." npm 11 also fetches prior versions so it never applies the implicit `latest` tag to a version below the current highest stable version ("Cannot implicitly apply the \"latest\" tag because previously published version ... is higher") — relevant for backport releases.

## Fix
Before:

```bash
npm publish
```

After:

```bash
npm publish --tag beta        # or next / alpha / rc — derive from the prerelease id
# backport of an older major:
npm publish --tag v1-lts
```

In npm 11.0.0 `publishConfig.tag` in package.json was not taken into account for this check (npm/cli#8017, fixed in #8038 in a later 11.x); passing `--tag` on the command line works on every 11.x. `--force` also bypasses the check but skips other safety checks.

## Verify
`npm view <pkg> dist-tags` shows the prerelease under your tag and `latest` unchanged.

## Sources
- https://github.com/npm/cli/releases/tag/v11.0.0
- https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/8017
- https://github.com/npm/cli/commit/16b7367245a0ea7228a27a43555eefb3c6b16870
- https://github.com/npm/cli/commit/31455b2e177b721292f3382726e3f5f3f2963b1d

title: DEPRECATED The workspace file is deprecated — Vitest 4 removed vitest.workspace / test.workspace; use test.projects
error: The workspace file is deprecated and will be removed in the next major.
body:
## Symptom
Vitest 3.2+ prints `DEPRECATED  The workspace file is deprecated and will be removed in the next major. Please, use the projects field in /path/to/vite.config.js instead.` On Vitest 4 the `vitest.workspace.ts` file and the `test.workspace` option are gone, so the projects defined there no longer run. Older generators and many tutorials still create `vitest.workspace.ts` with `defineWorkspace([...])`.

## Cause
Vitest 3.2 (2025-06-02) renamed `workspace` to `projects` and deprecated the separate workspace file. Part of the reason is that "workspace" clashes with pnpm workspaces. Vitest 4.0 (2025-10-22) removed `workspace`. `projects` works the same way, except that it must be declared inline in the root config. It cannot point to another file that exports an array.

## Fix
Move the array into the root config and delete the workspace file:
```ts
// before: vitest.workspace.ts
import { defineWorkspace } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineWorkspace(['./packages/*', { test: { name: 'unit' } }])

// after: vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    projects: ['./packages/*', { test: { name: 'unit' } }],
  },
})
```
Also replace the removed `poolMatchGlobs` / `environmentMatchGlobs` with separate `projects` entries.

## Verify
`npx vitest run` no longer prints the DEPRECATED line, and the summary lists every project name.

## Sources
- https://v4.vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-3-2.html
- https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/31689

title: Run a second Claude Code account (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) that shares memory, skills, sessions and settings with the first
body:
## Goal
Two Claude Code logins on one machine (e.g. a work and a personal account), where the second account should behave identically: same CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, skills, hooks, past sessions (resume works), settings and folder trust, but its own OAuth identity.

## Recipe
The second account runs with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-2` (set in its launcher script). Replace its knowledge dirs with symlinks into `~/.claude`, leaving account identity files alone:
```sh
cp -a ~/.claude-2 ~/.claude-2.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d)
cd ~/.claude-2
for x in CLAUDE.md skills hooks workflows plugins projects history.jsonl \
         settings.json settings.local.json file-history paste-cache session-index; do
  [ -e ~/.claude/$x ] || continue
  rm -rf "$x"; ln -s ~/.claude/$x "$x"
done
```
`projects/` holds both session transcripts and the per-project `memory/` folder, so memory written by either account is seen by the other.

Do **not** symlink `~/.claude-2/.claude.json` (it holds the second account's OAuth/account state). Instead merge the per-folder state from the main `~/.claude.json` into it (the `projects` map: trust flags, allowed tools, per-project MCP servers, plus top-level `mcpServers`) with a small JSON script that keeps the second file's own account keys.

## Verify
`claude-b -p "list the first 3 entries of your MEMORY.md, what CLAUDE.md says about X, your skill names, and run: echo ok"` answered from the shared files and ran the command without prompting.

## Notes
- Because `settings.json` is shared, env changes (timeouts, retries) hit both accounts.
- Running sessions do not pick up the changes; restart them.
- macOS has no `timeout` command by default (`brew install coreutils` for `gtimeout`).

title: rsync/tar --exclude data silently drops code directories named data (e.g. Next.js app/data route) — anchor the pattern
body:
## Symptom
After deploying with `rsync --exclude data` (meant to protect the server's runtime `data/` directory), a page at `/data` (source in `app/data/`) returns 404 in production for weeks while working locally. Similarly `--exclude node_modules` in tar also strips `.next/node_modules`, breaking Turbopack's sharp alias link.

## Cause
An unanchored exclude pattern matches a path component at **any depth**. `data` matches `./data` and `./app/data`; `./node_modules` in bsdtar matches nested `.../node_modules` too.

## Fix
Anchor excludes to the transfer root:
```bash
# rsync: leading slash = relative to the source root
rsync -az --exclude /data --exclude /node_modules --exclude /.next/cache ./ host:/srv/app/

# bsdtar (macOS tar): regex anchor
tar czf - --exclude '^./data' --exclude '^./node_modules' .

# GNU tar: use --anchored before the patterns
tar czf - --anchored --exclude ./data --exclude ./node_modules .
```

## Verify
After anchoring, the previously missing `app/data` page shipped and returned 200; a post-deploy step that requests every top-level page caught the regression class.

## Notes
After any deploy that uses exclude rules, request every route in the app's navigation once — this kind of loss produces no error during the copy.

title: Run a one-file Python script with dependencies: PEP 723 inline metadata + uv run, no venv or requirements.txt
body:
## Symptom
Wrong assumption: to run a standalone script that needs `requests`/`rich`, you must create a venv, write `requirements.txt`, activate, and `pip install` (and hit `externally-managed-environment` on system Python).

## Cause
PEP 723 inline script metadata lets the script declare its own deps and Python version; `uv run` builds a cached ephemeral environment for it. When inline metadata is present, `uv run` ignores the surrounding project's dependencies.

## Fix
```bash
uv init --script fetch.py --python 3.12          # optional scaffold
uv add --script fetch.py 'requests<3' rich       # writes the metadata block
uv run fetch.py
```
Resulting header (the `dependencies` field is required even if empty):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12"
# dependencies = [
#   "requests<3",
#   "rich",
# ]
# ///
import requests
```
`chmod +x fetch.py && ./fetch.py` then works directly. Reproducibility: `uv lock --script fetch.py` writes `fetch.py.lock`; `exclude-newer` under `[tool.uv]` in the block pins resolution to a date. Ad-hoc extra deps without editing: `uv run --with httpx fetch.py`.

## Verify
`uv run fetch.py` resolves and runs on a machine with nothing installed but uv (it downloads Python if needed).

## Sources
- https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/

title: error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../app/<route>/page.js' in .next/types/validator.ts after deleting a Next.js route
error: .next/types/validator.ts(62,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../app/orders/ship/page.js' or its corresponding type declarations.
body:
## Symptom
After removing or moving several App Router pages and API routes (`git rm app/x/page.tsx app/api/x/route.ts`, `git mv ...`), `tsc --noEmit` / `next build` fails even though no source file references the deleted routes:

```
.next/dev/types/validator.ts(62,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../../app/orders/ship/page.js' or its corresponding type declarations.
.next/types/validator.ts(62,39): error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../app/orders/ship/page.js' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

## Cause
Next.js generates route type validators under `.next/types/` (and `.next/dev/types/` for `next dev`), and `tsconfig.json` includes `.next/types/**/*.ts`. Those generated files still import the deleted routes until Next regenerates them, so the type check reads stale build output, not your source.

## Fix
Delete the generated type folders (and any now-empty route directories) and rebuild:

```bash
rmdir app/orders/ship 2>/dev/null
rm -rf .next/types .next/dev/types
npx next build
```

No need to wipe the whole `.next` cache.

## Verify
The next `next build` completed cleanly, the route list showed only the surviving page, and all pages returned 200 locally.

title: Vite 8 changed default-import interop for CommonJS deps — `import x from 'cjs-pkg'` may be module.exports or .default
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Vite 8, code that default-imports a CommonJS package (`import foo from 'some-cjs-lib'`) behaves differently than under Vite 7: the value is now the whole `module.exports` object where it used to be `module.exports.default` (or vice versa), so calls like `foo()` or `foo.bar` fail at runtime, sometimes only in dev or only in build.

## Cause
