Vite 8 (released 2026-03-12, Rolldown-based) handles the default import from CJS one consistent way in both dev and build. The default import is `module.exports` if any of these hold:
- the importer is `.mjs` or `.mts`;
- the importer's closest package.json has `"type": "module"`;
- the CJS module does not set `module.exports.__esModule = true`.

Otherwise it is `module.exports.default`. Previously dev (dependency optimizer) and build (`build.commonjsOptions.defaultIsModuleExports: 'auto'`) used different rules, so the result could differ. `build.commonjsOptions` is now a no-op.

## Fix
Preferred: make the import unambiguous in your code.
```js
// before (ambiguous)
import lib from 'some-cjs-lib'
// after: pick the shape explicitly
import * as ns from 'some-cjs-lib'
const lib = ns.default ?? ns
```
Temporary escape hatch (deprecated):
```js
export default defineConfig({
  legacy: { inconsistentCjsInterop: true },
})
```
Report affected packages upstream, linking Rolldown's 'Ambiguous default import from CJS modules' doc.

Related Vite 8 CJS changes: `require()` of externalized modules is kept as `require` (use `esmExternalRequirePlugin` from 'vite' to convert), and format sniffing between `browser`/`module` fields was removed (Vite follows `resolve.mainFields` order).

## Verify
Run both `vite` and `vite build && vite preview` and exercise the code path; `console.log(lib)` shows the same shape in both.

## Sources
- https://vite.dev/guide/migration#consistent-commonjs-interop
- https://vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8

title: OpenAI Responses API function tools are internally tagged and strict by default — not the Chat Completions shape
body:
## Symptom
Porting Chat Completions code to `client.responses.create`, the agent passes `tools=[{"type":"function","function":{...}}]` and `response_format=...`, reads `choices[0].message`, and returns tool results as `role: tool` messages. Requests fail validation or tool calls are not matched.

## Cause
Responses uses typed input/output Items. Differences documented in OpenAI's migration guide:
- Function definitions are internally tagged (`name`, `parameters` at top level), not nested under `function`.
- Omitting `strict` in Responses attempts strict mode (Chat Completions defaults to non-strict); if the schema can't be made strict it falls back and returns the tool with `strict: false`.
- Structured outputs use `text.format`, not `response_format`.
- Tool calls are `function_call` items; results go back as `function_call_output` items linked by `call_id`.

## Fix
```python
tools=[{"type":"function","name":"get_weather","description":"...",
        "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"location":{"type":"string"}},
                      "required":["location"],"additionalProperties":False}}]
resp = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, input=msgs, tools=tools)
for item in resp.output:
    if item.type == "function_call":
        msgs += [item, {"type":"function_call_output","call_id":item.call_id,"output":run(item)}]
```
Use `response.output_text` for plain text. Responses are stored by default; set `store=False` to opt out.

## Verify
Every `function_call_output` carries the matching `call_id` (a missing one is a listed migration error).

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses

title: `$:` is not allowed in runes mode, use `$derived` or `$effect` instead (Svelte 5)
error: `$:` is not allowed in runes mode, use `$derived` or `$effect` instead
body:
## Symptom
Svelte 5 compiler error `legacy_reactive_statement_invalid`:
```
`$:` is not allowed in runes mode, use `$derived` or `$effect` instead
```
This happens in a component that uses any rune and also has a Svelte 4 reactive statement such as `$: doubled = count * 2`. A related mistake: in runes mode a plain top-level `let count = 0` is no longer reactive.

## Cause
Svelte 5 (2024-10-22) replaced implicit reactivity with runes. State is declared with `$state()`, values computed from other state with `$derived()`, and side effects with `$effect()`. `$effect` runs at a different time from `$:`: after the DOM updates, with dependencies tracked at runtime.

## Fix
```svelte
<!-- before (Svelte 4) -->
<script>
  let count = 0;
  $: double = count * 2;
  $: if (count > 5) alert('Count is too high!');
</script>

<!-- after (Svelte 5) -->
<script>
  let count = $state(0);
  const double = $derived(count * 2);
  $effect(() => {
    if (count > 5) alert('Count is too high!');
  });
</script>
```
Use `$derived` for values (the usual case) and `$effect` only for side effects. For multi-statement derivations use `$derived.by(() => { ... })`.

## Verify
`npx svelte-check` passes, and the UI updates when `count` changes.

## Sources
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/compiler-errors

title: The parameter "dynamodb_table" is deprecated. Use parameter "use_lockfile" instead. (Terraform S3 backend)
error: The parameter "dynamodb_table" is deprecated. Use parameter "use_lockfile" instead.
body:
## Symptom
`terraform init` / `plan` prints a "Deprecated Parameter" warning:

```
The parameter "dynamodb_table" is deprecated. Use parameter "use_lockfile" instead.
```

Agents still scaffold a DynamoDB lock table (partition key `LockID`) for every new S3 backend.

## Cause
Terraform **1.11.0 (2025-02-27)** made S3-native state locking GA via `use_lockfile` and deprecated the DynamoDB arguments (`dynamodb_table`, `dynamodb_endpoint`). The docs say DynamoDB-based locking "is deprecated and will be removed in a future minor version." Locking is a lock object next to the state (`<key>.tflock`) using S3 conditional writes.

## Fix
```hcl
# before
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "mybucket"
    key            = "path/to/my/key"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    dynamodb_table = "tf-locks"
  }
}
# after
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket       = "mybucket"
    key          = "path/to/my/key"
    region       = "us-east-1"
    use_lockfile = true
  }
}
```
For a safe transition you can set both `use_lockfile = true` and `dynamodb_table` for one release cycle, then drop the table. IAM: the role needs `s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject` and `s3:DeleteObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::mybucket/path/to/my/key.tflock`. Run `terraform init -reconfigure` after editing the backend block. Keep bucket versioning on.

## Verify
During a `terraform apply`, `aws s3 ls s3://mybucket/path/to/my/` shows `key.tflock`; it disappears when the run ends, and init prints no deprecation warning.

## Sources
- https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/backend/s3
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/releases/tag/v1.11.0
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/internal/backend/remote-state/s3/backend.go

title: transformers v5: TRANSFORMERS_CACHE removed (use HF_HOME), use_auth_token→token, huggingface_hub 1.0 uses httpx
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to transformers v5: models download to the default cache even though `TRANSFORMERS_CACHE` is set; `except requests.HTTPError` no longer catches Hub download failures; `proxies=` passed in code is ignored/rejected; `HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1` does nothing; `transformers-cli` is gone.

## Cause
transformers v5.0.0 (2026-01-26) removed legacy env vars `TRANSFORMERS_CACHE`, `PYTORCH_TRANSFORMERS_CACHE`, `PYTORCH_PRETRAINED_BERT_CACHE` and pins `huggingface_hub>=1.0.0` (released 2025-10-27), which switched HTTP from `requests` to `httpx`, removed in-code proxy settings, and dropped `hf_transfer` for `hf_xet`. `use_auth_token` is deprecated everywhere in favour of `token`.

## Fix
```bash
# before
export TRANSFORMERS_CACHE=/data/hf
# after
export HF_HOME=/data/hf                 # cache lives under $HF_HOME/hub
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy:3128    # proxies only via env vars now
```
```python
# before
from_pretrained(repo, use_auth_token=tok)
try: ...
except requests.HTTPError: ...
# after
from_pretrained(repo, token=tok)
import httpx
try: ...
except httpx.HTTPError: ...
```
CLI: `transformers-cli ...` -> `transformers ...`; `transformers chat` now talks to `transformers serve` or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. `save_pretrained(safe_serialization=False)` was removed (safetensors only).

## Verify
`python -c "from huggingface_hub import constants; print(constants.HF_HUB_CACHE)"` points under your `HF_HOME`.

## Sources
- https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md
- https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/concepts/migration

title: FastAPI 2025–2026 breaking changes: pydantic.v1 dropped (0.128), Python 3.9 dropped, 401 not 403 for missing creds
body:
## Symptom
Upgrading an older FastAPI app to a current release breaks in several ways that pre-2025 knowledge won't predict: models imported from `pydantic.v1` stop working, installs on Python 3.9 resolve to an old FastAPI, auth tests asserting `403` for a missing bearer token now see `401`, and `ORJSONResponse`/`UJSONResponse` emit deprecation warnings.

## Cause
From the FastAPI release notes:
- 0.122.0 (2025-11-24): "Use 401 status code in security classes when credentials are missing" (previously 403).
- 0.125.0 (2025-12-17): drop Python 3.8; 0.127.0 (2025-12-21) added deprecation warnings for `pydantic.v1`; **0.128.0 (2025-12-27): "Drop support for pydantic.v1."**
- 0.129.0 (2026-02-12): "Drop support for Python 3.9."
- 0.130.0 (2026-02-22): JSON responses serialized by Pydantic (Rust) when there's a return type / `response_model`; 0.131.0 deprecated `ORJSONResponse` and `UJSONResponse`.
- 0.132.0: strict JSON `Content-Type` checking.

## Fix
```python
# before
from pydantic.v1 import BaseModel
from fastapi.responses import ORJSONResponse
app = FastAPI(default_response_class=ORJSONResponse)
# after
from pydantic import BaseModel           # migrate models to Pydantic v2
app = FastAPI()                          # declare return types/response_model for fast Rust serialization

@app.get("/items/{id}")
async def get_item(id: int) -> Item: ...
```
Update auth tests from `assert r.status_code == 403` to `401` for missing credentials (or follow the docs page "Use Old 403 Authentication Error Status Codes" to override the security classes). Use Python 3.10+. Install with `pip install "fastapi[standard]"` to get the CLI (`fastapi dev`, `fastapi run`) and uvicorn.

## Verify
`python -W error::DeprecationWarning -m pytest` passes against the latest FastAPI; `fastapi --version` shows the expected release.

## Sources
- https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/

title: Stripe basil: metered price without a meter errors; usage records API (createUsageRecord) removed — use Billing Meters
body:
## Symptom
Creating a price with `recurring: { usage_type: "metered" }` and no meter fails. `stripe.subscriptionItems.createUsageRecord(...)` / `listUsageRecordSummaries` are gone from the SDK. `aggregate_usage` and `billing_thresholds` params are rejected.

## Cause
`2025-03-31.basil` removed legacy usage-based billing. A legacy usage-based price is a price with `usage_type: metered` and no meter. The UsageRecord and UsageRecordSummary endpoints were removed, as were `billing_thresholds` on subscriptions and `aggregate_usage` on prices. Metered prices must reference a Billing Meter.

## Fix
```ts
const meter = await stripe.billing.meters.create({
  display_name: "API calls", event_name: "api_call",
  default_aggregation: { formula: "sum" },
})
const price = await stripe.prices.create({
  currency: "usd", unit_amount: 1, product: productId,
  recurring: { interval: "month", usage_type: "metered", meter: meter.id },
})
// report usage
await stripe.billing.meterEvents.create({
  event_name: "api_call",
  payload: { stripe_customer_id: customerId, value: "1" },
})
```
Stripe documents a stopgap: keep calling the legacy UsageRecords API through a raw request pinned to a pre-basil API version.

## Verify
Meter events show up under Billing → Meters, and the upcoming invoice preview reflects the usage.

## Sources
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil/2025-03-31/deprecate-legacy-usage-based-billing

title: New Gemini API projects can't rely on gemini-2.5-pro/flash: access limited to past users
body:
## Symptom
An agent picks `gemini-2.5-pro` or `gemini-2.5-flash` for a new project (widely the default in 2025 code) and the new API key/project cannot use it, although nothing on the page marks 2.5 as deprecated.

## Cause
Google's deprecations page (as of 2026-10-14): "we are limiting access to the 2.5 models to users who have actively used them in the past" and "These models are not deprecated and will continue to be served until further notice through the API." The dated 2.5 preview snapshots (`gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25/05-06/06-05`, `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20/09-25`) are already shut down.

## Fix
For new projects use the models Google recommends: `gemini-3.8-flash` or `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`; for pro-tier reasoning `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` (listed replacement for the 2.5 pro previews). `gemini-3-pro-preview` was shut down 2026-03-09.

## Verify
Call `client.models.list()` with the project's key and confirm the model is listed.

## Sources
- https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations

title: Terraform AWS provider v6: aws_eip vpc, aws_instance cpu_core_count, data.aws_region name removed or renamed
body:
## Symptom
After `terraform init -upgrade` pulls `hashicorp/aws` 6.x (or a loose constraint like `>= 5.0`), plans fail on arguments that worked in 5.x, or `region` on an S3 bucket suddenly means something else. Model-generated HCL still uses the 5.x forms below.

## Cause
AWS provider **6.0.0** was released 2025-06-18. It adds a `region` argument to most resources (Enhanced Region Support, multi-region without extra provider aliases) and removes long-deprecated arguments.

## Fix
Upgrade to the latest 5.x first and clear all deprecation warnings, then:

```hcl
# aws_eip: before
resource "aws_eip" "x" { vpc = true }
# after
resource "aws_eip" "x" { domain = "vpc" }

# aws_instance: before
cpu_core_count       = 2
cpu_threads_per_core = 1
# after
cpu_options {
  core_count       = 2
  threads_per_core = 1
}

# data.aws_region: before
data.aws_region.current.name
# after
data.aws_region.current.region

# aws_s3_bucket (resource and data source): the bucket's own region attribute
# is now bucket_region; `region` is the Enhanced Region Support argument
```
Other removals: `aws_eks_addon.resolve_conflicts` (use `resolve_conflicts_on_create` / `_on_update`), provider `endpoints.opsworks`, `endpoints.simpledb`/`sdb`, `endpoints.worklink`. `aws_instance.user_data` is no longer hashed in state and is stored in clear text, so do not put secrets in it. Pin `version = "~> 6.0"` (or `~> 5.0` until migrated).

## Verify
`terraform plan` with provider 6.x completes with no errors and no unexpected replacements.

## Sources
- https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/guides/version-6-upgrade
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/blob/main/website/docs/guides/version-6-upgrade.html.markdown
- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/releases/tag/v6.0.0

title: pnpm 10: eslint/prettier plugins no longer hoisted to root node_modules — editor/IDE can't find them
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to pnpm 10, an editor extension, a globally run `eslint`, or a shared config in a monorepo can't resolve `eslint-plugin-*`, `eslint-config-*` or `prettier-plugin-*` packages that are only dependencies of another package (e.g. a shared `@repo/eslint-config`). It worked on pnpm 9 because those were publicly hoisted to the root `node_modules`.

## Cause
pnpm 10.0.0 (2025-01-07): "`public-hoist-pattern`: nothing is hoisted by default. Packages containing `eslint` or `prettier` in their name are no longer hoisted to the root of `node_modules`."

## Fix
Preferred: declare the plugins/configs as direct devDependencies of the package that runs ESLint/Prettier (and of the workspace root if tools run from there):

```bash
pnpm add -D -w eslint-plugin-react prettier-plugin-tailwindcss
```

Or restore the old hoisting explicitly:

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml (pnpm 11 reads settings only from here)
publicHoistPattern:
  - '*eslint*'
  - '*prettier*'
```

(pnpm 10 also accepts `public-hoist-pattern[]=*eslint*` in `.npmrc`; pnpm 11 ignores non-auth `.npmrc` settings.) Then `pnpm install`.

## Verify
`ls node_modules | grep -E 'eslint|prettier'` at the root shows the packages (if hoisting), or `node -e "require.resolve('eslint-plugin-react')"` succeeds from the package directory.

## Sources
- https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v10.0.0
- https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.0.0

title: Gemini 3.x API: use thinking_level, not thinking_budget, and leave temperature/top_p/top_k unset
body:
## Symptom
Code written for Gemini 2.5 (with `thinking_budget` and a low `temperature` for "deterministic" extraction) misbehaved on Gemini 3.x models. Requests with `thinkingBudget` were rejected on a 3.x flash model, and runs with temperature lowered gave worse structured outputs than the defaults.

## Cause
Gemini 3.x replaces the token budget with a discrete `thinking_level` ("low" / "medium" / "high"), and the two must not be combined. Google's 3.x guidance is to leave sampling parameters at their defaults (temperature 1.0). Lowering them is not a determinism switch on these models.

## Fix
```python
from google.genai import types
cfg = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="high", include_thoughts=True),
    response_mime_type="application/json",
    response_schema=MySchema,
    media_resolution=types.MediaResolution.MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH,  # for drawings/scans
    # no temperature / top_p / top_k
)
```
For repeatable outputs, cache responses keyed by a hash of the full request payload (and pass a fixed `seed` if the endpoint accepts one) rather than lowering the temperature.

## Verify
After removing `thinkingBudget` and the sampling overrides, requests succeeded. With the payload-hash cache, the same input folder produced an identical quote every time, where uncached runs had shown 20-117% spread.

## Notes
Check the model's own "what's new" page when moving between Gemini generations. Parameter support changed between 2.5 and 3.x.

title: Windows .bat with Chinese text closes instantly / garbles after `chcp 65001` on line 1
body:
## Symptom
An `install.bat` with Chinese text in `echo` lines and paths (for example `set D=C:\<Chinese folder>`) flashed open and closed at once when double-clicked on a Chinese-locale Windows 10 PC. Run from an open `cmd` window, everything after the first line was garbage or "not recognized" errors.

The file started with:
```
@echo off
chcp 65001 >nul
```
and its bytes were GBK (cp936, the system ANSI code page). It had been converted with `iconv -f UTF-8 -t GBK`.

## Cause
cmd.exe reads a batch file a line at a time and decodes each line with the console's **current** code page. `chcp 65001` on line 2 switches that code page to UTF-8, so every later line, which is GBK bytes, gets decoded as UTF-8. Paths and commands turn to mojibake and the script dies. Double-clicking hides the error because the window closes.

The reverse also breaks: a UTF-8 file without `chcp 65001` on a cp936 system garbles in the same way.

## Fix
Make the console code page and the file encoding match. The simplest reliable option on Chinese Windows is to drop `chcp` and save the file as GBK with CRLF line endings:

```python
s = open('install.bat', encoding='utf-8').read().replace('\r\n', '\n')
s = s.replace('@echo off\nchcp 65001 >nul\n', '@echo off\n', 1)
open('dist/install.bat', 'wb').write(s.replace('\n', '\r\n').encode('gbk'))
```
(macOS `sed` failed on the GBK file with `sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence`. Do byte-level edits in Python instead.)

## Verify
On the same PC the fixed `install.bat` ran to the end and printed every Chinese progress line. It extracted portable Git and Python, installed the pip packages and created the target folder.

## Notes
To debug a batch file that "disappears", run it from an open `cmd` window (`cd /d <folder>` then `install.bat`) so the error stays on screen.

title: updateTag can only be called from within a Server Action: use revalidateTag(tag, 'max') in Route Handlers
error: updateTag can only be called from within a Server Action
body:
## Symptom
You replace a deprecated one-argument `revalidateTag('posts')` with `updateTag('posts')` in a Route Handler (for example a CMS webhook `app/api/revalidate/route.ts`) and it throws: `updateTag can only be called from within a Server Action`.

## Cause
`updateTag` is new in Next.js 16 (2025-10-21) and is Server Actions only. It immediately expires the tag so the next read waits for fresh data (read-your-own-writes). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components or anywhere else. `revalidateTag` (now `revalidateTag(tag, profile)`) is the API for Route Handlers and webhooks.

## Fix
Before:
```ts
// app/api/revalidate/route.ts
import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
export async function POST() {
  updateTag('posts') // throws
  return Response.json({ ok: true })
}
```
After:
```ts
import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
export async function POST() {
  revalidateTag('posts', 'max') // stale-while-revalidate
  return Response.json({ ok: true })
}
```
Keep `updateTag` for `'use server'` actions where the user expects to see their change right away. To refresh uncached data shown elsewhere on the page from an action, Next.js 16 also adds `refresh()` from `next/cache`.

## Verify
POST the webhook and it returns 200 with no thrown error. Pages tagged `posts` show new content on a later request.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#updatetag
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#improved-caching-apis

title: Next.js 16.3: error.tsx unstable_retry → retry, unstable_catchError → catchError; prefer retry() over reset()
body:
## Symptom Agents generate `error.tsx` with only `reset()` (the 13–15 API). After a server/data error, clicking "Try again" re-renders the same failed RSC payload and the error comes back. Code written against 16.2 uses `unstable_retry` / `unstable_catchError`, which were the preview names. ## Cause Next.js 16.2 (2026-03-18) added `unstable_retry()` to `error.js` props and `unstable_catchError()` in `next/error`. `retry` calls `router.refresh()` + `reset()` in a transition, so it re-fetches server data. Next.js 16.3 (2026-08-03) stabilized them: error.js version history says "`v16.3.0` `retry` prop became stable", and the 16.3 release post imports `catchError` from `next/error`. The docs now say: "In most cases, you should use `retry()` instead" of `reset()`. ## Fix Before (15-era or 16.2): ```tsx 'use client' export default function Error({ error, reset }) { /* or unstable_retry */ return } ``` After (16.3+): ```tsx 'use client' import type { ErrorInfo } from 'next/error' export default function Error({ error, retry }: ErrorInfo) { return (

{error.message}

) } ``` Custom nested boundary that does not swallow `notFound()`/`redirect()`: ```tsx 'use client' import { catchError, type ErrorInfo } from 'next/error' function Fallback(props: { title: string }, { error, retry }: ErrorInfo) { return } export default catchError(Fallback) ``` ## Verify Force a data-fetch failure, fix it, then click Try again. The segment re-fetches and renders without a full reload. ## Sources - https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error - https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16-3 - https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16-2

title: next build fails: venv python symlink "points out of filesystem root" when a Python venv lives inside the Next.js repo
error: points out of filesystem root
body:
## Symptom
`next build` (Turbopack) on a server failed while walking the project tree. The error referred to the Python interpreter symlink inside a virtualenv that had been created in the repo directory (e.g. `./.venv/bin/python -> /usr/bin/python3.x`), complaining that the link "points out of filesystem root".

## Cause
The app shells out to Python helpers, and the venv was created inside the Next.js project root. Turbopack treats the project root as its filesystem root and follows/validates symlinks it encounters while scanning. The venv's `bin/python` is an absolute symlink to the system interpreter, i.e. outside the project root, so the build aborts. Adding the folder to `.gitignore` does not help, because the scan is filesystem-based.

## Fix
Create the venv outside the repository and point the app at it via an absolute path or env var:
```bash
python3 -m venv /opt/myapp-venv
/opt/myapp-venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
# in .env.local / pm2 ecosystem
PYTHON_BIN=/opt/myapp-venv/bin/python
```
Then call `process.env.PYTHON_BIN` from the route handlers instead of a repo-relative `.venv/bin/python`.

## Verify
`next build` completed after the venv was moved; the deployed app ran its Python pipeline (CAD geometry + rendering + extraction) end to end with a live POST returning success.

## Notes
The same applies to any directory in the project tree that contains absolute symlinks outside the root (extracted AppImages, vendored SDKs). Keep such toolchains under `/opt`.

title: attempted to import the Node standard library module "stream" — Expo SDK 53 enabled package.json exports in Metro
error: The package at "node_modules\ws\lib\stream.js" attempted to import the Node standard library module "stream".
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading from Expo SDK 52 to 53 (React Native 0.79), bundling fails:
```
The package at "node_modules\ws\lib\stream.js" attempted to import the Node standard library module "stream".
```
Variants: `ws/lib/websocket.js` ... `"events"`. The usual trigger is `@supabase/supabase-js` → `@supabase/realtime-js` → `ws`. Firebase packages and others can break in less obvious ways.

## Cause
Expo SDK 53 (2025-04-30) / React Native 0.79 turned on Metro's support for the `package.json` `exports` field by default. Packages whose `exports` map points React Native at a Node build now resolve to that Node code. An Expo maintainer (brentvatne) tracks this whole class of issues in expo/expo#36375.

## Fix
1. Preferred: upgrade the offending library to a version that ships correct `exports` conditions, for example `npx expo install @supabase/supabase-js@latest`. Then run `npm ls ws` to make sure no old `realtime-js` remains.
2. Workaround: opt out in `metro.config.js`:
```js
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config')
const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname)
config.resolver.unstable_enablePackageExports = false
module.exports = config
```
Opting out can break packages that rely on `exports`, so remove it once the dependency is fixed. Clear the cache after either change with `npx expo start -c`.

## Verify
`npx expo start -c` bundles without the Node standard library error, and the realtime/websocket feature connects on a device.

## Sources
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-53
- https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/36477
- https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js/issues/1400

title: Next.js 16: local next/image src with a query string (/logo.png?v=2) is rejected unless images.localPatterns allows it
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Next.js 16, cache-busted local images such as `<Image src="/assets/photo.png?v=1" />` or `/api/images/123?t=...` fail to optimize (400 from `/_next/image`, docs error page `next-image-unconfigured-localpatterns`). The same image without the query string works.

## Cause
Next.js 16.0 (2025-10-21): "Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks." Once `localPatterns` is defined it is an allowlist. Paths that no pattern covers are rejected too.

## Fix
Before: no `images.localPatterns` and `src="/assets/photo?v=1"`.

After, allowing any query string under a path (omit `search`):
```ts
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig = {
  images: {
    localPatterns: [
      { pathname: '/assets/**' },      // ?v=123, ?t=456, or none
      { pathname: '/api/images/**' },
    ],
  },
}
export default nextConfig
```
Or allow exactly one query string: `{ pathname: '/assets/**', search: '?v=1' }`. `search` is an exact match with the leading `?` and no globs, so it rejects the plain path. `search: ''` means NO query string is allowed. Use `/**` (any depth). `/assets/` alone matches nothing below it. Patterns are case-sensitive. Also cover every other local image directory you serve, because the list is an allowlist.

## Verify
`curl -I "http://localhost:3000/_next/image?url=%2Fassets%2Fphoto.png%3Fv%3D1&w=640&q=75"` returns 200.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#local-images-with-query-strings-breaking-change
- https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/next-image-unconfigured-localpatterns
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: runs-on: ubuntu-20.04 jobs never start: the Ubuntu 20.04 GitHub-hosted runner image was retired 2025-04-15
body:
## Symptom
A workflow with `runs-on: ubuntu-20.04` sits queued or fails with no runner assigned; in March/April 2025 it failed only during certain hours (brownouts). Older docs, tutorials and model output still recommend `ubuntu-20.04` for glibc-compat builds.

## Cause
GitHub retired the Ubuntu 20.04 hosted runner image under its N-1 OS support policy. It was fully retired by **2025-04-15** (originally announced for April 1). Brownouts ran March 4 to April 8, 2025.

## Fix
```yaml
# before
runs-on: ubuntu-20.04
# after
runs-on: ubuntu-24.04   # or ubuntu-22.04
```

If you needed 20.04 for an old glibc baseline in released binaries, build inside a container instead, e.g. `container: ubuntu:20.04` on an `ubuntu-24.04` host, or use a manylinux/musl toolchain.

Note: `ubuntu-latest` itself moves from 24.04 to 26.04 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19; pin `ubuntu-24.04` if you need stability.

## Verify
The job's "Set up job" log shows `Runner Image: ubuntu-24.04` (or 22.04).

## Sources
- https://github.blog/changelog/2025-01-15-github-actions-ubuntu-20-runner-image-brownout-dates-and-other-breaking-changes/
- https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/11101

title: PostgreSQL 18: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) without STORED now makes a VIRTUAL column, not a stored one
body:
## Symptom
On PostgreSQL 18, a column declared `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)` with no keyword is computed on read instead of being written to disk. Expressions that call your own SQL functions or use custom types are rejected, and the column is not sent over logical replication. Before 18, `STORED` was the only kind and had to be written out, so older DDL always says `STORED`; newer hand-written or generated DDL may omit it.

## Cause
PostgreSQL 18 (2025-09-25) added virtual generated columns and made them the default kind. Docs: "A generated column is by default of the virtual kind. Use the keywords VIRTUAL or STORED to make the choice explicit." Virtual columns may only use built-in functions and types, and logical replication of generated columns (`publish_generated_columns`) currently supports only stored ones.

## Fix
Be explicit:
```sql
-- materialized on write (pre-18 behaviour)
height_in numeric GENERATED ALWAYS AS (height_cm / 2.54) STORED
-- computed on read, no storage
height_in numeric GENERATED ALWAYS AS (height_cm / 2.54) VIRTUAL
```
Use `STORED` when the expression uses user-defined functions/types, when the column must be replicated, or when you want to pay the cost on write.

## Verify
`SELECT attname, attgenerated FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'people'::regclass AND attgenerated <> '';` returns `s` for stored, `v` for virtual.

## Sources
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-generated-columns.html

title: ESLint 10 looks up eslint.config.* from each linted file's directory, not the cwd — affects monorepos
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to ESLint 10, running `npx eslint .` from a monorepo root lints `packages/*/src` files with each package's own `eslint.config.js` instead of the root config (or vice versa), so results change between v9 and v10. Scripts still passing `--flag v10_config_lookup_from_file` now error out.

## Cause
In ESLint v9 the config file was located starting from the current working directory. v9 offered the alternate behaviour behind the `v10_config_lookup_from_file` feature flag. ESLint v10.0.0 (2026-02-06) made it the default: ESLint searches for `eslint.config.*` starting from the directory of each linted file and walking up toward the filesystem root. The feature flag was removed, and passing it is now an error.

## Fix
- Remove the old flag everywhere: `--flag v10_config_lookup_from_file` on the CLI, the `ESLINT_FLAGS` env var, and the `flags` array passed to `new ESLint()` / `new Linter()` (`npx codemod @eslint/v9-to-v10` does this).
- If you want one config for the whole repo (old cwd-based behaviour), pass it explicitly:
```bash
npx eslint --config ./eslint.config.js .
```
- Otherwise, make sure each package's `eslint.config.js` is complete on its own (it no longer inherits anything from the root unless it imports it):
```js
// packages/web/eslint.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'eslint/config'
import root from '../../eslint.config.js'
export default defineConfig([root, { rules: { 'no-console': 'off' } }])
```
Also required for v10: Node.js 20.19+, 22.13+ or 24+ (Node < 20.19, 21 and 23 are unsupported), including the Node your editor's ESLint extension uses.

## Verify
`npx eslint --print-config packages/web/src/index.js` shows the config you expect for that file.

## Sources
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/migrate-to-10.0.0
- https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/

title: A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in NumPy 2.x as it may crash — upgrade the compiled package
error: A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in NumPy 2.0.1 as it may crash. To support both 1.x and 2.x versions of NumPy, modules must be compiled with NumPy 2.0.
body:
## Symptom
On import (often of torch, bottleneck, onnxruntime, older pandas/scipy wheels, Spyder kernels) you see:

```
A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in
NumPy 2.0.1 as it may crash. To support both 1.x and 2.x
versions of NumPy, modules must be compiled with NumPy 2.0.
Some module may need to rebuild instead e.g. with 'pybind11>=2.12'.
```
sometimes followed by `ImportError` or `_ARRAY_API not found`. The version in the message matches whatever 2.x is installed.

## Cause
NumPy 2.0 (2024-06-16) broke the C ABI. Any extension built against 1.x headers cannot load under 2.x. Extensions built against 2.x work on both 1.x and 2.x.

## Fix
Read the traceback to find the *compiled* package being imported, then:
```bash
pip install -U <that-package>        # a release built against NumPy 2
# stop-gap if no such release exists:
pip install "numpy<2"
```
If you build the extension yourself: build against NumPy >= 2.0 (and pybind11 >= 2.12); the resulting wheel runs on both 1.x and 2.x. Make sure you are changing the same environment the failing interpreter uses (`python -m pip`, not a bare `pip`).

## Verify
`python -c "import numpy, <pkg>; print(numpy.__version__, <pkg>.__version__)"` imports without the warning.

## Sources
- https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html
- https://github.com/spyder-ide/spyder/issues/22281

title: `params` should be awaited before using its properties: sync params/searchParams/cookies() fully removed in Next.js 16
error: `params` should be awaited before using its properties.
body:
## Symptom Next.js 15 logged in dev: `Route "/[lang]/blog/[slug]" used `params.lang`. `params` should be awaited before using its properties. Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/sync-dynamic-apis`. In Next.js 16 the sync compatibility layer is gone. `params.slug` is `undefined` (it is a Promise), TypeScript rejects the types, and `cookies().get(...)` / `headers().get(...)` no longer work without `await`. ## Cause Next.js 15 made the request APIs async and kept a temporary sync shim that only warned. Next.js 16 (2025-10-21) removed the shim, so these must be accessed asynchronously: - `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()` from `next/headers` - `params` in layout/page/route/default and in opengraph-image/twitter-image/icon/apple-icon - `searchParams` in page The same applies to enumerating them (`{...params}`, `Object.keys(params)`, `for (const c of cookies())`). ## Fix Run the codemod. The `upgrade` codemod does NOT run it for you: ```bash npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api . ``` Before: ```tsx export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) { const token = cookies().get('token') return

{params.slug}

} ``` After (Server Component): ```tsx import { cookies } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { const { slug } = await props.params const query = await props.searchParams const token = (await cookies()).get('token') return

{slug}

} ``` Client Components cannot be async, so use `React.use(params)`. Run `npx next typegen` (15.5+) to get the global `PageProps`, `LayoutProps` and `RouteContext` helpers. Do not destructure `params` in the function signature. Look for `@next-codemod-error` comments the codemod left behind, because they fail dev and build until you resolve them. ## Verify `next build` passes type checking, and `grep -rn "@next-codemod-error\|UnsafeUnwrapped" app/` returns nothing. ## Sources - https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#async-request-apis-breaking-change - https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/sync-dynamic-apis - https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/74406 - https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: Cannot use `export let` in runes mode — use `$props()` instead (Svelte 5)
error: Cannot use `export let` in runes mode — use `$props()` instead
body:
## Symptom
Svelte 5 compiler error `legacy_export_invalid`:
```
Cannot use `export let` in runes mode — use `$props()` instead
```
This happens when a component uses a rune such as `$state`, `$derived` or `$props` (which switches it to runes mode) and also declares props the Svelte 3/4 way with `export let`. `$$props` / `$$restProps` raise similar errors (`Cannot use `$$props` in runes mode`).

## Cause
Svelte 5 (2024-10-22) declares all props through one `$props()` destructure. Svelte 4 syntax only compiles in components that use no runes at all (legacy mode), and a single file cannot mix the two styles.

## Fix
```svelte
<!-- before (Svelte 4) -->
<script>
  export let required;
  export let optional = 'unset';
  let klass = '';
  export { klass as class };
</script>
<button class={klass} {...$$restProps}>click</button>

<!-- after (Svelte 5) -->
<script>
  let { required, optional = 'unset', class: klass, ...rest } = $props();
</script>
<button class={klass} {...rest}>click</button>
```
For TypeScript: `let { required, optional = 'unset' }: { required: string; optional?: string } = $props();`. Use `$bindable()` as the default value for props the parent binds with `bind:`.

To migrate a whole project automatically, run `npx sv migrate svelte-5`.

## Verify
`npx svelte-check` reports no `legacy_export_invalid` errors, and the parent still passes props.

## Sources
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/compiler-errors
- https://svelte.dev/blog/svelte-5-is-alive

title: Building a UI over `claude -p --output-format stream-json`: tool results arrive in type:"user" events
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imghdr' on Python 3.13 — use Pillow/filetype/puremagic instead
error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imghdr'
body:
## Symptom
On Python 3.13+ an import chain fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imghdr'` (seen in TensorBoard, tweepy, PGPy, beets mediafile, Medusa).

## Cause
`imghdr` (and `sndhdr`) were deprecated in 3.11 and **removed in Python 3.13** (PEP 594). No stdlib replacement exists.

## Fix
1. Upgrade the dependency first (e.g. TensorBoard 2.20.0 replaced `imghdr` with Pillow-based MIME detection).
2. In your own code:

```python
# before
import imghdr
kind = imghdr.what(path)

# after (Pillow already installed)
from PIL import Image
with Image.open(path) as im:
    kind = im.format.lower()       # 'png', 'jpeg', ...

# or: pip install puremagic
import puremagic
kind = puremagic.what(path)       # documented replacement for imghdr.what()
```

3. Stop-gap: `pip install standard-imghdr` restores a module named `imghdr`.

## Verify
`python -c "import yourpkg"` succeeds on 3.13; `grep -rn "import imghdr" .` returns nothing in your tree.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html
- https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorboard/issues/6964

title: error: externally-managed-environment — pip refuses to install into Homebrew/Debian/uv-managed Python
error: error: externally-managed-environment
body:
## Symptom
```
error: externally-managed-environment

× This environment is externally managed
╰─> To install Python packages system-wide, try brew install
...
note: If you believe this is a mistake, please contact your Python installation or OS distribution provider.
```
Appears for `pip install x` (and `pip install --user x`) on Homebrew Python, Debian 12+/Ubuntu 23.04+, Fedora 38+ system Python.

## Cause
PEP 668: the distributor ships an `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker file next to the stdlib, and pip refuses to modify that environment so it cannot break OS/Homebrew-managed packages. `--user` does not bypass it (Homebrew closed that as working-as-intended).

## Fix
Pick one; never `sudo pip`:
```bash
# project dependencies: a venv
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install requests
# or with uv
uv venv && uv pip install requests        # or: uv init && uv add requests

# CLI tools: isolated tool envs
uv tool install ruff        # or: pipx install ruff

# one-off script with deps
uv run --with requests script.py
```
Last resort (may break the system/Homebrew Python): `pip install --break-system-packages --user x`.

## Verify
`python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix)"` prints `True` inside the venv, and the install succeeds there.

## Sources
- https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/externally-managed-environments/
- https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/issues/188369

title: Supabase Storage download() returns stale JSON for up to an hour (Smart CDN, cf-cache-status HIT): use cacheNonce
body:
## Symptom
An app kept small JSON ledgers (HR records, rosters and so on) as files in a Supabase Storage bucket, doing read-modify-write via `supabase.storage.from('uploads').download(path)`. A user saved an entry, but the app did not show it. Production was reading a version of the file that was 23 hours old, right after the write had landed.

## Cause
Storage downloads go through Supabase's Smart CDN. The responses carried `cache-control: public, max-age=3600` and `cf-cache-status: HIT`, so the server's own reads came back cached. Read-modify-write on a stale copy can also silently drop earlier writes.

## Fix
Pass a cache-busting nonce on reads of mutable objects. storage-js supports it natively:
```ts
const { data } = await supabase.storage.from('uploads')
  .download(path, { cacheNonce: Date.now().toString() });
```
The fix proxied `storage.from().download` once in the shared client and added `cacheNonce` for `*.json` paths only, so images still benefit from the CDN.

## Verify
With the nonce, the response header showed `cf-cache-status: MISS`, and the user's exact flow (save an entry, reload) showed the new data at once.

## Notes
This only fixes staleness. Read-modify-write of a JSON blob across several app workers can still lose concurrent writes (an in-process lock is per worker). The durable fix is to move mutable records into Postgres tables.

title: Go 1.25 GOMAXPROCS follows the container CPU limit (cgroup) and updates at runtime; drop automaxprocs
body:
## Symptom
After moving to Go 1.25, a service in Kubernetes reports a lower `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0)` than the node's CPU count, throughput or latency profiles change, and it changes again when CPU limits are resized. Many codebases still import `go.uber.org/automaxprocs` to get this behaviour.

## Cause
Go 1.25 (2025-08-12) made the default GOMAXPROCS container-aware: on Linux it uses the cgroup CPU bandwidth limit (the Kubernetes CPU *limit*, not the request) when it is lower than the logical CPU count, and on all OSes the runtime periodically updates GOMAXPROCS when CPU count or limit changes. Both are disabled if you set `GOMAXPROCS` via env or `runtime.GOMAXPROCS`.

## Fix
- Usually: do nothing, and remove `automaxprocs` (and any `GOMAXPROCS` env var that only mirrored the limit) so the runtime can track resizes.
- Pods with only CPU requests and no limit still get GOMAXPROCS = node CPUs; set `GOMAXPROCS` explicitly if you want fewer.
- To restore old behaviour: `GODEBUG=containermaxprocs=0,updatemaxprocs=0`, or for modules `godebug containermaxprocs=0` in go.mod.

## Verify
Log `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0)` at startup; it tracks the pod CPU limit rather than the node CPU count (or equals the CPU count when there is no limit).

## Sources
- https://go.dev/doc/go1.25

title: SQLAlchemy 2.0 removed engine.execute(), raw SQL strings, implicit autocommit and select([...]) list syntax
body:
## Symptom
Code in the 1.3/1.4 style fails on SQLAlchemy 2.x: `engine.execute(...)` does not exist, `conn.execute("SELECT 1")` with a plain string is rejected, INSERTs "succeed" but are never committed, and `select([table.c.id])` errors.

## Cause
SQLAlchemy 2.0 (2023-01-26) removed the legacy APIs that 1.4 flagged with `RemovedIn20Warning`, e.g.: "The Engine.execute() function/method is considered legacy as of the 1.x series of SQLAlchemy and will be removed in 2.0"; "Passing a string to Connection.execute() is deprecated and will be removed in version 2.0. Use the text() construct, or the Connection.exec_driver_sql() method"; "Implicit autocommit will be removed in SQLAlchemy 2.0."

## Fix
```python
# before (1.x)
engine.execute("INSERT INTO foo (id) VALUES (1)")
rows = engine.execute(select([foo.c.id])).fetchall()

# after (2.x)
from sqlalchemy import text, select
with engine.begin() as conn:                     # commits on success
    conn.execute(text("INSERT INTO foo (id) VALUES (:id)"), {"id": 1})
with engine.connect() as conn:
    rows = conn.execute(select(foo.c.id)).all()
    conn.commit()                                # explicit when using connect()

# ORM
with Session(engine) as s:
    users = s.scalars(select(User).where(User.name == "x")).all()   # replaces s.query(User).filter(...)
```
To find remaining issues, run on 1.4 with `SQLALCHEMY_WARN_20=1 python -W always::DeprecationWarning ...` before upgrading.

## Verify
Tests pass on SQLAlchemy 2.x with `-W error::sqlalchemy.exc.SADeprecationWarning`.

## Sources
- https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/changelog/migration_20.html

title: Nuxt 4: srcDir defaults to app/ — pages/components/composables go in app/, server/ and public/ stay at root, ~ = app/
body:
## Symptom
In a new Nuxt 4 project (created with `npm create nuxt@latest`), an agent creates `pages/index.vue`, `components/Foo.vue` or `composables/useX.ts` at the project root, as in Nuxt 3. Pages and components then go undetected because `app/` exists and is the srcDir. A related mistake is creating `app/server/api/...`, which is not picked up because `server/` belongs at the root. Imports such as `~/components/...` resolve to `app/components/...`.

## Cause
Nuxt 4.0 (2025-07-15) made `app/` the default `srcDir`. `serverDir` defaults to `<rootDir>/server`. `layers/`, `modules/`, `public/` and `content/` resolve from the root, and the new `shared/` directory (auto-imports `shared/utils` and `shared/types`) also lives at the root. Nuxt auto-detects the old v3 layout when there is no `app/` directory, so existing projects keep working. Mixing the two layouts breaks.

## Fix
Target layout:
```
app/
  assets/ components/ composables/ layouts/ middleware/ pages/ plugins/ utils/
  app.vue  error.vue  app.config.ts  router.options.ts
server/   (api/ routes/ middleware/ plugins/ utils/)
shared/   (utils/ types/)
public/  layers/  modules/  content/
nuxt.config.ts
```
Migrate automatically with `npx codemod@latest nuxt/4/file-structure`, or the full recipe with `npx codemod@0.18.7 nuxt/4/migration-recipe`. To keep the v3 layout explicitly:
```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  srcDir: '.',
  dir: { app: 'app' },
})
```
Update tool configs (Tailwind `content` globs, ESLint) to point at `app/`.

## Verify
`npx nuxi dev` serves the pages, and `.nuxt/types` lists the auto-imported components from `app/components`.

## Sources
- https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/upgrade
- https://nuxt.com/blog/v4

title: macOS LaunchAgent can't connect to LAN devices (Local Network privacy); an IP_BOUND_IF-bound socket works
error: CONNECT FAIL
body:
## Symptom
A data collector worked when run from Terminal but not as a LaunchAgent. Under launchd, a C helper binary that did a plain `connect()` to a machine on the LAN (`192.168.x.x`, TCP 683) failed every time ("CONNECT FAIL"). Python reads in the same job that used a socket bound to a specific interface kept working.

## Cause
macOS Local Network privacy restricts background processes started by launchd from connecting to local-network addresses unless the responsible app has been granted the permission. Terminal had the permission, the launchd job did not, and no prompt appears for a background job.

## Fix used
Relay the helper's traffic through the Python process, whose outbound socket is bound to the LAN interface with `IP_BOUND_IF`:
```python
import socket
IP_BOUND_IF = 25                      # macOS <netinet/in.h>
idx = socket.if_nametoindex('en9')
def bound_socket(timeout):
    s = socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_IP, IP_BOUND_IF, idx)
    s.settimeout(timeout); return s
# listen on 127.0.0.1:<high port>, accept the helper, connect bound_socket() to the device, pump bytes both ways
```
The helper was rebuilt to take a port argument and connect to `127.0.0.1:<high port>`.

## Dead end
Listening on `127.0.0.1:683` (the device's own low port) as a normal user failed with `PermissionError: [Errno 13]`. Since Mojave, macOS lets non-root users bind ports below 1024 only on the wildcard address, not on a specific address such as loopback.

## Verify
After the relay change, all three devices behind the helper reported live status from the LaunchAgent alongside the others.

title: [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true — Node 24 spawn/execFile
error: [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.
body:
## Symptom
On Node 24+, CLIs and scripts print `(node:PID) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.` Typical trigger is the cross-platform idiom agents write to run `npm`/`npx` on Windows: `spawn('npm', ['install', pkg], { shell: true })`.

## Cause
DEP0190: when an `args` array is passed to `child_process.spawn`/`execFile` with `shell: true` (or a shell path), Node only space-joins the args — no escaping — which allows shell injection. Documentation-only in v23.11.0 / v22.15.0, runtime deprecation in Node 24.0.0 (2025-05-06, PR #57199).

## Fix
Prefer no shell:
```diff
- spawn('git', ['commit', '-m', msg], { shell: true });
+ spawn('git', ['commit', '-m', msg]);
```
If a shell is genuinely needed (pipes, redirection, or Windows `.cmd` shims like `npm.cmd`/`npx.cmd`, which Node refuses to spawn without a shell since the CVE-2024-27980 fix), pass a single command string and no args array, and only include values you control or have validated/quoted for that shell:
```diff
- spawn('npm', ['install', pkg], { shell: true });
+ if (!/^[@\w./-]+$/.test(pkg)) throw new Error('bad package name');
+ spawn(`npm install ${pkg}`, { shell: true, stdio: 'inherit' });
```
If the warning comes from a dependency, upgrade it (e.g. Storybook closed its report via PR #32382).

## Verify
`node --trace-deprecation script.js` shows no DEP0190.

## Sources
- https://nodejs.org/api/deprecations.html
- https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/32376

title: Mixing old (on:click) and new syntaxes for event handling is not allowed — Svelte 5 uses onclick + callback props
error: Mixing old (on:%name%) and new syntaxes for event handling is not allowed. Use only the on%name% syntax
body:
## Symptom
Svelte 5 compiler error `mixed_event_handler_syntaxes` (for example `Mixing old (on:click) and new syntaxes for event handling is not allowed. Use only the onclick syntax`) in a component that has both `on:click={...}` and `onclick={...}`. Event modifiers like `on:click|preventDefault` have no equivalent in the new syntax. `createEventDispatcher` is deprecated.

## Cause
In Svelte 5 (2024-10-22), DOM event handlers are plain properties (`onclick`), and component events are callback props. The `on:` directive, event modifiers and `createEventDispatcher` are deprecated, and one component cannot mix the old and new syntax. Duplicate handlers (`on:click={a} on:click={b}`) are not allowed either.

## Fix
DOM events:
```svelte
<!-- before -->
<button on:click|preventDefault={handler}>Save</button>
<!-- after -->
<button onclick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); handler(e); }}>Save</button>
```
Component events (child):
```svelte
<!-- before -->
<script>
  import { createEventDispatcher } from 'svelte';
  const dispatch = createEventDispatcher();
</script>
<button on:click={() => dispatch('inflate', 5)}>inflate</button>

<!-- after -->
<script>
  let { inflate } = $props();
</script>
<button onclick={() => inflate(5)}>inflate</button>
```
Parent: `<Pump on:inflate={(e) => size += e.detail} />` becomes `<Pump inflate={(power) => size += power} />`. The payload is passed directly instead of through `.detail`. To forward an element event, accept an `onclick` prop and spread `{...props}` (put local handlers after the spread). Use `onclickcapture` for capture.

## Verify
`npx svelte-check` passes, and `grep -rn "on:" src --include=*.svelte` only matches components you have deliberately left in legacy mode.

## Sources
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide
- https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/compiler-errors

title: Pydantic v1 → v2 renames: .dict()→model_dump(), parse_obj→model_validate, orm_mode→from_attributes, @validator
body:
## Symptom
Older models generate Pydantic v1 code; on v2 it raises deprecation warnings or errors: `.dict()`, `.json()`, `parse_obj`, `from_orm`, `class Config: orm_mode = True`, `@validator`, `@root_validator`, `Field(regex=...)`, `__root__` fields. A subtle one: `Optional[str]` without a default is now **required**.

## Cause
Pydantic V2 rewrote the API (pydantic-core). V1 names are deprecated or removed.

## Fix
| V1 | V2 |
|---|---|
| `m.dict()` / `m.json()` | `m.model_dump()` / `m.model_dump_json()` |
| `M.parse_obj(d)` / `M.parse_raw(s)` | `M.model_validate(d)` / `M.model_validate_json(s)` |
| `M.from_orm(obj)` + `orm_mode = True` | `M.model_validate(obj)` + `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` |
| `m.copy()` / `M.construct()` | `m.model_copy()` / `M.model_construct()` |
| `M.schema()` / `update_forward_refs()` | `M.model_json_schema()` / `model_rebuild()` |
| `M.__fields__` | `M.model_fields` |
| `@validator('x')` / `@root_validator` | `@field_validator('x')` / `@model_validator(mode='after')` |
| `@validate_arguments` | `@validate_call` |
| `Field(regex=...)`, `allow_mutation`, `const` | `Field(pattern=...)`, `frozen`, `Literal[...]` |
| `__root__: list[int]` | `class M(RootModel[list[int]])` |
| `allow_population_by_field_name` | `populate_by_name` (or `validate_by_name` from 2.11) |
| `anystr_strip_whitespace` | `str_strip_whitespace` |

```python
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, field_validator
class User(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
    name: str
    nickname: Optional[str] = None   # v2: needs '= None' to be optional
    @field_validator("name")
    @classmethod
    def strip(cls, v: str) -> str:
        return v.strip()
User.model_validate(orm_row).model_dump()
```
Automate most of it: `pip install bump-pydantic && bump-pydantic my_package`.

## Verify
`python -W error::DeprecationWarning -m pytest` passes (Pydantic emits `PydanticDeprecatedSince20` for V1 names).

## Sources
- https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/

title: Anthropic code_execution_20250522 + code-execution-2025-05-22 beta is legacy — use code_execution_20250825+
body:
## Symptom
An agent copies the May 2025 example: `{"type": "code_execution_20250522", "name": "code_execution"}` with header `anthropic-beta: code-execution-2025-05-22`, then parses `code_execution_result` blocks. It works for Python only and misses Bash/file features; newer web_search/web_fetch versions refuse to pair with it.

## Cause
The Python-only `code_execution_20250522` is legacy. Current versions need no beta header: `code_execution_20250825` (Bash + file operations), `code_execution_20260120` (adds REPL state persistence and programmatic tool calling), `code_execution_20260521` (same runtime; tells Claude about the 90 s per-cell limit). `web_search_20260209` / `web_fetch_20260209` and later require `code_execution_20260120` or later.

## Fix
```diff
- "type": "code_execution_20250522"
+ "type": "code_execution_20250825"   # or code_execution_20260521 for PTC
```
Remove `code-execution-2025-05-22` from `anthropic-beta`. Update response parsing: results now arrive as `bash_code_execution_result` and `text_editor_code_execution_*_result` instead of `code_execution_result`.

## Verify
Response contains `bash_code_execution_tool_result` blocks; no beta header in the request.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool

title: ITMS-90725: since 2026-04-28 App Store uploads must be built with Xcode 26 and an iOS 26-family SDK
error: ITMS-90725
body:
## Symptom
An iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS build uploaded to App Store Connect or TestFlight is flagged with ITMS-90725 (SDK version) or rejected because it was built with Xcode 16 / the iOS 18 SDK. CI images or engine toolchains pinned to Xcode 16 are the usual cause.

## Cause
Apple's SDK minimum requirement, in effect **since 2026-04-28**: "Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an SDK for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, or watchOS 26." The previous floor (since 2025-04-24) was Xcode 16 / iOS 18 SDK. A user report on the Unreal Engine forums shows a build stamped with the iOS 18.1 SDK triggering ITMS-90725 after the deadline.

## Fix
- Build with Xcode 26. On GitHub-hosted macOS runners select it explicitly, e.g. `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_26.<x>.app` (check the runner image's installed list).
- Your **deployment target** (minimum iOS your users need) is independent; keep `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` as low as you support.
- For engines/frameworks (React Native/Expo, Flutter, Unity, Unreal, Capacitor) upgrade to a version validated with Xcode 26 and confirm the produced binary's SDK.

## Verify
`xcodebuild -version` prints Xcode 26.x in CI; in the built app, `plutil -p Payload/App.app/Info.plist | grep DTSDKName` shows an `iphoneos26` SDK.

## Sources
- https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/
- https://developer.apple.com/app-store/submitting/
- https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/ios-26-sdk-app-store-submission/2717478

title: AutoCAD headless plot: monochrome.ctb does not blacken true-color entities; _Window plot area yields blank PDFs
body:
## Symptom
DWG -> PDF plots were run with `accoreconsole.exe /i in.dwg /s job.scr` and a LISP routine, using `DWG To PDF.pc3` and `monochrome.ctb`. Two problems showed up:
1. Some frames and title blocks still came out cyan or colored even though monochrome.ctb was selected.
2. On some DWGs, plotting a computed window (`_W` with two corners) produced a blank PDF.

## Cause
1. monochrome.ctb maps ACI index colors to black. Entities that carry a **true color** (DXF group 420) or a color-book color (430) bypass it.
2. Window plotting was unreliable on some drawings. Extents plotting was not.

## Fix
Before plotting, strip true color from every entity (and set layers to 7):
```lisp
(defun SY-BLACK (e / d)
  (setq d (entget e))
  (if (or (assoc 420 d) (assoc 430 d)) (progn
    (if (assoc 420 d) (setq d (vl-remove (assoc 420 d) d)))
    (if (assoc 430 d) (setq d (vl-remove (assoc 430 d) d)))
    (if (assoc 62 d) (setq d (subst (cons 62 7) (assoc 62 d) d))
                     (setq d (append d (list (cons 62 7)))))
    (vl-catch-all-apply 'entmod (list d)))))
```
To plot only the drawing frame, ERASE everything outside it, then `ZOOM E` and plot **Extents**:
```lisp
(command "_.ZOOM" "_E")
(command "_-PLOT" "_Y" "Model" "DWG To PDF.pc3" paper "_M" orient "_N" "_E" "_F" "_C"
         "_Y" "monochrome.ctb" "_Y" "_A" outPdf "_N" "_Y")
```
Pick orientation from EXTMIN/EXTMAX (w >= h -> `_L`) and the paper from the larger side. Save the `.scr` in the system ANSI code page (GBK on Chinese Windows), not UTF-8, when it contains non-ASCII paths.

## Verify
A 35-file test pack (27 DWG + 8 DXF) plotted with no colored leftovers and no blank pages, at 1.5–4.4 s per file with 6 concurrent accoreconsole slots.

## Notes
accoreconsole also resets FILEDIA to 0 in the user profile on exit. Restore it afterwards (see the related FILEDIA entry).

title: macOS Screen & System Audio Recording permission lost on every rebuild of ad-hoc signed app; sign with stable identity
body:
## Symptom
A small Swift app built from a script (`swiftc` plus a hand-assembled `.app` bundle) captured system audio with ScreenCaptureKit. After every rebuild, macOS treated it as a new app. Capture returned nothing, or the permission prompt reappeared, even though the app was already enabled under Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording.

## Cause
TCC keys the grant on the app's code signature (designated requirement). Ad-hoc signatures (`codesign -s -`) or unsigned builds get a new cdhash on every build, so the old grant no longer matches.

## Fix
Sign every build with the same real identity, e.g. a free Apple Development certificate:
```bash
codesign --force --deep --options runtime \
  -s "Apple Development: Your Name (TEAMID)" MyApp.app
codesign -dv --verbose=2 MyApp.app   # check Authority= line
```
Grant the permission once after the first signed build. Later rebuilds keep it.

## Verify
After switching the build script to sign with the development certificate, the app was rebuilt many times during a day and capture kept working with no new prompts.

## Notes
For testing without permissions, give the app a `--file input.aiff` mode that runs the same pipeline on a recorded file.

title: Moving ~/.colima (or any VM sparse disk) to an HFS+ external drive inflates it to full size
body:
## Symptom
Offloading `~/.colima` (or a Docker/VM data dir) to an external SSD with `rsync -a` or `cp` and symlinking it back: the copy keeps growing far past the space it used on the internal disk (e.g. 33 GB and climbing for a 100 GB virtual disk that was ~11 GB on APFS).

## Cause
The VM's datadisk is a **sparse file**. APFS stores it sparsely, but **HFS+ has no sparse-file support**, so every hole is written out as zeros on the destination. (`rsync -S` cannot help — the destination filesystem can't represent holes.)

## Fix
Archive instead of copying, or format the external drive as APFS:
```bash
cd ~ && tar -czf /Volumes/Ext/colima.tar.gz .colima   # compressed, holes compress to nothing
# restore later (needs free space for the real data size)
cd ~ && tar -xzf /Volumes/Ext/colima.tar.gz
```
Check the destination format first: `diskutil info /Volumes/Ext | grep 'File System Personality'`.

## Verify
The archive was ~5 GB for an 11 GB real disk; restored VM boots.

## Notes
macOS's bundled `openrsync` also failed with `--remove-source-files` to that drive; verify copies with `cmp` and delete separately.

title: Jest 30: toBeCalled / toBeCalledWith / toReturn / toThrowError aliases removed — use toHaveBeenCalled, toThrow
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Jest 30, tests that use `expect(fn).toBeCalled()`, `toBeCalledWith()`, `toThrowError()` and similar fail at runtime with a TypeError saying the matcher is not a function, or fail to type-check. Models trained on older code still generate these names.

## Cause
Jest 30.0.0 (2025-06-04) removed all matcher aliases (PR #14632). They had been deprecated since Jest 26. The behaviour of the canonical matchers is unchanged; only the names differ.

## Fix
Search and replace:

| removed | use |
|---|---|
| `toBeCalled()` | `toHaveBeenCalled()` |
| `toBeCalledTimes(n)` | `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` |
| `toBeCalledWith(a)` | `toHaveBeenCalledWith(a)` |
| `lastCalledWith(a)` | `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(a)` |
| `nthCalledWith(n, a)` | `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(n, a)` |
| `toReturn()` | `toHaveReturned()` |
| `toReturnTimes(n)` | `toHaveReturnedTimes(n)` |
| `toReturnWith(v)` | `toHaveReturnedWith(v)` |
| `lastReturnedWith(v)` | `toHaveLastReturnedWith(v)` |
| `nthReturnedWith(n, v)` | `toHaveNthReturnedWith(n, v)` |
| `toThrowError(msg)` | `toThrow(msg)` |

```ts
// before
expect(() => parse('x')).toThrowError('bad input');
expect(spy).toBeCalledWith(1);
// after
expect(() => parse('x')).toThrow('bad input');
expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1);
```
The `eslint-plugin-jest` rule `jest/no-alias-methods` can autofix these names.

In Jest 30 the types for `toHaveBeenCalledWith` also infer the mocked function's parameter types, so arguments with the wrong type can now cause TypeScript errors.

## Verify
`grep -rnE '\.(toBeCalled|toBeCalledTimes|toBeCalledWith|lastCalledWith|nthCalledWith|toReturn|toReturnTimes|toReturnWith|lastReturnedWith|nthReturnedWith|toThrowError)\(' src` returns nothing, and the suite passes.

## Sources
- https://jestjs.io/docs/upgrading-to-jest30
- https://github.com/jestjs/jest/releases/tag/v30.0.0

title: Clerk: createRouteMatcher() is deprecated (@clerk/nextjs 7.6) — protect each page/route/action instead of in proxy
body:
## Symptom
The standard Clerk pattern `const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]); export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => { if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect() })` logs a one-time deprecation warning in development. Agents keep generating it as the recommended setup.

## Cause
`@clerk/nextjs` 7.6.0 (2026-07-23) changelog: "Deprecate `createRouteMatcher()` in favor of resource-based auth checks." It still works, but will be removed in the next major. Clerk's reason: Server Functions (Server Actions) are invoked by ID, not by path, so path matching in middleware/proxy can't reliably protect them.

## Fix
Keep `clerkMiddleware()`, since Clerk needs it, but move auth gates to each resource:
```ts
// app/dashboard/page.tsx
import { auth } from "@clerk/nextjs/server"
export default async function Page() {
  await auth.protect()
  …
}
// server action
"use server"
export async function save() {
  const { userId } = await auth.protect()
  …
}
```
For non-auth path logic in the proxy, use `config.matcher` and `req.nextUrl.pathname` instead of `createRouteMatcher`. Clerk ships `@clerk/eslint-plugin` with the rule `@clerk/next/require-auth-protection` (ESLint 9+ flat config) plus a Bulk Fixer CLI to find and fix unprotected App Router resources.

## Verify
The lint rule passes. Calling a server action directly while signed out is rejected.

## Sources
- https://clerk.com/docs/guides/development/upgrading/upgrade-guides/migrate-from-create-route-matcher
- https://github.com/clerk/javascript/blob/main/packages/nextjs/CHANGELOG.md

title: PydanticImportError: `BaseSettings` has been moved to the `pydantic-settings` package
error: pydantic.errors.PydanticImportError: `BaseSettings` has been moved to the `pydantic-settings` package.
body:
## Symptom
```
pydantic.errors.PydanticImportError: `BaseSettings` has been moved to the `pydantic-settings` package.
See https://docs.pydantic.dev/2.6/migration/#basesettings-has-moved-to-pydantic-settings for more details.
```
Raised by `from pydantic import BaseSettings` in your code or in an older dependency (chromadb, mlserver, llama-cpp-python server, emmet) once pydantic 2.x gets installed.

## Cause
Pydantic V2 moved settings management into a separate distribution, `pydantic-settings`. Models also changed: `class Config` -> `model_config`.

## Fix
```bash
pip install pydantic-settings      # or: uv add pydantic-settings
```
```python
# before (pydantic v1)
from pydantic import BaseSettings
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    api_key: str
    class Config:
        env_prefix = "APP_"
        env_file = ".env"

# after (pydantic v2)
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="APP_", env_file=".env")
    api_key: str
```
If the import is inside a dependency, upgrade that dependency to a pydantic-v2 release; pinning `pydantic<2` is only a stop-gap (and V1 has Python 3.14 caveats).

## Verify
`python -c "from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings; import pydantic; print(pydantic.VERSION)"`.

## Sources
- https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/
- https://github.com/SeldonIO/MLServer/issues/1594

title: SpeechAnalyzer: SFSpeechErrorDomain Code=2 "Audio input timestamp overlaps or precedes prior audio input"
error: Error Domain=SFSpeechErrorDomain Code=2 "Audio input timestamp overlaps or precedes prior audio input"
body:
## Symptom
A live transcription pipeline on macOS 26 (ScreenCaptureKit / file audio -> `AVAudioConverter` to `SpeechAnalyzer.bestAvailableAudioFormat(...)` -> `AsyncStream<AnalyzerInput>` -> `SpeechAnalyzer` + `SpeechTranscriber`) produces no text; the results loop throws:
`speech results error: Error Domain=SFSpeechErrorDomain Code=2 "Audio input timestamp overlaps or precedes prior audio input"`

## Cause
Every chunk was yielded as `AnalyzerInput(buffer: out, bufferStartTime: CMTime(seconds: captureTime, preferredTimescale: 48000))`. After resampling, output chunk lengths jitter by a few frames relative to the capture timestamps, so a chunk's start time can fall slightly before the end of the previous chunk. The analyzer rejects any overlap and stops.

## Fix
Track the end of audio already handed to the analyzer; pass an explicit start time only after a real gap, otherwise let the input be contiguous (no timestamp):
```swift
private var outClock = -1.0   // seconds of audio already handed over
...
let dur = Double(out.frameLength) / out.format.sampleRate
if outClock < 0 || at > outClock + 0.25 {          // first chunk or a real gap
    let st = max(at, outClock)
    cont.yield(AnalyzerInput(buffer: out, bufferStartTime: CMTime(seconds: st, preferredTimescale: 48000)))
    outClock = st + dur
} else {
    cont.yield(AnalyzerInput(buffer: out))             // contiguous
    outClock += dur
}
```

## Verify
The same test file (`say -o q.aiff ...`, fed at real-time speed) then transcribed fully; live system audio produced finalized phrases ~0.13-0.4 s after speech stopped.

title: Claude Code silently deletes session transcripts after 30 days (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl); set cleanupPeriodDays
body:
## Symptom
Older Claude Code session transcripts were missing. The oldest `.jsonl` under `~/.claude/projects/` was only about a month old, and everything before that was gone. Nothing announces the deletion.

## Cause
Claude Code cleans up local session transcripts on a retention period, `cleanupPeriodDays`, which defaults to 30 days. Anyone relying on transcripts for search, audits, resuming old sessions or mining past work loses them without notice.

## Fix
Set a long retention in user settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`, or the settings.json in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if you use one):
```bash
cp ~/.claude/settings.json ~/.claude/settings.json.bak
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, os
p = os.path.expanduser('~/.claude/settings.json')
d = json.load(open(p)); d['cleanupPeriodDays'] = 36500
json.dump(d, open(p, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
EOF
grep cleanupPeriodDays ~/.claude/settings.json
```
Already-deleted transcripts can only come back from backups such as Time Machine.

## Verify
The setting was written and read back (`"cleanupPeriodDays": 36500`). Transcripts from that point on stayed (the archive kept growing, about 1.3 GB at the time).

## Notes
- Transcripts include full tool output, so plan for disk growth (a few GB/year for heavy use) and back them up.
- Sessions run on other machines (servers, remote PCs) keep their transcripts there, under the same setting on that machine.

title: error[E0133]: call to unsafe function `std::env::set_var` is unsafe and requires unsafe block (Rust 2024)
error: error[E0133]: call to unsafe function `std::env::set_var` is unsafe and requires unsafe block
body:
## Symptom
After setting `edition = "2024"` in `Cargo.toml`, code that sets env vars stops compiling:

```
error[E0133]: call to unsafe function `std::env::set_var` is unsafe and requires unsafe block
```

Same for `std::env::remove_var` and `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::before_exec`.

## Cause
Rust 1.85.0 (2025-02-20) stabilized the 2024 edition, which marks these functions `unsafe`. Changing the process environment is unsound if any other thread may be running (other threads can read the environment concurrently via libc). Earlier editions still accept the safe call.

## Fix
Preferred: do not mutate the environment at runtime. Pass config explicitly, or set env vars only for child processes:
```rust
std::process::Command::new("tool").env("FOO", "bar").spawn()?;
```
If you must (e.g. at the very start of `main` before spawning threads or starting a runtime):
```rust
// before (2021)
std::env::set_var("FOO", "bar");
// after (2024)
// SAFETY: called before any other threads are spawned
unsafe { std::env::set_var("FOO", "bar") };
```
Note: `#[tokio::main]` starts worker threads before your `main` body runs, so setting vars inside it is not single-threaded. In tests (which run in parallel threads), prefer passing values explicitly. Replace `before_exec` with `pre_exec` (also unsafe).

## Verify
`cargo build` and `cargo clippy` pass under `edition = "2024"`.

## Sources
- https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2024/newly-unsafe-functions.html
- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/tests/ui/rust-2024/unsafe-env.e2024.stderr
- https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/02/20/Rust-1.85.0/

title: DXF/DWG text renders as literal "\U+5256", "%%c", "\P": decode AutoCAD MTEXT/TEXT escape codes
body:
## Symptom
Drawings converted from DWG to DXF and rendered with a custom renderer showed garbage such as `\U+5256\U+9762`, `%%c20`, `{\fSimSun|b0|i0;...}` and `\P` instead of Chinese text, diameter signs and line breaks.

## Cause
DXF stores TEXT/MTEXT with AutoCAD's own escapes, which the renderer printed literally:
- `\U+XXXX`: a Unicode code point (common for CJK when the DXF codepage is ANSI)
- `%%c` / `%%d` / `%%p`: diameter `Ø`, degree `°`, plus/minus `±` (`%%%` is a literal `%`)
- MTEXT formatting: `\P` = paragraph break, `\~` = non-breaking space, `{...}` grouping, `\f...;` font, `\H...;` height, `\W...;` width, `\C...;` colour, `\A...;` alignment, `\L`/`\l` underline on/off, `\S a^b;` stacked fractions

## Fix
```js
function decodeAcadText(s) {
  return s
    .replace(/\\U\+([0-9A-Fa-f]{4})/g, (_, h) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h, 16)))
    .replace(/%%[cC]/g, 'Ø').replace(/%%[dD]/g, '°').replace(/%%[pP]/g, '±').replace(/%%%/g, '%')
    .replace(/\\P/g, '\n').replace(/\\~/g, ' ')
    .replace(/\\S([^;^#]*)[\^#]([^;]*);/g, '$1/$2')
    .replace(/\\[fFHWQACTp][^;]*;/g, '').replace(/\\[LlOoKk]/g, '')
    .replace(/[{}]/g, '');
}
```
Render with a font stack that has CJK glyphs (e.g. Noto Sans CJK) on the server.

## Verify
Re-rendered drawings showed proper Chinese titles, Ø/°/± symbols and line breaks. Previously cached PNGs were regenerated under new filenames, because the old URLs were served with immutable caching.

## Notes
ezdxf users can call `MText.plain_text()` and `ezdxf.tools.text.plain_text()` instead of hand-rolling the regex.

title: Gemini box detection returns [] silently unless you ask for canonical box_2d [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] (0–1000)
body:
## Symptom
Asking a Gemini flash-lite model to locate regions on a scanned drawing page (title-block cells, company names) with a custom JSON schema like `{x, y, width, height}` in pixels returned an empty array for most pages, with no error.

## Cause
The models are trained to emit detections in the canonical format `"box_2d": [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]` normalized to 0–1000. Custom coordinate schemas push the small models off-distribution and they fall back to an empty result. Prompt phrasing like "if there is none, output []" further encourages lazy empty answers.

## Fix
- Request free-form JSON with the canonical key and order, and convert afterwards:
```
Return a JSON list: [{"label": "...", "box_2d": [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]}] with coordinates normalized to 0-1000.
```
```js
const toPx = ([y0,x0,y1,x1], W, H) => ({ x: x0/1000*W, y: y0/1000*H, w: (x1-x0)/1000*W, h: (y1-y0)/1000*H });
```
- Don't include an explicit "output [] if nothing" escape hatch.
- For long OCR-style outputs raise `maxOutputTokens` (16384 used) and salvage-parse truncated JSON arrays.
- Add a sanity guard in code (e.g. drop boxes larger than a plausible size) — a recall-biased prompt once produced huge boxes covering drawing views.

## Verify
With the canonical format the same pages returned populated detections; the size guard alone would have caught the one hallucinated huge box seen in production.

title: Error: P1010: User was denied access on the database — Prisma 7 pg adapter now validates SSL certs
error: Error: P1010: User was denied access on the database <database>
body:
## Symptom
A Postgres connection that worked on Prisma 6 (often a managed DB with a self-signed or private-CA certificate) fails after upgrading to Prisma 7 with:

```
Error: P1010: User was denied access on the database <database>
```
The credentials are correct, so this looks like a permissions problem — it is not.

## Cause
Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (2025-11-19) connects through `node-pg` via `@prisma/adapter-pg` instead of the Rust query engine. The Rust engine ignored invalid certificates; node-pg validates them, so an untrusted cert now fails the connection (tracked in prisma/prisma#28795).

## Fix
Preferred — trust the CA:
```bash
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/ca.pem node server.js
# or use the system store
node --use-openssl-ca server.js
```
Less secure (restores v6 behavior):
```ts
import { PrismaPg } from '@prisma/adapter-pg'
const adapter = new PrismaPg({
  connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
  ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },
})
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter })
```

## Verify
`await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1`` succeeds with the same credentials.

## Sources
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/upgrade-guides/upgrading-versions/upgrading-to-prisma-7
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues/28795

title: macOS loses internet after plugging into a machine/PLC network: the cable's DHCP gateway becomes the default route
body:
## Symptom
