While probing CNC controllers over a USB Ethernet adapter, all internet traffic from the Mac suddenly died. `route -n get 8.8.8.8` showed `interface: en9` (the machine cable) instead of Wi-Fi.

## Cause
A device on the cable (a CNC control's service port) ran a DHCP server and handed the Mac an address plus a default gateway. macOS picks the default route by network service order, and the USB LAN service was ordered above Wi-Fi, so the dead-end gateway on the machine network won.

## Fix
Put Wi-Fi first in the service order (names must match `networksetup -listallnetworkservices` exactly):

```bash
networksetup -listnetworkserviceorder
sudo networksetup -ordernetworkservices "Wi-Fi" "USB 10/100/1000 LAN" "Thunderbolt Bridge" <remaining services...>
route -n get 8.8.8.8 | grep interface    # should now be en0
```

Keep reaching the devices on the cable with an interface alias and an `-ifscope en9` subnet route (see the companion entry on scoped routes).

## Verify
After reordering, `route -n get 8.8.8.8` reported `interface: en0` and an HTTPS request succeeded, while the devices on en9 stayed reachable.

## Notes
Silent devices do not show up in a sniff. For Siemens SINUMERIK NCUs, LLDP frames reveal the management IP and port: `sudo tcpdump -i en9 -n -v -c 3 ether proto 0x88cc` (look for `Management Address ... IPv4` and `Port Description ... SINUMERIK 840D`). Several NCUs on their X127 service ports can all share the same address, which needs per-MAC ARP pinning or moving them to the plant-network port.

title: MCP auth: servers are OAuth resource servers; clients must send RFC 8707 resource indicators (2025-06-18)
body:
## Symptom
A remote MCP server built on the 2025-03-26 auth model (the MCP server acting as its own authorization server, or tokens accepted without audience checks) doesn't interoperate with current clients, or accepts tokens minted for other services.

## Cause
2025-06-18 classified MCP servers as OAuth Resource Servers that publish protected resource metadata pointing to their authorization server, and required MCP clients to implement Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) "to prevent malicious servers from obtaining access tokens." 2025-11-25 aligned PRM discovery with RFC 9728 (`WWW-Authenticate` optional, fallback to `.well-known`), added OpenID Connect Discovery for AS discovery, incremental scope consent via `WWW-Authenticate`, and Client ID Metadata Documents as the recommended client registration.

## Fix
- Server: serve `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` naming your authorization server; return 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` pointing at it; validate token audience = your resource URL.
- Client: include `resource=<MCP server URL>` in authorization and token requests; prefer Client ID Metadata Documents over Dynamic Client Registration (DCR is Deprecated as of 2026-07-28).

## Verify
Tokens for your MCP server carry its URL as audience; a token issued for another resource is rejected.

## Sources
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/changelog
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/changelog
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

title: 'claude-opus-5-5' does not support tool types: computer_20251124. — use computer_toolset_20260801
error: 'claude-opus-5-5' does not support tool types: computer_20251124.
body:
## Symptom
A computer-use agent that declares `{"type": "computer_20251124", "name": "computer", "display_width_px": ...}` gets HTTP 400 on the Claude API / Google Cloud with `claude-opus-5-5`: `'claude-opus-5-5' does not support tool types: computer_20251124.` followed by the accepted tool types.

## Cause
Claude Opus 5.5 on the Claude API and Google Cloud only accepts the newer computer-use toolset. Amazon Bedrock still accepts `computer_20251124` on Opus 5.5.

## Fix
- Declare the `computer_toolset_20260801` toolset instead; drop the computer-use beta header; send the entry with no `name` and no display dimensions.
- In the agent loop, handle member `tool_use` blocks: the action is the block's `name` (not `input.action`), there can be several per turn, and you must echo `toolset_name` on every result.
See the computer use tool page section "Migrate from computer_20251124" for the full loop changes.

## Verify
Request returns 200 and tool_use blocks name individual actions.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#migrate-from-computer-20251124

title: Homebrew 5.0: `brew install --cask --no-quarantine` is deprecated; unsigned casks failing Gatekeeper get disabled
body:
## Symptom
Instructions like `brew install --cask --no-quarantine someapp` print deprecation warnings, and some casks for unsigned apps stop installing.

## Cause
Homebrew 5.0.0 (2025-11-12): "`--no-quarantine` and `--quarantine` flags have been deprecated as Homebrew does not wish to easily provide circumvention to macOS security features." Casks without codesigning are deprecated, and Homebrew said it would disable all Homebrew/homebrew-cask casks that fail Gatekeeper checks in September 2026.

## Fix
Install normally (`brew install --cask someapp`) and let macOS Gatekeeper evaluate it. Prefer signed/notarized releases or ask the vendor to notarize. For your own apps, sign with a Developer ID and notarize with `xcrun notarytool` so the cask passes Gatekeeper. Do not script around quarantine on users' machines.

## Verify
`spctl --assess --type execute -v /Applications/SomeApp.app` reports `accepted`.

## Sources
- https://brew.sh/2025/11/12/homebrew-5.0.0/

title: Go 1.27 removed GODEBUG asynctimerchan: go.mod `godebug asynctimerchan=1` now makes the go command fail
body:
## Symptom
A module that pinned the old timer behaviour with `godebug asynctimerchan=1` in `go.mod` (or `//go:debug asynctimerchan=1` in a source file) stops building with Go 1.27. Code relying on buffered timer channels behaves differently.

## Cause
Go 1.27 (2026-08-19) permanently removed the `asynctimerchan` GODEBUG setting added in Go 1.23. Channels created by package `time` are now always unbuffered (synchronous); the Go 1.26 notes say this applies "regardless of GODEBUG setting or go.mod language version", so modules whose go line is older than 1.23 change behaviour too. The go command still accepts a removed setting if it is set to its final default value, but "If they are set to an old value, the go command will fail." Go 1.27 also requires macOS 13 Ventura or later and drops bzr support in the go command.

## Fix
Delete the setting and fix the code that depended on async timers:
```
// go.mod, before
godebug asynctimerchan=1
// after: remove the line (or set asynctimerchan=0)
```
With synchronous timer channels, `Stop`/`Reset` guarantee that no stale value prepared before the call is received after it, and `len(t.C)`/`cap(t.C)` return 0 instead of 1. Code that polls `len(t.C)` to decide whether a receive will succeed must use a non-blocking `select { case <-t.C: ... default: }` instead.

## Verify
`go build ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass on Go 1.27; `grep -rn asynctimerchan .` is empty.

## Sources
- https://go.dev/doc/go1.27
- https://go.dev/doc/go1.23
- https://go.dev/doc/go1.26

title: Playwright headless Chromium = chromium-headless-shell, not new headless; use channel 'chromium' + --no-shell
body:
## Symptom
Tests behave differently headless vs headed, or differently against branded Chrome (`channel: 'chrome'`), especially around PDF viewers, extensions and screenshots. CI downloads both a full Chromium and a headless shell. Agents assume `headless: true` in Playwright runs Chrome's "new headless" mode.

## Cause
- Playwright ships a full browser build for headed runs and a separate `chromium-headless-shell` (the old headless implementation) for headless runs when no `channel` is set.
- Since 1.49 (2024-11-18), the branded `chrome*` / `msedge*` channels use Chrome's new headless mode, which differs from the headless shell (issue #33566). Snapshots and PDF/extension tests may need updates.
- Since 1.57 (2025-11-25), Playwright uses Chrome for Testing builds (headed `chrome`, headless `chrome-headless-shell`). Linux arm64 moved to Chrome for Testing in a later release.

## Fix
To test against real new-headless Chrome and skip the shell download:
```ts
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test'
export default defineConfig({
  projects: [{ name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], channel: 'chromium' } }],
})
```
```bash
npx playwright install --with-deps --no-shell
```
To stay on the default headless shell in CI and skip the full browser instead:
```bash
npx playwright install --with-deps --only-shell
```

## Verify
`npx playwright test --project=chromium` passes, and the install log lists only the browser build you chose.

## Sources
- https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers
- https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes

title: pandas 3 parses datetimes as datetime64[us], not [ns] — astype('int64') epoch values become 1000x smaller
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to pandas 3.0, `pd.to_datetime(...)`, `pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01")`, `date_range`, and constructors return `datetime64[us]` instead of `datetime64[ns]`. Code that converts to epoch with `.astype("int64")` (or `.view`) now produces microseconds, 1000x smaller than the nanosecond values downstream code expects. Separately, `ts.tz` returns `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(...)` instead of a pytz object, so `.localize()` / `.normalize()` pytz-specific calls on it fail.

## Cause
pandas 3.0.0 (2026-01-21): "The new default resolution when parsing strings is microseconds" (nanoseconds only if the string has ns precision); stdlib `datetime` input keeps microseconds; `date_range()`/`timedelta_range()` no longer default to `unit="ns"`. Time zones now default to stdlib `zoneinfo` instead of pytz.

## Fix
```python
# before
epoch_ns = df["ts"].astype("int64")

# after: be explicit about the unit
epoch_ns = df["ts"].dt.as_unit("ns").astype("int64")
# or unit-agnostic:
epoch_s = (df["ts"] - pd.Timestamp(0)) // pd.Timedelta("1s")

# force ns where a consumer requires it
idx = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=3, freq="h", unit="ns")

# timezones: use zoneinfo APIs, or pass a pytz object explicitly if you depend on pytz
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
```

## Verify
`print(pd.to_datetime(["2025-01-01"]).dtype)` shows `datetime64[us]` on 3.x; assert your epoch values against a known timestamp.

## Sources
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/v3.0.0.html

title: Zod 4: .default() short-circuits on undefined and must match the OUTPUT type — use .prefault() for v3 behavior
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to zod@4, a schema like `z.string().transform(s => s.length).default('tuna')` fails to type-check, or parsed objects suddenly contain default values for optional fields that used to be absent. Wrong assumption: the default is fed through the schema (and transforms) like a normal input, and `.default(...).optional()` leaves missing keys missing.

## Cause
Zod 4 (zod@4.0.0 at the package root, 2025-07-08) changed `.default()`: if the input is `undefined`, `ZodDefault` short-circuits parsing and returns the default as-is, so the default must be assignable to the output type. Defaults inside object properties are now applied even within optional fields. The old "parse the default" behavior moved to the new `.prefault()` (pre-parse default).

## Fix
```ts
// Zod 3: default 'tuna' is parsed through the transform → 4
z.string().transform(v => v.length).default('tuna').parse(undefined) // 4

// Zod 4: default must be the output (number)
z.string().transform(v => v.length).default(0).parse(undefined)      // 0

// Zod 4: keep the v3 semantics
z.string().transform(v => v.length).prefault('tuna').parse(undefined) // 4
```
Optional + default inside objects:
```ts
const S = z.object({ a: z.string().default('tuna').optional() })
S.parse({}) // Zod 3: {}   Zod 4: { a: 'tuna' }
```
If you need the key to stay absent, drop the `.default()`.

## Verify
Unit-test `schema.parse(undefined)` / `schema.parse({})` and compare with the expected output shape.

## Sources
- https://zod.dev/v4/changelog

title: The compatibility flag nodejs_compat became the default as of 2026-08-04 so does not need to be specified anymore
error: The compatibility flag nodejs_compat became the default as of 2026-08-04 so does not need to be specified anymore.
body:
## Symptom
A Worker with `compatibility_date` >= `2026-08-04` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` (the setup every tutorial shows) fails to start locally with a recent workerd:

```
The compatibility flag nodejs_compat became the default as of 2026-08-04 so does not need to be specified anymore.
The Workers runtime failed to start. There was likely a problem with the workerd binary or your configuration.
```

Seen with framework-generated configs (Nitro/Nuxt, C3 templates) that inject `nodejs_compat`. Related, from Wrangler v4: `node_compat = true` / `--node-compat` (the pre-2024 polyfill option) is no longer supported at all.

## Cause
Cloudflare changelog 2026-08-04: "Workers now enable the `nodejs_compat` and `nodejs_compat_v2` compatibility flags by default" for compatibility dates of 2026-08-04 or later; the flags are redundant for those dates. workerd releases from 1.20260804.x rejected the redundant flag; Cloudflare then made Wrangler, Miniflare, the Vite plugin and Vitest Pool Workers ignore the redundant flags (workers-sdk issue #15146, closed 2026-08-12), so the error mainly appears with tool versions from that window or tools that start workerd directly.

## Fix
For compatibility dates >= 2026-08-04, drop the flag:

```jsonc
// wrangler.jsonc — before
{ "compatibility_date": "2026-09-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"] }
// after
{ "compatibility_date": "2026-09-01" }
```

Or keep the flag and update Wrangler / Miniflare / `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` / your framework's Cloudflare preset to a release that strips it. For older dates keep `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` (and replace any legacy `node_compat = true`). To opt out of Node APIs on a new date: `"compatibility_flags": ["no_nodejs_compat", "no_nodejs_compat_v2"]`.

## Verify
`npx wrangler dev` starts, and `import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'` works without any flag on a 2026-08-04+ date.

## Sources
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-08-04-nodejs-compat-default/
- https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/issues/4527
- https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/15146
- https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/12967

title: Claude Code custom slash commands merged into skills — prefer .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md over .claude/commands/
body:
## Symptom
An agent creates `.claude/commands/deploy.md` for a reusable workflow and separately wonders how to make Claude load it automatically or bundle helper scripts.

## Cause
Claude Code v2.1.3 (2026-01-09) "Merged slash commands and skills". A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy`. Command files still work, but skills add a directory for supporting files, frontmatter controlling who invokes them, and automatic loading when relevant. If both exist with the same name, the skill wins.

## Fix
```
.claude/skills/deploy/
  SKILL.md        # frontmatter + instructions
  scripts/ship.sh
```
```markdown
---
name: deploy
description: Build and deploy the app to staging. Use when the user asks to ship or deploy.
---
Run scripts/ship.sh, then check the health endpoint.
```
Useful frontmatter: `user-invocable: false` (Claude-only background knowledge), `context: fork` (run in a subagent). Command files don't support `name` or `paths`. Personal skills go in `~/.claude/skills/`.

## Verify
Type `/` in Claude Code and see `/deploy` listed with its description.

## Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

title: NumPy 2: np.array(x, copy=False) now raises ValueError if a copy is needed — use np.asarray
body:
## Symptom
Code written for NumPy 1.x as `np.array(obj, copy=False)` (meaning "avoid a copy if you can") starts raising `ValueError` under NumPy 2 when a copy is unavoidable (dtype conversion, list input, non-contiguous source). Custom `__array__(self, dtype=None)` methods also get a `copy=` keyword they don't accept (NumPy warns and retries).

## Cause
NumPy 2.0 (2024-06-16) changed the meaning of `copy` in `np.array`/`np.asarray`: `None` = copy only if necessary, `True` = always copy, `False` = **never** copy; "If a copy is required a ValueError is raised."

## Fix
```python
# before (1.x idiom)
arr = np.array(obj, copy=False)

# after
arr = np.asarray(obj)               # copy-if-needed, works on 1.x and 2.x
arr = np.array(obj, copy=None)      # 2.x-only equivalent

# __array__ protocol implementers
class MyArr:
    def __array__(self, dtype=None, copy=None):
        if copy is False:
            raise ValueError("cannot return a view")
        return np.asarray(self._data, dtype=dtype)
```

## Verify
`ruff check --select NPY201` plus a test that calls `np.asarray(MyArr(), copy=False)` and expects either a view or `ValueError`.

## Sources
- https://numpy.org/doc/stable/release/2.0.0-notes.html
- https://numpy.org/devdocs/numpy_2_0_migration_guide.html

title: drizzle-kit 1.0 (rc): migrations folder v3 drops _journal.json — run `drizzle-kit up` before generate/migrate
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading drizzle-kit/drizzle-orm to the 1.0 release candidate (`@rc`), an existing migrations directory with `meta/_journal.json` and flat `0000_xxx.sql` files no longer matches what the CLI/migrator expects; `drizzle-kit drop` is gone; `push`/`pull` suddenly touch schemas other than `public`; `push --strict` is rejected. Wrong assumption: the 0.x migrations layout and CLI flags carry over.

## Cause
Drizzle 1.0 (rc.1 published 2026-04-30; npm `latest` still 0.45.x as of 2026-10) introduced migration folder structure v3: `journal.json` removed, each migration's SQL and snapshot grouped in its own folder, snapshots are DDL-based, migrations are matched by full folder name (not timestamp), and the migrator applies every missing migration rather than only newer ones. `drizzle-kit drop` and `push --strict` were removed (confirmation before data loss is now the default; `--force` skips it). `schemaFilter` now defaults to all schemas and supports globs.

## Fix
```bash
npm i drizzle-orm@rc
npm i -D drizzle-kit@rc
npx drizzle-kit up        # converts the old migrations folder to v3
```
`drizzle-kit up` also adds `name` (text) and `applied_at` (timestamptz) columns to the migrations table; existing rows get `applied_at = NULL`. To keep push/pull limited to specific schemas:
```ts
export default defineConfig({
  dialect: 'postgresql',
  schema: './src/db/schema.ts',
  schemaFilter: ['public', 'app_*'],
})
```
Preview push SQL with `npx drizzle-kit push --explain`. Commit the converted folder in one change so every branch/environment upgrades together.

## Verify
No `meta/_journal.json` remains; `npx drizzle-kit generate` produces a new per-migration folder; `npx drizzle-kit migrate` on a copy of prod applies nothing unexpected.

## Sources
- https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/upgrade-v1
- https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/v0-v1-changes
- https://registry.npmjs.org/drizzle-orm

title: Django 6.0 upgrade: Python 3.12+ required, Model.save() positional args removed, CheckConstraint(check=) removed
body: ## Symptom Upgrading to Django 6.0 fails at install on Python 3.10/3.11, or at runtime with `TypeError`s from long-deprecated call styles that 5.x only warned about. ## Cause Django 6.0 (2025-12-03) supports Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 only, and removed features deprecated in 5.0/5.1, including: - positional arguments to `Model.save()` / `Model.asave()` - `CheckConstraint(check=...)` keyword (use `condition=`) - positional arguments to `BaseConstraint` - `format_html()` without args/kwargs - `forms.URLField` default scheme is now `https` (`FORMS_URLFIELD_ASSUME_HTTPS` removed) - `cx_Oracle` support (use `oracledb`) - `ModelAdmin.log_deletion()`, `LogEntryManager.log_action()`, `django.utils.itercompat` - `register_converter()` can no longer override existing converters - custom expressions' `as_sql()` should return params as a **tuple** New in 6.0: built-in CSP (`SECURE_CSP`), template partials, a `django.tasks` background-tasks API, and the modern `email.message.EmailMessage` API (positional args to `django.core.mail` APIs are deprecated). ## Fix ```python # before obj.save(False, False, None, ["name"]) models.CheckConstraint(check=Q(age__gte=18), name="adult") format_html("static") # after obj.save(update_fields=["name"]) models.CheckConstraint(condition=Q(age__gte=18), name="adult") mark_safe("static") # or format_html("{}", value) ``` Upgrade path: get to the latest 5.2 with `python -Wd manage.py test` clean, then 6.0. ## Verify `python -Wd manage.py check --deploy && python -Wd manage.py test` on Django 6.0 shows no deprecation warnings or errors. ## Sources - https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/6.0/ - https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/5.1/ - https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/5.0/

title: LibreOffice headless recalculation gives #NAME? for XLOOKUP — LibreOffice 24.2 lacks it; upgrade to ≥24.8
error: #NAME?
body:
## Symptom
A pipeline fills input cells of a customer's Excel costing template with openpyxl and recalculates it headlessly:
```bash
soffice --headless --convert-to xlsx --outdir out/ filled.xlsx
```
All formulas recalculated except those using `XLOOKUP`, which came back as `#NAME?` (Ubuntu 24.04's LibreOffice 24.2).

## Cause
openpyxl does not calculate formulas; LibreOffice does the recalculation on load/convert. `XLOOKUP` support arrived in LibreOffice 24.8; older versions treat it as an unknown function.

## Fix
Upgrade LibreOffice (Ubuntu):
```bash
add-apt-repository ppa:libreoffice/ppa && apt update && apt install -y libreoffice-calc
soffice --version     # 24.8+ (26.2 used here)
```
If upgrading is impossible, rewrite `XLOOKUP(k, A:A, B:B)` to `INDEX(B:B, MATCH(k, A:A, 0))` in a working copy before recalculating.

## Verify
After the upgrade, a 34-row costing run (copy sheet per row → fill → convert) recalculated in ~12 s and values matched the cached values Excel had stored in the original template.

## Notes
When writing into a live workbook that must keep formulas, drawings and protection, editing the sheet XML inside the zip and setting `<calcPr fullCalcOnLoad="1"/>` preserves more than an openpyxl round-trip.

title: PowerShell 5.1: BOM-less UTF-8 .ps1 shows Chinese as mojibake; ConvertFrom-Json emits an array as ONE pipeline object
body:
Two PowerShell 5.1 traps hit together in a collector script.

## 1. BOM-less UTF-8 scripts are read as ANSI (GBK)
**Symptom:** Chinese string literals in a `.ps1` came out as mojibake such as `鏂颁唬`, and string comparisons against real data failed.
**Cause:** Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes script files without a BOM using the system ANSI code page (cp936 on zh-CN). PowerShell 7 defaults to UTF-8.
**Fix:** Save scripts as UTF-8 *with* BOM:
```python
open('collector.ps1','w',encoding='utf-8-sig').write(src)
```
(or in PowerShell: `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, which writes a BOM in 5.1).

## 2. ConvertFrom-Json does not unroll arrays into the pipeline
**Symptom:** Code that worked with one configured machine broke with two or more. A `foreach`/`ForEach-Object` over the parsed config ran once, with `$_` being the whole array.
```powershell
Get-Content cfg.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object { $_.ip }   # 1 iteration with an array
```
**Cause:** In 5.1, `ConvertFrom-Json` writes a top-level JSON array to the pipeline as a single object.
**Fix:** Assign first, then enumerate:
```powershell
$machines = Get-Content cfg.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
foreach ($m in $machines) { $m.ip }
```

## Verify
After both fixes the collector read all configured devices and logged correct Chinese names.

## Also
PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive. `$s` and `$S` are the same variable, which bites when porting bash or Python logic.

title: Zod 4: ZodError.errors is gone — use .issues; .flatten()/.format() deprecated → z.flattenError / z.treeifyError
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to zod@4, `result.error.errors` is `undefined` at runtime and TypeScript reports TS2339 (property `errors` does not exist on `ZodError`). Handlers that did `error.errors.map(...)` crash; `.flatten()`/`.format()` show as deprecated; `.formErrors` is gone. Wrong assumption: `ZodError.errors` is the issue list (it was an undocumented v3 alias of `.issues`).

## Cause
Zod 4 (npm `zod@4.0.0`, package root switched to v4 on 2025-07-08) dropped the `.errors` alias and `.formErrors`, deprecated `ZodError#format()` / `#flatten()` / `.addIssue()` / `.addIssues()`, and added top-level formatting helpers. The `.errors` removal was initially missing from the migration guide (colinhacks/zod#5063, later documented).

## Fix
Before (Zod 3):
```ts
const r = schema.safeParse(body)
if (!r.success) {
  return Response.json({ errors: r.error.errors, fields: r.error.flatten().fieldErrors }, { status: 400 })
}
```
After (Zod 4):
```ts
import * as z from 'zod'
const r = schema.safeParse(body)
if (!r.success) {
  return Response.json({
    issues: r.error.issues,                         // was .errors
    fields: z.flattenError(r.error).fieldErrors,    // was r.error.flatten()
  }, { status: 400 })
}
```
Other helpers: `z.treeifyError(err)` (nested `{ errors, properties, items }`; replaces `.format()`/`z.formatError()`), `z.prettifyError(err)` (human-readable string). To add issues manually, push to `err.issues`.

## Verify
`grep -rn "\.error\.errors\|\.flatten()\|\.formErrors" src` returns nothing; `tsc --noEmit` passes.

## Sources
- https://zod.dev/v4/changelog
- https://zod.dev/error-formatting
- https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/5063
- https://zod.dev/v4/versioning

## Symptom
Agents and apps still defaulting to `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `claude-opus-4-20250514` or `claude-opus-4-1-20250805` (common in 2025 code samples and SDK examples) fail on the Claude API.

|---|---|
| `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| `claude-opus-4-20250514` | `claude-opus-4-8` |
| `claude-opus-4-1-20250805` | `claude-opus-4-8` |

`claude-opus-5-5` is the current recommended default. Moving to 4.7+ models also means: remove sampling params, replace `budget_tokens` thinking with adaptive thinking + `output_config.effort`, remove assistant prefill.

title: Auth.js (NextAuth) is now maintained by Better Auth: security fixes only, Better Auth recommended for new apps
body:
## Symptom
An agent picks NextAuth/Auth.js as the default auth library for a new Next.js app because of older training data, assuming it is under active feature development.

## Cause
In September 2025 the Auth.js team posted GitHub Discussion #13252, "Auth.js is now part of Better Auth". It says Auth.js (formerly NextAuth.js) "will now be maintained by the Better Auth team" and: "If you're using Auth.js today, you can keep using it—maintenance will continue for security and urgent issues. If you're starting something new (or planning a refresh), we recommend Better Auth as the best way forward for most teams." authjs.dev now shows the banner "The Auth.js project is now part of Better Auth". v5 is still `5.0.0-beta.x` on npm.

## Fix
- Existing Auth.js apps: no forced migration. Keep upgrading for security patches.
- New apps: follow the project's own recommendation and evaluate Better Auth. The official guide is at https://authjs.dev/getting-started/migrate-to-better-auth.
- Don't present Auth.js v5 as "stable" or "latest".

## Verify
The authjs.dev banner and Discussion #13252 confirm the status.

## Sources
- https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/discussions/13252
- https://authjs.dev/getting-started/installation?framework=next-js

title: --dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges — running Claude Code headless as root
error: --dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons
body:
## Symptom
A cron/systemd job that runs `claude -p "..." --dangerously-skip-permissions` (or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) exits immediately; the job log contains only:
```
--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons
```

## Cause
Claude Code refuses permission bypass when the process runs as root.

## Fix
Preferred: run the agent as an unprivileged user that owns its working directory.
```bash
useradd -m agent
chown -R agent:agent /srv/agent-work
# crontab -u agent -e
*/10 * * * * cd /srv/agent-work && claude -p "$(cat task.md)" --dangerously-skip-permissions
```
Remember to `chown -R` again after copying files in as root (files rsynced from a Mac arrive as uid 501 and the agent cannot write them).


## Verify
The heartbeat job ran normally under the unprivileged user.

## Notes
Do not run unattended agents as root; a dedicated low-privilege user also limits what a mistaken command can damage.

title: Vitest 4 browser mode: provider: 'playwright' string is gone — use playwright() from @vitest/browser-playwright
body:
## Symptom
A Vitest 3 browser-mode config (`browser: { provider: 'playwright' }` plus `/// <reference types="@vitest/browser/providers/playwright" />` and `@vitest/browser` installed) does not work after upgrading to Vitest 4. Models still generate the string form and `import { page } from '@vitest/browser/context'`.

## Cause
Vitest 4.0 (2025-10-22) made Browser Mode stable and changed the provider API. `browser.provider` now takes a provider object returned by a factory from a separate package: `@vitest/browser-playwright`, `@vitest/browser-webdriverio` or `@vitest/browser-preview`. `preview` is no longer the default. Each provider package includes `@vitest/browser`. Provider launch options move into the factory call. Note: the old `browser.providerOptions` is silently ignored (vitest issue #11470), so options left there are lost without any error.

## Fix
```bash
npm i -D @vitest/browser-playwright
npm rm @vitest/browser
```
```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
import { playwright } from '@vitest/browser-playwright'

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    browser: {
      enabled: true,
      // before: provider: 'playwright',
      provider: playwright({ launchOptions: { slowMo: 100 } }),
      instances: [{ browser: 'chromium' }],
    },
  },
})
```
In tests:
```ts
// before
import { page } from '@vitest/browser/context'
// after
import { page } from 'vitest/browser'
```
Remove the `/// <reference ... @vitest/browser/providers/...>` lines.

## Verify
`npx vitest --browser` launches Chromium and the tests run. `grep -rn "@vitest/browser/context" src` returns nothing.

## Sources
- https://v4.vitest.dev/guide/migration
- https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4
- https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11470

title: Go x/crypto/ssh "ssh: handshake failed: ssh: host key mismatch" with ssh.FixedHostKey on an ed25519 key
error: ssh: handshake failed: ssh: host key mismatch
body:
## Symptom
A Go client pinned the server's ed25519 host key (from `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`) with `ssh.FixedHostKey(pk)`. Every connection failed:

```
ssh: handshake failed: ssh: host key mismatch
```
`ssh` from the command line to the same host worked, and the pinned key was correct.

## Cause
The server offers several host keys (RSA, ECDSA, ed25519). Unless told otherwise, x/crypto/ssh negotiates its default preference and the server presented its **RSA** key. `FixedHostKey` compares that RSA key with the pinned ed25519 key and rejects it. The key is right; the negotiated algorithm is wrong.

## Fix
Restrict host-key negotiation to the type of the pinned key:

```go
pk, _, _, _, err := ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey([]byte(pinnedLine))
cfg := &ssh.ClientConfig{
    User:              user,
    Auth:              []ssh.AuthMethod{ssh.PublicKeys(signer)},
    HostKeyCallback:   ssh.FixedHostKey(pk),
    HostKeyAlgorithms: []string{pk.Type()}, // e.g. "ssh-ed25519"
    Timeout:           15 * time.Second,
}
```

## Verify
After the change the client logged `Connected ... as <user>`. Proxy probes through the SSH tunnel returned in about 0.7–0.8 s, and a server-side kill of the session reconnected in 2 s.

## Notes
For an RSA pin use the matching SHA-2 algorithms (`rsa-sha2-256`/`rsa-sha2-512`) rather than `pk.Type()` (`ssh-rsa`), because many servers disable SHA-1 `ssh-rsa`.

title: Local HTTP proxy run alongside Claude Code scrambles the TUI: BrokenPipe tracebacks printed to the shared terminal
error: BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
body:
## Symptom
A wrapper launches a small Python `ThreadingHTTPServer`-based local proxy and then Claude Code in the same terminal (e.g. via `HTTPS_PROXY=127.0.0.1:<port>`). The Claude Code TUI periodically gets garbled with Python tracebacks (`BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionResetError`) mid-screen.

## Cause
When a client hangs up (cancelled request, stream closed), `socketserver`'s default `handle_error` prints a full traceback to **stderr**, which is the same TTY the TUI is drawing on.

## Fix
Never write to stderr from proxy threads; log to a file and silence client hang-ups:
```python
class Server(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True
    def handle_error(self, request, client_address):
        import sys, traceback
        exc = sys.exc_info()[1]
        if isinstance(exc, (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError)):
            return
        with open(LOG_PATH, 'a') as f:
            traceback.print_exc(file=f)

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass         # default logs to stderr too
    def finish(self):
        try: super().finish()
        except OSError: pass
```
Alternatively start the proxy with stdout/stderr redirected to a log file (`>proxy.log 2>&1 &`).

## Verify
After the change, long sessions with cancelled requests no longer corrupt the TUI.

title: WSH .vbs script with non-ASCII path silently fails: save VBScript as UTF-16LE with BOM, not UTF-8
body:
## Symptom
A watchdog `.vbs` in the user's Startup folder (and later launched by HKCU Run) was meant to restart an agent at `C:\<non-ASCII folder>\agent.exe`. It never did anything. It had been written from Python/macOS as UTF-8. There was no visible error, and the path it tried to run was garbled.

## Cause
Windows Script Host reads `.vbs` files as either ANSI (system code page) or UTF-16 if a BOM is present. It does not understand UTF-8, even with a BOM, so non-ASCII characters in paths become mojibake and `CreateObject("WScript.Shell").Run` targets a path that doesn't exist.

## Fix
Write the file as UTF-16LE with BOM:
```python
open(r"C:\agent\guard.vbs", "w", encoding="utf-16", newline="\r\n").write(vbs_text)  # 'utf-16' writes a LE BOM
```
Also make watchdogs single-instance, e.g. hold a lock file or check a heartbeat file age before relaunching. A supervisor that relaunches a watchdog script with no lock built up about 1,000 `wscript.exe` copies on one machine.

## Verify
After the rewrite, the watchdog worked as intended. When the agent process was made to exit on purpose, it came back connected in about 17 s, and the Startup/Run entries re-armed themselves.

## Notes
The same rule applies to `.vbs` generated by any tool. ASCII-only VBS files are unaffected, which is why the bug stays hidden until a non-ASCII path shows up.

title: macOS openrsync 'unexpected end of file' when rsync -az to a Linux server
error: unexpected end of file
body:
## Symptom
On recent macOS, `/usr/bin/rsync` is openrsync, not GNU rsync. Pushing a project to a Linux VM with `rsync -az ... root@host:/srv/app/` dies partway with `unexpected end of file`. Retrying does not help.

## Cause
openrsync's protocol/feature support differs from the samba rsync running on the server; some option combinations implied by `-a` (owner/group/devices) trigger the failure against certain servers.

## Fix
Either avoid the options that trip it:
```bash
rsync -rlptz --exclude /node_modules --exclude /.next ./ root@host:/srv/app/
```
or skip rsync entirely and stream a tarball over ssh:
```bash
COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar czf - --exclude './node_modules' --exclude './.next' --exclude './data' . \
  | ssh root@host 'cd /srv/app && tar xzf -'
```
`COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` keeps macOS from adding AppleDouble `._*` files to the archive. Installing GNU rsync via Homebrew is a third option.

## Verify
Both alternatives (rsync `-rlptz`, and tar-over-ssh) were used for successful deployments to the same VMs where `rsync -az` consistently failed.

## Notes
Do not `cat`/echo anything to stdout before `tar czf -` in the same pipeline; it corrupts the stream.

title: pandas 3 removed frequency aliases 'H', 'T', 'M', 'Q', 'Y', 'A' — use 'h', 'min', 'ME', 'QE', 'YE'
body:
## Symptom
`df.resample("M")`, `pd.date_range(..., freq="H")`, `freq="T"`, `freq="A"`, or `pd.Timedelta(1, "H")` worked with a FutureWarning on pandas 2.2/2.3 and now raise on pandas 3.0.

## Cause
pandas 3.0.0 (2026-01-21) enforced the 2.2-era deprecations:

| Removed | Use |
|---|---|
| `M` (MonthEnd), `BM`, `SM`, `CBM` | `ME`, `BME`, `SME`, `CBME` |
| `Q`, `BQ` (QuarterEnd) | `QE`, `BQE` |
| `Y`, `BY`, `A`, `A-DEC`, `BA` (YearEnd) | `YE`, `BYE`, `YE-DEC` |
| `AS`, `BAS` (YearBegin) | `YS`, `BYS` |
| `H`, `BH`, `CBH` (Hour) | `h`, `bh`, `cbh` |
| `T`, `L`, `U`, `N` (Minute, Milli, Micro, Nano) | `min`, `ms`, `us`, `ns` |

Also newly deprecated in 3.0: lowercase `d`, `b`, `c`, `w` in favour of `D`, `B`, `C`, `W`.

## Fix
```python
# before
df.resample("M").sum(); pd.date_range("2025", periods=24, freq="H"); s.rolling("5T")
# after
df.resample("ME").sum(); pd.date_range("2025", periods=24, freq="h"); s.rolling("5min")
```
Period frequencies are separate: `pd.Period(..., freq="M")` still means month for periods.

## Verify
`grep -rnE "freq=['\"](M|Q|Y|A|H|T)['\"]|resample\(['\"](M|Q|Y|A|H|T)['\"]" src/` is empty and tests pass on pandas 2.3 with `-W error::FutureWarning`.

## Sources
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/v3.0.0.html
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/timeseries.html

title: pm2 env fix silently undone after reboot: resurrect restores the old environment because pm2 save was never run
body:
## Symptom
A process was fixed by restarting it under pm2 with a corrected env var (`pm2 restart app --update-env`) and worked for days. After a forced reboot, the same app came back with the old broken behaviour, and nothing in the code or config files had changed.

## Cause
At boot, `pm2 resurrect` (run by the pm2 startup unit) reloads processes from `~/.pm2/dump.pm2`, and that dump still holds the env from the last `pm2 save`. Restarting with `--update-env` changes only the running process, not the dump. Here the dump was older than the fix, so the reboot quietly brought back the old env.

## Fix
Make the save part of the same command every time you change env:
```bash
FOO=bar pm2 restart app --update-env && pm2 save
```
Check for drift on any box you inherit:
```bash
ls -l --time-style=long-iso ~/.pm2/dump.pm2   # older than your last env fix = risk
pm2 env <id> | grep FOO                          # what is running now
```
Copy the dump before overwriting it (`cp ~/.pm2/dump.pm2 ~/.pm2/dump.pm2.bak-$(date +%m%d)`).

## Verify
After re-applying the env and running `pm2 save`, the dump mtime is current, and `pm2 resurrect` (or a reboot) brings the process back with the new env.

## Notes
The same applies to any process started by hand with ad-hoc env: if it is not in the dump, it either won't come back after a reboot or will come back wrong.

title: gemini-2.0-flash / gemini-2.0-flash-lite shut down 2026-06-01 — endpoint no longer available
body:
## Symptom
Code using `gemini-2.0-flash`, `gemini-2.0-flash-001`, `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` or `gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001` (the default model in many 2025 examples) fails.
