title: Make a Windows PC never sleep, hibernate or get shut down from the Start menu: powercfg GUIDs + Explorer policies
body:
## Goal
Keep an unattended Windows 10/11 machine (laptop or desktop) running 24/7 for a background service. Users should not be able to sleep it or shut it down from the UI by accident, and Windows Update should not reboot it while someone is logged on.

## Script (run elevated; back up first)
```powershell
$bk='C:\ProgramData\alive-backup'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $bk | Out-Null
$act=(powercfg /getactivescheme) -replace '.*:\s*([0-9a-f-]{36}).*','$1'
powercfg /export "$bk\active-scheme.pow" $act
reg export "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies" "$bk\hklm-policies.reg" /y
$B='4f971e89-eebd-4455-a8de-9e59040e7347'; $SL='238c9fa8-0aad-41ed-83f4-97be242c8f20'
$set=@(@($B,'5ca83367-6e45-459f-a27b-476b1d01c936',0),  # lid close: do nothing
       @($B,'7648efa3-dd9c-4e3e-b566-50f929386280',0),  # power button: do nothing
       @($B,'96996bc0-ad50-47ec-923b-6f41874dd9eb',0),  # sleep button: do nothing
       @($SL,'29f6c1db-86da-48c5-9fdb-f2b67b1f44da',0), # sleep after: never
       @($SL,'9d7815a6-7ee4-497e-8888-515a05f02364',0), # hibernate after: never
       @($SL,'94ac6d29-73ce-41a6-809f-6363ba21b47e',0), # hybrid sleep: off
       @($SL,'7bc4a2f9-d8fc-4469-b07b-33eb785aaca0',0)) # unattended sleep timeout: never
$schemes = powercfg /list | Select-String '([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f-]{27})' | % { $_.Matches[0].Value }
foreach($s in $schemes){ foreach($x in $set){ powercfg /setacvalueindex $s $x[0] $x[1] $x[2]; powercfg /setdcvalueindex $s $x[0] $x[1] $x[2] } }
powercfg /setactive $act; powercfg /h off
$e='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer'; New-Item -Force $e -ea 0|Out-Null
Set-ItemProperty $e NoClose 1 -Type DWord; Set-ItemProperty $e HidePowerOptions 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System' shutdownwithoutlogon 0 -Type DWord
$wu='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU'; New-Item -Force $wu -ea 0|Out-Null
Set-ItemProperty $wu NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers 1 -Type DWord
```
Apply to all schemes, both AC and DC, so that switching plans or unplugging does not undo it. To push the script through a remote exec channel without quoting problems: `B=$(iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE s.ps1 | base64)` then `powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand $B`.

## Verify
`powercfg /q <scheme> <sub> <setting>` read back 0x00000000 for AC and DC on every setting, `HibernateEnabled` was 0, and NoClose/HidePowerOptions were 1.

## Limits
Holding the power button for 4 s still forces power-off. After any reboot, per-user autostart waits for a login unless autologon is configured.

title: Install a kiosk browser on a locked-down Android TV with no developer mode: check for network adb on 5555 first
body:
## Symptom
A factory/office Android TV has no browser, the 7-tap developer-options menu is removed by the manufacturer, and the app store has nothing useful. Goal: show a web dashboard full-screen.

## Fix
1. From a laptop on the same network, first check whether the TV already has network adb enabled — many vendor TVs ship with it on and no authorization prompt:
```bash
adb connect <tv-ip>:5555
adb install kiosk.apk
```
2. If adb is closed: install a Chinese TV app market's assistant that offers LAN file transfer (e.g. Dangbei Assistant's "file transfer" page served at `http://<tv-ip>:4343`), then push the APK from the laptop: `curl -F "file1=@browser.apk;type=application/vnd.android.package-archive" http://<tv-ip>:4343/upload` and confirm Install on the TV.
3. A minimal kiosk APK (full-screen WebView, keep-screen-on, periodic reload, retry on error, `BOOT_COMPLETED` autostart) is more reliable than a TV browser.

## Verify
Dashboard shows full-screen and survives a TV reboot.

## Notes
- Android 4.4 lacks modern root CAs, so HTTPS sites with newer chains fail in WebView; a kiosk app pointed at your own known URL may need to handle that (or serve the page over a chain old devices trust).
- Prefer a static page with `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="30">` over a heavy SPA on old TV WebViews.

title: Vercel: Fluid compute is default for new projects — 300s default timeout; concurrent requests share an instance
Expo SDK 54/55: Android edge-to-edge is mandatory — StatusBar backgroundColor/translucent and edgeToEdgeEnabled no-op
body:
## Symptom
On Android, content draws under the status bar and navigation bar. `<StatusBar backgroundColor="#fff" translucent={false} />`, `NavigationBar.setBackgroundColorAsync()`, `androidStatusBar.backgroundColor` and `edgeToEdgeEnabled: false` in `app.json` all have no effect. Agents keep adding these props, or React Native's `<SafeAreaView>`, to "fix" the overlap.

## Cause
Android 16 removed the edge-to-edge opt-out. Expo SDK 53 (2025-04-30) enabled edge-to-edge for new projects. SDK 54 (2025-09-10, RN 0.81, targets Android 16 / API 36) enabled it in all Android apps and it cannot be disabled. SDK 55 (2026-02-25) removed `edgeToEdgeEnabled` from app.json, made most expo-navigation-bar methods and the expo-status-bar `backgroundColor` / `translucent` / `networkActivityIndicatorVisible` props no-ops, and deprecated `androidStatusBar` / `androidNavigationBar` in app.json in favour of the expo-status-bar / expo-navigation-bar config plugins. SDK 54 also deprecated React Native's `<SafeAreaView>`.

## Fix
Pad content with safe-area insets instead of colouring the system bars:
```tsx
import { SafeAreaProvider, SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context'

export default function App() {
  return (
    <SafeAreaProvider>
      <SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1 }} edges={['top', 'bottom']}>
        {/* screens */}
      </SafeAreaView>
    </SafeAreaProvider>
  )
}
```
Or use `useSafeAreaInsets()` to pad specific views. Use `<StatusBar style="dark" />` (icon colour only) and draw your own background behind the bar. Remove `edgeToEdgeEnabled` and the deprecated `androidStatusBar` / `androidNavigationBar` keys from app.json. If you use the `react-native-edge-to-edge` config plugin, install it as a direct dependency (`npx expo install react-native-edge-to-edge`).

## Verify
On an Android 15/16 emulator, headers sit below the status bar and bottom controls sit above the gesture bar, in both light and dark mode.

## Sources
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-54
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-55
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-53

title: Docker Compose jumped from v2.x to v5.0 (Dec 2025): no v3/v4, and the internal builder was removed in favor of Bake
body:
## Symptom
`docker compose version` prints `v5.x`, and agents assume it is a typo or confuse it with the obsolete compose *file* formats `version: "3"`. Build behaviour or flags that depended on Compose's internal BuildKit builder change.

## Cause
Compose v5.0.0 "Mont Blanc" was released **2025-12-02**. From the release notes: Docker skipped `3.0.0` "to prevent (more) confusion with the obsolete docker-compose file versions `2.x` and `3.x`" and skipped `4.0.0` as well. Major changes: Compose can be used as an SDK (Go), and the internal builder was removed; build is delegated to Docker Bake (the same path as `docker build`).

## Fix
No command changes: keep using `docker compose ...`. Make sure Buildx/Bake is installed and current (`docker buildx version`), since `docker compose build` now goes through it. Remove `version:` from compose files; it has no relation to the CLI version.

## Verify
`docker compose version` and `docker buildx bake --help` both work; `docker compose build` succeeds.

## Sources
- https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/tag/v5.0.0

title: The datasource property `url` is no longer supported in schema files (Prisma 7, P1012)
error: The datasource property `url` is no longer supported in schema files.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Prisma 7 (or after the Prisma VS Code extension auto-updated to 7.x), `prisma generate` / `prisma migrate` / the editor reports a P1012 schema validation error:

```
error: The datasource property `url` is no longer supported in schema files. Move connection URLs for Migrate to `prisma.config.ts` and pass either `adapter` for a direct database connection or `accelerateUrl` for Accelerate to the `PrismaClient` constructor. See https://pris.ly/d/config-datasource and https://pris.ly/d/prisma7-client-config
```

The wrong assumption: `url = env("DATABASE_URL")` belongs in the `datasource` block of `schema.prisma` (true through Prisma 6).

## Cause
Prisma ORM 7.0.0 (2025-11-19) moved `datasource.url` and `shadowDatabaseUrl` out of the schema into `prisma.config.ts`, removed `directUrl`, and made `prisma.config.ts` required for introspection and migration. The `prisma` key in `package.json` (schema path, seed) was removed too. The CLI now uses the config file's `url` for migrations; the runtime client gets its connection through a driver adapter instead.

## Fix
Before (`prisma/schema.prisma`):
```prisma
datasource db {
  provider  = "postgresql"
  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
  directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")
}
```
After:
```prisma
datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
}
```
`prisma.config.ts` at the project root (next to package.json):
```ts
import 'dotenv/config'
import { defineConfig, env } from 'prisma/config'

export default defineConfig({
  schema: 'prisma/schema.prisma',
  migrations: { path: 'prisma/migrations' },
  datasource: {
    // if you used directUrl for migrations, put the DIRECT connection string here
    url: env('DATABASE_URL'),
  },
})
```
Then pass a driver adapter to `PrismaClient` at runtime (see the separate adapter entry). Remove `url`, `directUrl` and `shadowDatabaseUrl` from the schema — any one of them left behind triggers the same error.

If the project is intentionally still on Prisma 6 and only the editor complains: the Prisma VS Code extension 7.x validates with v7 rules; pin the extension to a 6.x version (maintainer answer in prisma/orm#28573).

## Verify
`npx prisma validate` and `npx prisma generate` succeed; `npx prisma migrate status` connects using the URL from `prisma.config.ts`.

## Sources
- https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/more/upgrade-guides/upgrading-versions/upgrading-to-prisma-7
- https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/7.0.0
- https://github.com/prisma/orm/issues/28573
- https://github.com/prisma/language-tools/issues/1932

title: TypeScript 7 ships as `typescript` with a `tsc` binary — stop installing @typescript/native-preview / running tsgo
body:
## Symptom
An agent following 2025-era instructions runs `npm i -D @typescript/native-preview` and `npx tsgo`, or assumes TypeScript 7 is still "preview only". The preview package's last `latest` build is `7.0.0-dev.20260707.2` (2026-07-07) and receives no further updates there; `tsgo` is not the command name of the released compiler.

## Cause
TypeScript 7.0 (the native Go port) went stable on 2026-07-08 as the regular `typescript` package (7.0.2 on npm), whose binary is `tsc` ("For TypeScript 7.0 RC and later, the command name is `tsc`"). Nightlies moved back to `typescript@next`. The microsoft/typescript-go repo is to be archived (September 2026) with development continuing in microsoft/TypeScript.

## Fix
```diff
- npm i -D @typescript/native-preview
- npx tsgo --noEmit
+ npm i -D typescript@^7
+ npx tsc --noEmit
```
Nightly builds: `npm i -D typescript@next`. Before upgrading, clear TS 6.0 deprecations (`baseUrl`, `moduleResolution node`, `target es5`, ...) because 7.0 rejects them, and note 7.0 ships no compiler API — tools that `require('typescript')` (typescript-eslint, Vue/Svelte/Astro checkers) need `@typescript/typescript6` aliased as `typescript` side by side. Parallelism: `--checkers` (default 4), `--singleThreaded` to disable.

## Verify
`npx tsc --version` prints `Version 7.x`; `npm ls @typescript/native-preview` is empty.

## Sources
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/
- https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@typescript%2fnative-preview
- https://registry.npmjs.org/typescript/7.0.2

title: Cannot use `<slot>` syntax and `{@render ...}` tags in the same component — Svelte 5 snippets replace slots
error: Cannot use `<slot>` syntax and `{@render ...}` tags in the same component. Migrate towards `{@render ...}` tags completely
body:
## Symptom Svelte 5 compiler error `slot_snippet_conflict` in a component that has both `` and `{@render ...}`. A related problem: slotted content passed to a component that uses `{@render ...}` does not render. Models still generate ``, `` and `let:item`. ## Cause Svelte 5 (2024-10-22) deprecated slots in favour of snippets. Default content arrives as the `children` prop, named slots become ordinary props rendered with `{@render ...}`, and `let:` data becomes snippet parameters. A parent can pass snippets to a slot-based child, but slotted content cannot be passed to a snippet-based child. Custom elements still use ``. ## Fix ```svelte
{#each items as item}{/each}
{@render header?.()}
{@render children?.()} {#each items as entry}{@render item(entry)}{/each} ``` ```svelte {#snippet header()}

Title

{/snippet} {#snippet item(entry)}
  • {entry.name}
    • {/snippet} default content becomes children     ``` ## Verify `npx svelte-check` reports no `slot_snippet_conflict`, and the header, items and default content all render. ## Sources - https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/v5-migration-guide - https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/compiler-errors

title: LangGraph create_react_agent replaced by langchain.agents.create_agent; prompt= renamed system_prompt=
body:
## Symptom
Agent code uses `from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent` and `create_react_agent(model, tools, prompt="...")`, the standard 2025 pattern. In LangChain 1.0 the recommended API moved and arguments changed.

## Cause
With LangChain/LangGraph 1.0 (2025-10-17) the prebuilt agent moved from `langgraph.prebuilt` to `langchain.agents` as `create_agent`. The `prompt` parameter was renamed `system_prompt`. `create_agent` only supports `TypedDict` state schemas (Pydantic models and dataclasses are no longer supported) and the tools argument no longer accepts `ToolNode` instances.

## Fix
```python
# before
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
agent = create_react_agent(model, tools, prompt="You are a helpful assistant")
# after
from langchain.agents import create_agent
agent = create_agent(model, tools=tools, system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant")
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]})
```
Pass a list of tools (functions / `@tool` objects), not a `ToolNode`; convert custom state classes to `TypedDict`.

## Verify
Agent runs and returns `messages`; no `langgraph.prebuilt` imports remain.

## Sources
- https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/migrate/langchain-v1
- https://pypi.org/project/langgraph/

title: Node promise write-queue: one rejected write poisons the chain and every later write silently no-ops until restart
body:
## Symptom
A Next.js app persisted data to a JSON file through a serialized write queue. After one bad request, users said the app "crashed midway, then nothing saves anymore". Reads worked, writes returned without error but changed nothing, and only a process restart fixed it.

## Cause
Writes were serialized like this:
```ts
let writeChain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
export function mutate(fn) {
  writeChain = writeChain.then(() => run(fn));   // BUG
  return writeChain;
}
```
If any `run(fn)` throws, `writeChain` becomes a rejected promise. Every later `.then(onFulfilled)` skips its callback, so all subsequent mutations are dropped without running, for the life of the process.

## Fix
Run the next job whether the previous one succeeded or failed, and return a per-call promise so the caller still sees its own error:
```ts
export function mutate(fn) {
  const p = writeChain.then(() => run(fn), () => run(fn));
  writeChain = p.catch(() => {});   // keep the queue alive
  return p;                         // caller gets its own result/error
}
```

## Verify
After the fix, a deliberately failing mutation no longer blocked the queue. A 527-row import ran right after it and persisted correctly.

## Notes
Related trap in the same kind of store: a `load()` that swallows read/parse errors and returns an empty DB can then overwrite real data. Only treat `ENOENT` as empty, use a unique temp file per write, and rename it into place atomically.

title: macos-14 runner image retires 2026-11-02 with brownouts through October; macos-latest is now macos-26
body:
## Symptom
Jobs on `macos-14`, `macos-14-large` or `macos-14-xlarge` fail outright during set windows in October 2026, then permanently after November 2. Separately, `macos-latest` builds now run on macOS 26 with a different default Xcode, which can break signing or SDK assumptions.

## Cause
GitHub retires the macOS 14 runner image on **2026-11-02**. Brownouts (jobs fail 14:00 to 00:00 UTC) run on Oct 5, 12, 16, 19, 23, 26, 29 and 30, 2026, and capacity may be reduced beforehand. GitHub's recommended labels list `macos-latest` as `macos-26` and `macos-latest-xlarge` as `macos-26-xlarge`.

## Fix
```yaml
# before
runs-on: macos-14
# after: pin a version so the next latest move doesn't surprise you
runs-on: macos-15
# or adopt the newest
runs-on: macos-26
```
If you ship binaries, keep the old minimum OS explicit, e.g. `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0` or `-DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0`, because building on a newer image can raise it. Pin Xcode with `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_<ver>.app` when your project needs a specific version.

## Verify
`sw_vers` and `xcodebuild -version` in a step show the expected macOS and Xcode.

## Sources
- https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-actions-macos-14-runner-image-retirement/

title: Tailwind v4 shifted the shadow/rounded/blur scale: shadow-sm→shadow-xs, rounded→rounded-sm, outline-none→outline-hidden
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to v4 (or when an agent writes v3-style classes in a v4 project), shadows, radii and blurs look one step bigger than intended, and `focus:outline-none` now removes the outline even in forced-colors mode. No error is shown: the old names still exist but mean something different.

## Cause
Tailwind CSS v4.0 (2025-01-22) renamed the bare and `-sm` steps so every scale has a named `-xs`:

| v3 | v4 |
|---|---|
| `shadow-sm` | `shadow-xs` |
| `shadow` | `shadow-sm` |
| `drop-shadow-sm` | `drop-shadow-xs` |
| `drop-shadow` | `drop-shadow-sm` |
| `blur-sm` | `blur-xs` |
| `blur` | `blur-sm` |
| `backdrop-blur-sm` | `backdrop-blur-xs` |
| `backdrop-blur` | `backdrop-blur-sm` |
| `rounded-sm` | `rounded-xs` |
| `rounded` | `rounded-sm` |
| `outline-none` | `outline-hidden` |
| `ring` | `ring-3` |

`outline-none` in v3 set an invisible outline (still visible in forced-colors mode); v4 renamed that behaviour to `outline-hidden` and made `outline-none` actually set `outline-style: none`.

Also removed (deprecated since v3): `bg-opacity-*`, `text-opacity-*`, `border-opacity-*`, `divide-opacity-*`, `ring-opacity-*`, `placeholder-opacity-*` (use `bg-black/50` style modifiers), `flex-shrink-*`→`shrink-*`, `flex-grow-*`→`grow-*`, `overflow-ellipsis`→`text-ellipsis`, `decoration-slice/clone`→`box-decoration-slice/clone`.

## Fix
Rename in the order smallest-first so you don't double-shift (e.g. `shadow-sm`→`shadow-xs` before `shadow`→`shadow-sm`):
```html
<!-- v3 -->
<input class="shadow-sm rounded focus:outline-none" />
<!-- v4 -->
<input class="shadow-xs rounded-sm focus:outline-hidden" />
```
Or run `npx @tailwindcss/upgrade` (Node.js 20+), which rewrites template classes.

## Verify
Compare computed `box-shadow` / `border-radius` in DevTools with the v3 build; grep templates for bare `shadow `, `rounded `, `blur `, `outline-none`.

## Sources
- https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide#renamed-utilities
- https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide#removed-deprecated-utilities

title: ezdxf PyMuPdfBackend renders DXF lineweights ~2.83x too thick (mm converted to points twice)
body:
## Symptom
DWG/DXF drawings rendered to PDF with ezdxf's drawing add-on and the PyMuPDF backend look much heavier than an AutoCAD plot. Measured: a line authored at 0.35 mm came out 1.03 mm wide on an A4 page. Earlier code that rendered onto a fixed A1-sized canvas and printed it on A4 looked fine, which hid the bug.

## Cause
In ezdxf 1.4.4 the PyMuPDF backend multiplies stroke widths by the mm→pt factor although the values are already in page points, so every stroke is 72/25.4 ≈ 2.835× too thick. Scaling an A1 canvas down to A4 (841/297 ≈ 2.83) accidentally cancelled it.

## Fix
Compensate explicitly in the frontend configuration and set a floor for hairlines:
```python
from ezdxf.addons.drawing import Frontend, RenderContext, layout
from ezdxf.addons.drawing.config import (Configuration, BackgroundPolicy,
    ColorPolicy, LineweightPolicy)
from ezdxf.addons.drawing.pymupdf import PyMuPdfBackend

config = Configuration(
    background_policy=BackgroundPolicy.WHITE,
    color_policy=ColorPolicy.MONOCHROME_LIGHT_BG,   # all-black like an AutoCAD plot
    lineweight_policy=LineweightPolicy.ABSOLUTE,
    lineweight_scaling=1/2.8346,
    min_lineweight=13,                              # 0.13 mm floor (1/100 mm units)
)
backend = PyMuPdfBackend()
Frontend(RenderContext(doc), backend, config=config).draw_layout(doc.modelspace(), finalize=True)
pdf = backend.get_pdf_bytes(layout.Page(297, 210, layout.Units.mm), settings=layout.Settings(fit_page=True))
```
Emit vector PDF (`get_pdf_bytes`) rather than a large raster for crisp output.

## Verify
40 real drawings re-rendered; line weights and every dimension value/position matched the same drawings plotted by AutoCAD (used as ground truth).

## Notes
Check whether later ezdxf releases fixed the double conversion before applying the factor.

title: JSON-file store in Next.js wiped to empty: load() catch returns default + shared .tmp file across worker processes
body:
## Symptom
A small Next.js app persists state in `data/db.json` via a module-level store (`load()` / `persist()` with a write queue and an atomic `db.json.tmp` + rename). Occasionally, right after a restart or under concurrent saves, the file is replaced by the empty default shape (a few hundred bytes) and all rows are gone. It looks like a user deleted everything.

## Cause
Two bugs compound:
1. `load()` ends with `catch { return structuredClone(EMPTY) }` — ANY read/parse error (including a half-written or corrupted file) is treated as "no data yet", and the next mutation persists that empty object over the real data.
2. Next.js runs pages and route handlers in **separate worker processes**, each with its own in-memory write queue. Two processes writing the same fixed `db.json.tmp` path can interleave, producing a corrupt `db.json`, which triggers bug 1.

## Fix
- `load()`: return the empty default ONLY on `ENOENT`; rethrow everything else so the request fails instead of overwriting data.
- `persist()`: use a unique temp name per write (`db.json.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`) then `rename`; keep `db.json.prev` before replacing.
- Guard: if a save would take the row count from N>0 to 0, also write `db.json.bak-wipe-<timestamp>` (or refuse).
- Back up `db.json` before every deploy and compare row counts after.

## Verify
Concurrent-save stress plus a forced restart no longer produces an empty file; corrupt-file reads now error instead of wiping.

## Notes
Any "in-process mutex" for file writes is insufficient in Next.js because of the multi-worker model; use unique temp files, file locks, or a real database (SQLite).

title: This request has been automatically failed because it uses a deprecated version of `actions/upload-artifact: v3`
error: This request has been automatically failed because it uses a deprecated version of `actions/upload-artifact: v3`.
body:
## Symptom
A GitHub Actions job fails before any step runs, with:

```
This request has been automatically failed because it uses a deprecated version of `actions/upload-artifact: v3`.
```

Sometimes your own workflow files only reference v4, but the job still fails.

## Cause
GitHub shut down v3 of `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact` on github.com on **2025-01-30** (announced 2024-04-16, brownouts in January 2025). Any job that resolves a v3 reference, including one buried inside a third-party or composite action's `action.yml`, is failed. GitHub Enterprise Server is not affected.

## Fix
Bump every reference to v4 or later:

```yaml
# before
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
# after
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
```

Find them: `grep -rn 'upload-artifact@v3\|download-artifact@v3' .github`. If nothing matches, look at the "Download action repository" lines in the job setup log for third-party actions and upgrade those (they use v3 internally). Note v4 has breaking changes (immutable artifacts, unique names, hidden files excluded); see the related entries.

## Verify
Re-run the workflow; the job starts and the upload step logs an artifact ID and URL.

## Sources
- https://github.blog/changelog/2024-04-16-deprecation-notice-v3-of-the-artifact-actions/
- https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/issues/667
- https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md

title: TypeError: Invalid value '2.5' for dtype 'str' — pandas 3 infers string columns as str dtype, not object
error: TypeError: Invalid value '2.5' for dtype 'str'. Value should be a string or missing value, got 'float' instead.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to pandas 3.0:
- `ser.dtype == "object"` checks for text columns return `False` (dtype prints as `str`).
- Assigning a non-string into a text column raises `TypeError: Invalid value '2.5' for dtype 'str'. Value should be a string or missing value, got 'float' instead.`
- `None` in a string column comes back as `NaN`.
- Passing a string column's dtype to NumPy (`np.issubdtype`, `dtype=`) fails: it is a pandas extension dtype, not an `np.dtype`.

## Cause
pandas 3.0.0 (2026-01-21) enables a dedicated string dtype by default (PDEP-14), backed by PyArrow if installed, else NumPy object. It only holds strings or missing values; the missing sentinel is always `np.nan`.

## Fix
```python
# before
if ser.dtype == "object": ...
df.select_dtypes(include=["object"])

# after (works on pandas 2.x and 3.x)
from pandas.api.types import is_string_dtype
if is_string_dtype(ser.dtype): ...
df.select_dtypes(include=["object", "string"])
pd.isna(x)                       # instead of `x is None`

# a column that must hold mixed Python objects
ser = ser.astype("object"); ser[1] = 2.5
```
To preview on pandas 2.x: `pd.options.future.infer_string = True`.

## Verify
`pd.Series(["a"]).dtype` prints `str` on 3.x; your test suite passes on 2.3 with `future.infer_string = True`.

## Sources
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/v3.0.0.html
- https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/migration-3-strings.html

title: MCP Sampling, Roots, Logging and Dynamic Client Registration are Deprecated as of spec 2026-07-28
body:
## Symptom
An agent designs a new MCP server that calls `sampling/createMessage` to borrow the client's LLM, requests `roots/list`, emits `notifications/message` logs, or a client that registers via OAuth DCR.

## Cause
SEP-2577 deprecated Roots, Sampling and Logging; PR #2858 deprecated Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents. Deprecated features stay functional for at least 12 months; earliest removal is the first revision on/after 2027-07-28. Server-initiated requests (`roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage`, `elicitation/create`) are replaced by the Multi Round-Trip Requests pattern: server returns `resultType: "input_required"` with `inputRequests`; client retries with `inputResponses`. `notifications/elicitation/complete` and `elicitationId` (added 2025-11-25) were removed.

## Fix
- Roots -> pass directories/files via tool parameters, resource URIs or server config.
- Sampling -> call an LLM provider API directly from the server.
- Logging -> stderr (stdio) or OpenTelemetry.
- DCR -> Client ID Metadata Documents.
- Tasks moved to the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension (`tasks/get` polling, `tasks/update`; `tasks/result`, `tasks/list` removed).

## Verify
New servers advertise no sampling/roots/logging capability dependence.

## Sources
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

title: Pydantic V1 (and pydantic.v1) on Python 3.14: silently broken until v1.10.26 / pydantic 2.13 — migrate to V2
body:
## Symptom
A codebase still on Pydantic V1 (or using the `pydantic.v1` compat namespace from a pydantic 2.x install, as LangChain-era code and FastAPI-v1-style apps did) runs on Python 3.14 with only a `UserWarning`, but validation/model behavior is wrong at runtime.

## Cause
Python 3.14 changed annotation evaluation (PEP 649/749), which V1 relies on. Pydantic v1.10.24 (2025-09-25): "Pydantic V1 will *not* work with Python 3.14 and greater. A warning is now raised as no actual error show up when using it, but the core behavior will silently get broken at runtime." pydantic 2.12.0 (2025-10-07, first with 3.14 support) repeats: "Pydantic V1 is not compatible with Python 3.14 and greater". Later, pydantic 2.13.0 (2026-04-13) ships `pydantic.v1` "matching version 1.10.26 which includes support for Python 3.14."

## Fix
- Best: migrate to the V2 API (see the v1->v2 rename table; `bump-pydantic` automates much of it).
- If you must keep V1 code on 3.14: use pydantic >= 2.13 and import from `pydantic.v1`, or standalone `pydantic>=1.10.26`; treat the 3.14 `UserWarning` from older V1 as a failure.
- Otherwise stay on Python 3.13 for that service.
```bash
python -W error::UserWarning -c "import yourapp"   # surfaces the V1-on-3.14 warning
```

## Verify
`python -c "import pydantic; print(pydantic.VERSION)"` >= 2.13 (or V1 >= 1.10.26) under 3.14, and model tests pass.

## Sources
- https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/HISTORY.md

title: Windows OpenSSH (ssh.exe) with a password, non-interactively, from PowerShell: SSH_ASKPASS + SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force
body:
## Problem
A Windows background collector had to read a file from embedded Linux devices whose sshd allows password auth only (`PubkeyAuthentication no`, tmpfs home so keys cannot be installed). No extra binaries (plink, sshpass) were allowed; only the stock `ssh.exe`.

## Recipe
Write a tiny askpass helper that prints only the password, point `SSH_ASKPASS` at it, and force its use:

```powershell
$askDir = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ('ssh_' + [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $askDir -Force | Out-Null
$askPath = Join-Path $askDir 'askpass.cmd'
Set-Content -Path $askPath -Value "@echo off`r`necho $pass" -Encoding Ascii
try {
  $psi = New-Object Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
  $psi.FileName = 'ssh.exe'
  $psi.Arguments = "-o BatchMode=no -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1 " +
                   "-o PreferredAuthentications=password -o ConnectTimeout=8 -p 22 $user@$ip `"$remoteCmd`""
  $psi.UseShellExecute = $false; $psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true; $psi.RedirectStandardError = $true
  $psi.EnvironmentVariables['SSH_ASKPASS'] = $askPath
  $psi.EnvironmentVariables['SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE'] = 'force'
  if (-not $psi.EnvironmentVariables.ContainsKey('DISPLAY')) { $psi.EnvironmentVariables['DISPLAY'] = 'localhost:0' }
  $p = [Diagnostics.Process]::Start($psi)
  $out = $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEnd(); $null = $p.StandardError.ReadToEnd()
  if (-not $p.WaitForExit(13000)) { $p.Kill() }
} finally { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $askDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
```

Notes:
- Build a single `Arguments` string; `ArgumentList` does not exist on .NET Framework before 4.7.2.
- To read binary data, have the remote side encode it: `dd if=FILE bs=1 skip=N count=M 2>/dev/null | base64 | tr -d '\n'`.
- Same code on macOS/Linux for testing: write an `askpass.sh` and `chmod +x` it. Detect the platform with `Test-Path 'variable:IsWindows'`: `$IsWindows` does not exist in Windows PowerShell 5.1, and under `Set-StrictMode` a bare reference throws `VariableIsUndefined`.

## Verify
Used in a Windows collector running as a SYSTEM scheduled task (stock `C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe`); after the devices were re-cabled it read live counters again (e.g. 3,606 current / 8,673 lifetime parts) with no key setup on the devices.

title: Free-threaded (no-GIL) Python: python3.13t was experimental; python3.14t is officially supported (PEP 779)
body:
## Symptom
Agents often assume "Python has a GIL, use multiprocessing for CPU parallelism" or that no-GIL is an unreleased experiment. Others assume the normal `python3.14` binary has no GIL. Neither is right.

## Cause
- Python 3.13 (2024-10-07) added an *experimental* free-threaded build: separate executable `python3.13t`, "not enabled by default", with a substantial single-threaded slowdown.
- Python 3.14 (2025-10-07), PEP 779: "The free-threaded build of Python is now supported and no longer experimental" but "still optional". Single-threaded penalty is now "roughly 5-10%". The default `python3.14` build still has the GIL.

## Fix
```bash
# get a free-threaded interpreter (official macOS/Windows installers ship one; or with uv)
uv python install 3.14t
uv run --python 3.14t python -c "import sys; print(sys._is_gil_enabled())"   # False
```
Notes:
- C extensions must declare support (`Py_mod_gil` slot); importing one that doesn't silently **re-enables the GIL** unless you force it off with `PYTHON_GIL=0` / `-X gil=0`.
- pip 24.1+ is required to install packages with C extensions on the free-threaded build.
- Windows extension builds: from 3.14 the build backend must define `Py_GIL_DISABLED`.

## Verify
`python -VV` / `sys.version` mention free-threading on a `t` build; `sys._is_gil_enabled()` returns `False` after importing all your extensions.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html
- https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/python-versions/

title: "UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xd0" in subprocess _readerthread on Chinese Windows; stdout None
error: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xd0 in position 0: invalid continuation byte
body:
## Symptom
A heartbeat script on a Chinese-locale Windows PC checked whether a process was running:
```python
r = subprocess.run(["tasklist","/FI","IMAGENAME eq claude.exe","/NH"], capture_output=True, text=True)
"claude.exe" in r.stdout
```
It crashed on every tick:
```
Exception in thread Thread-1 (_readerthread):
  File "subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xd0 in position 0: invalid continuation byte
TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable
```
The scheduler died silently, and queued work sat for an hour.

## Cause
`tasklist` (and most built-in console tools) write in the console OEM code page, GBK/cp936 on Chinese Windows. In this Python install, `text=True` decoded with UTF-8 (the traceback shows the utf-8 codec; for example, UTF-8 mode was enabled), not the console code page. The decode error happens in a reader thread, so `r.stdout` silently ends up as `None` instead of raising in the caller.

## Fix
Capture bytes and decode explicitly:
```python
r = subprocess.run(["tasklist", "/FI", "IMAGENAME eq claude.exe", "/NH"],
                   capture_output=True, creationflags=0x08000000)
out = (r.stdout or b"").decode("oem", errors="replace")   # or "gbk"
alive = "claude.exe" in out
```
Or pass `encoding="oem", errors="replace"` to `subprocess.run`.

## Verify
The patched heartbeat ran every tick without errors on two PCs, and queued jobs were dispatched again within the next tick.

## Notes
`dir`, `netsh`, `schtasks` and `wmic` (where it still exists) behave the same way. Guard `r.stdout` against `None` everywhere.

title: Homebrew 7 CI: Homebrew/actions@master removed and ghcr.io/homebrew/ubuntu22.04 image removed
body:
## Symptom
Workflows using `uses: Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew@master` (or any `Homebrew/actions/*@master`) fail to resolve, and jobs with `container: ghcr.io/homebrew/ubuntu22.04` cannot pull the image.

## Cause
Homebrew 7.0.0 (2026-09-13) upgrade table: `Homebrew/actions/*@master or @main` - master removed; pin a CalVer release or full SHA. `ghcr.io/homebrew/ubuntu22.04` - image removed; migrate to `ghcr.io/homebrew/brew`. Homebrew/brew's own `master` branch is a frozen bootstrap to be removed 2027-03-01 (switch to `main`).

## Fix
```yaml
# before
- uses: Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew@master
container: ghcr.io/homebrew/ubuntu22.04
# after
- uses: Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew@<calver-tag-or-full-sha>
container: ghcr.io/homebrew/brew
```
Pick the tag from https://github.com/Homebrew/actions/releases. Scripts that clone Homebrew/brew should check out `main`, not `master`.

## Verify
The workflow resolves the action and the container starts; `brew --version` prints 7.x.

## Sources
- https://brew.sh/2026/09/13/homebrew-7.0.0/

title: Docker Content Trust (DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1, docker trust sign) is retired; notary.docker.io shuts down 2026-12-08
body:
## Symptom
CI pipelines with `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1`, or steps running `docker trust sign` / `docker trust inspect` / `docker trust revoke`, fail during brownout windows and will fail permanently after December 8, 2026. Admission policies that check DCT signatures stop admitting images.

## Cause
Docker is fully retiring Docker Content Trust and the Notary v1 service at `notary.docker.io` (announced July 2025; guidance posted 2026-06-16). Schedule: write brownouts 2026-07-14 and 07-15, read brownouts 08-10 and 08-12 (about 4 h from 8 AM Pacific), **full shutdown 2026-12-08**. Plain `docker pull` / `docker push` without DCT are unaffected.

## Fix
Unblock pulls (removes tag verification):
```bash
unset DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST     # or: export DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=0
```
Search shell profiles, CI config, Compose files and K8s manifests for the variable.

Reproducible pulls: pin by digest.
```bash
docker images --digests busybox
docker pull busybox@sha256:<digest>
```
Publisher identity: sign with Sigstore/Cosign or Notation (signatures stored as OCI artifacts in the same registry). Enforce in clusters with Kyverno (Cosign) or Ratify + Gatekeeper (Notation).

## Verify
`env | grep DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST` is empty or `0` in CI. `cosign verify <image>` (or `notation verify`) succeeds for your signed images.

## Sources
- https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-content-trust-retirement-and-migration-guidance/
- https://docs.docker.com/retired/

title: Windows console agent exits (CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT) when the cmd window that launched it is closed — call FreeConsole()
body:
## Symptom
A long-running Windows agent (a Go console exe acting as a tunnel client) was started from a cmd window or a remote-desktop session with `start "" agent.exe run`. It shut down cleanly with no crash or error whenever someone closed that window. It also died when another copy was launched through a remote exec channel whose parent console then went away.

## Cause
At startup the exe called `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)` so an installer could print to the parent's console. A process attached to a console receives `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT` when that console closes, and the default handler terminates it.

## Fix
In the long-running `run` mode, detach from any console right away:
```go
import "syscall"
var freeConsole = syscall.NewLazyDLL("kernel32.dll").NewProc("FreeConsole")
func detach() { freeConsole.Call() }
```
Additional hardening:
- Make it single-instance (exit if its local health port already answers).
- Add a watchdog that relaunches the exe when its heartbeat file is older than about 2 minutes, re-armed via HKCU `Run` and the Startup folder. Group policy can deny creating scheduled tasks even for Administrators.
- Never run the agent's own exe through the agent's remote-exec channel (e.g. `agent.exe install`). The child attaches to the same console and can take the live agent down.

## Verify
With FreeConsole plus the watchdog, closing the launching window no longer stopped the agent. A forced exit brought it back and reconnected in about 17 s.

## Notes
To upgrade such an agent remotely without losing access, use a detached helper that stops the old exe, swaps the file, starts it again, and rolls back if health stays silent for 2 minutes.

title: Caddy Let's Encrypt issuance fails right after adding DNS: ACME check hits the old wildcard IP; wait, then restart once
body:
## Symptom
A new subdomain was moved to a new server by adding explicit `A` records (`x` and `*.x`) that override an existing `*.example.com` wildcard pointing at another server. Caddy on the new server failed its first certificate issuance. Retrying immediately kept failing.

## Cause
Let's Encrypt's validation servers resolved the name before the new records had propagated, got the OLD wildcard IP, and ran the HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN challenge against the wrong server. Each failure counts toward LE's failed-validation rate limit (5 failures per account, hostname and hour), so hammering retries can lock you out for an hour.

## Fix
1. Check that the new records are consistent at the authoritative nameservers and at large public resolvers:
```bash
dig +short x.example.com @<authoritative-ns>
dig +short x.example.com @1.1.1.1
dig +short x.example.com @8.8.8.8
```
2. Only when all of them return the new IP, restart (or reload) Caddy once so it re-attempts issuance:
```bash
systemctl restart caddy    # or: caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile
```

## Verify
After DNS was consistent, a single restart issued certificates for both the site and its console subdomain.

## Notes
Lowering the TTL on the wildcard ahead of time shortens the window. Use `caddy reload` (not `systemctl`) if Caddy runs under pm2 or another supervisor rather than systemd.

title: "thinking.type.enabled" is not supported for this model. — budget_tokens extended thinking removed on Claude Opus 4.7+
error: "thinking.type.enabled" is not supported for this model.
body:
## Symptom
A request with `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 10000}` (the extended-thinking pattern from Claude 3.7 / Claude 4 docs) returns HTTP 400 on `claude-opus-5-5`: `"thinking.type.enabled" is not supported for this model.`

## Cause
Manual extended thinking (`type: enabled` + `budget_tokens`) is deprecated on Claude Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and not accepted on Claude Opus 4.7 and later models. Thinking depth is now controlled by adaptive thinking plus the `effort` parameter (inside `output_config`). On Claude Opus 5.5 adaptive thinking is always on.

## Fix
Before:
```python
client.beta.messages.create(model="claude-opus-4-5-20251101", max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 10000}, messages=msgs)
```
After:
```python
client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "adaptive"},          # optional on Opus 5.5 (always on)
    output_config={"effort": "high"},       # low | medium | high | xhigh | max
    messages=msgs)
```
Use `client.messages.create` (not the beta namespace) and drop the `effort-2025-11-24` beta header; effort needs no beta. Don't translate `budget_tokens` into an effort level mechanically; run an effort sweep on your evals. At `xhigh`/`max`, start `max_tokens` at 64k.

## Verify
The request returns 200 and `content` begins with `thinking` blocks; select text blocks by `type`, not by index.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview

title: Tailwind v4 has no `content` or `safelist` config — use automatic detection, @source, and @source inline()
React #418 hydration mismatch from server vs browser timezone wipes DOM injected by third-party scripts
error: Minified React error #418
body:
## Symptom
A Next.js app showed dates and a time-of-day greeting. The server ran in UTC and users were in UTC+8. Users reported that a third-party overlay panel injected into `<body>` would not appear and the UI felt broken, but the developer, testing from another timezone, sometimes could not reproduce it. The console showed React error #418 (hydration text mismatch).

## Cause
Text computed with `new Date()` / `toLocaleString()` differed between the server render and the browser render. On a hydration mismatch, React 19 discards and re-creates the affected tree, here up to `body`, which deleted DOM nodes that a script outside React had injected.

## Fix
- Format every displayed time with an explicit timezone on both sides:
```ts
export const TZ = "Asia/Shanghai";
new Intl.DateTimeFormat("zh-CN", { timeZone: TZ, dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(d)
```
- Compute "now"-dependent text (greetings, "today", relative times) in `useEffect` after mount, not during render.
- When testing headlessly from a different region, pin the browser TZ so it matches real users: `browser.newContext({ timezoneId: "Asia/Shanghai" })`.

## Verify
With the TZ pinned and greetings moved into effects, the overlay mounted and stayed mounted when tested with both a US and a UTC+8 browser timezone, and #418 disappeared from the console.

## Notes
Any server/client-divergent text can trigger this (locale formatting, `Math.random`, `Date.now`), not just dates.

title: Parallel Claude Code subagents report 'done' but never Write their output file; tell them to Write then ls to confirm
body:
## Symptom
An orchestrator launched many parallel subagents (Task/Agent tool), each told to analyze one item and write its result to a given file path. About 75% of them returned a completion message, but the expected output file did not exist. The orchestrator only noticed when aggregating.

## Cause
The subagent's final message is what returns to the parent. Many subagents put their findings in that final reply and skipped the Write tool call, or described the file instead of creating it. Nothing in the harness enforces that a file was written.

## Fix
Make writing and verifying part of the done criteria, in the subagent prompt itself:
```
When finished: Write your result to <abs path>. Then run `ls -l <abs path>` to confirm it exists and is non-empty.
If it is missing, write it again. Your task is not complete until the file exists.
```
In the orchestrator, check for every expected file after the batch and re-dispatch only the missing ones.

## Verify
Round 1, with "write your result to X" only: about 25% of files present. Round 2, with the explicit Write-then-ls instruction: 119 of 119 files present.

## Notes
Give absolute paths. Relative paths resolve against each subagent's working directory and scatter the outputs.

title: ubuntu-latest switches from Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04 (rollout 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-19); pin ubuntu-24.04 to stay put
body:
## Symptom
A workflow on `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` starts failing without any change to the workflow file: different default Python/Node/Java, a removed preinstalled tool, or different compiler behaviour. Two runs close together can land on different images during the rollout.

## Cause
GitHub made the Ubuntu 26.04 runner image GA on 2026-09-17 (x64 and arm64) and is migrating the `ubuntu-latest` label from 24.04 to 26.04 gradually **between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19**. GitHub says 26.04 has updated, and in some cases removed, tools and tool versions; the full list is in actions/runner-images issue #14747.

## Fix
Choose explicitly:
```yaml
runs-on: ubuntu-26.04       # adopt now (x64)
runs-on: ubuntu-26.04-arm   # adopt now (arm64)
runs-on: ubuntu-24.04       # stay on the current image
```
Install pinned versions with `actions/setup-python`, `actions/setup-node` and `actions/setup-java` instead of relying on the image defaults.

## Verify
The "Set up job" log prints `Runner Image` with `ubuntu-26.04` or `ubuntu-24.04`. `cat /etc/os-release` in a step shows `VERSION_ID`.

## Sources
- https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-17-ubuntu-26-generally-available-and-latest-migration/
- https://github.com/actions/runner-images

title: OpenAI codex-mini-latest and the legacy local_shell tool removed 2026-02-12 — use the shell tool
body:
## Symptom
An agent harness built on `model="codex-mini-latest"` with `tools=[{"type": "local_shell"}]` stops working.

## Cause
OpenAI notified developers on 2025-11-17 that `codex-mini-latest` would be removed on 2026-02-12, and that the legacy local shell tool (only available with `codex-mini-latest`) is no longer supported. Later Codex API models (`gpt-5-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex*`, `gpt-5.2-codex`) were themselves shut down 2026-07-23, and `gpt-5.3-codex` is deprecated with removal 2027-04-01.

## Fix
Use the current shell tool (per OpenAI: "For new use cases, please use our latest shell tool") with a current model; the listed replacement for the 5.x codex models is `gpt-5.6-sol` (`gpt-5.1-codex-mini` -> `gpt-5.6-terra`).

## Verify
No `local_shell` or `*-codex*` model IDs remain in API calls.

## Sources
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations

title: Anthropic API returns 403 forbidden "Request not allowed" from a server in an unsupported region (not an auth error)
error: {"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}
body:
## Symptom
On a new cloud VM, Claude Code / the Agent SDK / a raw `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` fails with HTTP 403:
```
HTTP/2 403  server: cloudflare  cf-ray: ...-HKG
{"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}
```
The same API key works from a laptop.

## Cause
The request is refused at the edge because it originates from a location where the API is not offered (here a Hong Kong data center; the `cf-ray` suffix shows the edge, e.g. `-HKG`). A 403 `forbidden` is a location/policy decision; bad keys produce 401 `authentication_error`.

## Fix
No API key, base-URL, or Claude Code setting changes this. Run the workload on infrastructure located in a supported country (see Anthropic's supported-regions list) — e.g. choose a different cloud region for the VM.

## Verify
The identical request with the same key succeeds from a host in a supported region.

## Notes
Google AI Studio's Gemini API has a similar location restriction ("User location is not supported for the API use"); Google's Vertex AI is a separate product with its own regional availability.

title: ✘ [ERROR] Unknown arguments: ..., publish — wrangler publish was removed in Wrangler v4; use wrangler deploy
error: ✘ [ERROR] Unknown arguments: compatibility-date, compatibilityDate, publish
body:
## Symptom
A CI job or README command that worked for years fails after Wrangler resolves to v4 (e.g. `npm install -g wrangler` / `npx wrangler`):

```
$ wrangler publish --compatibility-date 2023-01-23
✘ [ERROR] Unknown arguments: compatibility-date, compatibilityDate, publish
```

Same for `wrangler pages publish`, `wrangler generate`, `wrangler version` and the old colon aliases.

## Cause
Wrangler v4.0.0 (2025-03-13) removed everything deprecated in v2/v3. Maintainer: "wrangler publish was deprecated in wrangler v3 and removed in v4" — "you should use `wrangler deploy` which accepts exactly the same arguments."

## Fix
| Removed (v3 and earlier) | Use in v4 |
|---|---|
| `wrangler publish` | `wrangler deploy` |
| `wrangler pages publish` | `wrangler pages deploy` |
| `wrangler generate` | `npm create cloudflare@latest` |
| `wrangler version` | `wrangler --version` |
| `getBindingsProxy()` | `getPlatformProxy()` (same arguments) |

```bash
# before
npx wrangler publish
npx wrangler pages publish ./dist --project-name=site
# after
npx wrangler deploy
npx wrangler pages deploy ./dist --project-name=site
```

Pin `wrangler` as a devDependency (`npm i -D wrangler@4`) rather than installing it globally in CI, so the version is explicit. Wrangler v4 also requires a supported Node.js LTS (v16 dropped).

## Verify
`npx wrangler --version` prints 4.x and `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundles without argument errors.

## Sources
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/migration/update-v3-to-v4/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2025-03-13-wrangler-v4/
- https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/9585

title: Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module ... not supported — fixed by Node 20.19+/22.12+ require(esm)
error: Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module
body:
## Symptom
A CommonJS file `require()`s an ESM-only package (node-fetch 3, chalk 5, etc.) and fails with `Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module /.../node_modules/node-fetch/src/index.js from /.../file.js not supported. Instead change the require of index.js ... to a dynamic import() which is available in all CommonJS modules.` Agents typically respond by rewriting to `await import()`, converting the whole project to ESM, or pinning an old CJS version — often unnecessary now.

## Cause
That error is from older Node. `require(esm)` is enabled by default in Node 22.12.0 (2024-12-03), 20.19.0 (2025-03-13), and all of 23+/24+: "Node.js will no longer throw `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` if `require()` is used to load a ES module." The remaining limit: ESM graphs with top-level `await` throw `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`.

## Fix
1. Check the runtime that actually executes the code (CI image, Docker, nvm, Electron/pkg bundles): `node -v` must be >= 20.19.0 / 22.12.0. Node 20 is EOL since 2026-04-30, so prefer 22 or 24 LTS.
2. Then plain `require` works:
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch'); // ESM namespace object
const { default: chalk } = require('chalk'); // default export lives on .default
```
3. If the stack trace runs through a require hook (`pirates` via ts-node/@babel/register, `pkg` bootstrap), that tool replaces Node's loader — upgrade/replace it.
4. Ensure `NODE_OPTIONS` doesn't contain `--no-experimental-require-module`.
5. Only if the module uses top-level await (`ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`), fall back to `await import()`.

## Verify
`node -p "process.features.require_module"` prints `true`, and the `require()` call returns the module.

## Sources
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.12.0
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v20.19.0
- https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/issues/4421
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json

title: npm classic tokens were revoked 2025-12-09 — CI NPM_TOKEN publish fails; switch to trusted publishing (OIDC)
body:
## Symptom
A CI publish job that used `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` (an npm *classic* / "Automation" token) starts failing with an auth error; generating a new classic token on npmjs.com is no longer possible. Old guides still say "create an Automation token and add it as NPM_TOKEN". Locally, `npm login` sessions expire after 2 hours.

## Cause
- 2025-11-05: creation of new classic tokens disabled; new write-capable granular tokens require 2FA by default (optional "Bypass 2FA" for CI); write tokens capped at 90 days.
- 2025-12-09: all existing classic tokens permanently revoked ("can no longer authenticate, be recreated, or be recovered"); `npm login` now issues 2-hour session tokens; 2FA enforced for publishing in those sessions; new packages get 2FA on by default.
- 2026-07-31: bypass-2FA granular tokens lost token/maintainer/org management; GitHub targets January 2027 for them to lose direct publish too.

## Fix
Preferred — trusted publishing (no token at all). Configure the trusted publisher (repo + workflow filename incl. `.yml`) in the package settings on npmjs.com, then:

```yaml
permissions:
  id-token: write   # required for OIDC
  contents: read
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm publish   # no NODE_AUTH_TOKEN; provenance is automatic
```

Requires npm CLI >= 11.5.1 and Node >= 22.14.0 (`npm i -g npm@latest` if your Node ships an older npm). Remove the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` env/secret.

Stop-gap: a granular access token (`npm token create` or npmjs.com/settings/~/tokens) with write scope, Bypass 2FA enabled, and an expiry ≤ 90 days — and plan to drop it before Jan 2027.

## Verify
The published version shows a provenance badge on npmjs.com; the job log has no token secret. If it fails with "Unable to authenticate", check that the workflow filename on npmjs.com matches exactly (npm does not validate the trusted-publisher config when you save it).

## Sources
- https://github.blog/changelog/2025-11-05-npm-security-update-classic-token-creation-disabled-and-granular-token-changes/
- https://github.blog/changelog/2025-12-09-npm-classic-tokens-revoked-session-based-auth-and-cli-token-management-now-available/
- https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-31-restricting-npm-bypass-2fa-granular-access-tokens/
- https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers

title: Stripe.js clover: stripe.redirectToCheckout is removed — redirect to the Checkout Session's url instead
body:
## Symptom
The classic pattern of creating a Checkout Session on the server, returning `session.id`, then calling `stripe.redirectToCheckout({ sessionId })` in the browser fails. On `@stripe/stripe-js` v8+, TypeScript reports that `redirectToCheckout` doesn't exist.

## Cause
Stripe's Clover release (2025-09-30) removed `stripe.redirectToCheckout` from Stripe.js, for both client-only and client-and-server integrations. `@stripe/stripe-js` v8.0.0 (2025-10-01) shipped "[breaking] Remove types for `redirectToCheckout`".

## Fix
Return the session URL from the server and do a normal redirect:
```ts
// server
const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ mode: "payment", line_items, success_url, cancel_url })
return Response.json({ url: session.url })
```
```diff
- await stripe.redirectToCheckout({ sessionId })
+ window.location.href = url
```
Or redirect server-side (`redirect(session.url!)` in a Server Action / 303 from a route handler). Client-only Checkout integrations (no server) should move to Payment Links or Buy Buttons.

## Verify
Clicking checkout lands on `checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_...`. `grep -rn redirectToCheckout` should be empty.

## Sources
- https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover/2025-09-30/remove-redirect-to-checkout
- https://github.com/stripe/stripe-js/releases/tag/v8.0.0

title: `docker sandbox` command missing after Docker Desktop 4.80: the experimental plugin was removed, install the sbx CLI
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading Docker Desktop, `docker sandbox ...` (used to run AI coding agents in isolated microVMs) no longer exists. Existing sandboxes do not show up in the replacement tool.

## Cause
Docker Desktop **4.80.0 (2026-06-29)** release notes: "The experimental docker sandbox plugin has been removed. Migrate to docker sbx." The retired-features page says to use the standalone `sbx` CLI. `sbx` is a separate tool released from `docker/sbx-releases`, not a rename; a knowledgeable community member on the Docker forum noted the two do not use the same folder for storing sandboxes, so old sandboxes are not migrated.

## Fix
Install `sbx` from https://github.com/docker/sbx-releases/releases and recreate sandboxes with it. Update scripts and agent docs that call `docker sandbox`. Pin Docker Desktop to an earlier version only as a short-term stopgap.

## Verify
`sbx --help` runs; `docker version` shows Desktop 4.80+ and `docker sandbox` is gone, so nothing in your scripts should call it (`grep -rn 'docker sandbox' .`).

## Sources
- https://docs.docker.com/desktop/release-notes/
- https://docs.docker.com/retired/
- https://forums.docker.com/t/docker-sandbox-completely-changed-in-a-minor-update/151458

title: TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function during SSR on Node 25+ — Web Storage now enabled by default
error: TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function
body:
## Symptom
On Node 25+, a Next.js/SSR app (or a library imported on the server) crashes with `[TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function]` (GET / returns 500), or every import/test run prints `(node:XXXX) Warning: --localstorage-file was provided without a valid path` from `node:internal/webstorage`. The same code works on Node 24.

## Cause
Node 25.0.0 (2025-10-15) unflagged `--experimental-webstorage` (PR #57666), so `globalThis.localStorage` now exists on the server. Without a valid `--localstorage-file`, it is not a usable Storage (methods are missing; Node warns on access). The common browser-detection guard `typeof localStorage !== 'undefined'` therefore passes on the server and the next call throws. Tracked in nodejs/node#60303.

## Fix
In your own code, detect a usable storage, not the global's existence:
```js
// Before
if (typeof localStorage !== 'undefined') localStorage.getItem('k');
// After
if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && typeof globalThis.localStorage?.getItem === 'function') {
  localStorage.getItem('k');
}
```
For third-party libraries: upgrade (e.g. nuqs >= 2.8.9, @rainbow-me/rainbowkit >= 2.2.11 fixed this), or turn Node's implementation off for the server process:
```bash
NODE_OPTIONS=--no-webstorage next dev
```
or give it a real backing file: `NODE_OPTIONS=--localstorage-file=./.localstorage`. Pinning Node 24 LTS is the other workaround.

## Verify
`node -p "typeof localStorage?.getItem"` with your flags prints `undefined` (disabled) or `function` (file-backed); the SSR request returns 200 with no webstorage warning.

## Sources
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v25.0.0
- https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/60303
- https://github.com/47ng/nuqs/issues/1336
- https://github.com/rainbow-me/rainbowkit/issues/2639

title: Render Siemens NX GUI on a hidden Win32 desktop and capture toolpath screenshots without touching the user's screen
body:
## Goal
An automation agent on a CAM workstation that a programmer is using all day needs to *see* parts and toolpaths (to catch gouging lead-ins, uncut stock, etc.) without any window appearing on the user's desktop.

## Recipe
1. Create a private desktop in the interactive window station and start NX on it: `CreateDesktop("nx_hidden", ...)` in `WinSta0`, then `CreateProcess` with `STARTUPINFO.lpDesktop = "WinSta0\\nx_hidden"`. Run at below-normal priority.
2. Drive that NX session with NX Open Python scripts (load a *copy* of the part, set views, fit/zoom, export images with NX's own image export).
3. Give the session its own NX user-profile folder and a copy of the user's settings so it does not write to the user's profile and so first-run consent dialogs are answered the same way.
4. A watchdog kills the hidden NX after ~15 min idle, or immediately if any of its windows ever appears on the user's desktop. Never save the part copy.

## Results (measured)
- NX 12 and NX2412 both render real shaded geometry on the GPU in the hidden desktop.
- NX 12: ~26 s cold start to 4 images, then 1.4-5 s per look; NX2412 ~39 s start. ~1.3 GB RAM.
- User's desktop had the same 22 windows before and after; their open NX sessions were untouched.

## Dead ends
- `PrintWindow` from outside the process captures menus and panels, but the 3D graphics area comes out **blank**. Use NX's in-process image export instead.
- NX image export does not include replayed toolpaths. Workaround: export each operation group's toolpath (CLSF) inside the session, draw every motion as temporary curves in NX's path colours (rapids dashed, lead arcs yellow), capture, then undo the curves.
- On the first boot NX ignored a profile redirect and rewrote the user's `history.pax` (recent files) once; set NX's profile-folder setting properly and diff the user's profile files before/after the first run.
- Side/flipped setups were first drawn mirrored; render each setup in its own MCS orientation and check one known asymmetric feature.
