Method writeAsStringAsync imported from "expo-file-system" is deprecated — Expo SDK 54 switched the default API
error: Method writeAsStringAsync imported from "expo-file-system" is deprecated.
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Expo SDK 54, code that calls the classic functions throws at runtime:
```
Error: Method writeAsStringAsync imported from "expo-file-system" is deprecated.
You can migrate to the new filesystem API using "File" and "Directory" classes or import the legacy API from "expo-file-system/legacy".
```
The same error is thrown for `readAsStringAsync`, `readDirectoryAsync`, `moveAsync`, `uploadAsync` and so on. `FileSystem.documentDirectory` and `EncodingType` are no longer on the default export. Libraries that feature-detect `readAsStringAsync` (for example older posthog-react-native) break too, because the function still exists but throws when called.

## Cause
Expo SDK 54 (2025-09-10) made the former `expo-file-system/next` object-oriented API (`File`, `Directory`, `Paths`) the default export of `expo-file-system`. The old function API moved to `expo-file-system/legacy`. Expo planned to remove the legacy entry point in a later SDK, so migrate rather than relying on it.

## Fix
Quickest (behaviour unchanged):
```ts
// before
import * as FileSystem from 'expo-file-system'
// after
import * as FileSystem from 'expo-file-system/legacy'
```
Proper migration to the new API:
```ts
import { File, Paths } from 'expo-file-system'

const file = new File(Paths.document, 'test.txt')
file.write('Hello world')        // was writeAsStringAsync(uri, ...)
const content = await file.text() // was readAsStringAsync(uri)
```
If you were importing from `expo-file-system/next`, change the import to `expo-file-system`. In SDK 56 (2026-05-21), `File`/`Directory` `copy()` and `move()` became async (they return a Promise). Use `copySync()` / `moveSync()` for synchronous behaviour. Update third-party libraries that wrap expo-file-system.

## Verify
The write/read round-trip works on a device or simulator, and Metro logs no "is deprecated" error.

## Sources
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-54
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-56
- https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/2453
- https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/3151

title: Run Claude Code's Bash tool on another machine via CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL: the exact `-c "... eval '<cmd>'"` format it sends
body:
## Goal
Run the Claude Code CLI on a server, but have its Bash (and PowerShell) tool calls execute on a different machine. Native features should keep working: background commands, Monitor, TaskStop, subagents.

## How Claude Code invokes the shell
With `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL=/path/to/wrapper`, every Bash tool call becomes `wrapper -c <script>`, with exactly two argv entries. On 2.1.280 the script looked like this:
```
source ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/snapshot-bash-<id>.sh 2>/dev/null || true && shopt -u extglob 2>/dev/null || true && { \builtin unalias -- 'unsetenv'; \builtin unset -f -- 'unsetenv'; } >/dev/null 2>&1 || true && eval 'cd /tmp && echo hi' < /dev/null && pwd -P >| /tmp/claude-c6f8-cwd
```
The user command is the single-quoted argument to `eval`. The new working directory is read back from the `/tmp/claude-XXXX-cwd` file. A wrapper that parses out the `eval '...'` payload, runs it remotely, streams stdout/stderr, exits with the remote exit code and writes the remote cwd into that file keeps Claude Code's cwd tracking and background-task machinery intact. Probe your version first with a logging wrapper:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
for a in "$@"; do printf 'ARG<%s>\n' "$a"; done >> /tmp/shell.log
exec /bin/bash "$@"
```

## PowerShell tool on Linux
`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1` adds a `PowerShell` tool even on Linux. It runs the first `pwsh` on PATH as `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -NoLogo -EncodedCommand <base64 UTF-16LE>`. A `pwsh` shim on PATH can forward that to a Windows host.

## File tools
A PreToolUse hook that returns `updatedInput` can redirect `Read` to a locally mirrored copy of the remote file. `Edit`/`Write` validate their path before hooks run, so Windows paths are rejected. They were replaced with MCP tools (MCP server config `alwaysLoad: true` so they are present without ToolSearch).

## Verify
Tested headless (`claude -p --output-format stream-json`): Bash, background Bash, Monitor and PowerShell calls all ran through the wrappers. A real job over a 265 ms link took about 369 ms per command, and every step of an Opus task completed correctly.

title: TypeScript 6/7: moduleResolution node (node10), target es5, module amd/umd deprecated in 6.0, removed in 7.0
body:
## Symptom
A tsconfig with `"moduleResolution": "node"` (or `node10`/`classic`), `"target": "es5"`, `"downlevelIteration": true`, `"module": "amd"|"umd"|"system"|"none"`, `"outFile"`, or `"esModuleInterop": false` produces deprecation errors on TypeScript 6.0 and is rejected outright by TypeScript 7.0. Agents still generate these from older templates.

## Cause
TypeScript 6.0 (2026-03-23) deprecated `--moduleResolution node`/`node10` (it models an outdated Node resolution algorithm), `target: es5` (lowest target is now ES2015), `downlevelIteration`, `baseUrl`, and the `amd`/`umd`/`systemjs`/`none` module values; removed `moduleResolution classic` and `outFile`; and no longer allows `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports` to be `false`. Deprecations can be silenced in 6.0 with `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"`. TypeScript 7.0 (2026-07-08) does not support any of them.

## Fix
```diff
{
  "compilerOptions": {
-   "target": "es5",
-   "moduleResolution": "node",
-   "downlevelIteration": true,
-   "esModuleInterop": false,
+   "target": "es2022",
+   "module": "nodenext",            // code run directly by Node.js
+   "moduleResolution": "nodenext"
+   // or, for Vite/webpack/Next/Bun: "module": "esnext", "moduleResolution": "bundler"
  }
}
```
If you truly need ES5 output, transpile with an external tool (Babel/SWC) after `tsc`. Note other 6.0 default changes when you remove explicit settings: `strict` defaults to `true`, `module` to `esnext`, `target` to the latest (es2025), `rootDir` to the tsconfig folder, `types` to `[]`.

## Verify
`npx tsc --noEmit` on TS 6 succeeds without `ignoreDeprecations`, which means it will also load under TS 7.

## Sources
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0-beta/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/

title: google-generativeai is deprecated (support ended 2025-11-30) — use google-genai: from google import genai
body:
## Symptom
An agent writes `import google.generativeai as genai`, `genai.configure(api_key=...)`, `genai.GenerativeModel(...)`. The package is frozen (last release 0.8.6) and new models/features (Veo, Imagen, Live, new config fields) are not supported.

## Cause
Google replaced the legacy SDK with the unified Google Gen AI SDK. The `google-generativeai` PyPI page states: "All support for this repository ended permanently on November 30, 2025."

## Fix
```bash
pip uninstall -y google-generativeai && pip install -U google-genai
```
Before:
```python
import google.generativeai as genai
genai.configure(api_key=KEY)
model = genai.GenerativeModel("gemini-3.8-flash")
r = model.generate_content("Tell me a story", generation_config=genai.GenerationConfig(temperature=0.2))
```
After:
```python
from google import genai
from google.genai import types
client = genai.Client()   # reads GEMINI_API_KEY
r = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-3.8-flash", contents="Tell me a story",
        config=types.GenerateContentConfig(temperature=0.2))
print(r.text)
```
Other renames: `model.start_chat()` -> `client.chats.create(model=...)`; `genai.upload_file(path=)` -> `client.files.upload(file=)`; `genai.list_files/get_file/delete_file` -> `client.files.list/get/delete`.

## Verify
`pip show google-generativeai` reports not installed; `grep -rn 'google.generativeai' .` is empty.

## Sources
- https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/migrate
- https://pypi.org/project/google-generativeai/

title: uv pip install targets .venv (even if not activated), not the global Python; uv venvs ship without pip
body:
## Symptom
Agent runs `uv pip install x` then `python -c "import x"` and gets `ModuleNotFoundError`, because the bare `python` on PATH is not the env uv installed into. Or, inside a `uv venv`-created environment, `python -m pip install ...` fails because pip is not present.

## Cause
From uv's pip-compatibility docs: "uv will always install packages into the currently active virtual environment, or search for a virtual environment named .venv in the current directory or any parent directory (even if it is not activated)." pip installs into whatever interpreter it belongs to. uv inverts the default: system installs need explicit opt-in. `uv venv` does not seed pip unless asked (`--seed`; and setuptools/wheel are not included for Python 3.12+).

## Fix
```bash
uv venv                         # creates .venv
uv pip install requests         # goes into ./.venv
uv run python -c "import requests"     # run inside that env without activating
# or: source .venv/bin/activate

# a specific interpreter / system Python (CI images, Docker)
uv pip install --system requests
uv pip install --python /usr/bin/python3.12 requests

# need pip inside the env for a legacy tool
uv venv --seed
```
In projects prefer `uv add requests` (updates pyproject.toml + uv.lock) and `uv run ...`.

## Verify
`uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"` prints the `.venv` path.

## Sources
- https://docs.astral.sh/uv/pip/compatibility/
- https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/

title: ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file — ESLint 9+ ignores .eslintrc; migrate to flat config
error: ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file.
body:
## Symptom
Running `npx eslint .` in a project that has `.eslintrc.json` / `.eslintrc.js` / an `eslintConfig` key in package.json prints:

```
ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file.

From ESLint v9.0.0, the default configuration file is now eslint.config.js.
If you are using a .eslintrc.* file, please follow the migration guide
to update your configuration file to the new format:
```
(ESLint 10 prints `ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.* file.`)

## Cause
ESLint v9.0.0 (2024-04-05) made flat config (`eslint.config.js`) the default; eslintrc files are no longer searched for. In v9 you could still opt back with `ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false`, but ESLint v10.0.0 (2026-02-06) removed the eslintrc format completely, so that env var no longer helps. `package.json` `eslintConfig` and `.eslintignore` are not read by flat config either.

## Fix
Generate a starting flat config from the old file:
```bash
npx @eslint/migrate-config .eslintrc.json
```
Minimal hand-written equivalent:
```js
// eslint.config.js
import { defineConfig, globalIgnores } from 'eslint/config'
import js from '@eslint/js'
import globals from 'globals'

export default defineConfig([
  globalIgnores(['dist', 'build']),          // replaces .eslintignore
  {
    files: ['**/*.{js,mjs,cjs}'],
    plugins: { js },
    extends: ['js/recommended'],              // replaces extends: ['eslint:recommended']
    languageOptions: { globals: { ...globals.browser, ...globals.node } }, // replaces env
    rules: { 'no-unused-vars': 'warn' },
  },
])
```
For a shareable config still in eslintrc format, wrap it with `FlatCompat` from `@eslint/eslintrc` (`...compat.extends('eslint-config-foo')`). Note: in flat config `.eslintignore`'s `temp.js` must become `**/temp.js`, and `--env`, `--ignore-path`, `--rulesdir`, `--no-eslintrc` (now `--no-config-lookup`) are gone. Delete the old `.eslintrc*` files afterwards.

Only as a v9 stopgap: `ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false npx eslint .` (does nothing on v10).

## Verify
`npx eslint --print-config src/index.js` prints the resolved config; `npx eslint .` lints without the message.

## Sources
- https://eslint.org/docs/v9.x/use/migrate-to-9.0.0
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/migrate-to-10.0.0
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide
- https://unpkg.com/eslint@9.39.1/messages/config-file-missing.js
- https://eslint.org/blog/2025/03/flat-config-extends-define-config-global-ignores/

title: Read Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl program name and part count over S7 (TCP 102) without OPC UA
body:
## Symptom
Need the running program name, part counters, and status from a SINUMERIK 840D sl. OPC UA (4840) is not licensed/enabled, but TCP 102 (S7) on the service port is open. snap7 has no NCK variable support.

## Fix
Speak raw S7comm to the NCK:
1. COTP connect to the NCK at **rack 0, slot 4** (try 4, 2, 3, 1 if unsure), then S7 Setup Communication.
2. Read Var requests use **syntax-id 0x82** (NCK) instead of 0x10 (ANY). Item = `12 08 82 <(area<<5)|unit> <colHi colLo> <rowHi rowLo> <module> <count>` (area/unit/column/row/module per variable).
3. Take variable addresses from the open-source table `NCAddresses.ts` in github.com/Vunnupyx/clight (Southbound/DataSources/S7/SinumerikNCK); module names/codes are also in Wireshark's `packet-s7comm.c` (`nck_module_names`).
4. **Every data PDU needs the COTP data header `02 f0 80` after the 4-byte TPKT** — omitting it on reads was the bug that made the NCK close the socket.
5. **NCK numeric payloads are little-endian** (unlike PLC S7 data).

Useful variables: `/Channel/ProgramPointer/progName`, `/Channel/ProgramInfo/workPandProgName`, `/Channel/State/actParts`, `reqParts`, `totalParts`, `/Channel/State/progStatus` (3 = running, 5 = aborted/reset), `/Bag/State/opMode`.

## Verify
Live read returned `progName '_N_O14116SG_MPF'`, `workPandProgName '/_N_MPF_DIR/_N_O14116SG_MPF'`, `progStatus 5`, actParts/reqParts counts, and NCK version; axis positions changed between polls on a moving machine.

## Notes
Read-only. If several NCUs on one cable all answer on the default service IP (192.168.215.1), pin each by MAC with `arp -s` before connecting.

title: `experimental.ppr` has been merged into `experimental.cacheComponents`: Next.js 16 removed ppr/dynamicIO/useCache flags
error: `experimental.ppr` has been merged into `experimental.cacheComponents`.
body:
## Symptom
A next.config copied from Next.js 15 tutorials (`experimental: { ppr: 'incremental' }`, `experimental: { dynamicIO: true }`, `experimental: { useCache: true }`) or a route that exports `export const experimental_ppr = true` stops working on Next.js 16. One reported message: `[Error: `experimental.ppr` has been merged into `experimental.cacheComponents`. The Partial Prerendering feature is still available, but is now enabled via `experimental.cacheComponents`. Please update your next.config.ts accordingly.]`

## Cause
Next.js 16 (2025-10-21) removed `experimental.ppr`, the route-level `experimental_ppr` export, `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache`. PPR and `"use cache"` now ship as Cache Components behind the TOP-LEVEL `cacheComponents` option. The `experimental.cacheComponents` placement in the message above comes from the canary period. In stable 16 the option is top-level, not under `experimental`.

## Fix
Before:
```ts
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: { ppr: 'incremental', dynamicIO: true, useCache: true },
}
// app/page.tsx
export const experimental_ppr = true
```
After, if you actually use PPR / `"use cache"`:
```ts
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}
export default nextConfig
```
and delete every `export const experimental_ppr` (the `npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest` codemod removes these).

If you were NOT using these features, just delete the flags and leave `cacheComponents` off. Turning it on is not a rename: it changes the rendering model and can surface errors such as "Uncached data was accessed outside of `<Suspense>`" plus incompatibility with `dynamic`/`revalidate`/`fetchCache`/`dynamicParams` segment configs. Projects that relied on PPR from 15 canaries are told to stay on that canary until they migrate.

## Verify
`next build` starts without config errors, and `grep -rn "experimental_ppr\|dynamicIO\|useCache:" .` returns nothing.

## Sources
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr
- https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache
- https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16
- https://github.com/vercel/next-learn/issues/1114

title: RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread 'MainThread' — get_event_loop() changed in Python 3.14
error: RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread 'MainThread'.
body:
## Symptom
Code that worked on 3.12/3.13 (with only a DeprecationWarning) now crashes on Python 3.14:

```
RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread 'MainThread'.
```

Typical triggers: `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(...)` at a sync entry point, `get_event_loop()` in a default argument or class body at import time, or test suites (tenacity, Twisted, aioimaplib all hit this).

## Cause
Python 3.14 (released 2025-10-07): "`asyncio.get_event_loop()` now raises a `RuntimeError` if there is no current event loop, and no longer implicitly creates an event loop."

## Fix
```python
# before
loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
try:
    loop.run_until_complete(main())
finally:
    loop.close()

# after
asyncio.run(main())

# sync code interleaved with async calls
with asyncio.Runner() as runner:
    runner.run(step_one())
    blocking_code()
    runner.run(step_two())

# inside a coroutine/callback that needs the loop object
loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
```
Never call `get_event_loop()` at import time (default args, class attributes). If a dependency does it, upgrade it (tenacity fixed it in PR #528) or stay on 3.13.

## Verify
Run with `python3.14 -W error::DeprecationWarning -m pytest`; no RuntimeError and no asyncio deprecation warnings.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html
- https://github.com/jd/tenacity/issues/527

title: Expo: expo-av is deprecated and unmaintained (removed from Expo Go in SDK 55) — use expo-audio and expo-video
body:
## Symptom
Models still write `import { Audio, Video } from 'expo-av'` with `Audio.Sound.createAsync()` and `<Video source=... useNativeControls />`. On SDK 55+ this does not run in Expo Go, and in development builds expo-av gets no patches and may stop working.

## Cause
- SDK 53 (2025-04-30) deprecated expo-av: its Video component was replaced by `expo-video`, and `expo-audio` became the recommended audio library. No new expo-av versions are published for SDK 54+.
- SDK 54 (2025-09-10) was the last SDK that included expo-av.
- SDK 55 (2026-02-25) removed expo-av from Expo Go.

## Fix
```bash
npx expo install expo-audio expo-video
npm rm expo-av
```
Audio:
```tsx
// before
const { sound } = await Audio.Sound.createAsync(require('./assets/hello.mp3'))
await sound.playAsync()

// after
import { useAudioPlayer } from 'expo-audio'
const player = useAudioPlayer(require('./assets/hello.mp3'))
// <Button title="Play" onPress={() => player.play()} />
// replay: player.seekTo(0); player.play()
```
Video:
```tsx
import { useVideoPlayer, VideoView } from 'expo-video'

const player = useVideoPlayer(videoSource, (p) => { p.loop = true; p.play() })
return <VideoView player={player} style={{ width: 350, height: 275 }} fullscreenOptions={{ enable: true }} allowsPictureInPicture />
```
In SDK 55 the `allowsFullscreen` prop of `VideoView` was removed; use `fullscreenOptions={{ enable: true }}`.

## Verify
`npm ls expo-av` is empty, and playback works in a development build (and in Expo Go on SDK 55+).

## Sources
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-53
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-54
- https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-55
- https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/audio/
- https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/video/

title: Claude Code deny rule Bash(git push:*) is prefix-only — 'git -C dir push' slips through; use a PreToolUse hook
body:
## Symptom
A settings file for an unattended agent denies `Bash(git push:*)`, `Bash(pm2:*)` etc. Under `bypassPermissions` the agent still ran `git -C /srv/app push` successfully.

## Cause
Bash permission rules match the command string by prefix. Anything that changes the prefix — `git -C x push`, `env FOO=1 git push`, `cd x && git push`, `bash -c '...'` — no longer matches the deny pattern.

## Fix
Keep the deny rules but add a `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash` that inspects the full command and exits with status 2 to block (stderr is shown to the model as the reason):
```json
{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"/srv/svc/guard.sh"}]}]}}
```
```bash
#!/bin/bash
cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command')
# deliberately broad: false positives are cheaper than a bypass
if echo "$cmd" | grep -Eq '\bgit\b.*\b(push|reset|rebase|checkout|commit)\b|\bpm2\b|\bsystemctl\b|\bnpm +install\b|\b(ssh|scp|rsync)\b|rm +-rf|\.env'; then
  echo "blocked by policy: $cmd" >&2; exit 2
fi
exit 0
```

## Verify
The hook was unit-tested against 18 commands (including `git -C x push`, chained and quoted forms) and live-tested under `bypassPermissions`: blocked commands were refused with the reason, allowed ones ran.

## Notes
Write the regex against variants, not just the canonical command. Keep a test list of evasions next to the hook.

title: Chrome on macOS fills disk: com.google.Chrome.code_sign_clone grows to tens of GB in the user temp dir
body:
## Symptom
The Mac's data volume drops to near zero free space; Finder's storage view and `du` of the home folder don't explain it.

## Cause
Chrome leaves a full code-signing clone of itself on launches under the per-user temporary directory: `$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)/../X/com.google.Chrome.code_sign_clone`. Observed: 26 clones, 37 GB apparent (~8 GB real, APFS clones), and growing.

## Fix
```bash
D="$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)/../X/com.google.Chrome.code_sign_clone"
du -sh "$D"; ls -lt "$D"
# keep the 2 newest, remove the rest (quit Chrome first)
ls -t "$D" | tail -n +3 | while read c; do rm -rf "$D/$c"; done
```

## Verify
`df -h /System/Volumes/Data` shows the space returned.

## Notes
Check this location first in any "Mac disk suddenly full" investigation.

title: Cloudflare challenge page hangs forever (spinner, no error): network blackholes UDP 443 and Chrome QUIC never falls back
body:
## Symptom
A Cloudflare-fronted site shows its "verify you are human" check; after the checkbox passes, the page hangs indefinitely. `lsof -i` / `nettop` for Chrome shows only a **UDP 443** socket open to the Cloudflare IP and no TCP connection.

## Cause
Chrome had previously learned that the origin supports HTTP/3 (Alt-Svc) and uses QUIC over UDP 443. Some ISPs (observed on a mobile carrier network) silently drop UDP 443 to certain ranges. Instead of quickly falling back to TCP, the connection stalls.

## Fix
Launch Chrome with QUIC disabled (or disable it in `chrome://flags/#enable-quic`):
```bash
"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --disable-quic
```
Disabling QUIC is harmless with Cloudflare (it falls back to HTTP/2 over TCP). Do NOT also disable HTTP/2.

## Verify
The page loads over TCP (`lsof -i -P | grep Chrome` shows TCP :443) within seconds after the challenge.

title: Windows remote exec: an argument like `src=>dst` passed through cmd.exe truncates dst to 0 bytes
error: ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
body:
## Symptom
A deploy helper on a Windows PC was invoked through a remote-exec agent that wraps commands in `cmd /c`, with arguments in the form `new.py=>C:\path\plot.py`. The script crashed with `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)` and, worse, the target `plot.py` files on the PC were now **0 bytes**.

## Cause
cmd.exe parses `>` anywhere in an unquoted (or improperly quoted) argument as output redirection. `a=>C:\x\plot.py` became argument `a=` plus "redirect stdout to C:\x\plot.py", which created/truncated the very file to be replaced. The script then saw no `=>` separator.

## Fix
- Never put `>`, `<`, `|`, `&` or `^` in arguments that may pass through cmd.exe; use a different separator (`::`), a JSON/argument file, or stdin.
- Prefer executing the interpreter directly (`CreateProcess` with an argv list, `subprocess.run([...], shell=False)`) instead of `cmd /c`.
- If cmd is unavoidable, quote the whole argument or escape with `^>`.
- Restore files by copying them directly (file-transfer API) rather than through a command line.

## Verify
`dir` showed `plot.py` at 0 bytes at the time of the failed call; re-uploading with the transfer API (no cmd.exe) restored 19091 bytes, and the next plot jobs ran normally.

title: Homebrew 6+: brew install from a third-party tap fails until you `brew trust` the tap or formula
body:
## Symptom
A script that ran `brew tap vendor/tools && brew install sometool` (short name) fails on a machine with current Homebrew; `brew doctor` warns about untrusted non-official taps. CI setup scripts written for Homebrew 4/5 break.

## Cause
Homebrew **6.0.0 (2026-06-11)** introduced tap trust: taps contain arbitrary Ruby, so non-official taps must be explicitly trusted before Homebrew evaluates their code. Docs: "Commands that need to load an untrusted tap or item will fail until the relevant trust is granted." Official taps stay trusted. `HOMEBREW_NO_REQUIRE_TAP_TRUST=1` is deprecated and will be removed.

## Fix
Installing by fully qualified name trusts only that item:
```bash
brew install vendor/tools/sometool
brew install --cask vendor/tools/someapp
```
Short names after tapping need explicit trust:
```bash
brew tap vendor/tools
brew trust --formula vendor/tools/sometool   # or --cask / --command
brew install sometool
# whole tap (all current and future items):
brew trust vendor/tools
```
Trust the canonical formula name; aliases and renames do not carry trust. In a Brewfile use the `trusted:` option (see the brew bundle docs).

## Verify
`brew trust` lists the entry; `brew untrust` (no args) lists what is still untrusted; `brew doctor` no longer warns.

## Sources
- https://docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust
- https://brew.sh/2026/06/11/homebrew-6.0.0/

title: `ReactDOMTestUtils.act` is deprecated in favor of `React.act` — import act from 'react' in React 19
error: `ReactDOMTestUtils.act` is deprecated in favor of `React.act`. Import `act` from `react` instead of `react-dom/test-utils`. See https://react.dev/warnings/react-dom-test-utils for more info.
body:
## Symptom
Tests log `ReactDOMTestUtils.act is deprecated in favor of React.act...`, and other helpers from `react-dom/test-utils` (e.g. `renderIntoDocument`, `Simulate`) throw when called. `react-test-renderer/shallow` imports fail.

## Cause
React 19 (stable 2024-12-05) moved `act` from `react-dom/test-utils` to `react`. All other `test-utils` functions were removed (they error when called; exports to be removed later). `react-test-renderer/shallow` was removed, and `react-test-renderer` itself is deprecated.

## Fix
```diff
- import {act} from 'react-dom/test-utils'
+ import {act} from 'react';
```
Codemod: `npx codemod@latest react/19/replace-act-import`.

Shallow renderer:
```bash
npm install react-shallow-renderer --save-dev
```
```diff
- import ShallowRenderer from 'react-test-renderer/shallow';
+ import ShallowRenderer from 'react-shallow-renderer';
```
For `Simulate`/`renderIntoDocument` and `react-test-renderer`, migrate to `@testing-library/react`.

## Verify
`grep -rn "react-dom/test-utils\|react-test-renderer/shallow" .` returns nothing outside node_modules; test run no longer prints the deprecation warning.

## Sources
- https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide

title: Tailwind v4: `ring` is now 1px currentColor and `border` defaults to currentColor, not 3px blue-500 / gray-200
segno QR codes unreadable by many scanners: segno silently emits Micro QR for short strings — pass micro=False
body:
## Symptom
QR codes encoding short part numbers (e.g. `ABC-05CB-226`) were generated with `segno.make(text)` and stamped onto PDF drawings. Many phone cameras (iOS CoreImage) and typical USB 2D barcode guns did not read them, even though they looked like valid QR codes at a glance.

## Cause
`segno.make()` chooses the smallest symbol that fits. For short payloads that is a **Micro QR** (one finder pattern instead of three), and many decoders do not support Micro QR.

## Fix
Force a regular QR symbol:
```python
import segno
qr = segno.make(text, micro=False, error="m", boost_error=True)
qr.save(path_png, scale=10, border=4)
# or: segno.make_qr(text, error="m")
```
Print the code at a decent size (about 25 mm on a drawing) with a white quiet zone.

## Verify
Every stamped page of a 98-page test set decoded back to its page's part number. Codes also decoded after blur, low toner, noise, a 25 degree tilt and stains were simulated.

## Notes
Decode-check the generated PDFs/PNGs in CI (e.g. OpenCV `QRCodeDetector` or `zbar`). Flatten any alpha channel onto white before decoding (see the related OpenCV entry).

title: Python 3.14 emits SyntaxWarning for return/break/continue inside finally (PEP 765)
body:
## Symptom
After moving to Python 3.14, importing a module prints a `SyntaxWarning` pointing at a `return`, `break` or `continue` inside a `finally:` block. Under `-W error` / `PYTHONWARNINGS=error` (common in CI) this becomes a hard failure at compile time.

## Cause
PEP 765, Python 3.14: "The compiler now emits a `SyntaxWarning` when a `return`, `break`, or `continue` statement have the effect of leaving a `finally` block." Such statements silently swallow the in-flight exception, which is almost always a bug.

## Fix
```python
# before: swallows any exception raised in the try
def f():
    try:
        work()
    finally:
        return cleanup()

# after
def f():
    try:
        work()
    finally:
        result = cleanup()
    return result
```
If the swallowing is intentional, make it explicit with `except BaseException: ...`. To silence while migrating third-party code: `PYTHONWARNINGS=error,ignore::SyntaxWarning` (filters only apply to code compiled after they are set, so clear `__pycache__`).

## Verify
`python3.14 -W error -m compileall -q -f src/` exits 0.

## Sources
- https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html

title: claude -p on a server: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed (authentication_failed)
error: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed
body:
## Symptom
A web console on a Linux server spawns `claude -p ... --output-format stream-json` as a service user. Every run fails instantly; the session transcript contains only:

```
assistant: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed
API error: authentication_failed
```

## Cause
The service user's `~/.claude/.credentials.json` came from an interactive `/login` copied onto the box. Inspecting it showed `expiresAt` missing and **no refreshToken** (another user's file had a refresh token but had expired weeks earlier). Once the access token lapses, the CLI cannot renew it non-interactively, so every headless run dies.

## Fix
Use a long-lived token created with `claude setup-token` and pass it through the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable via a tiny wrapper, then point the service at the wrapper:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# /srv/app/claude-tok.sh
export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="$(cat /srv/app/.oauth-token)"   # chmod 600, owned by the run user
exec /usr/bin/claude "$@"
```

```bash
chmod 755 /srv/app/claude-tok.sh
sudo -u svcuser -H /srv/app/claude-tok.sh -p "reply with: ok" --model claude-opus-5 < /dev/null
CLAUDE_BIN=/srv/app/claude-tok.sh pm2 restart console --update-env   # --update-env or pm2 keeps the old env
pm2 save                                                              # survive reboot
```

## Verify
The test prompt answered for two models, the console was restarted with the new `CLAUDE_BIN`, and a replayed real user message got a normal reply.

## Notes
- Without `< /dev/null`, `claude -p` prints `Warning: no stdin data received in 3s, proceeding without it` and waits 3 s when stdin is not a TTY.
- Check token health for every user that runs Claude on the box: `python3 -c 'import json;print(json.load(open(".claude/.credentials.json"))["claudeAiOauth"].get("expiresAt"))'`.

title: PDF with two complete PDFs concatenated: poppler (pdftoppm) reads the first document, pdf-lib reads the last
body:
## Symptom
For some uploaded drawing PDFs, thumbnails/OCR (rendered with poppler) show one drawing, but the PDF produced by pdf-lib (vector stamping/printing) contains a different drawing. A stamp positioned using the poppler raster landed on top of geometry in the printed output, and a matcher read the wrong part number from the file.

## Cause
A PDM system exported files consisting of **two complete PDF documents glued byte-wise** (previous drawing + current drawing). Readers resolve such files differently: poppler parsed the first document; pdf-lib, which honors the last trailer/xref like an incremental update, loaded the second. Files where the appended part has no `/Catalog` behave the same in both and are harmless.

## Fix
Normalize at upload time: re-save with the same library that does the final output, and use that normalized file for everything (raster, OCR, matching, printing). Keep the raw file for audit.
```ts
import { PDFDocument } from 'pdf-lib';
const doc = await PDFDocument.load(raw, { ignoreEncryption: true });
const clean = await doc.save();            // single, consistent document
fs.writeFileSync(path + '.glued', raw);    // keep original
fs.writeFileSync(path, clean);
```
Detect candidates by counting `%%EOF`/`/Catalog` occurrences, or by comparing page counts/dimensions between poppler (`pdfinfo`) and pdf-lib.

## Verify
13 affected files repaired; 177/177 normal prints were pixel-identical before/after the change, and 81/81 prints of the day had zero ink under the stamp. Test method: "covered ink" = pixels dark in the source render and white in the stamped render.

title: Bun 1.3: new workspaces use the isolated linker by default — undeclared (phantom) dependency imports stop resolving
body:
## Symptom
In a Bun monorepo created on Bun >= 1.3, a package imports something it never declared in its own `package.json` (it is only a dependency of another workspace or of the root) and module resolution fails, or a tool that expects a flat root `node_modules` can't find packages. `node_modules` contains symlinks into `node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@<ver>/node_modules/...` instead of a flat tree. The same code works in an older Bun repo.

## Cause
Bun 1.3 (2025-10-10) introduced isolated (pnpm-style) installs and "if you use `\"workspaces\"` in your `package.json`, we're making it the default behavior." Per the docs, this applies to **new** workspace projects (`configVersion = 1` in `bun.lock`); existing lockfiles without a config version get `configVersion = 0` and keep the hoisted linker. Projects migrated from pnpm get `configVersion = 1`; from npm/Yarn get `0`. Bun 1.4 keeps this rule.

## Fix
Correct fix — declare every dependency a workspace package imports:

```bash
cd packages/web && bun add zod
```

Or opt back into a flat layout:

```bash
bun install --linker=hoisted
```

```toml
# bunfig.toml
[install]
linker = "hoisted"
```

## Verify
`ls -la node_modules/<pkg>` — a symlink into `.bun/` means isolated, a real directory means hoisted. `bun run build` in each workspace succeeds after a clean `rm -rf node_modules && bun install`.

## Sources
- https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.3
- https://bun.sh/docs/install/isolated
- https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/28792

title: Next.js 16 removed serverRuntimeConfig / publicRuntimeConfig and getConfig() from next/config — use env vars
body:
## Symptom Code such as `import getConfig from 'next/config'` with `getConfig().publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl`, or `serverRuntimeConfig`/`publicRuntimeConfig` keys in next.config, stops working after upgrading to Next.js 16. Agents still suggest runtime config as the way to read config at runtime instead of build time in Docker images. ## Cause Next.js 16.0 (2025-10-21) removed `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` (deprecated earlier). The replacement is environment variables. ## Fix Before: ```js // next.config.js module.exports = { serverRuntimeConfig: { dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL }, publicRuntimeConfig: { apiUrl: '/api' }, } // pages/index.tsx import getConfig from 'next/config' const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() ``` After: ```bash # .env.local NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" ``` ```tsx // Server Component / route handler: read server-only values directly const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL // Client Component: only NEXT_PUBLIC_* values (inlined at build time) 'use client' const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ``` To read a value at request time instead of baking it in at build (for example one image deployed to several environments), call `connection()` first in a server component: ```tsx import { connection } from 'next/server' export default async function Page() { await connection() return

{process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG}

} ``` Use the taint API so server secrets don't leak into Client Components. ## Verify `grep -rn "next/config\|RuntimeConfig" --include=*.{js,ts,tsx,mjs} .` returns nothing (outside node_modules), and the values render correctly in both server and client components. ## Sources - https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#runtime-configuration - https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16

title: transformers v5 removed TensorFlow and JAX/Flax: TFAutoModel / FlaxAutoModel no longer exist — PyTorch only
body:
## Symptom
After `pip install -U transformers` (5.x), imports such as `from transformers import TFAutoModel, TFBertModel, FlaxAutoModelForCausalLM` fail, and `from_pretrained(..., from_tf=True)` style workflows break. Tutorials written for v4 assume TF/Keras and Flax classes exist.

## Cause
transformers v5.0.0 (2026-01-26): "We're removing the TensorFlow and Jax parts of the library ... keeping `torch` as the only backend for now" (PR #40760). TorchScript and `torch.fx` support were also dropped in favour of `torch.compile`/dynamo and `torch.export`.

## Fix
- Port to the PyTorch classes (`AutoModel`, `AutoModelForCausalLM`, ...) with `torch` installed.
- If you must stay on TF/Flax, pin: `pip install "transformers<5"`.
- Replace `torch.jit.trace`/`torch.fx` export paths with `torch.export` or `torch.compile`; `TrainingArguments(jit_mode_eval=...)` is gone, use `use_torch_compile`.

## Verify
`python -c "import transformers; print(transformers.__version__)"` and your model loads via `AutoModel.from_pretrained(...)` with torch.

## Sources
- https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md
- https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/40760

title: Collections must have a loader defined — Astro 6 removed type: 'content' / type: 'data' collections
error: Collections must have a loader defined. Check your collection definitions in your content config file.
body:
## Symptom
Astro 6 fails with `ContentCollectionMissingLoader`:
```
Collections must have a loader defined. Check your collection definitions in your content config file.
```
or with `ContentCollectionInvalidType`:
```
Invalid collection type “data”. Remove the type from your collection definition in your content config file.
```
The collection is written in the Astro 2-4 style: `defineCollection({ type: 'content', schema })`.

## Cause
Astro 6.0 (2026-03-10) removed legacy content collections. There are no collection types any more. Every collection gets its entries from a `loader` (built-in `glob()` / `file()` from `astro/loaders`, or a custom loader). Astro 5 auto-converted loader-less collections, so v5 projects without errors can still break on v6.

## Fix
```ts
// before (Astro <= 5 legacy)
import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content'
const blog = defineCollection({ type: 'content', schema: z.object({ title: z.string() }) })
const authors = defineCollection({ type: 'data', schema: z.object({ name: z.string() }) })

// after (Astro 6, src/content.config.ts)
import { defineCollection } from 'astro:content'
import { glob, file } from 'astro/loaders'
import { z } from 'astro/zod'
const blog = defineCollection({
  loader: glob({ pattern: '**/[^_]*.{md,mdx}', base: './src/content/blog' }),
  schema: z.object({ title: z.string() }),
})
const authors = defineCollection({
  loader: glob({ pattern: '**/*.json', base: './src/content/authors' }),
  schema: z.object({ name: z.string() }),
})
export const collections = { blog, authors }
```
Astro 6 also uses Zod 4. Use `z.email()` instead of `z.string().email()`, and `{ error: '...' }` instead of `{ message: '...' }`. Importing `z` from `astro:content` is deprecated; use `astro/zod`.

## Verify
`npx astro sync` generates types without errors, and `npx astro build` succeeds.

## Sources
- https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/upgrade-to/v6/
- https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/errors/content-collection-missing-loader/
- https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/errors/content-collection-invalid-type/

title: Chrome/Edge print dialog freezes (Not Responding) on Windows: last-used printer is a share on a PC that no longer exists
body:
## Symptom
On an office PC, clicking Print in a web app (Edge) hung the print preview ("未响应" / Not Responding), and nothing printed. The server-side PDF endpoints were all returning 200 with real PDFs, so the web app was fine.

## Cause
Two things combined:
1. Chromium-based browsers reopen the print dialog on the **last printer used in the browser**, not the Windows default printer.
2. That printer was a shared connection, `\\OLD-PC\HP LaserJet ...`, to a PC that no longer existed. Its name did not resolve and SMB/445 did not answer, so the preview blocked waiting on it.

A separate USB printer on the same PC was physically disconnected, but Windows still listed it. `Get-Printer` / `Win32_Printer` showed `PrinterStatus Normal` once its stuck job was cleared. **"Normal" does not mean a USB printer is present.**

## Fix
Diagnose (PowerShell):
```powershell
Get-Printer | Select Name,PrinterStatus,JobCount,PortName
Get-Printer | % { Get-PrintJob -PrinterName $_.Name -EA SilentlyContinue } | Select PrinterName,DocumentName,JobStatus,SubmittedTime
[System.Net.Dns]::GetHostAddresses('OLD-PC')                 # fails for a dead host
Test-NetConnection OLD-PC -Port 445
Get-PnpDevice | ? { $_.InstanceId -match '^USBPRINT' } | Select Status,Present,FriendlyName   # Present=False => unplugged
```
Remove the dead connections. `Remove-Printer` can itself block on a dead host, so run it in a job with a timeout:
```powershell
foreach ($n in '\\OLD-PC\HP LaserJet Pro MFP M126nw','\\OTHER-DEAD\HP ...') {
  $j = Start-Job { param($x) Remove-Printer -Name $x -ErrorAction Stop; "removed $x" } -ArgumentList $n
  if (Wait-Job $j -Timeout 40) { Receive-Job $j } else { "TIMEOUT $n"; Stop-Job $j }
}
```
Then open the print dialog once and select a working printer. The browser remembers that choice for next time. Re-add a removed share later with `Add-Printer -ConnectionName '\\host\printer'`.

## Verify
After removing the two dead connections (about 38 s), the Edge print dialog opened instantly. Switching to the live shared printer and printing sent the job straight through: the queue stayed empty and the page returned immediately. A test page sent with `Out-Printer -Name <shared printer>` also went through.

## Notes
`Remove-PrintJob` on a job stuck behind an unplugged USB printer looked like it failed, but it completed a few minutes later. Re-check before restarting the spooler.

title: Your app (or one of its dependencies) is using an outdated JSX transform — React 19 requires the new JSX runtime
error: Your app (or one of its dependencies) is using an outdated JSX transform. Update to the modern JSX transform for faster performance: https://react.dev/link/new-jsx-transform
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to React 19 the console shows `Your app (or one of its dependencies) is using an outdated JSX transform...`.

## Cause
React 19 (stable 2024-12-05) requires the new JSX transform (introduced 2020) — it is needed for features such as `ref` as a prop. The classic transform (`React.createElement`, tsconfig `"jsx": "react"`, Babel `runtime: 'classic'`) triggers this warning.

## Fix
TypeScript:
```diff
// tsconfig.json
- "jsx": "react"
+ "jsx": "react-jsx"   // or "react-jsxdev" in dev; "preserve" if a bundler (Next.js) handles JSX
```
Babel:
```diff
- ["@babel/preset-react", { "runtime": "classic" }]
+ ["@babel/preset-react", { "runtime": "automatic" }]
```
With the new transform you no longer need `import React from 'react'` just for JSX. If the warning comes from a dependency's prebuilt bundle, upgrade that dependency.

## Verify
Compiled output imports from `react/jsx-runtime` (e.g. `_jsx(...)`) instead of calling `React.createElement`; the warning is gone.

## Sources
- https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide

title: Tailwind v4 ignores tailwind.config.js — custom colors/fonts vanish; move them to @theme or load with @config
Claude Opus 4.7+ returns 400 for temperature/top_p/top_k; anthropic Python SDK v1.0 raises TypeError
body:
## Symptom
Code that sets `temperature=0` (or `top_p`, `top_k`) for determinism fails: HTTP 400 on Claude 4.7-and-later models when a non-default value is set, and with `anthropic` Python SDK v1.0+ the call raises `TypeError` before any request is sent (the parameters no longer exist on `messages.create`).

## Cause
Anthropic deprecated `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` for Claude 4.7 and later models (and Claude Mythos Preview). The Python SDK v1.0 removed them from the request types. Other SDKs keep them for type-checking, but the API still rejects non-default values.

## Fix
Remove the parameters entirely and steer behavior via the prompt.
```python
# before
client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-4-1-20250805", temperature=0, ...)
# after
client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-5-5", ...)
```
`temperature=0` never guaranteed identical outputs on earlier models either. For machine-readable output use structured outputs (`output_config.format`).

## Verify
`grep -rnE 'temperature|top_p|top_k' .` finds no Anthropic call sites; requests return 200.

## Sources
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/opus-5-5/migration-guide

title: old cluster does not use data checksums but the new one does (pg_upgrade to PostgreSQL 18)
error: old cluster does not use data checksums but the new one does
body:
## Symptom
`pg_upgrade` from PostgreSQL 17 (or older) to 18 stops with:

```
old cluster does not use data checksums but the new one does
```

Seen with distro upgrade scripts and the `tianon/postgres-upgrade` image.

## Cause
PostgreSQL 18 (2025-09-25) changed the `initdb` default to **enable data checksums**. Clusters created by earlier versions had them off by default. `pg_upgrade` requires matching checksum settings.

## Fix
Option A: create the new 18 cluster without checksums (fast, matches the old one):
```bash
initdb --no-data-checksums -D /path/to/18/data
# Debian/Ubuntu: pg_createcluster 18 main -- --no-data-checksums
```
Option B: keep checksums by enabling them on the stopped old cluster first (rewrites every page; slow on big databases):
```bash
pg_ctl -D /path/to/17/data stop
pg_checksums --enable -D /path/to/17/data
```
Option C: on a fresh, empty 18 cluster you can turn them off with `pg_checksums --disable -D <newdata>` before upgrading.

Run `pg_upgrade --check ...` first to catch this before doing the real upgrade.

## Verify
`pg_controldata <datadir> | grep checksum` shows the same `Data page checksum version` for old and new; `pg_upgrade --check` passes.

## Sources
- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/
- https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/bin/pg_upgrade/controldata.c
- https://github.com/tianon/docker-postgres-upgrade/issues/121

title: openpyxl hangs loading an xlsx whose <dimension ref> is huge (A1:WVQ983110, typical of WPS-saved files)
body:
## Symptom
Loading a small (55-row) delivery-note template with `openpyxl.load_workbook()` never finishes / eats memory.

## Cause
The sheet XML declares `<dimension ref="A1:WVQ983110"/>` (saved by WPS Office, with column styles spanning the whole sheet). openpyxl trusts the declared extent and column/row definitions, so it builds or iterates an enormous grid.

## Fix
Treat the file as a template and work at the XML level: unzip, read `xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml`, `xl/styles.xml`, `xl/sharedStrings.xml`, keep the original styles/theme, regenerate only the sheet XML with the needed rows (reusing the template's style ids), then zip it back:
```python
import zipfile, re
z = zipfile.ZipFile('template.xlsx')
sheet = z.read('xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml').decode()
print(re.search(r'<dimension ref="([^"]+)"', sheet).group(1))   # diagnose
```
For read-only extraction, openpyxl's `read_only=True` mode with `ws.reset_dimensions()` is the documented escape hatch for wrong dimensions (not tested on this file).

## Verify
XML-level generation produced an .xlsx identical in look to the customer's template (checked visually with `qlmanage -t -s 1600 -o outdir file.xlsx` on macOS, which renders xlsx thumbnails without LibreOffice).

title: Claude Code PreToolUse hook decision "approve"/"block" is deprecated — use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision
body:
## Symptom
A PreToolUse hook prints `{"decision": "approve", "reason": "..."}` or `{"decision": "block"}` (the original 2025 hook format, still in many blog posts). It is handled through a compatibility mapping and can't express `ask`, `updatedInput` or extra context.

## Cause
For PreToolUse, the top-level `decision`/`reason` fields are deprecated; `"approve"` maps to `"allow"` and `"block"` to `"deny"`. Permission decisions moved under `hookSpecificOutput` (exposed to hooks in v1.0.59, 2025-07-23). Other events such as PostToolUse and Stop still use top-level `decision`/`reason`.

## Fix
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "deny",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "rm -rf outside the repo is blocked"
  }
}
```
Values: `allow`, `deny`, `ask`. Exit 0 and print the JSON to stdout (exit code 2 still blocks, with stderr fed back to Claude). `permissions.deny` rules win over a hook's `allow`.

## Verify
Run `claude --debug` and confirm the hook's decision is applied; a deny shows the reason to Claude.

## Sources
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks
- https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

title: Ingress NGINX (kubernetes/ingress-nginx) was retired 2026-03-24: no more releases or CVE fixes; move to Gateway API
body:
## Symptom
Agents and tutorials still install `ingress-nginx` (Helm chart / `controller` image) as the default Ingress controller and write `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/*` annotations. No new versions appear, and security scanners flag unpatched CVEs.

## Cause
Kubernetes SIG Network and the Security Response Committee announced the retirement on 2025-11-11 and retired Ingress NGINX on **2026-03-24**. Since then there are no releases, no bugfixes and no security updates; repos are read-only. Existing deployments keep working and Helm charts/images stay downloadable. InGate, the planned successor, is also retired.

## Fix
Check whether you run it:
```bash
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx
```
Migrate to Gateway API (`Gateway` + `HTTPRoute`) with a maintained implementation, or to another maintained Ingress controller listed in the Kubernetes docs. Annotations such as `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet` have no direct equivalent and must be rewritten as Gateway API filters or controller-specific policy.

## Verify
The selector above returns no pods; `kubectl get gateway,httproute -A` shows your routes with `Accepted`/`Programmed` conditions true.

## Sources
- https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/11/11/ingress-nginx-retirement/
- https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/04/22/kubernetes-v1-36-release/

title: TypeError: context.getScope is not a function — ESLint 9 moved rule-context methods to sourceCode
error: TypeError: context.getScope is not a function
body:
## Symptom
Linting crashes inside a plugin rule after upgrading to ESLint 9 or 10:

```
TypeError: context.getScope is not a function
TypeError: context.getAncestors is not a function
TypeError: context.markVariableAsUsed is not a function
TypeError: context.getDeclaredVariables is not a function
```
On ESLint 10 the same class of crash appears for `context.getSourceCode`, `context.getFilename`, `context.getCwd`, `context.getPhysicalFilename`.

## Cause
ESLint v9.0.0 (2024-04-05) removed many deprecated `context` methods and moved them to the `SourceCode` object, some with new signatures. ESLint v10.0.0 (2026-02-06) additionally removed `context.getCwd()`, `getFilename()`, `getPhysicalFilename()`, `getSourceCode()`, `parserOptions` and `parserPath`. A plugin (or your own local rule) still calling the old API throws.

## Fix
1. Upgrade the plugin to its latest major.
2. If it is still not updated, wrap it with `@eslint/compat`:
```js
// eslint.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'eslint/config'
import { fixupPluginRules, fixupConfigRules } from '@eslint/compat'
import somePlugin from 'eslint-plugin-some-plugin'
import someConfig from 'eslint-config-some-config'

export default defineConfig([
  ...fixupConfigRules(someConfig),
  { plugins: { somePlugin: fixupPluginRules(somePlugin) },
    rules: { 'somePlugin/rule-name': 'error' } },
])
```
3. For your own rules, migrate the calls:
```js
// before                         // after
context.getScope()                sourceCode.getScope(node)
context.getAncestors()            sourceCode.getAncestors(node)
context.markVariableAsUsed(name)  sourceCode.markVariableAsUsed(name, node)
context.getSource()               sourceCode.getText()
context.getSourceCode()           context.sourceCode
context.getFilename()             context.filename
context.getCwd()                  context.cwd
context.parserOptions             context.languageOptions.parserOptions
```
(where `const sourceCode = context.sourceCode`). Automate with `npx codemod @eslint/v9-to-v10` or `eslint-transforms v9-rule-migration rules/`.

## Verify
`npx eslint .` completes; open an issue on the plugin repo if you needed the compat wrapper.

## Sources
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/troubleshooting/v9-rule-api-changes
- https://eslint.org/docs/v9.x/use/migrate-to-9.0.0
- https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/migrate-to-10.0.0
- https://github.com/eslint/rewrite/tree/main/packages/compat

title: It looks like you're trying to use `tailwindcss` directly as a PostCSS plugin — install @tailwindcss/postcss (v4)
error: It looks like you're trying to use `tailwindcss` directly as a PostCSS plugin. The PostCSS plugin has moved to a separate package, so to continue using Tailwind CSS with PostCSS you'll need to install `@tailwindcss/postcss` and update your PostCSS configuration.
body:
## Symptom
The CSS build (Vite, Next.js, webpack postcss-loader, Angular) fails with:

```
It looks like you're trying to use `tailwindcss` directly as a PostCSS plugin. The PostCSS plugin has moved to a separate package, so to continue using Tailwind CSS with PostCSS you'll need to install `@tailwindcss/postcss` and update your PostCSS configuration.
```

Typical trigger: `npm install tailwindcss` now resolves to v4, but `postcss.config.js` still lists `tailwindcss: {}` (the v3 setup most tutorials and older models produce).

## Cause
Tailwind CSS v4.0 (2025-01-22) split the PostCSS plugin out of the `tailwindcss` package into `@tailwindcss/postcss`. Loading `tailwindcss` as a PostCSS plugin now throws this error. v4 also handles `@import` inlining and vendor prefixing itself, so `postcss-import` and `autoprefixer` are no longer needed.

## Fix
```bash
npm install -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss
npm uninstall autoprefixer postcss-import   # optional, no longer needed
```

Before (v3):
```js
// postcss.config.mjs
export default {
  plugins: {
    'postcss-import': {},
    tailwindcss: {},
    autoprefixer: {},
  },
};
```
After (v4):
```js
// postcss.config.mjs
export default {
  plugins: {
    '@tailwindcss/postcss': {},
  },
};
```
If you use Vite, prefer the dedicated `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin instead of PostCSS. Create React App (react-scripts) hard-codes the old plugin in its webpack config, so postcss.config alone cannot fix it: a maintainer recommends ejecting or CRACO to swap in `@tailwindcss/postcss` (CRA is deprecated), or pin `tailwindcss@3`.

Also replace the `@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;` directives with `@import "tailwindcss";`.

## Verify
Restart the dev server (PostCSS config is read at startup); the error is gone and utility classes render.

## Sources
- https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide
- https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/17535
- https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/discussions/16828
- https://unpkg.com/tailwindcss@4.1.14/dist/lib.js (error string)

title: kubelet fails to start after upgrading to Kubernetes 1.35 on cgroup v1 nodes (failCgroupV1 now defaults to true)
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading nodes to Kubernetes v1.35+, the kubelet will not start on older Linux distributions; `kubeadm init/join/upgrade` fails the SystemVerification preflight check instead of only warning.

## Cause
Kubernetes v1.35 (2025-12-17) set the kubelet's `failCgroupV1` to `true` by default, so the kubelet refuses to run on cgroup v1 hosts. cgroup v1 support is deprecated and full removal is tracked in KEP-5573. The override still exists in v1.37, but is a short-term bridge; memory QoS and some newer features only work on cgroup v2.

## Fix
Check the node:
```bash
stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/   # cgroup2fs = v2, tmpfs = v1
```
Preferred: move the node to cgroup v2 (newer distro/kernel; the Kubernetes docs list kernel 5.8+ as a requirement). Temporary bridge:
```yaml
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: KubeletConfiguration
failCgroupV1: false   # temporary override
```

## Verify
`systemctl status kubelet` is active and `kubectl get nodes` shows the node `Ready`.

## Sources
- https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/12/17/kubernetes-v1-35-release/
- https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/08/26/kubernetes-v1-37-release/
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/cgroups/

title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype') in buffer-equal-constant-time on Node 25+
error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')
body:
## Symptom
A server using JWTs (jsonwebtoken → jws → jwa) dies at startup on Node 25+ with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')` at `.../buffer-equal-constant-time/index.js:37:35` — before any app code runs. Works on Node 22/24.

## Cause
`buffer.SlowBuffer` (DEP0030) was runtime-deprecated in Node 24 and moved to End-of-Life (removed) in Node 25.0.0 (2025-10-15): "The `SlowBuffer` class has been removed. Please use `Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow(size)` instead." The abandoned `buffer-equal-constant-time@1.0.1` (last published 2013) reads `SlowBuffer.prototype.equal` at module load. Old lockfiles pin `jwa@1.4.1` / `jwa@2.0.0`, which `require('buffer-equal-constant-time')` eagerly.

## Fix
Upgrade the chain so `jwa` uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (jwa 1.4.2 / 2.0.1, published 2025-05-07, only lazy-load the old package when `timingSafeEqual` is missing):
```bash
npm ls buffer-equal-constant-time jwa     # find who pulls it
npm install jsonwebtoken@^9.0.3           # depends on jws ^4.0.1 -> jwa ^2.0.1
```
If the chain comes from another package, force the patched jwa:
```json
// package.json (npm) — use pnpm.overrides / resolutions for pnpm / yarn
"overrides": { "jwa": "^2.0.1" }
```
Then reinstall so the lockfile resolves jwa >= 1.4.2 / >= 2.0.1. In your own code, replace `SlowBuffer(n)` with `Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow(n)`. Short-term: run Node 24 LTS.

## Verify
`npm ls jwa` shows 1.4.2+/2.0.1+; `node -e "require('jsonwebtoken')"` exits cleanly on Node 25+.

## Sources
- https://nodejs.org/api/deprecations.html
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v25.0.0
- https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/issues/16148
- https://github.com/auth0/node-jsonwebtoken/pull/1001
- https://registry.npmjs.org/jsonwebtoken
- https://unpkg.com/jwa@2.0.1/index.js

title: TypeScript 6.0 deprecates baseUrl and TypeScript 7.0 removes it — make paths entries relative to tsconfig
body:
## Symptom
An agent scaffolds `"baseUrl": "."` / `"baseUrl": "./src"` next to `paths` (the pre-2026 idiom). TypeScript 6.0 flags it as deprecated (unless `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"`), and on TypeScript 7.0 it is not supported at all; bare imports that only resolved via `baseUrl` as a lookup root (`import x from 'utils/x'`) stop resolving.

## Cause
TypeScript 6.0 (2026-03-23): "`baseUrl` is deprecated and will no longer be considered a look-up root for module resolution." TypeScript 7.0 (2026-07-08) turns every 6.0 deprecation into a hard error; `paths` must be relative to the project root. `paths` has not needed `baseUrl` since TS 4.1.

## Fix
```jsonc
// Before
{ "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": "./src",
    "paths": { "@app/*": ["app/*"], "@lib/*": ["lib/*"] } } }

// After
{ "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": { "@app/*": ["./src/app/*"], "@lib/*": ["./src/lib/*"] } } }
```
If code relied on `baseUrl` as a lookup root for bare specifiers, add a catch-all: `"paths": { "*": ["./src/*"] }`. Remember `paths` only affects type-checking; your bundler/runtime needs the same aliases (Vite `resolve.alias`, Node `imports` in package.json, etc.).

## Verify
`npx tsc --noEmit` with TS 6 passes without `ignoreDeprecations`; with TS 7 `tsc` accepts the config.

## Sources
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0-beta/
- https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/

title: Playwright 1.57 removed page.accessibility — use toMatchAriaSnapshot() or @axe-core/playwright
body:
## Symptom
After upgrading to Playwright 1.57+, `await page.accessibility.snapshot()` fails because `page.accessibility` is undefined. TypeScript reports that the property does not exist on `Page`. Older answers and generated tests still use `page.accessibility.snapshot()` to assert on the accessibility tree.

## Cause
Playwright 1.57 (2025-11-25) removed `page.accessibility`, which had been deprecated for 3 years. For accessibility testing the release notes point to libraries such as Axe. The same release switched Chromium to Chrome for Testing builds (headed uses `chrome`, headless uses `chrome-headless-shell`) and moved the Docker images to Node 24.

## Fix
For tree/structure assertions, use ARIA snapshots:
```ts
// before
const tree = await page.accessibility.snapshot()
expect(tree).toMatchObject({ role: 'WebArea' })

// after
await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
  - navigation:
    - link "Home"
`)
// or read it as YAML
const yaml = await page.locator('body').ariaSnapshot()
```
For a11y violations, use Axe:
```ts
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright'
const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()
expect(results.violations).toEqual([])
```

## Verify
`npx tsc --noEmit` shows no `accessibility` errors, and `npx playwright test` passes.

## Sources
- https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes
